title: The Nature of Prophetic Word and Divine Wrath
english: The preceding text for the clarification of Zechariah, who is the eleventh of the Twelve Prophets, having an eye of the intellect enlightened, having been made god-like by the word that came to him, saw a great vision and announced a prophetic word in many ways and in many forms. Since we are eager to understand this, let us begin with the clarification concerning him, entreating that a word may be given in the opening of the mouth, with you all running together in prayer, being confident that such a thing will be attained for the one who strives.
Zechariah 1:1: In the eighth month of the second year, during the reign of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying.

In the second year of the reign of Darius the Persian king, in the eighth month of the second year of the beginning of the one ruling, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, declaring how a great wrath has come upon the fathers of those being reproved, with God being indignant against those being accused.

And Zechariah, to whom the word of God came, is called by the voice of the Hebrews, but to the memory of the Greeks he is being interpreted as God. For how is it not a memory of God the one who is not [missing text] of God [missing text] having? And of that same [missing text] both Berechiah is and [missing text] being named after the memory of [missing text], the father of Zechariah, [missing text] Iddo.

A tradition came to us then, to remember the bearers of prophets when they themselves also happen to be healers of God. And it is shown especially how the preceding prophet and his fathers, being of the priestly race and according to the Gospel of Luke: for the father of the Baptist John, Zechariah, and Berechiah, the parent of this one, were given these names. For as the later ones encounter the same kind as those who preceded, especially when they are saints, they possess the same callings.
And they become memories in the prefaces.

Regarding the prophecies of the ancestors called by God to prophesy and the time of their prophecy. And it is [stated] for the sake of security, so that it does not become a deception through homonymy or pseudonymity.

1.7 The word of God becomes toward someone when he participates in it, just as virtue and knowledge become in a diligent and knowledgeable man. But what the word of God implies and argues against the one established by prophetic word will be clear from the following.
1.8 'These,' he says, 'says the Lord of hosts: The Lord was angry with your fathers, a great anger' (Zechariah 1:3).

1.9 A great anger comes upon those sinning greatly and being impious; for God, giving judgment 'to each according to his works' (Romans 2:6) and according to the practice of the one transgressing the divine laws, does not threaten the same punishment to all, but [one] proportionate and corresponding to those who have sinned. And the threat breathes much goodness; for if God were to punish defensively those cast into this, he would not foretell, but would bring the punishment upon them without delay.

1.10 The possessor of the divine word stands as a protector to urge the captured toward repentance, saying: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn to me,' keeping my commandments and coming to know my truth; for thus you will find me having turned to you. For I, being unmoved and unchangeable, always being the same and likewise, seem to turn away from you and to distance myself from you when you endure this.

1.11 He speaks, indeed, to those being reproved as to one to all: 'Because you know, I will cast you away and I will cast you away from serving me; remember the law of your God, and I will remember your children.' And regarding certain sensible things such a thing appears; for the earth, while being motionless upon its own seat, those departing from it by ships, they themselves, distancing themselves, receive the sensation as if it were distancing.
1.12 The greatness of the goodness

title: Mathematical properties of 24 and the vision of Zechariah
english: Standing by, he who says these things says that the Almighty will do such things; for having great compassion and extreme goodness, he calls those who distance themselves from God and from virtue to return and draw near, so that having approached him and staying near him, they may obtain eternal salvation, according to what is written: 'Draw near to the Lord and he will draw near to you' (James 4:8). These said retreats and proximities occur in relation and disposition, but not in place.

Turning to me, and I to you. You do not become like those who begot you according to wickedness, whom the prophets called before the present time, so that you might not suffer the same things as them. And what did they call to them? Or to turn away from faulty customs and evil ways? But not having heard and not having attended to them, they perished along with those deceived by false prophets, so that there are no longer even the foxes or those snatched away by their sorcery. Since therefore neither the prophets nor the deceived are [present], you, to whom I bring the word of God, walk the divine ways and do not pursue the evil ones.

For divine and profitable instructions are announced to us in our Spirit—this is the Holy—by my servants the prophets who have it; for these, having the Spirit of truth and being prepared by it for speaking, benefit those who pay attention to them, of whom those called fathers have had experience; because they neither heard nor paid attention to them, they were answered through their works. Just as the Lord has stretched out to do, so it shall happen to them, even if God has stirred them to repentance, so that they might not suffer the things threatened.

In the fourth and sixth [month] in the twelfth month—this is the month of Sabbath—in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying (Zechariah 1:7). All things happening and being given by God have order and harmony which has proportion, 'doing great and unsearchable things,' 'arranging all by measure and number.' Moreover, the word of the prophet lying before us, becoming visible more by scientific theory than by being heard, is arranged having much certainty according to number in a tetrad...

And the twenty-fourth of the twelfth month according to the Hebrews. The number 24 is powerful as a square; for this is divided by its parts thus: half 12, a third 8, a fourth 6, a sixth 4, an eighth 3, a twelfth 2, a twenty-fourth 1. That which is born from 24 according to the composition of its parts is a square, for six times six. And nothing is so certain of forms as the square.

The one before us has an exceptional quality, that each of its sides has composed a perfect number, the six. Likewise with 24, and the 12, being composed of its parts, produces a square: half 6, a third 4, a fourth 3, a sixth 2, a twelfth 1; these parts, being composed together, fulfill the sixteen, the latter being also a square, a small square of four. And this has an exceptional quality according to its own sides; for the square is a ten in power thus: 1, 2, 3, 4.

I saw in the night, and behold a man riding a red horse, and he was standing among the two mountains of shade, and behind him red and mixed and variegated and white horses (Zechariah 1:8). When the word of the Lord came to Zechariah by night, there was seen to him a man riding a red horse, standing among the two mountains of shade (Zechariah 1:7). And the man riding the red horse is the Savior who became man. And a red horse is that which surrounds a body; for the human flesh is red by nature, because blood flows through it. But where did he see the man standing, and between whom, and when was the one receiving God to stand watch?

He saw him, then, 'among the mountains of shade.' These two covenants happen to be fruitful and shady because of the density of meanings and the ambiguity of the words concerning theology and incarnation. And since each of those announced in the two covenants has much obscurity with enigma and depth, in a night he saw the approach of the man to the horse, similarly to what was said about him: 'He set darkness as his hidden garment' (Zechariah 6:5); for in this expression, that which is hidden is signified by the obscurity, just as in: 'The abyss was as his enveloping garment' (Psalm 183:6). To see the interpreted man riding the red horse, and the horses coming behind him, very...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Isaiah's multifaceted ministry and the indwelling Christ
english: It has been viewed theologically. And those following him come behind him; for Moses, the great theophany, not yet being able to see his face knowningly, has been set to see those behind him, that is, those with him, and not other things existing of the creation of God. For having neglected to show those after God, which are called behind him, he wrote down the Creation, beginning from: 'In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth' (Gen 1:1).

A different color of the horses behind the one appearing is written down, since some of them are men, and others are divine 'spirits, being sent for service for those about to inherit salvation.' For those who have handed over the human things of the Word's appearing and becoming flesh, are red, especially since even he, behind whom they exist, says 'a garment of red from Bozrah,' as it was said to him by those who saw: 'Why are your garments red?' saying his garments which surround the flesh and the blood sprinkled upon it. These things have been made more clear in the commentaries of the prophet Isaiah.

After the red horses behind the one being praised, various and dappled and white horses appeared. And perhaps the various and dappled ones are those who lead the teaching in many ways concerning the sensible and the intelligible, which the divine words say are 'visible and invisible,' while the white ones are those announcing the theological things apart from all matter. It must be said according to another thought that the various and dappled ones are those fitting in teaching to the various condition of those being instructed. Or was not Paul a various horse, being a follower of the Christ speaking in him, when to the Jews he became a Jew to win these, and to the lawless as lawless, to turn them from the lawless disposition, and to those under law as under law, so that he might win them also, persuading them to transcend 'the law of shadow' (Heb 10:1)? After having said these things, he says: 'I have become all things to all, so that I might save all' (1 Cor 9:22).

And not only those after the appearing, but also those before it had this variety, participating in 'the manifold wisdom of God' (Eph 3:10), of which it is enough to mention two, so that the discourse may not become long, d...

Having been present and having moved to the others by thought. 1.28 Isaiah, having received all the kinds of helpful words from God through divine visions, possessed them all at once. For as a prophet, seeing the things that were to come with a prophetic eye (Isa 7:14), he said: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son.' As a lawgiver, he commanded and forbade, saying: 'Cease from your evils, learn to do good' (Isa 1:16). But he also wrote history concerning King Sennacherib of the Assyrians and Hezekiah, who held sway over the Hebrews. Along with these was song, where he says: 'I will sing indeed to the beloved a song of the beloved to my vineyard' (Isa 12:5), and where: 'On that day they shall sing this new song: Behold, a strong city, and our salvation' (Isa 25:1).

1.29 Likewise David, as a singer, said: 'O God, a new song we will sing to you'; as a lawgiver: 'Turn away from evil and do good' (Ps 17:14); as one foretelling the future, he cried out: 'The God of gods shall be seen in Zion' (Ps 50:5). Nor did the historical narrative fail, having detailed many things that happened sensuously against the Egyptians and Pharaoh for the sake of the Israelites in many psalms. 1.30 What then are the spiritual horses that worked behind the man mounted on a red horse? In the following words of the prophet at hand, let us see.

1.31 Zach. I, 9: 'And I said, What are these, Lord? And the angel speaking in me said to me, I will show you what these are.' 1.32 The prophet himself says to the angel speaking in him: 'What are these, Lord?' And the angel speaking in him—that is, the angel standing by the prophecy—is he, or according to another thought, is it the Savior himself, about whom the prophet says: 'His name shall be called Angel of Great Counsel' (Isa 9:6). And the teacher speaks in the listener when he participates in him or is by disposition in him.

1.33 The testimony of the former is: 'But Christ lives in me,' and also: 'Of the Christ speaking in me.' By this understanding also the singer said: 'I will listen to what the Lord God will speak in me,' and Habakkuk: 'I will stand watching to see what the Lord will speak in me' (Hab 2:1). And of the latter: 'Priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem,' not of every teacher speaking to the heart of those listening, but of the one directing his mind to the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rest of the Dwelling and the Virgin Bride
english: While learning according to intellect and the quality of the lessons. For they are doing only this thing, making a buzzing noise in the ear, not benefiting the understanding of those being instructed; and what one speaks and speaks to him, is not always the one striking the ear in the heart speaking.

And the man who stood in the midst of the mountains answered and said to me: 'These are those whom the Lord has sent to go around the earth' (Zechariah 1:10). If anyone were to seek what comes from where, having seen the prophet's coming horses, red, varied, speckled, white, the speaking angel promises him to show him what was seen.

Not then, since there is a twofold vision concerning these, one more introductory and one having ascended higher, to the one who has known the introductory showing, the divine instructor promises the more perfect one, having received the perfect love of the revelation. The man who stood in the midst of the mentioned mountains answered twice: 'These are those whom the Lord has sent to go around the earth' (Zechariah 1:10).

According to a second vision, the people from the Hebrews and the nations happen to be overshadowed by two mountains, of whom, standing in the midst, the man already interpreted initiates into the mystery who those sent to go around the earth are. And they are excellent teachers from among men and angels, as it has been said nearby.

It is not in vain that they were sent to go around the earth by the Lord, not all of those promising to teach or those going around having been sent by the Lord. 'Going indeed around the earth' is the devil, as he himself said, in the examining of Job and the other athletes of God, doing this by especially bad intention, but not having been handed over by God.

What then do the sent ones say they have seen in the going around, or that the whole earth is inhabited and is at rest, as the following wording presents it thus. And they answered the angel of the Lord who stood in the midst of the mountains, and they said: 'We have gone around all the earth and behold, all the earth is inhabited and is at rest' (Zechariah 1:11).

Since not every angel is of the Lord, it is not even of him those having left the heavenly dwelling, so it is fitting that the ones going around answer the angel of the Lord as if the whole earth is being inhabited.

And it rests. Regarding the apostates, even if they are simply called angels, they do not serve the Lord, which is still clearly shown from the scriptures, where it says: 'God did not spare angels who sinned' (Hebrews 11:34 / 2 Peter 2:4), for he did not say that; but where it is said by the Apostle speaking in Christ: 'We shall judge angels' (Jude 1:6 / 2 Peter 2:4).

One should consider what it means for the whole earth to dwell and to be at rest. Since the rational soul is self-moving and ever-moving, when it moves well and blessedly, it is calm and rests from disordered shaking, and it bears this stability from divine reverence.

For it is written: 'The earth was afraid and was still when God arose to judgment' (Psalm 46:2), and: 'He who dwells on hope is still from every evil' (Proverbs 1:33), according to the inspired writing of the Proverbs. By this understanding, regarding the agitator Cain, moved as if God says: 'You sinned, be still' (Genesis 4:7), he is not only saying: 'Having sinned with disordered shaking, put an end to the disordered impulse'; for then you will be praised to be still, 'turning away from evil and doing good' (Proverbs 4:27).

To him who thus rests, dwelling follows. As for how this is, the prostitute woman introduced in Proverbs—whoever this is—'does not have feet that rest in the house' (Proverbs 7:11), having them wandering outside, being a wayward and serious woman, dwelling in the house of a noblewoman and a lady, guarding the lawful marriage rites toward the bridegroom, which is immediately followed by bearing children. For it is said in the Psalms concerning the bride of God the Word: 'He who dwells in the house, having once been a virgin, so that he may become a mother of legitimate children, rejoicing' (Psalm 45:4).
The angel of the Lord answered and said: 'Lord Almighty, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you overlook, until this seventieth year?' (Zechariah 1:12).

Having seen prophetically the angel of the Lord Almighty the whole earth dwelling and resting, and all the nations having believed in the Lord who came among them, he deems it worthy to be granted the knowledge of the King of all, until when and when Jerusalem and the cities of Judah beneath it will be shown mercy, the seventieth year of the captivity already having entered, through which they seemed to be passing by. And since many times Jerusalem in various ways...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Comforting Words of the Lord
english: It has been interpreted, according to each interpretation, that the cities of Judah might also be taken. If, therefore, Jerusalem is the perfect and enlightened soul receiving all things peacefully and steadily—for she is received into the 'vision of peace'—the cities of Judah are the inferior souls still struggling forward. 1.49 If the name Jerusalem signifies the Church, being the 'holy one standing by Christ,' then the cities of Judah are interpreted as the souls that have not become such. The Apostle makes such a difference when writing to the Corinthians, blessing 'the Church with all those who call upon the name of the Lord' (1 Cor 1:2), as the Church is allegorically Jerusalem, while the cities of Judah are those who call upon the name of the Lord. 1.50 According to both interpretations, Jerusalem and the cities subordinate to her sometimes suffer the same thing as the mother-city, so that, having received perception from the over-seeing, they may redistribute themselves, so as to suffer no longer the things of the captivity, 'the seventy-year period having come in.' 1.51 For there shall no longer be laborious work, the Sabbath year having been fulfilled; for the number seventy, having been composed of seven decades, brings perfect rest, providing it through the one having come to 'proclaim liberty to the captives' (Luke 4:18), having risen out of Judah. For concerning the Savior it is announced: 'My King, Judah,' and toward him it is said regarding blessings: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you, your hand is upon the loins of your enemies, and all the sons of your father shall worship you' (Gen 49:8-9). 1.52 When these divine words are announced, which kind of soul is it that is called Jerusalem, but also confessing, being the cities of Judah—for Judah is interpreted 'confessing'—that they might learn from Jesus 'that he is gentle and lowly in heart, that I might find rest' (Matt 11:29), pure souls heard, the seventy-year period being fulfilled.
From the circular motion of the sun of righteousness, circling the pure and transparent intellects.

1.53 Zechariah 1:13: And the Lord Almighty answered the angel who was speaking beautiful words and comforting sayings in me. 1.54 To the angel who had spoken, 'How long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?' (Zechariah 1:14), the Lord Almighty answered with beautiful words concerning the fact that Jerusalem and the cities under it would be shown mercy, and with comforting sayings manifesting and bringing much consolation. For how do they not encourage and restore those returning from captivity, so as to say thankfully: 'When the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion, we became like those having been relieved, we became rejoicing' (Psalm 126:1)? May the Lord Almighty also answer us through the angel with beautiful words of His great counsel, so that, becoming worthy of all praise, we may be perfectly comforted, being led into a free and blessed life by His perfect words.

1.55 Zechariah 1:14-15: And the angel who was speaking in me said to me: 'Declare, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been very jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy, and I am very angry with the nations that are attacking, whereas I was only a little angry, but they have attacked for evil' (Zechariah 1:14). 1.56 He says that a prophet is to be given a command by the angel of the Lord Almighty to cry out formally: 'Thus says the Lord: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy, bringing great anger upon the nations'—those who are suffering, since, after the guardian had led them on for a little and short time of discipline and return, they attacked wildly and crudely. 1.57 It is necessary for those seeing the ones belonging to God being abandoned to be struck with fear, to be flogged for the evils they committed, and to be struck with piety, lest they suffer the same things, but instead they attacked for evil, lamenting and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Zion, Jerusalem, and the Peace of Christ
english: cutting corners

“But I will be jealous for you.” He pre-announced these things by stirring her up, so that she would not fall to the threats, guarding the justice of the household undefiled. 1.64 Zion and Jerusalem call the one being zealously loved so that she might no longer be exhausted by those attacking her toward evils, because of the virtues having come to her. For Zion is interpreted as a lookout, a settled commandment, and Jerusalem as a vision of peace; Zion is called by upward movement the one who looks not at the temporal things but the eternal things in order to do the commandments having been given.

Following such a state is the unmixed and undisturbed nature of those succeeding. And peace is seen, that of which Jesus says: “My peace I leave to you” (John 14:27). And this is given with divine grace from God the Father and Lord Jesus Christ, as Paul teaches. And both these things, peace and grace, I say, the Savior is. For it is said concerning him: “He is our peace” (Eph 2:14). And again, he who succeeds from it and through it says: “Not I” did these certain exploits succeed, “but the grace with me” (2 Cor 12:9). This grace and peace, God the Father providing, Jesus establishes them, granting himself to partake in the grace and peace of those having known him to be. 1.66 May we also become such by good choice, so that we may not be abandoned, like a woman having dishonored her husband, becoming zealous ones desiring him.

1.67 Zach. 1:16: Because of this these things the Lord says: “I will return to Jerusalem in mercy, and my house shall be rebuilt in her,” says the Lord of hosts, “and a measuring line shall be stretched over Jerusalem still.” 1.68 Since nothing happens by chance by the one providing for all things, because of this, causal conjunctions are often placed before things happening, God saying to those subject to his administration: instead of “these things you said or did,” “these things shall be brought to you.” Immediately indeed, even in the present word, there is carried the word having this manner: “Because of this these things says the Lord of hosts.” 1.69 What is this, or the “I will be jealous for Zion and Jerusalem with great zeal” (Zechariah 1:14)? Since, “after my being angry a little, they attacked toward evils” (Zechariah 1:15) the enemies of those being envied, “I will return to Jerusalem in mercy” (Zechariah 1:16), pitying her like a protector and genuine helper, for he is a “father” to this.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rebuilding and Measuring of Jerusalem
english: The manner of having mercy on Jerusalem is immediately announced: 'For my house shall be rebuilt in it' (Ezekiel 37:27) and in its midst, so that by dwelling and walking among its citizens, He may perfectly have mercy on it, no longer allowing it to be desolate or plundered, proving Himself a zealot and one to be remembered, stretching out a measure over it again as before when it had prosperity and fruitfulness. For a desolate and neglected land that is not being surveyed, the land being pitied by God is instead measured like a fruitful land. And the city is measured, being laid out into groves and squares, and cut into gymnasia.

What is the measure being imposed upon it in these things will be shown by an angel appearing, holding a geometric cord. The house being built in the midst of the pitied Jerusalem is the Church of the living God, in which it is fitting for the Healer of God, sanctified according to law, to dwell. This the Apostle speaking in Christ cries out to Timothy, writing thus: 'If you are delayed in seeing how one must conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Timothy 3:15).

According to another understanding, the house being rebuilt in Jerusalem, which is Jesus, who was brought forth from Mary, having been built by the wisdom of God, has according to the proverbial decree thus: 'Wisdom built a house for herself' (Proverbs 9:1), concerning which the building wisdom said to the opponents: 'Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up' (John 2:19); this, he says, 'was speaking about the temple of his body,' as the evangelist wrote. Regarding the things said, each of the faithful is also a house being raised up to be a temple of God. 'For do you not know, he says, that you are a temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Corinthians 3:16). And the Savior himself says this clearly: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and I will love him, and we will come to him and make a dwelling with him' (John 14:23). A temple and a house and a dwelling: 'And the angel who was speaking with me turned and said to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Cities shall again be scattered in prosperity, and the Lord will show mercy' (Zechariah 1:17).
the good things of the land
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Craftsmen of Mercy and Faith
english: Open your eyes and see: Who has demonstrated all these things? The one who leads out the world by number... and the prophet, placed for examination, lifting up his eyes to the true light, has seen... desiring to know who they are.

And the four horns lying over the citizens of Zion and Jerusalem are builders. There are no others among those enemies about whom the Apostle and the rest say: 'Our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers and authorities and the cosmic powers of this darkness and the spiritual forces of wickedness' (Ephesians 6:12). Consistent with the multitude of the powers of the evil ones against which the struggle is for the saints, and the singer who says regarding the one overcoming the enemies: 'He shall mount upon a shield and a basilisk, and shall trample the lion and the dragon' (Psalm 91:13). And since each of the said evil ones rises tyrannically, he says they rule lawlessly.

These horns, promised through enigma, the prophet saw, lifting up the eyes of his mind, so that from having seen the preparation and the power of them, he might put on the invincible panoply of God. Who then are the builders sharpening the presented horns? It is possible to learn from the following, having such [knowledge].

Zechariah 2:2: And he said to me: These horns which scattered Judah and Israel have ascended. The responding angel, showing to the prophet the clarified four horns, the work and the need for which they were brought, says to the one being enlightened, that the horns were brought for no other reason than to scatter Israel and Judah from the holy city, so that, having been scattered into captivity, they might become outside of unity and harmony. It was said previously as Judah confessing; but he, seeing God in his mind, is called Israel.

Zechariah 2:3-4: And the Lord showed me four builders. And I said: What are these coming to do? And he said to me: These horns which scattered Judah and Israel have ascended, and none of them bowed his head; and they entered...
The four horns sharpen themselves against the nations raised against the Lord's earth, in order to scatter it.

The seer, being pleased by the multitude of approaching enemies, is shown by the one pointing out the numbers called for help that the craftsmen are praiseworthy; for not all who fashion appropriate works are praised, but some are also counterfeit, whom they send away from one another according to the proverbial rule: 'Good men fashion mercy and faith; evil craftsmen do not know mercy and faith.'

This worst workshop of the craftsmen is nothing other than the four horns, being an instrument of all unfaithfulness and crudity. Those whom God shows coming are craftsmen of mercy and faith, performing practical virtue through mercy toward neighbors, loving them as themselves, and fashioning faith through pious and scientific contemplation. No one else leads and shows to the seer the eyes of the soul, nor does God, who through doing good shows those able to help the afflicted.

Having seen those shown to him and coming by God, he asks the one showing him what they will do having come, and God answers him that they come to sharpen the nations raised against God's earth, the four [horns], in order to take the ones being handed over into captivity, so that they may scatter Judah and humble Israel, so that no one of the afflicted is able to lift up his head or defy the approaching enemies. But the word of the horns presents a greater weakness, for even after sharpening, it has not become possible for them to tear apart the ones handed over to them, even while the craftsmen who are sharpening them are present.

The word makes it manifest how the one being scattered is brought down, undergoing destruction by proximity, just as the one coming down from Jerusalem encountered spiritual robbers such that he became like a naked man to them, especially when they stripped him of the garment he had worn in the holy city, which was equal in power to weapons; the Apostle writes concerning this to those being stirred up to war: 'Put on...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Downward Fall of the Sinner
english: weapons of light. 1.94 It is carried in the manuscripts instead of 'they brought down Israel,' [as] 'they led Israel down,' showing also by this word that the one sinning is brought from on high to below. And many are the writings that show this, such as: 'How has the morning star fallen from heaven, rising in the morning?' (Isa 14:12) and: 'They shall enter into the lowest parts of the earth' (Ps 18:6). And other myriad words are revealing that the diligent ascends and is elevated, but the lover of pleasure descends, having a material choice, as to become 'fleshly, having been worked by sin.'

1.95 I read an explanation of someone having taken that the four builders are the four evangelists. Whether it is so, let those encountering the one who wrote thus judge. It is possible to say the four builders [are] 'to gather the sent angels to gather the elect of God from the four winds,' that is, from the four climates of the inhabited world. 1.96 In order that the four builders might be understood, they are shown and led by the Forethinker of all things, God, against those lifted up with audacity and arrogance, and against those having fallen by God's judgment, not lifting up the head, neither of the captor nor of the captives, the holy builders being set in opposition. It is also worn away in custom that those acting badly do not lift up the head.

1.97 And if the mind is sometimes signified by the name of the head, even this is not lifted up when someone 'is delivered to an unapproved mind, having not tested God to have in knowledge' (2 Tim 4:3). For how can he who has been held in an unapproved mind still think of the things above or split the heart in heaven, not having treasured in heaven? It corresponds to the scattering of Israel being recognized or being led away, that which is announced with full force by those having scattered against those having seized by force: 'Our bones have been scattered by the underworld' (Ps 142:10). 1.98 Since it seems the prophetic word is poured out from an unsuitability of composition, it should be changed thus—
geometric cord
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Measurement of Jerusalem and the Young Man
english: Having been assigned the interpretations of the Savior, whom the prophet Jeremiah shows, saying: 'Behold, a man, Rising is his name' (Jer 27:2). And Rising is called 'the true light.' And John the Baptist said concerning him: 'A man comes after me who has become before me' (John 1:15).

This man, being a builder of Jerusalem, architecturally measures its width and length, having previously laid its foundations and having been cast down, and after the destruction which he underwent from the coming of wars and those capturing her, so that he may lay the foundations in the proper places, symmetrically and in order, upon which it was fitting for her walls to be raised.

And there was shown to the prophet a geometric measuring line, woven from various architectural threads, so that the previously prophesied might be fulfilled in: 'And a measure shall be stretched out over Jerusalem yet again' (Zech 2:2). And not far from the Savior being the architect, according to what was said concerning 'the city of the Lord of Powers,' that: 'God has founded it for eternity,' the apostle Paul is writing in concert concerning this divine city, which is expected by all those having pleased through faith, thus: 'For they received the city having foundations, of whom God is the craftsman and builder' (Heb 11:10).

The angels and holy men who rebuild with him, like excellent craftsmen, hold the aforementioned geometric measuring line in his hand called the practical power. Paul indeed writes concerning himself: 'As a wise architect, I laid a foundation' (1 Cor 3:10).

Furthermore, in Ezekiel, a man is seen holding a builder's rod and a reed to measure and found the holy temple of God (Ezek 40:5). In such a way he measured and crafted the building, it is possible to know, the one reading the prophet.

Since therefore the Savior is also shown to be the builder of the upper and spiritual Jerusalem, and even more he shall be shown by the Father pointing him out and saying: 'This one shall build my city,' and those contributing as both angels and men to the rebuilding of the city, according to all the clarifications assigned, ought to follow the man shown by the prophet Zechariah saying: 'Behold, a man, and in his hand a geometric measuring line' (Zech 2:1), and: 'Where is he going?' (Zech 2:2) so that...

By chance, one holding the geometric cord approaches to measure how much the width and length of Jerusalem is. For he is taking care to build well, knowing the location and the opportunity of the plots, so that each of the parts of the city, having been taken with appropriate width and length, may place the divisions, temples, monasteries, streets, and squares in harmony, so that in these streets the wisdom of God may carry itself with boldness, being proclaimed on the edges of the city walls according to what is philosophized in Proverbs, as if to say to those guarding this holy city to proclaim Him within it and upon its walls, day and night, by no means being silent but always speaking things for the salvation of its citizens.

Thrice Jerusalem has been often assigned by analogy, both of the visible soul and of the 'glorious Church not having a pillar or a support' because of holiness and fullness, and of the heavenly city of the living God, in every way to have its width and length measured by him having the geometric cord in his hand, a man being assigned by him having the reason of wisdom and knowledge. And behold, the angel speaking in me stood. And another angel was coming out to meet him, and said to him, saying: 'Run and speak to that young man there, saying.' He says that he saw the angel standing speaking in himself, and another angel coming out saying to him: 'Running, say to this young man what it is time to say.'

In many ways it has been interpreted before what it is that is spoken in the prophet by a divine angel and how this is made manifest, especially when the promise comes from another angel coming out. For it is not possible for the things being announced to be heard while remaining within and by oneself, but by coming out through condescension. Indeed, the showing of the things of the mystery happens not toward a man but toward a young man. For just as the holy man is a young man toward the divine angels, especially when he exists clothed as a young man, as it was said concerning him in the divine Proverbs such as this: 'A young man with the holy one, and his way is straight.' For how...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Participation in Virtue and the Fruitfulness of the Holy City
english: Is not the way of the one traveling with holiness straight? Regarding those having such a participation in virtue, John in his epistle addresses them, saying: 'I wrote to you, young men, that you are strong and have overcome the evil one.' (1 John 2:14). Everyone alone who thus waters according to the mind is instructed by the one coming forth, the angel, to speak the following things made clear.

And see if it is in the power of the one coming forth, the angel of the same power, to be said by the choir of the saints: 'You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your Christs,' and to him: 'I went forth from God and I have come.' For salvation and divine enrichment become the race of men cast out from paradise, having trodden the divine laws, when the 'angel of the will' of the 'great' God comes forth in order that he might lead in through obedience and divine instruction the one cast out, saying: 'Today with me you shall be in paradise.' The one coming forth promises to show great things concerning the spiritual Jerusalem, which the following word, having such a character, signifies.

Jerusalem shall be inhabited abundantly from a multitude of men and beasts in its midst, and I shall be to her, says the Lord, a wall of fire all around, and I shall be in her glory in its midst (Zechariah 2:8-9). In whatever way all the trees in paradise bear much fruit, so also the holy city Jerusalem is inhabited abundantly, having a multitude of men and beasts in its midst; for it is neither fitting nor possible for the divine and holy city to be found unfruitful, the unfruitful tree being cut off and given out to the fire.

Such was the one to whom the holy one cries: 'Therefore God brings you to an end, to uproot you and to transplant you from a dwelling, and your root from the land of the living' (Psalm 52:8), while everyone remaining in the house of God says thankfully: 'I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God' (Psalm 52:8). For how can the one dwelling in the house of God, nourished by the divine light, not bear fruit, in doing what is necessary and thinking the pious doctrines? Thus the man blessed in the first Psalm was a fruitful tree; for it has been said concerning him: 'He shall be like the tree planted by the streams of water, which brings forth its fruit...'
firmly
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Flight from the North and the Gathering to Zion
english: It consumes, 'a consuming fire,' especially those thorns and briers that bear fruit, and even more so those that are cut off and thrown out because they do not make good fruit but destructive and poisonous fruit. Similarly to the holy city, the Lord is said to be around the people in one of the songs of the ascents: 'The Lord is around his people' (Ps 121:4).

Just as a wall of fire has become around Jerusalem the fallen, and has risen up as a glory in its midst, due to the being glorified by divinity and blessedness of those dwelling in the holy city which is encircled by God, about which the hymn-singer said, rather towards it: 'The city of God was spoken of as having been glorified' (Ps 48:14), and also: 'Great and exceedingly praiseworthy is the Lord, in the city of our God, on his holy mountain' (Ps 87:2).

And it will also be to us by the grace of the beneficent God to bear the fruits of the Spirit, so that around us the Lord might become like a fiery wall, illuminating and guarding us, while consuming the enemies coming to cast us down, so that we might triumphantly declare, showing the incorruptible city: 'Behold, a strong city and our salvation.'

'O, O, flee from the land of the north,' says the Lord (Zech 2:6); 'for from the four winds of heaven I will gather you,' says the Lord; 'be saved, you who dwell in the daughter of Babylon' (Zech 2:6).

The word stirs up those scattered 'in the north, where the evils are burned up from the face of those dwelling in the land,' concisely desiring the flight to take place from the hands [of the enemy], which is signified by the name of the north, doubling the epithet of the exhortation, saying: 'O, O, flee from the land of the north.' He flees from the hands and from the punishment of poets being eager for repentance, going out from evil. The same as fleeing from the land of the north is: 'Turn away from evil,' and: 'Cease from your evils.'

And this is fulfilled when an abstinence from every kind of evil occurs, with only the good and praiseworthy being held fast, according to the exhortation of the apostolic advice: 'Test all things, hold fast to the good, abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thess 5:21-22). And he alone and everyone flees from what is harmful, he who considers the good to be the good.

And by doing so. The flight becomes unobstructed from the north when the Benefactor and Provider of all things gathers the citizens of the beautiful city of Jerusalem, who were scattered among the four winds. By providing an easy escape, He makes it manifest where and in which city salvation occurs for those fleeing from the harsh and cold north wind; for it is written about it: 'Boreas is a harsh wind' (Job 37:9), and again: 'A cold north wind shall blow' (Job 37:9). Holy Zion is the place where those who formerly inhabited the daughter of Babylon can be safely restored. The multitude of those inhabiting her is her daughter.

And since the name 'Babylon' is taken to mean 'confusion,' everyone whose mind is disordered and poured out is Babylonian; he who is to be separated and of a disposition to have love for Zion ought to be restored, so that he may hymn and sing to God, since there it is fitting to hymn God, and it is right to sing a harmony to Him. For it has been said: 'A hymn is due to You, O God, in Zion' (Psalm 66:5), and: 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion' (Psalm 87:2).

And since it is not possible to hymn and sing to God while inhabiting the daughter of Babylon and the north, the Holy Spirit cries out like a herald, saying: 'O, oh, flee from the land of the north, says the Lord; be restored to Zion, you who inhabit the daughter of Babylon, because from the four winds I will gather you,' that is, from all climates of the earth's surface. This is equivalent to: 'From the four winds I will gather you,' which the Savior said in the Gospel, 'to send the angels to gather the elect from the four winds' (Matthew 24:31).

When Zion and the daughter of Babylon are allegorized, the winds must also be allegorized, namely, as fleshly powers or the various winds of false teaching, tossing and carrying away into atheistic mindsets and uncertain practices those who are infants in intellect, which is not praiseworthy; for the Apostle writes about such a state: 'Lest we be infants, tossed and carried about by every wind of teaching in cunning' (Ephesians 4:14). Sometimes the winds are taken to mean trials and circumstances, as in...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Glories and the Descent of the Word
english: In the Gospel, rains and rushing rivers are remembered as coming to strike and blow violently against the houses of those who heard the words of Jesus, being unable to harm or overturn those who turned the words of the Teacher into works, since he laid the foundation upon the saving rock, destroying the building of the one hearing the divine words and not doing them, since he had cast its foundation upon the sand.

1.137 Thus having the winds interpreted, God gathers from all of them those fleeing from the north and dwelling in the daughter of Babylon, so that they may be saved in Zion, concerning which the Apostle writes: 'You have come to Zion, mountains and city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem' (Rev 21:2). For only thus will the existing prophecy be understood loftily.

1.138 Zach. II, 12: 'For thus says the Lord of hosts: I have been sent after glory to the nations that plundered you, because I touch you as one touches the apple of his eye; for behold, I bring my hand upon them, and they shall be servants to those who have served them, and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me.'

1.139 The Lord God the Almighty gives a reason for being sent after glory to the nations that plundered the true Israelites; and since God the Almighty is the one saying these things, the 'after' and the 'before' are not to be understood bodily. For the 'after' of God is that which is after his previous existence.

1.140 For being unbegotten and eternal, he exists before all, and with him and after him occur those things directed toward the created and his administration, of which the incarnation and his visitation occur, which the God-wise men are able to perceive and have the concept of, one of whom is the hierophant Moses.
1.141 Having therefore entreated God to see him known, his [manifestation] of God...

As he withdraws himself, he himself says: 'My back shall be seen, but my face shall not be seen by you' (Exodus 33:23), 'my passing before in my glory.' During the visitation of the God Word, the 'becoming flesh' and being seen in flesh occurs behind his glory, before such a glory was being 'only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14).

This theory is also submitted by what was said by the Apostle and those agreeing with him: 'Even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, but now we no longer know [him]' (2 Corinthians 5:16), a first glory existing of the Son, by which the Only-begotten God Word is, the second [glory] being according to the man-making and after the first, by which 'he was sent to the nations who plundered' (referring to the nations) God's people; the nations plundering those made at home by God, having taken him captive.

And this happens through much goodness; for if as God, eternal and unbegotten, he judged the ungodly, and the whole [world] went out, descending also and not observing all the lawlessness of those being judged, he benefits rather than punishes. And indeed, the pre-warning and pre-announcing of dangerous things to those being punished through kindness and patience gives a place of repentance to those willing to go out from the impiety they made.

By the same goodness and philanthropy the descent of the Savior has happened, having been seen according to the flesh, so that after these things 'the glory of the Son from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14) might be seen, so that by way and tomb 'he might be manifested in flesh, justified in spirit, seen by angels' (Romans 1:4); for thus 'having been seen in the world, preached among the nations, he shall be taken up in glory' (Acts 1:11).

Understand if the word of Jeremiah submits this thought, having it thus: 'This is our God, another shall not be reckoned toward him. After these things he was seen upon the earth and associated with men' (Jeremiah 10:10). For such an association with...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Mission of the Descending Lord
english: An apostleship occurring to men follows the glory of the one called God, being Almighty; for he was not sent as Almighty, but in the manner of 'emptying himself' and 'taking the form of a servant' by descent. What is being pre-announced to those still at their peak while being plundered by nations? 'He who touches, he says, of you, touches the apple of his eye' (Exodus 4:6), harming himself rather than striking the righteous or those he intends to harm, similarly to the one striking the apple of his own eye. This theory gathers from many places of Scripture: Cain, wishing to harm, exposed himself before he intended to murder (Genesis 4:8). The same happened to Saul pursuing David in order to kill (1 Samuel 24:1-22), and to Absalom attacking his father tyrannically (2 Samuel 15:1-14).

In the present prophetic [text] it signifies harming through touching, and especially through those whom God himself says to those attacking murderously against his own people: 'Touch not my anointed ones, and do evil to my prophets' (Psalm 105:15). To touch lightly lies in: 'It is good for a man not to touch a woman' (1 Corinthians 7:9), signifying approaching shamefully and licentiously. From this verb it is also shown that to touch well is to join through contact, as in that said by Jesus: 'Someone touched me' (Mark 5:27), when the woman with the issue of blood, desiring to be healed, touched by grasping the hem of Jesus' garment. Having fallen so many [interpretations] upon the present voice of 'touching,' the now present prophetic word signifies harming through maltreatment. But he who intends evil against those guarded by God touches the apple of the eye of the inner man. And it is manifest how he who touches the servants of God touches the apple of his own eye, because of the saying: 'I will lay my hand upon them' (Ezekiel 28:26), making manifest the disciplinary power, so that they become plunder to those they formerly plundered, leading them into captivity, so that they serve those against whom they formerly ruled tyrannically. Which event [leads to] 'you shall know that I am the Lord Almighty' (Ezekiel 20:23), having been sent by the Lord Almighty, is the completion of the things pre-announced. The God Word is being sent Almighty from the Almighty, coming to men by the good pleasure of the Father.
pan-king
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The People of God and the Inheritance of Judah
english: The Lord has come and has tabernacled in her midst, the temple having been raised again and God dwelling in it. 'Rejoice and be glad,' says the prophet, 'daughter of Zion.' In many places of the Scripture, the daughter of each city is called, meaning the citizens who fulfill her.

The delight and the gladness which the divine word commands to have is the same as the joy which happens to be the fruit of the Holy Spirit, arranged together with divine love and blessed peace, which the holy Apostle makes manifest writing thus: 'The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace' (Galatians 5:22). Having experienced this stability, those delivered from captivity say: 'When the Lord turned the captivity, we became as those who are returned; then our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with shouting' (Psalm 126:1). And in another Psalm it is brought in harmony: 'When the Lord turns the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad' (Psalm 126:3).

For those who mourned, being torn away from their own fatherland by the law of captivity, follow a return to it, to delight and be glad because the Lord has tabernacled in its midst, the cause of the delighting and the gladness. And what is the cause of the gladness and delight—is it the enjoying of the currents of the river filled with waters, about which it is written: 'The river of God was filled with waters,' and also: 'The currents of the river make glad the city of God; God is in its midst, it shall not be moved' (Psalm 46:4-5), no longer departing or abandoning, but because of goodness remaining with it?

And what good and salutary will attach to the indwelling of the Lord in the midst of the beautiful city, or the 'fleeing of many nations' repenting 'unto the Lord in the day' when the sun of righteousness is grasped, of which the patriarch Abraham, having received light, seeing it, rejoiced, and with him the sons and children of him who are according to faith and his works having become, as saying thanks: 'This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it' (Psalm 118:24). And the 'many nations having fled unto the Lord' shall receive the people to enrich the one to whom they have fled, no longer atheistic and without hope.

remaining; concerning these things God says in the prophet: 'I will call him who is not my people my people, and he himself will say: Lord my God you are' (Hosea 2:23), so that they may be addressed as 'a holy nation, a holy priesthood, a race of God' (Exodus 19:6).

For he says to those fleeing to God in the same manner as mentioned by him to whom they have fled: 'You shall be to me an elect race, a holy nation, a royal priesthood, my people, through whom I shall display my virtues' (Exodus 19:6).

What then follows for those who have become the people of God, or the dwelling in the midst of the heavenly and blessed Zion? For then then it will be known, by divine and accurate vision, 'that the Lord Almighty sent' (Isaiah 60:22) the one redeeming her, saying concerning his own Father: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me to preach to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives' (Luke 4:18).

For because of preaching to the poor, Jesus, who dwells in the midst of Zion, was anointed with the Holy Spirit and the power of God, proclaiming release to the captives held by unseen enemies, her children. For thus the All-King, the benefactor of her, will inherit Judah, those who confess. For the confession of Judah is interpreted. And so he will first inherit those called unto salvation; for from of old they were part of him and before that they suffered dispersion and captivity.

But where will he inherit Judah being part of him, except upon the holy land in which he will be long-enduringly well-suffering, he who honors his Father God and his Mother the Church being Jerusalem, whom he still loves, taking again and reigning in her midst, knowing that he has come to dwell in her midst, sent from the Lord Almighty, when bowing heaven he descended to us humans, saying: 'I have descended from heaven to do the will of him who sent me' (John 6:38), 'to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10).

For thus they will no longer remain in perdition, for whom he has come, so that he might become the cause of eternal salvation for them. And the Jerusalem being fulfilled by us as the Church of the living God shall also have such a faith and works making beatitude, so that he who washed and brightened her with his own blood may still love her.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Light Cloud of the Incarnation
english: Her. 1.168 Zach. 2:17: Let all flesh stand in awe before the face of the Lord, because he has been raised from his holy clouds. 1.169 The term 'flesh' being homonymous signifies many things, as it stands for the God-breathed writing itself. For when it is said in the Psalms, 'To give food to God to all flesh' (Ps 50:12), it stands for all mortal animals being sustained by food in living, as also in: 'All flesh is gathered according to its kind' (Gen 15:28). And when the Apostle writes: 'For who has ever hated his own flesh? But nourishes and warms it' (1 Cor 12:3), the body joined to the rational soul is signified, as it is possible to learn from the apostolic word itself having this: 'In this manner men ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. For who has ever hated his own flesh?' (Eph 5:28), and the following.

1.170 But there is also when only men are revealed by the designation of flesh, as in: 'Hearken to prayer, to you all flesh shall come' (Joel 2:28). And it comes to God in relation and disposition, not the irrational, but the humanity, being made worthy of the bountiful gift of the Holy Spirit by the one saying: 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy' (Joel 2:28). 1.171 This so-called flesh, being rational, is receptive of divine awe; for indeed, 'to stand in awe from the face' of the one appearing to it is commanded, concerning which the pure of heart, saying, send up a prayer: 'Appear your face and we shall be saved' (Ps 41:2). And he gives the reason hereafter for why all flesh ought to stand in awe before the face of the Lord God, bringing forth: 'Because he has been raised from his holy clouds' (Zach 2:17).

1.172 But holy clouds are not those that cause sensible rain, but those that bring the spiritual downpour, according to that said in Isaiah concerning Israel, by way of allegory called a vineyard, from the face of the Lord: 'I will command the clouds not to rain upon it' (Isa 5:2), because of the thorns and not having grapes as fruit. 1.173 For of the vineyard being allegorized, the clouds were also taken up in harmony, sometimes raining to water, sometimes being prevented from doing this. Concerning such rain-givers, again in that same prophet, it is commanded by God:

“Let the clouds rain down righteousness.” For since righteousness is a virtue of the rational soul, it is not the sensible clouds that pour rain, but the divine prophets, being called clouds by upward analogy.

Since therefore the Savior has come forth from these clouds to fulfill the law and the prophets, for this reason “let all flesh stand in awe from the presence of the Lord” (Ps 96:1) the God, which was predicted and shown when the prophecy having this character was fulfilled: “The God of gods shall be seen in Zion” (Ps 50:5), and he shone so that “we might behold his glory, as the only-begotten from the Father” (Jn 1:14).

Having come forth from the holy clouds, which were interpreted to be Moses the great hierophant and the prophets who possessed the Holy Spirit, he arrived upon a light cloud, having mounted upon the world which is among us, Egypt which is called by analogy. And the prophecy concerning these things begins from this place: “Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud, and he shall come into Egypt, and the works of her hands shall be shaken” (Isa 19:1).

Having been transferred from Egypt to the place concerning the earth, in harmony the light cloud shall be raised to the humanization of the Savior, the God the Word sitting upon that which had gone forth from Mary.

For what light cloud does not have the weight of sin, or the flesh of Jesus which did not consist of the union of man to woman being heaviest, but from the Holy Spirit having come upon the virgin not having experience of man, and upon whom the power of the Most High overshadowed, to make the born one holy without marriage. And even more the lightness and thinness of the lordly cloud is revealed from the fact that it was not made by sin nor did the soul of Jesus know it.

For nothing else drags and weighs down the soul of men like lawlessness, being compared to a talent of lead, because it searches and drags down those practicing it; but the soul of Jesus was not tried by this weight, “having loved righteousness and hated lawlessness” (Ps 119:160); nor did he have “neither deceit in his mouth” (Ps 33:13) which scatters the sins of all, the one having it.
Therefore it was necessary for the Savior, having come forth from his own holy clouds, fulfilling the pre-proclamations concerning him, to be established kingly upon the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Devil Standing at the Right Hand
english: A light cloud is assigned to bring the evangelical rain upon the fruitful crops and to shield from the heat from which the prudent man is saved, according to the proverbial decree: 'A prudent son was saved from the heat.' It also shields from the frost of sin, as it is written: 'As a pit chills water, so its wickedness chills.' To this, one will take allegorically: 'A cold north wind shall blow.'

Taking these things said according to contemplation, having possessed fleshy hearts that resembled God's judgments and commands, we might have been reverent toward God so that we might do right, so that God, benefiting the flesh even more, might engrave a divine writing in them with His living Spirit, not as stones, by which we might be helped to be perfected so as to face face to face with the truth, surpassing the seeing of it iconically and in part.
And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the face of an angel of the Lord, and the devil stood at his right hand to oppose him (Zech 3:1).

But God shows great and superlative things that happen, which are neither sensible nor human. Because of this, God shows to the prophet the great priest Joshua not standing humanly, but standing divinely before the face of an angel of the Lord; not merely the son of Josedech as is shown through him, but the truly great priest, having traversed the heavens, the one ordained 'according to the order of Melchizedek,' not according to the power of a fleshy commandment for a certain time, but according to an unpassable priesthood; for it has been said of him: 'You are a priest forever' (Ps 110:4). Jesus the great priest was not shown merely as it happened, but standing unshakeable and firmly established, similarly to what was said in the Gospel: 'Jesus cried out saying: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink' (John 7:37).

For everyone coming to him drinks, because he stands ready. Regarding the one standing, he is seen by God in the presence of an angel of the Lord, and the devil was seen standing at his right hand to oppose him. For what was necessary for the devil to oppose and stand against, if not the right hands of the one shown by the Lord, standing in addition to the angel of the great counsel?

And he stood also at the right hand of Judas, as it is said in the 108th Psalm: 'Set the sinner against him, and let the devil stand at his right hand.' But see the great difference in the words; for regarding the one betraying the Savior, he stands at the right hands having already taken them, 'having given place to the devil.' For it is said that 'he cast into his heart to betray' the one who had chosen him as best teacher and also Savior. And after the casting into the heart, he had entered into him in order to work the things of betrayal in him as he works in the children of disobedience. For it is written that 'after the morsel Satan entered into him.'

But the great priest did not stand at the right hands any other way than by opposing him, especially when he attempts to seize those being helped and instructed by him; does he not stand opposing from the right hands when he seeks to exclude those called to faith and the rest of virtue, according to what was said: 'Behold, Satan has asked of you to sift you like wheat, and I have prayed for you,' O Peter, our disciple, 'so that your faith may not fail' (Luke 22:31)?

Regarding not being harmed by those whom he opposes, and they receive authority against him, so that they tread upon all the power of the one opposing hostily, they suffer no harm at all because of hoping in the one who is being crushed under the feet of the saints, the standing and muddy devil; for it is written: 'Everyone having hope in God' (Romans 15:13) will remain without infirmity and undefeated, not fainting, not falling away.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rebuke Within the Devil
english: The evil one is being covered by the right hand of God, who helps. See what the hymn-singer is crowing toward him who is thus being found under the hand of God: 'The Most High is my refuge; evil shall not approach you, and a rod shall not come near your dwelling, because he commands his angels concerning you' (Ps 91:2); and shortly after: 'He shall tread upon the lion and the dragon' (Ps 91:13).

Regarding this lion and dragon thus spoken of, in the Apocalypse of John it is said that he is 'the ancient Satan' (Rev 12:9). From a parallel it will seem to be revealed in such a theory that 'devil' and 'Satan' are the same, the name Satan being Hebrew, meaning 'adversary' in the Greek voice. These things being thus considered, it is blessed to have the devil as an enemy and an adversary and not a friend; for his fellowship is harmful and strikes toward destruction. Immediately, too, approaching Judas, he made him a 'son of perdition' (John 17:12) and his own child, so as to share in his designation.

For the Savior says concerning him to the twelve disciples: 'Did I not choose you, the twelve? And one of you is a devil' (John 6:70). And even to this Jesus, as a man having become [one] having taken up a soul and a body of a man, stood in the desert as an adversary at the right hand, fasting forty days and nights equally. Was he not, as an adversary, having led him painfully to the pinnacle of the temple, saying, 'Cast yourself down from here' (Matt 4:5); and having shown all the kingdoms of the inhabited world and their glories, saying, 'All these things I will give to you, if falling you worship me' (Matt 4:8)? Even if he said these things with deceit, he was overturned and cast down, having become wretched under the one 'being tempted in all things' (Heb 4:15) by other men.

May God, the helper of the helpless, grant also to us, who have 'against the powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this [world], and the spiritual [forces] of wickedness' (Eph 6:12), to remain unassailable and undefeated, not being touched at all by the evil one.

Zechariah III, 2: And the Lord said to the devil: 'The Lord rebuke you, O devil, and the Lord who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you.' Is this not like a brand plucked from the fire? The Lord, he says, said to the...

The Lord rebukes the devil: 'The Lord rebuke you, Satan.' And in the present text, the Lord speaks concerning the Lord, the Father concerning the Son, as has been previously stated. How then does the Lord speak, and what does He mean by rebuking the devil?

The Master of all does not use a spoken word in any one of the human dialects to converse with the devil; for He Himself, being incorporeal and existing as a spiritual essence, does not use vocal organs, nor does the devil, whose hearing is struck by words composed of syllables, have a hearing toward Him, especially when God is the one speaking. Indeed, encountering the book of Job, finding there God speaking to the devil and the devil to God, we are not so small-minded as to think that questions and answers occur according to the vocal utterance of human dialect; it is otherwise fitting and proper for the persons present. For God indeed says when He wishes to make manifest to those whom He has judged to hear, as if He again hears those conversing with Him, knowing what they have in their ruling principle.

And in the present context, the Lord said to the devil, making manifest to him the thing being announced, having it thus: 'The Lord rebuke you, Satan,' but not saying: 'You shall be a vessel of wrath in which also the tormentors may rebuke those who have worked wickedly as they deserved.' But if He says to him 'in you,' the word has such a meaning: since, having sinned hidden within yourself, and not escaping notice in doing this, God, who hides your secret and foreknows all, rebukes in you, overseeing the malice hidden in you.

Because the devil thus works malice, and many born according to wickedness by him, God says toward him in Isaiah: 'But you have said in your mind, I will ascend into heaven,' and the following until: 'I shall be like the Most High' (Isa 14:14). This is consistent with what is said in the Psalms: 'The transgressor says that he sins in himself' (Ps 51:4). For sinning in himself and saying in his mind, 'I will ascend into heaven,' he receives the rebuke in himself without escaping. It is equivalent to what was said: 'The fool has said in his heart, There is no God' (Ps 14:1).
Having shown how even he who sins in secret does not escape punishment, he shows hereafter who it is that rebukes, that He who has chosen Jerusalem exists.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Filthy Garments of Sin and the Priestly Restoration
english: In many ways, the identity of the chosen city of God is revealed. For the pure soul that sees "the peace surpassing all understanding" (Phil 4:7) is called Jerusalem, and so is the glorious Church of Christ, "the holy and immaculate, having no spot or wrinkle" (Eph 5:27); and through an elevated allegory, it is the heavenly city of the living God, according to it having been thus written: "Come up, O Zion, mountains and city of the living God, Jerusalem, heavenly and with myriads of angels, in festival" (Zechariah 2:6).
What will result from "rebuking the Lord against the devil" (Zechariah 3:2) is made clear; for it says: "Is this not like an ember torn out of the fire?" (Zechariah 3:2).

An ember is half-wood, having reached the point of turning into charcoal, no longer possessing the strength and hardness of wood. Such were also the enemies of the King of the Hebrews, concerning whom God said to him: "Do not fear, nor let your soul faint because of these two smoking embers" (Zechariah 3:3).

Just as these appeared weak, having fallen under the punishment of fire, so also the one receiving rebuke from the Lord who chose Jerusalem has become weak, as if no longer bearing fruit, having been deprived of vital power, according to the ember torn out of the fire; for a plant thus scorched can no longer bear fruit, even if it was torn from the fire so that it might not be wholly consumed and turned into ash, being useful for other needs, for which God takes it, for the sake of beauty to those being fashioned, being molded and beaten out as silver and gold vessels (2 Tim 2:21).

For how can the one liberated from the fire of captivity—by the one proclaiming remission and descent to the captives and giving it to the fatherland which he formerly inhabited before the enemies came, seized and scattered them—not be torn from the fire?

Zechariah III, 3–5: And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and he stood before the angel. And he answered and said to those standing before him, saying: "Take away the filthy garments from him." And he said to him: "Behold, I have taken away your iniquities, and clothe him in festive attire, and place a clean turban upon his head." And he clothed him with festive attire.

Regarding the spoken words set forth concerning Jesus the high priest, who iconically demonstrates the truly faithful high priest, possessing an unassailable priesthood. For since the saints are found to be loving, they sympathize with those in misfortune, weeping from sympathy, 'weeping with those who weep' (Job 44:17).

Because of this, while the fallen Israel is still at its peak in captivity, the priest who holds the care in his hands, mourning and suffering with them, is clothed in filthy garments, which the angel present with him protects should be removed from him. And the filthy garments are the deeds performed without law; for after it is said, 'Take away his filthy garments' (Zech 3:4), it is harmoniously brought forward: 'Behold, I have taken away your iniquities' (Zech 3:4).

Once the iniquities having been taken away—which are filthy garments—he is clothed in the foot-reaching, priestly tunic, adorning even to the feet the one wearing it, and a clean mitre is placed upon the head of the one priestally healing 'the Lord who has come and dwelt in the midst' (Matt 1:23) of Zion and Jerusalem.

Upon the restoration and rebuilding of the city and the temple, the leader of those liberated from captivity is clothed in a 'garment of salvation and a tunic of joy' (Isa 61:10), having cast off the filthy garments so as to no longer mourn, but to rejoice and be glad, having been saved from the captivity of those who were tested by it.

For what does the [angel] command to be removed from him, the mourning garments, named filthy, or is it because of the causes having occurred in sinning, such that these were clothed? It is possible to take angels to be divine, receiving the command, intervening around those who fear God to save them, so that they no longer sink down and look sullen in the face of present misfortune.
Regarding the things said, [apply them] to the explicit narrative, and those to be contemplated by intellect.

Jesus the great high priest, of whom the iconic Jesus passing through Babylon with the captives carries the type, was clothed in filthy garments, the sins of all mankind, not himself sinning nor being tested by sin. When he shall cast off and discard the fabric of sin which he clothed himself in for our sake, he ascends upon the cross, like the theologizing Peter, the apostle.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Garments of the High Priest and the Ways of God
english: Regarding Christ, it is written: «He bore our sins in his own body on the wood, so that being removed from sins we might live by his righteousness» (1 Pet 2:24).

In concord with this and regarding «the vessel of election», Paul writes thus: «Having stripped off the principalities and powers, he triumphed with boldness on the wood, blotting out the handwriting of our debt, having abolished it and taken it out of the way» (Col 2:15), so that having triumphed in boldness, he might strip off the principalities and powers which he previously surrounded himself with. For how can he who acts not be clothed by those who subject him to evil inclinations and bad dispositions? The contrary view must be constructed.

He who practices and thinks what the Savior teaches, being Christ, puts on [Him], according to: «Put on the Lord Jesus» (Rom 13:14), and: «As many as were clothed with Christ» (Gal 3:27). He who practices and reasons according to the principalities and powers of the evil ones, toward which those striving for salvation have the struggle, is clothed by them, receiving the qualities according to them. These the Lord and our Savior stripped himself of, taking upon himself our sins; for it is said of him: «He bears our sins and suffers on our behalf» (Isa 53:12), and with other things in the prophecy of Isaiah it is said: «And he shall open the sins of many» (Isa 53:12).

Even so, if Jesus is seen clothed in filthy garments, these do not belong to him, nor are they fabrics, nor did he manufacture them. Rather, for the sake of those who made them and previously wore them, by the grace of the good God, he put them on, «so that having tasted death for all» (Heb 2:9), he might make dead those for whom he tasted, only by touching and approaching them. Immediately also, having clothed himself in the filthy garments, he stood before the face of the angel, in no way being separated from them.

What then does the angel say to those standing before the face of Jesus? «Take the filthy garments from him»; for they are not his, but yours; since, because you are practicing the forbidden things, he is clothed in the garment that becomes filthy; having recognized that which you were sinning in, make him free from the filth of sins.

It must also be said in another way: «Jesus, not knowing sin, sin became on our behalf by God» (2 Cor 5:21), having accepted the cross, «so that we might become the righteousness of God in him» (2 Cor 5:21).
When this happens, one infers from it that sin has occurred, so that he no longer has the filthy garments of others.

Likewise, a filthy garment is wrapped around him when a curse becomes for all of us so that we may receive a blessing, which is given out when we receive the blessing, which he received as a curse in order that we might become according to God, having despised shame. After the removal of the filthy garments, being a great and true high priest, he puts on the priestly tunic called the long-reaching one, and he places upon himself a clean ephod, and he is clothed by us in the garment of the human body. For we have become the cause of him using such a garment, we clothe him.

However, even if the said garment has been clothed upon God, saying, 'But I will prepare a body for me,' yet the great priest remains, surrounded by the priestly tunic, that long-reaching one, of which the weavers, filled with the spirit of wisdom, prepared it for the sensible. For the whole tent and its vessels and the world which the high priest surrounds were constructed according to the pattern shown on the holy mountain.

But consider the head, that is, the mind, the clean ephod of the great priest; and perhaps the head of the theology concerning Christ is the ephod, having nothing material or defiling, and the long-reaching one is the contemplation concerning his incarnation.

And the angel of the Lord stood. And the angel of the Lord testified to Jesus, saying: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: If you walk in my ways and keep my statutes, and you will distinguish my house. And if you guard my court, I will give you those returning in the midst of these standing ones.' (Zach. 3:7)

The angel of the Lord, standing firmly and immovably, testified to Jesus, saying: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: If you walk in my ways and keep my statutes.' The ways of the Lord are the virtues, being fulfilled according to the keeping of his statutes, concerning which the holy one says to God: 'Make known to me your ways, O Lord, and teach me your paths.'
