(Ps 25:4) He who walks them and continually treads the paths will attain divine rewards, receiving from...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Standing and the Turning
english: The Lord's 'distinguishing his house and guarding his divine court.' One must not understand 'house' in these matters as a place or a building, but the sum of those completing it, as the Apostle says: 'But Christ, as a son, upon his house, of which we are the house' (Galatians 4:9). And to Timothy he writes: 'In case I delay, so that you may know how you ought to behave in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Timothy 3:15).

And this house is distinguished by Jesus, placing in the Church 'apostles, prophets, shepherds, teachers, for the equipping of the saints' (Ephesians 4:11). For it is not as it happens, but with much distinction and arrangement, so that one is placed in the rank of an apostle, another in the place of a prophet, and others to tend the flock of Christ and to exert the divine instruction for other saints who are well-disposed toward learning. Similar to this is that which has in the Psalms thus: 'God has stood in the congregation of gods, and in the midst he distinguishes gods' (Psalm 82:1).

The house of God, thus utilizing [members] according to another thought, becomes the body of Christ, composed and being equipped from many members; his eyes, indeed, are those seeking the contemplative life, just as his hands are the practical ones, working the works of virtue, and the ears are called the prudent listeners of this body, of whom each one says: 'The instruction of the Lord opens my ears' (Psalm 119:66). Appropriately, the feet of the body of Christ would be said to be 'those not sluggish in haste.'

Consequently, regarding the distinguishing of the Lord's house, [it is] also the distinguishing of the divine body, so that one may be an eye as previously mentioned, and another a vigorous hand, of whom it is good to work and to be useful. Harmoniously, regarding the other members, it shall be said. Similarly, regarding the distinguishing of the house of God, and the guarding of his divine court, concerning which the Holy Spirit cries out to those hurrying...

...to rub within it: 'Worship the Lord in his holy court.' (Ps 99:2). What is the contest of the one distinguishing God's house and guarding his court shown in: 'And I will give you those turning among these standing ones'? (Acts 14:22). For 'standing' shows those firmly established according to holiness, having received a permanent position according to faith, to whom the Apostle writes speaking: 'For in faith you have stood' (Acts 14:22). The Savior says in the Gospel, signifying those 'founded and rooted' perfectly 'in love': 'There are some of those standing here.'

Among those thus standing, those turning according to a divine manner of life and a contemplation of the truth are given by Jesus through God. Among those humans who truly become according to the image and likeness of God, Jesus, having received them from the Father, turned about among them, 'having appeared on the earth in order that he might turn about with humans,' providing a pattern and a model for those previously mentioned to imitate him.

By a second meaning, say that 'standing' shows the dancing angels being gathered according to 'thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads,' praising the All-King Savior and ministering to him. These, who are shown turning among their own Creator, are given to become equal-angels after the resurrection, no longer marrying or being married, no longer able to die, the succession of marriage and child-rearing having ceased, since 'their corruptible put on incorruption and their mortal immortality' (1 Cor 15:53-54).

For how does he who perfects celibacy not turn about among the standing immortal angels and the other divine powers, always being 'mindful of the things of the Lord, without distraction' (Col 3:2), desiring to serve him priestically and to serve him nobly, being 'a fellow-worker,' so to phrase it, having set this before him. Similarly, also 'the virgin, being holy in spirit and body,' is without distraction pleasing to the divine bridegroom.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Eternal Priest and the Spiritual Priests
english: Nor is it endured to what extent he is left behind. And to say collectively, all those approaching the Savior turn about in the midst of those standing always and continuously in holiness to partake of him. One of those turning about in this way sang to the King of all: 'Against angels I will sing to you.' (Zach. III, 8-9: 'Hear, then, O Jesus, the great priest, you and those near you and those sitting before your face, because they are men of wonders. Because behold, I am bringing my servant to the east, because upon the stone which I gave before the face of Jesus, upon the one stone, seven eyes are.')

The angel testifying to Jesus, the great priest, says these things: 'Hear, you, Jesus, being the great priest; and let those near you and those sitting before your face hear also, being men of wonders, because I call my servant to the east, because upon the stone which I gave before the face of Jesus, seven eyes are upon it.'

The great priest Jesus, who was previously given according to the order of the priesthood of Melchizedek, concerning whom the Apostle writes to the Hebrews: 'Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, understand the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus, being faithful to him who made him' (Heb. 3:1).

And see that those able to understand how faithful he is to him who made him, the apostle and high priest of our confession, are found to be holy, partaking of a heavenly calling. For it is not for everyone to see how faithful he is to him who made him, the apostle and priest Jesus, but only for him who is able to speak in all things with wisdom to the perfect, he who is able to say: 'I have seen Jesus' with the eyes of my heart enlightened toward the true light.

Therefore, those not partaking of the heavenly calling are negligent, and from this word they themselves are deceived, having been previously misled, saying that the Son of God is a creature and a work. But the foolish stumble thoughtlessly, taking 'him who made him' to mean creation and production into being, the writer of the epistle not intending this. For to become the faithful apostle and high priest is made manifest as certain and immovable to be apostle and priest; for one is not always apostle and priest.

He is Jesus, but from the time when those to whom he is sent and for whom he intercedes exist, through whom the descent here has happened of the one sent by the Father, when 'bending heaven he descended' (Ps 18:4) to those to whom he was sent and of whom he is priest.

Many scriptures signify the certain and unshakeable through the faithful. For that which is said about God: 'All his commandments are faithful, established for an age of ages' (Ps 89:35), and that: 'I will give you the faithful blessings of David' (2 Sam 7:12), and even that: 'I will raise for myself a faithful priest' (Ps 110:4), declare the certain and unchangeable, of the commandments of God existing faithful according to the spiritual law because of the unchangeable, and of the commandments according to the shadow of the law being transferred from the letter to the spirit and from the shadow to the truth.

By this theory also [are] those of the true David, in whom the Savior is according to man, whose faithful blessings are to remain forever, the words of him remaining even if heaven and earth pass away; therefore also a faithful priest exists, having an unshakeable priesthood for the age, becoming and having been shown according to the order of Melchizedek. To this great priest the angel of the Lord says: 'Hear then, O Jesus, the great priest, you and those near you' (Zech 6:5), the spiritual priests, those having been appointed under you being high priest, to whom also in Isaiah it is said they are righteous ones: 'But you shall be called priests, servants of God' (Isa 61:6). And they possess this promise especially, those who through all-pervading holiness in celibacy serve God.

Not only, however, do these hear of the angel with Jesus the great priest, but also those sitting before his face. These are those in the regeneration according to the resurrection of the dead sitting before the face of the Savior, being judge and king, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

These who hear the divine words of the angel with Jesus are not others than the apostles; being near him and sitting before his face, they are not found to be infants or children, but perfect men having encountered the perfect man of the fullness of the knowledge of the Son of God. Therefore also they are observers of wonders, wisely attending to the wondrous powers of...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sign and Wonder of Christ's Incarnation
english: Of the Lord, as to how to grasp what is made manifest through them. Of this knowledge, the great hierophant Moses and his brother Aaron the high priest are [examples]; for it has been written, 'God set among them the words of His signs and His wonders' (Ps 105:7). How then is the divinely-inspired observer not merely looking at the sight of wonders and signs, but at their words, according to which these things are accomplished?

And it is to be testified by the theory of one and two [things] recorded in the Gospels: a sign and a wonder was the leading of the blind man from birth to sight (Matt 9:27-31), his eyes having been anointed with clay, having been brought from the ground and from the spittle of the benefactor. Because of this having happened paradoxically, the one observing the prototype made manifest through it is a wonder-observer.

For the people from the nations, who previously were not seeing at all, should be considered to be blind from birth by the subversion of atheism and ignorance of God, having looked up then when, having known Christ according to the flesh, the eyes were anointed with the clay made from the spittle of Jesus, having gained experience of the incarnation which brought him to see Him. Alongside these is also the woman with the flow of blood for all twelve years (Luke 8:43-48), who had become outside the bearing of unclean blood through which she was prevented from giving birth, from touching the hem of Jesus. Paradoxically and wondrously it was accomplished; the one having gained knowledge of it is a wonder-observer, transferring that which happened wondrously to the woman into the purified Church from the nations.

Having shown all things observed in the existing words, 'I, says the Almighty Lord, lead my servant toward the East,' calling Him his servant, He who happens to be of the seed of David according to the flesh, 'the one having taken the form of a servant, having emptied himself while being in the form of God' (Phil 2:7). This servant of God who was brought low is that East concerning which it is said in the Gospel: 'An East from on high, to shine upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death' (Mal 4:2), no other being 'of the true light.' Showing His own servant, the Father says: 'Behold, a man, East is his name' (Mal 4:2), calling him a man because of the incarnation, and East because of having been raised up, being a sun of righteousness; for indeed it has been written about him in the last of the Twelve Prophets, from the person of the one who sent...
my name
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fig and the Vine
english: "The stone which was rejected by you, the builders, has become the head of the corner." [Ps 118:22]. For how did the two walls not join and complete one single corner: the one being built from the Jews coming to the gospel, and the other from the Gentiles who believed? For when the Church of both Jews and Greeks was gathered, Christ having become its head, He completed one corner, with all those joined to one building in one faith, all people from the two peoples being created into one new man [Eph 2:15].

This stone, thus announced as the cornerstone, chosen, precious, which God placed in the foundations of Zion, no longer to be shamed by any sin, having become pure for everyone believing upon it. Those coming to the immortal living Word, living themselves, are being built up as hidden stones, so that a spiritual house may be composed and an intelligible altar, upon which the sacrifice of praise is offered and all things being like it are spiritual.

May we also, living, become holy stones, rolling upon the earth of God, so that, having been built up on the foundation of the apostles and prophets of Christ Jesus [Eph 2:20], we may be completed as a temple and a spiritual house, so that God may dwell in us.

"I dig a pit," says the Lord of all, "and I will search out all the injustice of that land in one day" [Zech 3:9]. "On that day," says the Lord of all, "let each call his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree" [Zech 3:10].

"I dig," says the Lord of all, "a pit, in order to make all the hidden things manifest, in order to touch and feel all the injustice of that land;" it is clear that of the one being dug, in the one day of illumination, then most especially when "the Lord God shines" [Ps 104:4] the Lord of all "the secrets of darkness, and makes manifest the purposes of the hearts," in order to condemn those having done all injustice.
One day can be called the season of our Savior's visitation, in which the benefactor who shines also searches all the injustice of the revealed land, taking away the sin of the world.

Because of this, once the cause of all strife and every unjust war has been overcome, there will be a deep peace, such that no one fears anymore, since strifes are dissolved and wars are ended, and the demons and other opposing powers, which are called 'rulers of this darkness', are gone, so that everyone may live fearlessly and invite his neighbor under the fig and the vine.

This peaceful and stable state is being described, and the prophet Micah foretells presciently that day, saying: 'Each one will call his neighbor and his brother under his fig tree and his vine, not being afraid' (Micah 4:4). For how can anyone still be afraid, when all strifes and wars are dissolved?

What is meant by the mentioned plants, the vine and the fig trees—whether the contemplative or the active life? The vine, producing fruit that makes the contemplative and scientific life joyful, and the fig, being somewhat severe and rough due to the toil and sweat for the sake of possessing virtue.

Regarding the fig thus given, the proverb says: 'He who plants a fig tree will eat its fruits, but he who guards the Lord will be honored' (Proverbs 12:14), which is not contrary to history; for many having planted a sensible fig tree neither sat down nor ate its fruits, either being prevented by death or being driven far away from the plant they planted, while only he who eats the fruits of a spiritual tree eats alone and for all.

The fig is said to be the active and energetic life of good things; likewise the vine should be understood, becoming like a branch of the true vine. For each of the disciples of Jesus is a vine, becoming a branch of the one saying, Savior: 'I am the vine, you are the branches. Every branch remaining in me bears more fruit' (John 15:5).

Those who have cultivated the said trees, becoming fellow-laborers and brothers, invite one another under the vine and the fig tree in peace, to live in luxury. For when you see the contemplative man hurrying to lead his neighbors under the wise theory of God and of His doctrines and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Golden Lampstand and Spiritual Nourishment
english: Regarding matters of practical wisdom, observe how he summoned those whom he loves, the neighbor as himself, under his own vineyard, so that they might pray and rejoice together. Likewise, the maker of good works leads his friends under the planting of a practical virtue fig tree, so that they might simultaneously find rest, having entered into the joy of their own master.

And the angel who was speaking in me returned, and he roused me just as a man is roused from his sleep (Zach. 4:3). And he said to me: 'What do you see?' And I said: 'I have seen, and behold, a golden lampstand, and the lamp upon it, and seven lamps upon it, and seven lampstands for the lamps upon it. And two olive trees upon it, one on the right of its lamp, and one on the left (Zach. 4:2).'

The angel speaking in me returned from one revelation to another vision, which I was to behold; he roused me, having moved me as if from sleep, a man sleeping, and says to me: 'What do you see?' And I said to him: 'I have seen, and behold, a golden lampstand, and a lamp upon it, and seven lamps and an equal number of lampstands supplying oil to the lamps. And I saw also two olive trees upon the lampstand, one on the right and one on the left of the lamp.'

What, then, is signified by each of the things shown to the prophet? The holy one says that the angel, having turned toward me and speaking in me continually and repeatedly, perhaps turns out to be 'the angel of the great counsel.' He roused me similarly to a man being awakened from sleep, having arrived at sobriety. And this awakening is praiseworthy, so that the one expecting it might say with confidence: 'I shall arise at dawn.' This being fulfilled through the outcome of what was pre-announced, he cries out gratefully: 'I have arisen, for the Lord shall take hold of me.' This voice is referred to regarding the Savior, having been raised from the dead, who slept...

It has become according to man. For how was he not raised from sleep when he rose from the dead after having remained in the heart of the earth three days and three nights, having benefited even the souls in Hades, rejoicing them and filling them with the luxury available there?

He says, indeed: 'I satisfied every thirsty soul, and I filled every hungry soul,' providing 'wine that gladdens the heart of man and bread that sustains the ruling part of the meal.' And I was raised and I saw the intoxicating drunkenness that had come to be for the drinking souls, and how they were filled with the saving food. Therefore, 'sweet has become to me sleep' (Ps 116:9), that is, 'death, of which I have tasted above all things by grace' of the well-pleasing God.

Similarly to this, the divine prophet, being the 'man who is in a wound and knows how to bear weakness' (2 Cor 12:10), having been raised, hears from the angel who awakened him: 'What do you see?' To which the one who had seen the vision arrived at comprehension replied with the eyes of the heart enlightened: 'I see a golden lampstand, all of it.' By saying that the lampstand is all golden, it is indicated that it is a spiritual and incorporeal lampstand, entirely filled with light through all its parts.

We do not often find in the Scripture that the intelligible is signified by the name of gold; perhaps, therefore, the intelligible lampstand turns out to be the spiritual house and temple of God, as it is said in the Revelation of John, when he who shows the revelation to the one being initiated says: 'The seven churches which I saw with the eye of the soul are seven lampstands' (Rev 1:12-20).

Upon the whole golden lampstand, there is a torch above, the luminous Word concerning the Trinity. From the moment the torch was extinguished by the wise virgins who met their divine bridegroom, they shall enlighten a light of knowledge, participating in the light of God which exists, in which no darkness of evil or ignorance exists, and participating also in the true light, becoming partakers of the holy.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Lamp as Spiritual Insight
english: The Spirit dances, carrying torches. Just as a torch appeared above the interpreted lamp, so also seven lamps appeared above that lamp, being a seven-fold radiance. For just as the manner of perfect luminous intellect is called seven eyes, and seven pillars support the house of wisdom, so also the seven lamps sit upon the lamp, in another manner being that which the Savior took during His visitation, soul and flesh.

For how is this whole lamp not golden, having not committed sin nor known it, upon which sit seven lamps: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of divine counsel, and strength, and knowledge, and piety, and fear of God. And how does each of these stand in relation to the one who ceased rising from the root of Jesse, having been made clear previously when it was foretold: 'A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse' (Isaiah 11:1), and the whole scope of the prophecy announcing these things.

And this seven-shining power of the seven lamps above the lamp is nourished and increases, the oil being dispensed through the seven wicks, flowing as the nourishment and guarding the light. And this is nothing other than the study of the knowledge of the truth. For from studying we bear fruit in memory and a stronger vision.

Upon all those things observed—the lamp, the torch, the seven wicks, and the lamps—two oils were also seen above the lamp, one of which was on the right and the other on the left of the torch. And see if the study concerning the intelligible things and the gifts of the Holy Spirit is oil being harvested from the oil on the right, while that concerning the world and its constitution and the providence from God is pressed from the oil on the left.

They suppose, according to a theory, to say another, an oil being on the right of the torch, to be the theory concerning the Only-begotten Son of God, the one on the left nourishing the Word concerning the incarnation. For this one also shines, but not in the same way as the theory on the right and preceding. I once heard a teacher leading the Catholic Church clarifying the presented word, that the torch above the lamp is the...

The light is the illumination of the Father, and the oils on the right and from the good-smelling ones are the words concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit. But he did not provide this interpretation, bearing this meaning, as to how one thing is on the right and the other is from the good-smelling ones.

Since the present theory concerning the lamp is not a sensible but a mental one, see whether this is not that which Moses saw on the mountain according to the pattern shown to him, and not another being of the so-called idea; toward the invisible and mental lamp the sensible one was constructed according to the description of the hierophant Moses.

It is not untimely to write alongside the things seen and that which was said in the Gospel by Jesus: 'No one,' he says, 'having lit a lamp, puts it in a hidden place or under a vessel or a bed, but on the lamp, so that all those in the house may see the light' (Matt 5:15).

It is possible in these things to take the house to be the Church of the living God, becoming His house, in which those remaining and dwelling, standing according to its doctrines, are illuminated toward the lamp placed by the lamp, which is snatched away by the one educating those traversing in the house of God according to the statutes and canons and doctrines of the ecclesiastical opinion. And this teacher illuminates when he lifts up his own mind like a lamp, which he does not hide under a bed or vessel, but places upon his spoken word, being allegorically addressed as a lamp, having 'a tongue of instruction' as it must be said.

It is also possible to call the practical life a lamp, upon which the enlightened mind of the one who has enlightened himself with the light of knowledge rests. Let him who is urging on the present clarity of the existing prophetic word examine whether it is necessary to receive it or to seek another from those... having stepped into understanding. For thus an exactified intellect comes to bear fruit.

'And I asked and said to the angel speaking in me, saying, What are these, Lord? And the angel speaking in me answered and said to me, saying, This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might nor by power, but by my spirit, says the Lord of all' (Zech 4:6). The prophet says he asked the angel speaking in him, desiring to learn what the divine things shown to him were.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of Christ and the Mountain of the Lord
english: Visions, that is, all things revealed, or those specifically preceding the present word, which is about the whole golden lampstand and the things upon it: a lamp, seven small lamps, and equal lamps, and two olives, one on the right and the other on the left of the lamp.

Regarding the question of whether these are not perceived by the senses, the one asked immediately answered that they are the word of God from the person of Zerubbabel, from which it appears that the things shown were intellectual visions and that this is true. The showing of the revealed things happened to the prophet while he was still in Babylon, in which neither the house of God was built, nor the vessels in it, of which the lampstand and the things upon it are. Since these are thus viewed, one must remain with the interpretation spoken of them or seek something greater than it.
The word which... the angel said to the prophet was not done by great power or by the strength of man or of any other creature, but in the Spirit of the Lord it was spoken and was revealed.

The Holy Spirit of the Lord is continually called so in the Scriptures, as also in other Scriptures besides the present one. Concerning Him, a lament and that in Isaiah is announced thus: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me' (Isaiah 61:1). In agreement with these, the apostle Paul, writing to the Corinthians, says: 'For what man knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God, which searches even the mystic depths of God' (1 Corinthians 2:11). And again in Isaiah, the Originator and Provider of all things says: 'A Spirit shall go out from me' (Isaiah 59:19).

By this Spirit, the things shown before the person of Zerubbabel were revealed, but not by great power or strength of any creature. For there is another power provided with the Spirit to those worthy, about which the Savior, in the Acts of the Apostles, says to his disciples, as he was being taken up into heaven to his Father: 'You shall receive power upon the coming of the Holy Spirit' (Acts 1:8). Correspondingly, at the end of the Gospel according to Luke, the Savior, ascending from where he came, having given the Holy Spirit to the apostles, says: 'But you shall sit in the city...'

"...until you are clothed with power from on high." This power is not a different power from that of Christ, who is "the wisdom and power of God," from which the evangelical preaching has surpassed the apostles, one of whom, Paul, writes: "My speech and my preaching are not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in a demonstration of Spirit and power" (1 Cor 2:4), which is sometimes provided by God who has stretched out His hand, as it is said concerning John in the Gospel, "having gone before the Lord in spirit and power" (Luke 1:80).

Understand precisely if the thing announced to Mary by the holy angel Gabriel has the same understanding: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you" (Luke 1:35). In the mentioned Spirit of God, in the words set forth and many others, the announcement has occurred before Zerubbabel and the power joined with him, "and not by any other great power and might" (Zech 4:7). For this is inferior, even if it be divine and highly esteemed.

Who are you, O great mountain before Zerubbabel, to level the stone of the inheritance to be equal to its grace (Zech 4:7)? As a logical and understandable approach to a divine voice through speech, either the discerning prophet or the angel speaking in him approaches. What is it that he says to him? Who are you, O mountain standing before Zerubbabel to level, and who is the stone which I will make equal to the inheritance by grace? Regarding these things, whoever says the two designations exist in parallel concerning the visiting Savior. For many scriptures name him both mountain and stone.

For in "The mountain of the Lord shall be made manifest at the end of days" (Isa 2:2), the Son of God is, concerning whom He spoke at the end of days after speaking through Moses and the prophets. Of Him also it is demonstrative: "Ascend the mountain of Zion, O evangelizer, Zion" (Isa 2:3). And there are ten thousand other testimonies concerning this, which the present writer should refrain from passing over, lest the word become too much beyond what is necessary, especially since often the things concerning the mountain being the Savior have been interpreted in the commentaries of the divine Psalms and of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Mountain and the Stone
english: Regarding the final vision of Isaiah. Even the named mountain, Savior, is called a stone in the saying: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner' (Ps 118:22). Remembering this word in the Acts of the Apostles, the preeminent disciple of the Savior, Peter, most strictly rebuked the Pharisees, scribes, and Sadducees who were listening to the Jewish teaching, saying: 'This is the stone which was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner' (Acts 4:11).

And since it is not only the head of the divine building but also the foundation, God promises concerning it, saying: 'Behold, I lay a cornerstone in the foundations of Zion, chosen, precious, upon which the believer has unashamed hope' (Isa 28:16). Laying out these words, Peter, the disciple of Christ, upon whom the Church is built, exhorts and advises those to whom he has inscribed his epistle: 'To whom approaching the living stone, you are being built up into a spiritual house in which spiritual sacrifices are offered' (1 Pet 2:5).

Of what inheritance does the stone belong? It is of that inheritance concerning which it is brought forth in Isaiah: 'There is an inheritance to those healing the Lord' (Isa 35:10), and of that inheritance concerning which the hymnodist said, singing: 'My inheritance is most strong for me; you are the one restoring my inheritance to me' (Ps 16:5).

See then whether the stone is the inheritance of that inheritance being fulfilled from the God-fearing ones according to each, which is chosen and desired, existing from the cause of all things, according to that which was announced by the spirit-bearing men, apostles and evangelists, prophets and the great high priest of all things, Moses: 'He chose for us his own inheritance,' God, clearly, 'the beauty of Jacob whom he loved' (Jer 31:3).

It is equal to the voice from the Psalm and that in the great song of Deuteronomy having here: 'Jacob became a part of the Lord, a portion of his inheritance, Israel' (Deut 33:9). But especially the stone being hymned is the inheritance of that which is signified in the second Psalm toward this stone: 'The Lord said to me, Son are you, I have today become your father. Ask of me and I will give you nations for your inheritance' (Ps 2:7-8).
Toward the assigned theory, the mountain and the stone from parallel...

Regarding how it is to be carried, it must be said and otherwise that one part is the mountain and another part is the stone. And the mountain of achievement is the unwedded Mary; but the stone coming forth from her, whom she bore as a son without a man, exists. The book of the most wise Daniel initiates us into these mysteries.

For it has been said in it that the striking stone—the various kingdoms and the image completed from them—has been cut and torn away from it without the custom and the practiced way toward the generation of the energy from parents. For as many as have the generation from both parents, they are torn and cut away from the hands of the marriage acts and from those who conceive; but only the one born from the virgin, not knowing the man, has been torn away and cut from her without hands. Before the face of Zerubbabel, it happened that the stone from the mountain was to be cut without hands, so that Jesus is also traced through lineage from it. It is interpreted, therefore, as 'a movement of a flow' because the customary flow of parents is moved, by a virgin alone without a man being brought to pass.

But the stone placed outside of the inheritance has grace upon grace, according to the thought of what the Baptist John said, 'for from the fullness we have all received' (John 1:16). For the whole visitation of the Savior and the salvation upon it happened by grace, as the theologian says to those whom he addresses in his epistle: 'You are saved by grace, and this is not from us, but the gift of God' (Ephesians 2:8). [Zechariah 4:8-9: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall complete it, and he shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you.]

The prophecy of the seen house is not spoken concerning a sensible building. For it has already been said that this prophet, while still in Babylon, with the seventieth year of the captivity already having come, was initiated into the placed revelations. But not in Babylon, but in Jerusalem and after the captivity, the sensible house was built. Therefore, the present voice does not happen to be about it; for as if concerning the temple being present and already having come, it is said pointedly about it: 'This house.' But it is not subject to the sight of...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shortening of the Days
english: Regarding the house raised in Jerusalem after the descent of the captivity while in Babylon. Even if these things are said about the sensible building, they reveal the prototype of the visible, being something intelligible and like an idea constructed toward its likeness. It was said previously that just as the tent and the vessels in it were constructed according to the pattern of an invisible tent shown on the mountain, that is, of the height of the archetype, so the bodily house raised from sensible stones is a copy and an image of that shown to the prophet Zechariah by way of vision, but not by a collision of the senses.

The hands of Zerubbabel laid the foundation of this archetype, and its active powers shall complete it. When this happens, you will know toward whom the promise is, that 'The Lord of hosts has sent me to you' (Zech 4:6), so that you may be enlightened and intelligently contemplate the things established through divine seeing. And the prophet before us might say the same things as he who speaks in Christ, Paul, having this: 'I will come into revelations and visions of the Lord' (2 Cor 12:1). In agreement with the one speaking in revelations to those who are discerning according to the inner man, the hymnist in the Psalms says: 'Then you spoke in vision to your sons' (Ps 89:1), not in ears nor by voice to those who have the spirit of adoption speaking the Word of God.

For as a true light, it enlightens the intellect of those whom it wishes to receive its divine conversations; it speaks in vision rather than in ear. Immediately also, regarding Isaiah speaking of God thus: 'The vision that Isaiah saw' (Isa 1:1), it is not visible things, but words are brought forward. For how is it visible: 'Hear, O heaven, and listen, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I have begotten and exalted sons, but they have rebelled against me' (Isa 1:2)? Similarly also concerning the fifth of the Twelve Prophets. For after saying: 'The vision of Habakkuk' (Hab 1:1), there is no sight...

Not through sensation, but through words they are brought forward, having such [words]: 'Thus says the Lord to Edom: I have heard a sound from the Lord, and I have sent a signal to the nations; you are being punished exceedingly,' and the following. 1.320 Zach. IV, 10: 'Why is it that one has made the days small?' And they shall rejoice, and they shall see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel; these seven are eyes looking over all the earth. 1.321 'Why is it that one is making the days small?' These are the [days] with which the restoration takes place, of those descending to their own fatherland by the law of the captivity having happened in Babylon. And small days are those which are few in number, especially also those which are cut short, not remaining long while the sun is in the upper hemisphere above the earth; the former [meaning] is more likely [to be meant], because the revelations were shown to the prophet in the seventieth year of the captivity, as to say to the prophet himself toward God: 'How long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you see this seventieth year?'

1.322 This theory agrees with that in the Gospel said by the Savior: 'If those days had not been cut short, all flesh would not have been saved.' The cutting short of the days of tribulation signifies that the afflictions will not remain for a longer time, ceasing quickly, so that the strength of those being afflicted may endure for the purpose of bravely contending to obtain prizes and crowns. 1.323 For one should not believe Tatian the heretic, erroneously saying that the former days had become fewer than the present ones, because the hours of the day and night were briefly contracted, due to it being announced by the singer to God: 'By your ordinance the day remains.' 1.324 But since it is impossible according to history for the days to be cut short in this way, one must recover the Gospel [teaching] concerning the cutting short of the days and that which is lying concerning the small days in the prophetic [text].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Seven Eyes and the Cherubim
english: It shall say. The days of the intelligible realm possess greatness and abundance near the sun of righteousness, and this is due to the difference between those being illuminated and the light itself. For when the Lord says concerning the righteous one who 'dwells in the help of the Most High' (Ps 90:14): 'I will fill him with length of days,' we do not say that a long life is promised to the righteous one who desires to 'depart so that he may be with Christ' (2 Cor 5:8), as he says: 'Woe, that my sojourn has been lengthened' (Ps 118:77).

Indeed, history also struggles against such a view, since those honoring parents are not becoming long-lived in every way, it having been said to each: 'Honor your father and your mother, so that it may go well with you and you may be long of years upon the earth which the Lord your God gives you' (Ex 20:12). For one finds those keeping this commandment becoming short-lived and outside of life in a short time.

Therefore, since the spoken word is shown not to have [the meaning] as many suppose, that which is said in the Psalms concerning length of days, and as elsewhere in the God-breathed Scripture is like: 'He sought life and you gave him length of days unto the age and unto the age of the age' (Ps 35:9), and that in Proverbs: 'The righteous shall make many years in wealth' (Prov 10:6).

But that the increasing illumination and length of days is the prophet of the divine laws, Moses, saying to the God-lover: 'This is your life and the length of your days: to love the Lord your God with all your soul and with all your heart' (Deut 6:5). For since love that is attentive to God is luminous, it prepares long and great days, so that those participating in it find themselves having many-dayed and long-lasting [existence].

Compared to these days, the introductory gleams are found to be small days, which he who is not undervaluing will easily be tempted by, following the bright progresses. In whichs the one born will rejoice in 'joy inexpressible and glorified' (1 Pet 1:8), existing in 'fruit of the Holy Spirit' (Gal 5:22).

And what follows him who rejoices thus, or to see the tinny stone in hand, that is, in practice, of Zerubbabel, from whom the one from Abraham and David and finally from Mary, Jesus, is genealogically descended, who works through all things to be luminous and discerning.

Regarding those approaching him. He said there are seven eyes, observing and looking upon all the earth, especially when those dwelling on the earth learned to do righteousness, walking without blemish and working righteousness. That these look upon things by the Lord is learned from the Psalmist saying: 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears to their prayer' (Psalm 34:15).

The whole has seven divine eyes, being inherently perceptive; in this way also the most holy Cherubim, at whom God attends, according to the vision of Ezekiel, are eyed all over, it having been said they are full of eyes, just as they have eyes on their sides and on their faces for the inspection of superabundant and great wonders. The Cherubim are interpreted as a multitude of knowledge; from which it appears that they see what they know and what they look upon and impose.

See then that: 'Who has made it into small days?' (Zechariah 4:11) does not indicate a sparingly seen thing, but someone called by some specifically, and by others an individual, similarly to the apostolic word having thus: 'Every house is built by someone' (Hebrews 3:4).

And I answered and said to him: 'What are these two olive trees which are by the right side of the lampstand and by the two olive branches?' (Zechariah 4:12). And I inquired a second time and said to him: 'What are the two olive branches which are in the hands of the two golden pipes that pour out and bring up the golden oil-streams?' (Zechariah 4:13). And he said to me: 'Do you not know what these are?' And I said: 'No, Lord.' And he said: 'These are the two sons of stability who stand beside the Lord of all the earth' (Zechariah 4:14).

When the angel speaking in the prophet asked: 'What do you see?' he answered and said inquiringly: 'What are these two olive trees which are on the right and by the olive branches of the lampstand?' An answer not being given to him, he inquires a second time about the two olive branches which are in the hands of the two pipes that pour out and bring up the golden oil-streams. To whom the angel said: 'Do you not know what these are?' 'No, Lord,' saying the prophet, the angel said: 'These are the two sons of stability who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.'
For one having the beginning of initiation, it is not possible at all to know what are those on the right and by the olive branches.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vision of the Flying Sickle
english: The oil of the lamp; therefore, he asks a second time concerning two branches of the olive trees. It has been made clear in the previous discourses that the divine study is called olive, because of their fruit increasing and nourishing the light. 1.337 Since it is not possible to perceive through all the trunks and the shoots of the plants in question the one 'knowing and prophesying in part' (1 Cor 13:9), he approaches a second inquiry concerning two branches of olives; for only through these is it possible to have a knowledge that imposes the truth 'through a mirror and an enigma' (1 Cor 13:12), so that, having been benefited from the partial, he might at last be able to know what the olives actually are. 1.338 And since one interpretation of what those who explained the text took as the two olives was the discourse concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit, see if the branches of these olives would grasp what is attainable to the one knowing in part. For while there is the olive of Christ, the becoming of the Word into flesh would be a branch; and of the Holy Spirit, his introductory contemplation, which is called his 'earnest money' (2 Cor 1:22). 1.339 Having asked a second time about these, the one receiving God heard from the angel who initiates into the mysteries: 'Do you not know what these are?' To which the one hearing replied: 'No, Lord.' 'These,' he says, 'are the two sons of fatness; they shall present to the Lord all the earth' (Ps 65:16). 1.340 For just as, by way of the discourse concerning the Father, which is the lamp above the lamp, as has been interpreted a little earlier, so the discourse concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit is being matched to the contemplation of the Father's fatness, being its sons, as it is possible for one still in the body to know. 1.341 According to another interpretation, the mystical understanding of the God-breathed Scriptures is the fatness of the house of God, according to that which is said in the thirty-fifth Psalm to the Lord God: 'They shall be intoxicated from the fatness of your house' (Ps 65:5); and it is clear that 'those who hope in the wings of God' (Ps 91:4) are sons of men, being two sons: the one having come by circumcision, and the other according to the Gospel of Christ. 1.342 Understand, if you are able, to take two sons of fatness having been presented to the Lord, those seen in glory with Jesus on the mountain, Moses and Elijah (Matt 17:2-3), making manifest the Law and the Prophets. For just as the spiritual law becomes a son of the

Just as there is a certain quality of firmness, so too is the word of the prophet who has been opened. He read in a secret book that Enoch and Elijah are the two sons of firmness, as it is fitting because they resemble others. For Enoch was translated so as not to see death, and Elijah was taken up, being carried by a chariot of fire and a horse 'as into heaven' (2 Kings 2:11). Considering these things as being by power like our own, though brief, we set forth the following of the prophet, desiring also to understand them, if the one who enlightens the prophet through revelations should 'give a word by the opening of our mouths' (Zechariah 10:2).

And I turned and lifted up my eyes; and I saw, and behold, a flying sickle. And he said to me, 'What do you see?' And I said, 'I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits in length and ten cubits in width.' And he said to me, 'This is the curse going out over the face of the whole earth; because every thief from this shall be judged until death, and every one who swears falsely by this shall be judged until death. And I will execute it,' says the Lord of all (Zechariah 5:4), 'and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of the one swearing falsely by my name, and it shall destroy in the midst of his house, and it shall consume him and his wood and his stones.'

Turning from the passing vision, I lifted up my eyes of the mind. And I see a flying sickle, having a length of twenty cubits and a width of ten cubits. This is the sickle which, he says, shows the vision concerning it: this is the curse, that is to say, the punishment, being brought upon all the earth, to cut and consume the thief and the perjurer. And behold the greatness of the instruction occurring through revelation, making manifest from the visible things the things not visible, and from the sensible things the things understood.

For when the just Judge is examining the righteous and the impious upon the ballot, giving to each according to his practice and his works, the things brought against the unrighteous and impious men for punishment, where he names a sword and arrows, and elsewhere an axe and a sickle. When, therefore, 'the wicked and sorcerous men' and with them the predatory demons, being hostile and seditious because of the violence they possess, happen to be...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sickle of Judgment
english: Swords and spears are brought as appropriate punishment, as seen in the Great Song of Deuteronomy where the Lord says: 'I will drink my arrows from blood, and my sword shall be satiated with the blood of the wounded,' and also: 'I will strike them with my sword, and my arrows shall finish them.'

And since punishment touches not only those sinning upon the earth, but also angels who have fallen into wickedness—for it is written: 'God did not spare angels who sinned,' having left their heavenly home—it is said in Isaiah from the mouth of God: 'My sword was drunken in heaven.'

The impending judgment brought against the ungodly is most clearly known in Amos, the second of the Twelve Prophets, who says: 'All the sinners of the people shall perish by the sword.' For the prophetic word is not about a physical instrument of war, as it was never the case that all the sinners of the people were lifted up by a visible sword.

Equally, in the seventh Psalm, the singer threatens those called to repentance: 'If you do not turn away, he will make his sword shine; he has bent his bow, and prepared his weapons of death in it; he has made his arrows for those being burned.' Regarding the weapons of death, it is said in Jeremiah: 'How long will the sword of the Lord cut, how long will you not be at rest? Turn back to your slayer.'

Sufficiently having set forth the weapons of war that strike and harm the impious and rebellious men and even demons, let us see also what is announced enigmatically concerning trees not bearing good fruit, regarding the weapons of their wrath or their punishments. 'For make fruits worthy of repentance,' and also: 'Already the axe lies at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not making good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.'

According to these interpreted plants, the curse brings justice upon them in being cut down, those of whom it was said they bear destructive and harmful fruit: 'Our enemies are senseless. For their vine is the vine of Sodom, and their vine-branch is from Gomorrah; their cluster is a cluster of gall.'
[a] cluster of bitterness to them, their wine is the fury of dragons, and the unyielding fury of shields.

Regarding a choice of will, like a harmful vine producing poisonous fruits, it was necessary to cut it away with a sharp sickle, and to have the vine and the cluster removed. Since these things have been made more apparent, see also how each part is to be clarified as much as possible.

Turning back from what the prophet had already seen and taught, lifting up the luminous eyes of his heart, he sees a sickle flying, not perceptible to the senses, but understood clearly, having a length of twenty cubits and a width of ten cubits, cutting away 'every planting which the heavenly Father has not planted' (Matt 15:13). And everything being cut away turns out to be unclean.

The cutting is done with a sickle twenty cubits in length; for the number twenty is not pure, being two in tens. But since length does not remain alone, it takes on a width of ten cubits. And this number resembles a unity. It is shown through the measurements laid down that a blessed and profitable end occurs for those who are cleansed by means of the sickle.

The sickle is called a curse because it brings toil and injuries to those being cut down, bringing vengeance against everyone who steals and swears by the name of the Lord upon a lie. Therefore, if no one is to suffer these things, let him keep the commandments which are thus held, in the Mosaic teaching: 'You shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal' (Exod 20:14); and in the apostolic [teaching]: 'Let him who steals steal no longer, but rather let him toil, working for what is good' (Eph 4:28).

In the same way that theft must be avoided because of the curse called the sickle, so perjury must be fled from, 'not taking the name of the Lord in vain' (Deut 23:10). Shortly after the prophecy, perjury is forbidden thus: And those taking the name of the Lord upon a lie, 'and do not love a false oath' (Heb 12:2).

Concerning such a curse, the Lord says that the sickle exists: 'I will bring it to pass' by a vote of judgment, 'and it shall enter into the house of the thief and the perjurer, and it shall complete him, even his timber and his stones.' Just as the house being completed is not a sensible building, so too the things completing and making it whole—timber and stones—are not visible.
Among the others of those who have interpreted the Hebrew Scripture,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Measure of Deeds
english: The veil is the scourge, covering those who steal and perjure themselves with it. This sickle flies most quickly, coming upon all the earth. And by a second meaning, it flies so that it touches not only those sinning upon the earth, but also those in the air and those being punished for acting impiously everywhere.

In the middle of the house, that is, the ruling principle, the sickle destroys, similarly to the sword that split the judge of Israel who remained adulterously according to Sophronius. For in this word, that he was split in the middle, it signifies the dividing of his ruling principle.

And the angel, the one speaking, came out to the prophet, not remaining within, in order to show the iniquity and the measuring line and the talent of the lead being taken out (Zechariah 5:5-8): 'And the angel, the one speaking with me, came out and said to me: Look up with your eyes and see this one coming out. And I said: What is it? And he said: This is the measuring line coming out. And he said: This is their iniquity in all the land. And behold, a talent of lead is being taken out, and behold, a certain woman sat in the middle of the measuring line. And he said: This is iniquity; and he threw her into the middle of the measuring line and threw the stone of lead into her mouth.' The one speaking, usually an angel, came out to the prophet, not remaining within, in order to show the iniquity and the measuring line and the talent of the lead being taken out. What each of these signifies, it is good for those having understood to observe.

Therefore, the measuring line being shown to come out is the fullness of all wickedness and impiety; which did not previously exist for the Amorites and the rest of the nations, nor did it punish the named nations, suffering punishment when their sins were filled up, with no kind of iniquity being absent, according to that which was said concerning some: 'Woe to a sinful nation, a people full of iniquity' (Isaiah 5:21).
In the same manner, concerning those filled according to Sophronius with adulterous, prudent love, it is said: 'And the two elders came, full of...'

of an intention. And concerning the sorcery of Elymas, the Apostle spoke abruptly, bringing the reproaches most strikingly against him: 'O full of deceit and of all craftiness, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, do you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord?' (Acts 13:10). This theory is constructed especially from what the Savior said to those Jews who were speaking: 'If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. So you testify that you are sons of those who killed the prophets; therefore, you also fulfill the measure of your fathers.' (Matthew 23:32).

For even if ten thousand had been killed in a murderous way against the prophets, there remained, in order to complete the measure of the ungodly, the audacity of him who says these things, by which they have branded him on the cross; for only then is the measure of their impiety fulfilled, when they, along with those who prophesied, judged the one prophesied to be dead. Just as there is a measure of sins for those to be punished, so also there is a measure of good works and of mindsets for those who have taken upon themselves a life of diligence and according to godliness.

And this measure is also fulfilled when no just opinion or piety is lacking. Toward these two ranks, both the good and the evil, the Savior said: 'With the measure you measure, it will be measured to you.' For to those who fulfill the measure of that which is praiseworthy, promises are being measured out which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have they risen up upon the heart of man, to be prepared by God for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9). But to those who handle deceitful and fraudulent works of both words and thoughts, punishment is brought in accordance with their worth, such as to go out 'into the outer darkness' (Matthew 25:30), and to depart 'into the fire prepared for the devil and his angels' (Matthew 25:41). Realize whether the Savior spoke by both measures or only of the measure of righteous works.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Contrast of Wisdom and Folly
english: “A measure, good, shaken, pressed, and overflowing, they will give into your bosom,” [Luke 6:38]—this was your governing principle.

Perhaps it is said only concerning the sown seed, giving a hundredfold and greater than “what we ask and understand” [Matthew 13:8], the reward of the sower; but for those who do not observe all the lawlessness, the one who knows hearts and understands the mind of all, does not give a measure that follows, but gives a measure to such people that is not shaken, not pressed, and not overflowing, but lacking and incomplete, so that I might phrase it thus, from mercy and goodness, “the one examining the sons of men with an eyelid.”

In the middle of the measuring vessel, a woman was seen sitting, being neither other lawlessness nor an opposing power subduing her. For the prophet himself said, pointing to this woman: “This is the lawlessness of all the earth” [2 Thessalonians 2:16], but I say of humanity, which he also named injustice: “For everyone, he says, who does injustice and lawlessness does so, and lawlessness is sin.”

Consequently, the one being initiated sees the lead talent being removed and the woman seen thrown into the middle of the measure, being lawlessness. And why was the woman seen not simply in the measure, but in its middle? Either because the middle has seized the center of all evil, ruling tyrannically.

And the removed lead talent falls into her mouth. This word is brought down and lowly and deprived of brightness, having an opposing position to the word which has attained virtue; “for silver, he says, is the refined tongue of the righteous” [Proverbs 21:28].

For that which concerns orthodox opinion and practical virtue has much that is precious and bright, but not the one in the mouth of lawlessness, since it happens to be heavy and lowly, especially since it is deceitful and crafted with trickery. Such was also the [one] of the magician Elymas, bringing forth [speech] “with all guile and every deceit” [Acts 13:10].

It is not necessary to consider it paradoxical if the designation of the woman is arranged according to a skillful, bad opinion and a wicked power that performs such things. For just as lawlessness is called a woman here, so in the Divine Proverbs, folly was named a woman [Proverbs 9:13]. And the word concerning this has it thus, from...

The wise man's words are being reported to the listener: 'Son, pay attention to my wisdom, and apply your ear to my words, so that you may preserve a good understanding; and I command you to be mindful of the sensation of my lips. For it is sweet to depart from the lips of a fornicating woman, which for a little while sweetens your throat; but later you will find it more bitter than gall.' (Prov 5:3-5). And after a little: 'For the feet of folly lead down after death into Hades.' (Prov 7:27).

Regarding unchastity, it is said in the book of Proverbs how a woman crouches when there is darkness and gloom at the corner, in order to deceive and harm the youth lacking sense. For having appeared in a fornicating manner, bringing lewd words, she says—wishing to ensnare him with a shameless face, being unbridled and unrestrained, so that she might inflame the heart of the young man: 'A peace offering to me is today; I give my vows, because of this I have come to meet you, desiring your face; I have found you.' And with other things: 'Come, and let us be enclosed in love; come, and let us enjoy friendship until dawn.' After such lewd words and those following them, the wise man says: 'Much conversation led him astray,' or 'crowd-conversation,' as some copies have, 'and with loops from the lips he hollowed him out.'

However, even if the youth was led astray, the teacher again awakens him: 'Do not walk in the way with her. The paths of Hades, her house, lead down into the chambers of death; for having wounded many, it has cast them down, and they are countless whom it has slain.'

In the same way that vices are named after women, so also virtues. For the wise man says concerning wisdom: 'I became a lover of her beauty, and I led her toward living with myself.' Regarding her being led thus like a bride, this proverbial ordinance forbids: 'Wisdom gives prudence to a man.' (Prov 14:1). To this man he commands: 'Delight yourself in her and she will exalt you; honor her so that she may take hold of you.' Toward the one who has given birth to a serious man from virtue, the Holy Spirit points out, saying: 'Your wife is like a vine growing straight in the trellises of your house; your sons are like young olive shoots around your table.' (Prov 12:4). Since these things are instituted not concerning a mortal woman and her sons, the...
