title: The Two Evils and the Unclean Creature
english: The verse bringing [it] forward implies: 'Behold, thus shall a man be blessed who fears the Lord.'

For if anyone takes such things in a human way, many of the great saints, being most devout, would not have had the blessing, not having lived with women, nor having given birth at all. To provide certainty, it is enough to bring forward Elijah the great prophet and Elisha, his spiritual son according to godliness; [text gap] concerning John the Baptist; and others are more numerous who have practiced celibacy, so that they 'may care for the things of the Lord.'

For John saw in the Apocalypse many thousands of male virgins not defiled by a woman. Even if the things concerning the virgins who fulfill the number one hundred and forty-four are raised, yet because of a pure and sober conduct, it is not distressing to accept the word as it stands at hand.

Much is shown in the book of instruction inscribed to the Shepherd concerning women and virgins, whose virtues and blessings it shows, and also their evils and punishments, which one encountering will be struck by from the book.

Zechariah 5:9-11: 'And I lifted up my eyes and saw; and behold, two women coming forth, and a spirit in their wings; and these had wings like the wings of an ephah; and they took up the measuring line in the middle of the earth and in the middle of the heaven. And I said to the angel speaking in me, "Where are these carrying the line?" And he said to me, "To build him a house in the land of Babylon, and to prepare it, and they will set him there upon his preparation."'

And now, lifting up the eyes of the inner man as in the previous visions, he saw two women coming forth, winged, and a spirit was in their wings. And their wings were like the wings of a bird called an ephah. These women coming forth thus took up the measuring line, in the middle of which the woman called iniquity was found, and they took it up in the middle of the earth and of the heaven. Having seen these things thus, I desired to ask the angel speaking in me, 'Where are these carrying the line?' And he said to me, 'To build him a house in the land of Babylon, and to prepare it, and they will set him there...'

Regarding his preparation. One must examine what two kinds of women these are. See if the two evils are the moral evil of the habitual transgression of the divine commands, or the false glory concerning those who are prudent and the evil powers working through them.

They appeared having wings, filled with spirit, that of which the Apostle writes: 'In whichs also you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the authority of the air, the spirit of the one now working in the sons of disobedience' (Ephesians 2:2). It is perhaps related, though the thing in the lying wings is trivial, to the unclean spirit cast out by Jesus from the man, which having been cast out by Jesus, if returning it finds it idling and having swept the place where it was cast out, having an empty hand and having swept, having all the good things it had been cast away, it takes other seven spirits more evil than itself, enters and 'dwells,' and the last things of that man become worse than the first (Matthew 12:44).

To represent that the wings are seven, the wings of the women were compared and made like the wings of the epic. But this creature is unclean, being a friend of the dead and of human refuse; indeed, it feeds in the tombs and makes a nest for itself out of human filth, so that having settled in the diseased cauldron, it may boil and make new ones like itself.

It had this designation from overseeing and looking upon human things. The women use it having been led into bad inclinations, namely those receiving [them] into... [gap] and envy, or the leading into an unrestrained and erotic potion.

One must observe what this creature must take by way of ascent, and see if it is possible. It either signifies the devil, or the antichrist. And each of the heterodox must not be unknown. The devil rejoices, and the anti-god antichrist, and the word of the heresies is to feed on tombs, the same being for the graves according to allegory, 'they are covered without, but within they are full of all unchastity,' and of the adjacent thoughts separating from God because they are crooked. For it is said in the most perfect Wisdom of Solomon: 'Crooked...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Call to Flee Babylon and the Vision of the Four Chariots
english: Reasonings separate [one] from God.

Regarding the question of whether the remembered creature is unclean and finds joy in bad habits, he builds his own beauty from human toil. What follows this, besides that he himself, whom I call the watcher, and his youths live in uncleanness? For this, observing human things, he received this title; but I say human things are the strifes, rivalries, and false zeal, about which the Apostle writes, rebuking those held by them: 'For where there is strife and rivalry among you, are you not human, and are you walking according to the flesh?' (1 Cor 3:3). Those called such flesh, you might graciously say are women, taking on bad habits, perhaps having been struck and eaten by the said watcher, in an allegorical sense, so as to cast out those seized by fear lest they be destroyed, and to raise filters leading to licentiousness.

It is proper for the one taking up wings like a dove to abstain from these women and their wings, in which the one spread out rests, finding 'the Sabbath which remains to the people of God' (Heb 4:9); you will understand the Holy Spirit descending in the form of a dove in the Jordan, whom he holds alone, and everyone who rests between the two covenants, called lots according to: 'If you sleep between the lots, wings of a dove are fluttering about.' To be winged according to these things is blessed; for they take up the one having them into heaven and the things above the world.

Of the two women being winged according to the watcher, hovering over the measure upon which lawlessness sits between heaven and earth—for even the sinful angels, and the earthly demons, and men who 'bear the image of the swine' (Matt 7:6) have tested it—the one seeing the revelation seeing [it] hovering and being carried away with the measure upon which lawlessness sits, says to the angel speaking in him: 'Where are these carrying the measure?' And the angel answering says: 'To build him a house in the land of Babylon, and they shall set him there upon his preparation' (Rev 18:2). For what other fitting place is there for the one having lawlessness by measure, except the confusion, so that he may find ready...

Will it be a whale to those pressing upon it? Therefore, one must depart and flee from Babylon because the measure has been placed there to be found ready for those willing. Thus the divine word cries out like a herald to one desiring to be diligent: 'Come out of Babylon, fleeing from the land of the Chaldeans' (Rev 18:4). Having understood the vision of the prophet to be such, let us love to have wings formerly, having been made to fly according to the Holy Spirit; for in this way it is most easy to pass into the super-celestial things.

And I turned and lifted my eyes and saw; and behold, four chariots proceeding from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze (Zech 6:1). In the first chariot were red horses, and in the second chariot were black horses, and in the third chariot were white horses, and in the fourth chariot were variegated, speckled horses. And I answered and said to the angel speaking in me: 'What are these, Lord?' And the angel speaking in me answered and said: 'These are the four winds of heaven, proceeding to stand ready for the Lord of all the earth' (Zech 6:5). In which [chariot] were the black horses, they were proceeding toward the earth of the north, and the white [horses] were proceeding after them, and the speckled [horses] were proceeding toward the earth of the south, and the variegated [horses] were proceeding and were looking to go and to go around the earth. And they went around the earth. And he cried out and spoke to me saying: 'Behold, the ones proceeding toward the earth of the north have stilled my wrath in the land of the north' (Zech 6:8).

Turning to receive yet another revelation, the prophet saw four chariots from between two bronze mountains. The first chariot had red horses yoked together, the second black, the third white, the fourth variegated and speckled. Having beheld the four chariots, desiring to learn about them, he inquires of the angel speaking in him what the seen things are. But he answers saying they are the four winds of heaven, making manifest the four climates of the inhabited world. And the black [ones] were seen proceeding from the land of the north, the white [ones] proceeding after them; but the speckled and variegated [ones] were coming from the south. Everything was said to me about the horses as much as possible when they were seen in the first...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Bronze Mountains and the Measure in Babylon
english: Following the vision of a man riding a red horse, those satisfied with such things do not consider the things now spoken regarding the things mentioned. It is said there are two bronze mountains from the midst of which the chariots went forth. And see if the phrase 'surpassing the bronze' is shown to have much pouring out. The sophists and heretical teachers use this, becoming 'a resounding bronze and a sounding cymbal' (1 Cor 13:1), because the divine love toward the lawlessness [mentioned] at 1.398, says to the angel speaking in it: 'Where do these carry the measure?'

And the angel answering says: 'To build him a house in the land of Babylon, and they shall set him there upon his preparation.' For what other fitting place is there for the one having lawlessness by measure, except the confusion, so that he may be found ready for those approaching him? Therefore, one must turn away and flee from Babylon because the measure is placed there to be found ready for those willing. Thus the divine word cries like a herald to one wanting to be diligent: 'Come out from Babylon, fleeing from the land of the Chaldeans' (Rev 18:4).

Having understood the vision of the prophet to be such a thing, let us hate having wings once, having been flown by the Holy Spirit; for thus it is most easy to cross into the heavenly things. And I turned and lifted my eyes and saw; and behold, four chariots going forth from the midst of two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze (Zech 6:1). In the first chariot red horses, and in the second chariot black horses, and in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot variegated horses (Zech 6:2). And I answered and said to the angel speaking in me: 'What are these, Lord?' And the angel speaking in me answered and said: 'These are the four winds of heaven, going forth to stand by the Lord of all the earth' (Zech 6:5).
speckled
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Iron, Bronze Mountains, and the Purpose of Divine Anger
english: Iron, as one who most strictly reproves God for being unyielding and having the appearance of a harlot, and for having shamed everyone and not submitting oneself to the gentle yoke of Jesus (Matt 11:30): 'I know that you are hard; and your forehead is bronze, and the sinew of your neck is iron.'

Two bronze mountains are said to exist because of the twofold nature of those exalted against the knowledge of God. For it is possible to hold false opinions regarding both practical and intellectual virtue, not being any other than the knowledge of truth; for those from the heresies are impious concerning both kinds of virtue.

Regarding the black horses coming from the north as vessels of wrath (Rev 6:8), 'from which the evils are burned upon those dwelling on the earth,' white horses were shown coming after them. These are the ministers of propitiation and of joy, and of profitable things. Since punishments are brought for the improvement of those surrendered to them, they follow harmoniously behind, clearly following them, weaving and announcing the bright and light-like things.

A soul, having experienced these, having become through perception, cries out most clearly toward that which approaches the destruction of the harmed (Mic 7:8): 'Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen; I shall rise again,' meaning, having repented. For even if, having fallen, I was cast down by punishment through the wrath of God, yet having endured and having bravely received the wrath that was incited, I have come into a propitiatory state and a rejoicing intercourse, saying: 'I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against Him, until He justifies my judgment (Ps 119:71); and He will execute my judgment, and He will lead me out into the light, and I shall see His righteousness.'

For even if God is angered for the sake of improvement and benefit, He does not always do this; for He says: 'When the anger of the spirit arises, I will heal again.' He who has been benefited from such providence says gratefully to the one who has chastised for salvation by a little: 'I will bless You, Lord, that You were angry with me for salvation; You turned Your face and had mercy on me.'

Regarding the black horses having come from the land of the north so that they might rest the wrath of the Lord, the variegated and speckled ones were seen coming from the south; from that, namely, concerning that in which...
the spear of spears
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Gold and Silver of Salvation
english: bearing God

As if there are virtues and wise thoughts there. For having been benefited from the shameless and painful state, they acquired the good things about which it is said in the first song of the ascents toward the one blessed by the Lord: 'See the good things, Jerusalem' (Ps 122:2), and also: 'You shall trust in the Lord and He will bring you up to the good things of the earth', which is the inheritance given to those who learn from Jesus 'that He is gentle and humble in heart' (Matt 11:29). Concerning which the hymnist has cried out: 'I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living' (Ps 27:13). Similarly, also the blessed prophet Isaiah exhorts to take a desire for the interpreted good things: 'For if, he says, you wish and you listen to me, you may eat the good things of the earth' (Isa 1:19).

Having received the command from the captivity regarding this, having received it through the Word of the Lord having come to him, he is commanded to enter into the house of Josiah, who is receiving [the name] 'saving'. For it is fitting for the one being saved by the Lord, about whom it is written: 'Our God is a God of saving', having come 'to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10), to be a son of Zephaniah, interpreted as 'Jehovah is timing'. For a timing is being approached by God for the one having been saved with eternal salvation, of which the Savior is the cause, concerning which the Apostle writes concerning the Savior: 'Having been perfected, He became to all those obeying Him the cause of eternal salvation' (1 John 5:20).

To the one commanded to enter into the house of the one having come from Babylon into the holy city Jerusalem, a command is given to take silver and gold and to make crowns so that they may be placed on the head of the high priest, and this is Jesus, of the true Jesus being the salvation of God, receiving [the name] 'Salvation is Jehovah', meaning that of God; for one of the names of God is Jehovah in the Hebrew voice. Let us observe more of the gold and the silver from which crowns are constructed by the one having received the command. Silver is the word and gold is the mind, they are taken up by the law of allegory. For it is said in the Song of Songs concerning these being spiritual treasures for the bride by the friends of her bridegroom, the king being: 'I will make you likenesses of gold after a moment of silver, until the king reclines on his couch' (Song 1:11). It is probable that the likenesses of the spiritual gold...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Shadows and Spiritual Crowns
english: The writings before the arrival of the Savior are shadowy and iconic pedagogies; which the Apostle says are 'shadows of the things to come' (Colossians 2:17) and 'an image of the things hereafter attained' (Colossians 2:17); and these are the things to come, consisting according to the life-giving Spirit.

2.17 And since the likenesses of the said intelligible gold are variegated and constructed from the divinely-breathed sayings, the likenesses of the intelligible gold receive their variety from the flakes of silver. What then is the silver from which the flakes decorate the likenesses of the gold, or is it 'the pure words of the Lord, being silver refined in a furnace on the earth' (Psalm 12:6)?

2.18 Concerning the said intelligible gold and the appropriate silver in that bridal chamber, it is said regarding the peaceful bridegroom: 'King Solomon made for himself a throne from the wood of Lebanon; he made for himself pillars of silver, and his canopy was gold' (1 Kings 10:18). Of this spiritual throne, the pillars are made of the aforementioned silver, and its canopy is inherently spiritual gold.

2.19 And since it happens that those striving for piety are shown to be victors from the said treasures, 'contending even unto death for the sake of truth' (2 Timothy 4:7), from them the crowns are constructed of the spiritual treasures, so that the martyrs of the truth and all those who have overcome the fleshly adversaries may be honored, having taken under their feet those called 'rulers, authorities, and cosmic powers of this darkness, spiritual evils' (Ephesians 6:12).

2.20 Since there are many and diverse combats, it is necessary that the prizes also be many and diverse. Therefore, not one but many crowns are crafted by him who has received the command. For every virtue and the works performed according to it has its own proper crown.

2.21 For he who has heard the laws of his Father God and 'has not rejected the statutes of his mother' (Galatians 4:26), 'the free Jerusalem above' (Galatians 4:26) and 'the glorious Church' (Ephesians 5:27), receives a 'crown of graces' upon his own head, being adorned with a 'golden garland' which decorates the submissive power of the soul, allegorically called the 'neck'. And in the...
has a divine mind for its construction
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rising of the Just Man
english: that having been proven, he shall receive the crown of life, which God promised to those loving him. And since it is the same thing to endure a trial in the sense of a struggle, to compete in the good contest, to finish the race, and to keep the faith, it is likely that the crown of righteousness is the same as the crown of life.

2.27 Many crowns made of the intelligible gold and silver are placed upon the head of Jesus, the [one] of righteousness—for indeed the [name] Iesedek is taken into the Greek sound from the Hebrew into 'righteousness'. And see how the one head of Jesus receives many crowns. For he was tested 'in all things without sin' (Hebrews 4:15), having overcome the contests.

2.28 Understand by theory another way how the head of Jesus, the great high priest, receives the crowns of all. All those believing are the body of Christ and members; for it has been said regarding those completing the sum of the Church: 'You are the body of Christ and members of the member' (1 Corinthians 12:27). Of these members of the body, forty-five are hands, feet 'not lazy in haste', eyes that are discerning according to the mind, and a head are the rulers who legally preside as is necessary.

2.29 Those being thus a head and seeing sharply and hearing the parables of Jesus—and since many are those called head allegorically in this way, because of the practical and contemplative life they have—consequently the head of the high priest receives all the crowns. And [he is] a great high priest, and in the epistle to the Hebrews it is written thus: 'Having therefore a great high priest, Jesus, who has passed through the heavens, let us hold fast the confession' (Hebrews 4:14).

2.30 And it is not paradoxical for one man's head to receive all the crowns. For if each [virtue] is, rather, each virtue is a crown, and the perfect man has all the best dispositions, following the virtues themselves, the one having all [them] is revealed by many crowns.

First, the one taken up by the God-Word was a man; then his imitators, who are themselves called Christs because they are partakers of that of whom it is said: 'The Christ is the wisdom and power of God' (1 Cor 1:24).

2.31 Zach. VI, 12: 'And you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord of Hosts: Behold, a man, an ascending-sun is his name, and he shall rise up beneath him, and he shall build the house of the Lord; and he himself shall take virtue, and he shall be established and prepared upon his throne, and he shall be a priest at his right hand, and a peaceful counsel shall be between the two of them.' 2.32 'And the crown shall be to those enduring, and to those useful to it, and to those having known it, for a grace of the son of Wisdom and for a psalm in the house of the Lord. And those far from them shall come and shall build in the house of the Lord. And you shall know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you; and it shall be, if listening, you shall listen to the voice of the Lord your God.'

2.33 'You shall say,' he says, 'to him,' making clear that it is the son of Wisdom; 'Thus says the Lord of Hosts: Behold, a man, an ascending-sun is his name.' But these things are said concerning our Savior who has come among us, being a man according to his being born from Mary, the temple of the God-Word, and being a sun of true light and righteousness.

2.34 What is said in the prophet Jeremiah agrees with the present matter, having thus: 'Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a just rising, and he shall reign and reign, and he shall understand and do judgment and righteousness upon the earth. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell trusting, and this shall be his name, which the Lord shall call him, Joshedek among the prophets' (Jer 33:15).

2.35 For the just rising rising up from David is that which is shown by the hierophant in the: 'Behold, a man, an ascending-sun is his name.' This same man is called an ascending-sun because of the sun of righteousness.

title: The Davidic King and the Firstborn
english: the righteous rising of David

Regarding the one who is truly David by hand, he rose up to shepherd the sheep who hear the voice of Jesus, being 'sheep of the hand' of Jesus and 'a people of his pasture'; thus, a most excellent general having been sent by the Father's good pleasure, having raised up from a shoot as if a vassal, he turned the enemies who had become afraid into flight, bringing their hands to their necks.

He is also praised and glorified by his own brothers, having been shown to be their firstborn, according to the voice of the Apostle: 'Whom He foreknew and predestined,' God declares, 'to be conformed to the image of His own Son, so that He might be the firstborn among many brothers' (Rom 8:29). Concerning whom the firstborn says to God: 'I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing your praise' (Ps 18:5). These things are said concerning the one who is glorified as being from Abraham and David, as Matthew writes: 'The book of the genealogy [of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham]' (Matt 1:1).

It is fitting for the brothers who praise him, and also the sons of his mother, and it is evident that they are of the upper Jerusalem, to worship him 'in spirit and in truth' (John 4:24), in the same manner as it was said concerning the angels: 'Let all the angels of God worship him' (Rev 22:9). All excellencies are perfected, having received the end of the prophecy existing here: 'There shall be the root of Jesse and the one rising to rule the nations; upon him the nations shall hope' (Isa 11:10).

Equally to the one rising from the root of Jesse as the ruler of all nations, what was fully spoken has the force of Jeremiah's word. For the same as 'rising from the root of Jesse the king of the nations' is: 'Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a righteous dawn, reigning as king, in whose days [the people] shall be saved' (Jer 23:5), he who confesses, being called 'Judah' with the voice of Hebrews, and the mind seeing God, being called 'Israel,' 'will tabernacle trusting,' according to that which is said by those who confess to the Lord of all: 'Have mercy on us, Lord, for in you we have trusted' (Ps 116:2). Concerning all who have stood thus boldly and manfully, it has been written: 'Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his hope' (Ps 40:4). And what name shall be called to the one rising from David, reigning as king, having understood the resting upon him...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rising of the Horn of Salvation
english: A spirit of God's wisdom and understanding, being a spirit that made judgment and righteousness upon the earth, or the 'Josedech in the prophets'? 'Josedech' is interpreted as righteousness existing in the prophets, announcing its arrival toward us, according to that which is proclaimed in the hymns, where it says: 'Righteousness descended from heaven' (Ps 89:12), and where: 'Righteousness rises in his days' (Ps 72:11).

Having clarified the received prophetic things for the demonstration of the prophetic word of Zechariah, it is time to contemplate it also. 'Behold,' he says, 'a dawn is his name.' In relation to the things said, the humanization is shown from: 'Behold, a dawn is his name'; confirm if the bridegroom who has the bride is called a man here. For this the Apostle makes manifest, writing to the Corinthians: 'I want to unite all of you to one man, a pure virgin' (1 Cor 7:37).

There is an expectation to reach this man, those having been filled with the knowledge of the Son of God, as Paul himself, speaking again in Christ, marks out: 'Until we all reach a perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness' (Eph 4:13) of the Son of God; for toward this perfect man, concerning whom John the Baptist says, 'No one has arisen among females greater' (Matt 11:11), [he says]: 'A man comes after me who has been before me' (Matt 3:11); this man he signifies, asserting: 'He who has the bride is a bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom rejoices in joy because of the bridegroom's voice' (John 3:29).

This man shown by the prophet is called a dawn, concerning which in the Gospel Zechariah, the father of the Baptist, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke out: 'A dawn from on high has appeared to those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death' (Luke 1:78), in order that, the darkness being released and the shadow of death no longer existing, we might pass from death into life, and having shone forth, we might become light in the Lord, casting away the darkness of the ignorance of God and of the rest of evil, we might become light in the Lord according to the philosophy of those writing: 'For you were darkness, but now light in the Lord' (1 Pet 2:9). Concerning this dawn, having risen from David, the father of the Baptist, toward another...

Regarding God, he says this: 'A horn of salvation has arisen for us from the house of David' (Luke 1:69), which is to say, a king of salvation. For in many places of the Scripture, and not at all least in the wise Daniel, kings and queens are called horns.

Using this one who has risen in the house of David, the wise say to God: 'We horn our enemies in you.' 'From below' the one being shown, called a rising, 'rises'—that is, a light, or a plant bearing salutary fruits—for the word 'to rise' is arranged commonly according to light and plant—which rises from below the great teacher, lawgiver, and king.

But what are those below him? Or are they those things subjected to divine laws and naturally conforming to instruction? For how is not every man called praiseworthy below, since Christ is his head? And all the members of Christ, being fulfillers of the Church being the body of Christ, exist below Christ, who is the head of the Church.

Thus also, regarding a king and teacher, you say 'below' the subjects and the disciples, from whom there becomes a rising of the light of the knowledge of truth and a tree bearing good fruit, concerning which one discourses as a farmer, as God says: 'I planted you as a truly fruitful vine' (Jeremiah 2:21); but let it perish for each god-fearing one: 'How have you turned to bitterness, you foreign vine?' (Jeremiah 2:27).

And 'to rise' below the spiritual farmer, you say, also the virtues according to their kind and the works of these, being generations of righteousness, about which the Apostle writes: 'God sanctifying the generations of your righteousness' (Romans 6:22), and the prophet Hosea: 'Seek the Lord until he comes, the generations of righteousness to you' (Hosea 10:12). These 'those sowing them in tears shall reap in joy' (Psalm 126:5), that is, with toil and sweat for the sake of piety.

It is possible to understand this: 'From below him it rises,' and thus: the Word having become flesh, Jesus, 'born of a woman' (Matthew 1:25), rose from below 'the rising from on high' of the God Word, who is true light. From the possession and it must be said this: from the right hands of the Father, the Son having sat, below him 'the enemies were placed as a footstool' (Psalm 110:1), who, having been benefited from becoming under the feet,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Dual Throne of the Rising Sun
english: It rose up like light and offspring. He who, having risen up below according to the theologized [statement], 'will build the house of the Lord'—the Church of the living God—especially he who, having risen up below the God-Word during the visitation, is a man. But also those who, having risen up below according to the other interpretations, being obedient to the All-King and good teacher, having changed the commandments of the one ruling and instructing them into practices, built their life like a house upon the rock which is Christ, setting the foundations and bases of the house upon the solid and indestructible faith into the Trinity, a rock so named toward the one confessing it toward the one having been confessed, according to it thus having been said: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it' (Matt 16:18).

But also those who, according to the third interpretation, having been placed under the feet of the All-King as enemies, becoming instead different friends, will build the house of the Lord, 'that he may dwell and walk in them' (Rev 2:7), having called and having improved them. He who, having risen up below according to the visitation, similarly to: 'Truth from the earth has risen up' (Ps 89:37), 'shall receive virtue,' [is one of] those bearing it, those being saved toward him and being led into great glory. For how does he not receive this from the one becoming in him the righteousness of God, having become sin on behalf of them, according to the apostolic philosophy: 'For he who did not know sin, he made sin on behalf of us, that in him we might become the righteousness of God' (2 Cor 5:21)? For how does he not receive virtue being the righteousness and abundance of peace in the days of his incarnation?

As he intends to receive the virtue being made in men, let each of the faithful bear fruit and offer it; the one preferring to be temperate, decency and temperance, also purity and virginity; the one self-controlled, self-control, 'always carrying the death of Jesus in his body' (Gal 6:14) to himself. And those 'using the honorable marriage and the undefiled bed' (Heb 13:4) also offer virtue. Such as Joseph was, and Susanna, and Anna the prophetess and Elizabeth the mother of the baptizer, and as many as...

Others and others have excelled in purity. They claimed a great and unshakeable faith, a virtue that was superlative, 'those who have fought the good fight for the truth even unto death' (Heb 12:4), having confessed in them the Son of God before men, so that He himself might also confess them before the heavenly Father and the holy angels.

2.65 The one called the Rising Sun 'is seated and shall reign upon his throne' (Ps 45:6). And his throne is double, the one as king, the other as priest, as it is possible to demonstrate from the written words.

2.66 The Pantocrator is made manifest from the recurring decree having it thus: 'When a righteous king sits upon a throne, nothing evil opposes him' (Ps 72:1); but also from: 'Your throne, O God, is unto an age of ages; a rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingship' (Ps 45:6); and from that which is said in the Psalms: 'The Lord King is seated for ever' (Ps 45:13).

2.67 Concerning the priestly aspect, in the [Epistle] to the Hebrews; for the one who inscribed the epistle wrote: 'Such a high priest became fitting for us, holy, blameless, undefiled' (Heb 5:8), and he says: 'Let us therefore approach with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help' (Heb 4:16), calling the throne of grace the [throne] of the holy, blameless, and undefiled high priest.

2.68 Since therefore the one about whom it is said 'is seated and shall reign upon his throne' (Ps 45:6) has received 'the throne of David his father, that he may reign for the ages, his kingship having no end' (2 Sam 7:13), but also 'an unshakeable priesthood' (Ps 110:4). For it has been said concerning him: 'You are a priest for ever' (Ps 110:4).

2.69 Upon the double throne he is seated and shall reign, he alone having the throne of kingship and priesthood. When having sat upon the throne he shall reign firmly, thus: 'there shall be a priest at his right hand, in the midst of a peaceful counsel between both' (Ps 110:3). Who then is this, or is it Melchizedek, whom the Apostle writes remains a priest perpetually, being made like unto the Son of God (Heb 7:3)?

2.70 And thus the apostolic voice has toward the Hebrews: 'Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but having been made like unto the Son of God, he remains a priest perpetually' (Heb 7:3). Since...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Incorruptible Crown of Glory
english: He is not a shadowy God-healer, but truly and according to the Spirit, he will be at the right hand of the one sitting and beginning upon his throne. Being made like the Son of God, and remaining a priest forever, he has a peaceful will toward the one whom he was made like; and likewise the Son of God is making peace toward the king of Salem, that is, the king of righteousness, who is this Melchizedek. For how does he not have a peaceful will toward the one to whom he is a priest according to the order, remaining for an age?

And the true and divine crown is given to those who endure with greatness of soul, according to what was said, of which we also briefly remembered: 'Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for having been proven, he shall receive the crown of life which God promised to those loving him' (James 1:12). How great is the desire to attain this, [as] his head being lifted up, he achieved endurance, concerning which James writes: 'Count it all joy, brothers, when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing works endurance' (James 1:2-3), as to praise those who achieved it with joy, where as one all of them, having through harmony one soul and one heart: 'Waiting, I waited for the Lord and attended to him and he heard my prayer' (Psalm 40:1); and where: 'And now what is my endurance? Is it not the Lord? And my subsistence is with you' (Psalm 73:26).

And this holy and beautiful crown exists not only for those enduring, but also for 'the useful and those having known it.' Of the present vision of the prophet or the previously mentioned virtue, what is this crown, pre-eminently named by those previously mentioned, having come from silver and gold? The Lord of Sabaoth himself, as it is brought forth in the prophet Isaiah: 'On that day the Lord of Sabaoth will be a crown of glory' (Isaiah 62:5).

For this is a contest of glory, to be given to those who glorify God in their own bodies; and the pious hold a conception, and of those who are prudent, rather of the pious dogmas. For according to this we are called orthodox, those having ecclesiastical knowledge.

2.76 And this crown is woven not of gold and costly stones, but of the right glory concerning the truth. And this same is the incorruptible, about which the Apostle writes literally: 'He who struggles exercises self-control in all things' (1 Cor 9:25), but one who, having run the lower and human contests, competes 'so that he may receive a corruptible crown' (1 Cor 9:25), 'but we [receive] an incorruptible' (1 Cor 9:25), which has also been called unfading by the most supreme Apostle Peter (1 Pet 5:4).

2.77 For he is writing to those who shepherd the true flock under the shepherd, concerning which things God promises to give to his spiritual sheep, saying: 'I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they shall shepherd you with knowledge' (Jer 3:15), and the word of Peter has it thus: 2.78 'I exhort the elders among you to shepherd the flock that is among you, not by compulsion but willingly, so that, when the Chief Shepherd appears (1 Pet 5:4), you may receive the unfading crown of glory' (1 Pet 5:4), to be yielded to those having guarded the faith orthodoxly and to those leading to the end, the command saying: 'Then give glory to our God' (Ps 67:5), and again: 'Give glory and honor to the Lord' (Ps 29:3).

2.79 This crown is given 'for a song of Zephaniah and a psalm in the house of the Lord' (Zeph 3:4), about which the hymn-writer says: 'Take a psalm and give a timbrel, a pleasing harp with lyres' (Ps 150:4). And it is a psalm which it is necessary to take, the word concerning those doing and thinking well, to which it is fitting to give a timbrel, a pleasing harp, and a lyre.

2.80 And he who has received a word concerning temperance gives a timbrel, 'dead are the members upon the earth, fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desire' (Rom 8:13), 'carrying the death of Jesus in the body' (Rom 8:13), by which

title: The Prophecy to Zechariah
english: He enslaved and treated with contempt; for the timbrel has the construction of a dead skin.
These are beaten and struck by the five prudent virgins, according to that which is sung in Psalm 67:5: 'Princes have gone before, singing in the midst of young women, timbrel players.'

The Hebrew women used the interpreted timbrels after they had departed from Egypt and crossed the Red Sea, of whom the prophetess Miriam, sister of Moses and Aaron, came forth, having taken the timbrels of themselves in hand; singing triumphantly in accordance with the choir leader, they said: 'I will sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously exalted; He has cast horse and rider into the sea' (Exodus 15:1), and the following until the end of the song.

For it is not even probable to think that such a multitude of timbrels could be found in a completely desert place with such myriads of women, it being quite possible that the timbrels spoken of allegorically have already been found in more advanced years among the God-fearing, especially spurred on toward the spiritual dance, from which they have been seen to have happened paradoxically for the sake of becoming outside of Egypt.

And they are given by those having received the psalms with the timbrel and a pleasant harp along with lyres, joined to the powers of the soul and the senses toward the divine melody; but sobriety is necessary so that one does not take false instruments and songs, which God rejects, saying: 'Turn away from me the sound of your songs, and I will not hear the melody of your instruments' (Amos 5:23).

He who turns away from what is rejected by God sings and chants praiseworthily, according to the exhortation of the writing Apostle: 'Speaking to one another in psalms, spiritual songs, singing and chanting in the heart' (Ephesians 5:19).

After the crown into the graces of Zephaniah and into the psalm in the house of the Lord, these existing, those who are still far off from the captives will arrive in order to approach the one who has proclaimed to them forgiveness; and praising, [they say] 'they shall build in the house of the Lord,' in order that they may serve continually in the manner of priests, according to the blessed prophet Samuel.

And each shall be completed, being fulfilled through vision, when the useful ones, having heard, shall hear the voice of the Lord, and having known the cause of the [gap] which they waited for for a time.

Those who approached and those being far away, the ones who received benefits in the house, they hear the practical things and the mysteries of the kingdom, the priestly iniquities, the things set forth by the Lord Pantokrator.

In the fourth year of Darius the king, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, who is Chashaleu (Zechariah 7:1-3). The king and his men sent to Bethle Sahara and Arbess to appease the Lord, saying to the priests in the house of the Lord Pantokrator and to the prophets, saying: 'The holy offering has come here in the fifth month, just as I have already done for sufficient years.'

In the fourth [year] of the captivity, [he] sent to Arbess and the men to appease the [Lord], saying: 'The holy offering, the service, according to the fourth [year] of the beginning of Darius, to be recorded'; some were being falsely written and being refuted in public.
Some, supposedly of prophecy, having turned away, were written in the Hebrew voice, the number nine upon the receiving in the ninth month.

title: Sacrifice of the Body and Zechariah's Prophecy

Elevating [missing], 'I prepared a lamp for my Christ.' A lamp, John [says], 'a burning lamp,' the peak of the sanctification of righteousness. Concerning the sanctification of Isaiah here: 'Sanctify him, Lord, and he will be a fear to you, and if you have trusted in him, it will be to you for sanctification' (Isaiah 8:13).
They say, 'Your throne, O God, is unto the age of ages' (Psalm 45:6). The Lord of Israel, [missing] to the apostles, [missing] an epistle to them, 'Therefore enter...'

Regarding the one coming into the world, he says: 'You did not desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me; you were not pleased with burnt offerings and [sacrifices] concerning sin; then I said: Behold, I have come.' (Hebrews 10:5).

[The text is heavily corrupted with long strings of dots/placeholders] ... to whom there shone ... to be present, so that you might see ... the image of his salvation ... whom he loved, of whom one was among his men. title: The Living Spring and the Sower
english: You drink, not you seventy years without fasting, those whom the Lord spoke; these are the ones of whom I prophesied, for so it has happened.

By the way of the Savior casting, providing, and what he does with his hand, he says in that place: 'there is a spring of water' (John 4:14), which is in him living, by the action of the Holy [Spirit], you will drink, those in the thirst of desire. The sower went out to sow (Mark 4:3), and what he had spoken came forth; he went out from fasting and [on] the seventh [days], namely those, it is to be observed.

title: The Abundance of Spiritual Fruitfulness
english: “Clothe the naked, take in the poor homeless into your house. For then, he says, your light will break forth early (Isa 58:8), and your healing will quickly rise up (Isa 58:8).”

To those who fasted and cut [fasts] in the fifths and sevenths not as was fitting, the Lord says: “Behold, seventy years you have spent in Babylon, having been carried away in it by the law of captivity (Jer 29:10); not the fast that I accept you fasted for me, but eating and drinking your own pleasant things, doing nothing according to the words in the hands of the prophets before, when Jerusalem was being inhabited and prospering, and the cities of Judah around her, of which she is the metropolis, and the mountain and the plain were being inhabited?”

For how would the metropolis not have prospered with the cities under it, and the mountain and the plain inhabited around it, bringing deep peace and being ruled with the right law, having driven far away every war and enemy? Thus, regarding Jerusalem and the cities around her making peace and having much stability, there was abundant prosperity while the plain and the mountain land were being inhabited.

It happens for such places to be inhabited when there is much fruitfulness and prosperity, for men to dwell able to live well in the mountain, the planting of trees being full of oaks, and the plain bringing wheat and barley and the other crops. For in places multiplying, a multitude of men loves to dwell, some indeed farming, others enjoying the abundance.

Jerusalem being inhabited and prospering, and the cities around her, the Church finds [this] by analogy, and the orthodox views; of which the mountain, producing fruits, is the doctrines of piety and of the orthodox faith, having much abundance of products in the moral instruction in the low plain.
Concerning such a spiritual prosperity in the fourth...

And it is brought forward by the sixty-fifth Psalm: 'You have visited the earth and made it drunk, you have filled it to make it prosperous. You have made its channels drunk, you have multiplied its generations; in its drops it shall be glad, rising up. You shall bless the crown of the year with your goodness, and the plains and all that is in them shall rejoice. The mountains of the wilderness shall be soaked, and the hills shall rejoice and be girded. The rams of the flocks have entered, and the valleys are filled with grain; for they have cried out and shall sing.' (Psalm 65:9-13).

Since this abundance and all-fruitfulness is of a spiritual nature, how could the mountains and the plains not be inhabited by men, along with the true word which makes them so, to the point that they might cry out and sing thankfully to the God who has granted so many things?

And a sign of a painless habitation in the mountains and the plains is that the rams of the flocks have put on fat-footed steps, because the pasture has been made to grow abundantly in the places of the mountains and the plains.

When the longing for this spiritual enjoyment of prosperity enters, let him listen to the words given by God into the hands of the prophets, transforming them into actions, so that also from his own practical powers the spring of life may rise up, 'water leaping into eternal life,' by the grace of the Savior who provides all these things.

And it happened that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: Judge with a righteous judgment, and show mercy and compassion to each one toward his brother, and do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner, or the poor, and let no one in your heart bear a grudge against his brother.' (Zechariah 7:9-10).

The word of the Lord which came to the prophet, as was said before, announces what the Lord Almighty has commanded, beginning from: 'Judge with a righteous judgment, and mercy and compassion each one...' to those hearing [to] 'do'...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Just Judgment
english: "...toward his own brother"; and he adds, "not to oppress the widow or the orphan," and he adds, "the sojourner and the poor." For in this way the "malice of the brother, not bearing a grudge against each in their own hearts" will easily exist. What does he intend by these things? I say it is time to see.

The word of the Lord, having appeared many times already in Zechariah and now appearing in it, forbids these things. "These things," he says, "says the Lord of Hosts" to each of the rulers of the people: "Judge a just judgment" (Zech 7:9), as there is one who judges unjustly through bribery and grants [favors] through friendship, and even when there is a bribe toward someone being judged. To such complaints the divine word cries out to those: "How long will you judge injustice and accept the faces of sinners? Judge the orphan and the poor, justify the lowly and the needy" (Isa 5:4). Such are also those concerning whom the prophet Isaiah speaks: "Those justifying the ungodly because of gifts and removing the right of the righteous" (Isa 5:4).

Concerning those who lawlessly act thus, the prophet Habakkuk cries to God: "Judgment has become contrary to me and the judge takes [bribes]; therefore the law is dissolved and justice does not go to its end, because the ungodly oppresses the righteous" (Hab 1:4). It must be said to those examining things in this way, who dispute among themselves, that they are not to be considered just judges, but altogether unrighteous and lawless judges.

For it is fitting that no one should observe the judge, whether he prefers wealth, status, or lineage, whether he prefers friendship, or looks toward a bribe, but rather toward the facts of the things being judged. The priest who receives God proclaims these things to those being ordained to judge in this way: "Both the great and the small you shall judge, you shall not accept a face," "and the poor you shall not show mercy in judgment," "for the judgment of God is." It is not right to distribute and measure the things of God to whoever happens to be. For of their own things, let each have authority to grant to whomsoever it may seem to him; not of his own, but of God is the judgment according to the divine law.
It occurred to one of the ancients to say that the judge is a living justice, that is, possessing and subsisting, perfect...
As one having been established according to justice, so that just as in other works of virtue he pursues the just, so also in judging.

The power of the one being observed is known from the opposite; for just as he who has his disposition and his practice established according to justice pursues the just, so he who is regulated according to inequality and malice pursues the unjust. All such people existed toward whom the word says: 'How long do you judge unjustly and receive the person of sinners?' (Amos 5:24) of the divine lawgiver saying: 'You will judge the great and the small, not receiving a person' (Deut 10:17), even if the one being judged is rich, even if he has honor and rank. For the law of those being judged does not count the abundance of wealth and poverty, nor rank and dishonor, but works and deeds having been performed according to virtue or malice.

Just as therefore it is not necessary to take advantages from the wealth and rank of those being judged, so also you will not lack wealth and the lowliness of dishonor; 'For you will not show mercy to the poor in judgment' (Ps 82:3). For the just judgment and the things of the poor must be examined. For in this way someone will justify an orphan and a widow, and a poor man and a needy person, not granting him the just right if he acts unjustly, so that the legal judgment may not be perverted.

The righteous word, having commanded that a just judgment be brought forth, proceeds to forbid: 'Not to tyrannize the widow, the orphan, the sojourner, and the needy' (Exod 22:22). For it is not proper to impose punishment tyrannically against those deprived of human help, but from the opposite to reach out to them with righteousness, according to that which is commanded: 'Become, he says, as a father to orphans, and instead of a husband to their mother' (Ps 68:5), 'judging orphans and justifying widows.'

For this is unassailable and according to the will of the one who composed all, as James writes in the epistle in which he addressed the believers thus: 'Pure and undefiled religion before God the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world' (James 1:27). He who thus serves God, how could he unjustly judge these whom he visits in their affliction, filling up their lacks through almsgiving and other help and protection as they may need?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Forgiveness and the Law
english: Regarding those who are being benefited? 2.146 In the same way as one must not oppress a widow and an orphan through a husband or parents, one must not likewise oppress a sojourner staying with those to whom he has taken refuge, whom they consider a stranger and a non-native. If any of those named—a widow, an orphan, or a sojourner—is deprived of resources, one should share equality with him, not by oppressing or by harming him in any other way. 2.147 It is indeed good and pleasing to God to stand up for those who are in such a state according to history, but especially according to allegorical interpretation. 2.148 A widow is praised according to theory if she has cast off the evil husband she had, meaning no one other than the devil or some other evil spirit. Likewise, an orphan is good if the father who sired him through sin has died. This is symbolized by one who has come out of his own father's house having been called by God, and that woman to whom it is said in the Psalms: 'Be favorable to your people and to your father's house,' even after you have died. 2.149 The divine Bridegroom, being also a Father, lifts up those souls who have thus become widows and orphans, according to what is said in the Psalms about him: 'He will take up the orphan and the widow.' For 'the Father is the judge of orphans and widows,' according to what is said in another Psalm, also caring for sojourners who have left idolatry and turned to piety, enriching every poor person and needy one because of us, according to the apostolic word that stirs up those who suffer well, saying: 'Know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for us, so that through his poverty we might become rich.' 2.150 Having taught how one must not oppress those in need of protection and help, he harmoniously brought forward also that one must not be vengeful, not only in word but from the depth of the mind, saying: 'And let no one be vengeful against his brother in your heart.' What was said by the Savior in the Gospel is equal to the prophetic: 'If you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you your trespasses.' 2.151 In accord with the existing prophecy, Jeremiah says on behalf of God: 'And the malice of the [near...'

Let no one of you hold a grudge in your hearts against his debt. The Savior makes this perfect forgiveness of whatever one has done sinfully manifest in the parable of the servant owing ten thousand talents; for this is chosen by the master who forgave the debts to the 'unworthy servant' for all of us: 'So also will your Father do if you do not each forgive from your heart those who owe you' (Matt 18:35).

Taking the whole parable in hand, understand its words and its meaning precisely, so that, being benefited toward goodness, you may forgive the debts from your whole heart to all those who owe, remembering no more those things by which the one who wronged you sinned against you.

Regarding the brother, being understood in two ways—the one being a fleshly kinsman, the other having been born from God who also begot you—it is proper to hold a grudge from the heart against either.

And they refused to pay attention, and they gave a stubborn ear, and their ears became heavy so as not to listen, and they set their heart to be disobedient, not to listen to my law and the words which the Lord of all has sent in His Spirit by the hands of the prophets before them (Zech 7:11-12).

Since God has given a divine law to the people of the Hebrews, an exhortation from the one who gave it was brought forward in the seventy-seventh and seventy-seventh Psalm thus: 'Pay attention, my people, to my law' (Ps 76:7). He who follows the exhortation in this way 'meditates on the law of the Lord day and night' (Ps 1:2), according to what is philosophized in the first Psalm, which Moses the high priest previously established saying from the face of God:

'All these words, as many as I command you this day, shall be in your heart and in your soul, and you shall speak of them sitting in your house and walking on the way, looking and wandering, and you shall touch them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be unshakable'—or 'unmoving'—for the scripture is carried either way—'before your eyes' (Deut 6:6-8).

To the one thus keeping the given commandment, paying attention and obeying the legislation follows. For how will one who has the holy words in heart and soul disobey in paying attention, as speaking of them while being at home and walking on the way, looking and wandering? Or he does not carry them...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Turning away from the Divine Words
english: Looking toward the Lord of all, the speaker says: 'If I remembered you on my bed in the watches, I meditated on you' (Psalm 63:6).

But also the one fasting does the same, having the words of God in memory, as if speaking boldly to God: 'God, my God, toward you I rise early' (Psalm 43:27). The prophet Isaiah, having this same zeal, said: 'My spirit rises toward you in the night, O God' (Isaiah 26:9). Believe that it has the same mind and that which is thus announced: 'At midnight I arose to confess to you' (Psalm 119:62).

He who is thus zealously disposed toward the words of God, having turned them into works, grasps them upon his practical power, the hand called allegorically, so that having them before his eyes, he may contemplate the beauty of their thought, whether they be shaken or unshaken—for I said there are two kinds of writing of the word. And the words and the meanings completed from them are shaken before the eyes of the heart when we act according to what has been legislated.

Or are the words grasped upon the hand and understood and practiced not shaken, indicating the other writing of the unshaken, which is said before the eyes of the legislated, the permanent and certain of the established things, agreeing with the prophetic here: 'The word of the Lord remains forever' (Psalm 119:89), and with the words of the Psalmist: 'All his commandments are sure, established unto the age of ages' (Psalm 119:152). According to this thought, 'the words of Jesus shall not pass away, even if heaven and earth pass away' (Matthew 24:35).

He who is secured through all the things contemplated, having the words of the Lord in heart and soul, and speaking in them while being at home or walking on the way, looking and fasting, will by no means be inattentive or disobedient, nor again 'will he give heed to one acting foolishly.' How then will he who is disobedient in paying attention give heed to one acting foolishly?

This happens when someone becomes so foolish as to have the most corrective things said to him, beginning from the ninety-fourth Psalm: 'God said to the sinner: Why do you recount my judgments and take up my covenant by your mouth? But you hated instruction and cast out my words...'

Not toward the back. For how have they not turned away from the divine commands, having given them neglect, 'the one running with a thief and after committing adultery, setting his own portion,' doing the same things as those who transgress, turning away from: 'You shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal' (Exodus 20:14-15), and the laws given along with these.

2.164 It happens that they stumble and disregard those to whom the words of God have been given as a matter of neglect, just as they have turned away from the very one to whom the words belong. For each of those persisting thus and cutting short, dishonors the Lawgiver God, transgressing what has been legislated, as the Apostle says regarding the one who falsely and with deceit claims to have the truth and guards what God has legislated: 'He who boasts in the law, by the transgression of the law, dishonors God' (Romans 2:29), as it was said by this dishonored God toward those who have perverted the will, as if not only to cast the divine words into the background, but also to give neglect to the one to whom the words belong, turning away crudely: 'They turned their neglect toward me and not toward their faces,' which is necessary for the enlightened one of the inner man to have the face as the cause of all good, just as it is said by the wise one through whom all things unclear and hidden of wisdom are revealed: 'Toward you I lifted up my eyes, the one dwelling in heaven' (Psalm 123:1); and again: 'My eyes are toward the Lord always, because he will deliver my feet from the snare' (Psalm 25:15).

2.165 Not only did these wanderers not do this, but they also showed neglect with an unslumbering eye to the overseer, having gone entirely after Baal and regarding all idolatry as to worship and adore evil demons, those hidden among soulless statues, enjoying itching and smoke, and incantations and other things, being burned upon altars built lawlessly and most impiously.

2.166 But how has it come to pass for the ill-fated to give neglect, disregarding what is brought forth: 'For they made their ears heavy, he says, not to listen, and they set their heart disobedient, not to listen to the divine law and words of which the Lord the Pantokrator spoke in his Spirit' (Ezekiel 3:7).
2.167 For someone makes his own ears heavy, not those of the body, for this is not upon us, but those of the soul; by pre-choice.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Hardening of the Senses
english: For these things weigh down and cause a sharp hearing. For the hymn-writer stretches himself out concerning certain things, saying: 'The sinners have been made strangers from the womb, they have been led astray from the stomach, they have spoken falsehoods. Like a deaf and ringing shield are the ears, which will not hear the voice of one singing, nor the medicine being prepared by a wise man.'

How is it that those who weigh down and ring the ears are not inattentive and deaf, those who have been made strangers from the womb of God, and having been led astray, have spoken falsehoods from the stomach? These things are said as children's things regarding those who have been made strangers from the womb of the Church which bore them, and having been led astray, spoke falsehoods at the same time as they came forth from its stomach, ringing the ears according to the shield; for it is an evil and venomous power.

Concerning such things the most wise John, the disciple loved by Jesus, says in which he inscribed in a holy epistle: 'They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us' (1 John 2:19). For they seemed to be from the apostles and disciples of Christ, and having taken the same gospel to themselves, and having been born 'through the bath of rebirth,' they became outside of the holy mother who bore them and of those born from her who remained in having 'the spirit of adoption.'

What, then, followed their apostasy, or the ringing and weighing down of the ears according to the shield of palm-leaves, which in no way hears those singing the holy words of God and preparing the medicine logically, capable of putting to sleep and hardening, so that, having been prepared, it might cast out the poisonous virus, as is the inheritance of the holy mountain of God, having come forth from the blessed and holy rod from the root of Jesse?

But more about these things has been said to us clearly, interpreting the territory of the prophet Isaiah, reaching to: 'And a child infant shall lay his hand upon a bed of shields, and they shall by no means do evil or defile anything upon the mountain...'

“...my holy, because the whole was filled to know the Lord.” 2.172 That the weighing down of the ears of the inner man is a matter of choice, as has been closely stated, is testified to by the prophecy of Isaiah, being proclaimed in such a way to those who attend to these things with a heavy heart: “For the heart of this people has become thick, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and their eyes they have dimmed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them” (Isaiah 6:10). For, desiring to remain as they had chosen to have through malice and impiety, they weighed down the ears and their eyes were dimmed, the heart of them having become thick, so that, not having heard the words concerning virtue and the knowledge of the truth, they might not be improved and turn back to Him from whom they had turned away through their sunset and blindness.

2.173 Many symbols of such healings are carried forth in the Gospels, and sensorially of Jesus having healed these things; for he healed the deaf and the blind to hear sharply and to see keenly, healing “every disease and weakness” (Mark 7:34) of the body, and much more of the soul. 2.174 Just as in the saying of Isaiah, those having become thick in heart weighed down the ears so as not to hear, and the things brought down worked toward their own harm, so also in the present voice of Zechariah, those having set their heart to be disobedient so as not to hear the law and the words sent in the Spirit of the Lord of all, weighed down the ears of the intellect, so that, not receiving the saving and blessed teachings and the words sent in the Spirit of the Lord of all, which the Holy Spirit is, [they might remain in error]. 2.175 Let the heretics be rebuked, for they propose natures uneducated and altogether untrained, differing from men; for they dogmatize some as being unfit for virtue, and others as not being of a nature for the assumption of malice; following which they disregard not even the law, nor exhortation, nor reproof, nor—
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The removal of evil and the hardness of heart
english: An exhortation, not a prayer offered to God. The most impious ones have embraced this doctrine, having understood very well the new and the old testament. For in the Gospels, he says that regarding men, as having free and autonomous choice: 'If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and let him take up his cross, and let him follow me' (Matt 16:24). And again: 'Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest; and unyoke yourselves and learn from me that I am gentle' (Matt 11:28). For the 'come' and the 'unyoke' and 'learn' are addressed to autonomous persons. Immediately, indeed, he makes the beginning of his teaching thus, saying to those who are knowledgeable: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near' (Matt 4:17). For repentance is a change of mind regarding things done previously, having free choice, not a nature unparticipating in virtue or vice. For neither will the foolish be diligent, nor the good be evil, according to the impious logic of those asserting [fixed] natures.

Having set forth the testimonies from the new testament concerning man being autonomous, he will also bring forward those from the old. And first the Mosaic ones, then those of the prophets. First is of the ten sayings spoken by God through Moses: 'You shall have no other gods besides me' (Exod 20:3); and next: 'You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any likeness of anything, whatever is in the heaven above, and whatever is in the waters below the earth' (Exod 20:4). And after a little: 'Honor your father and your mother, so that it may go well with you' (Exod 20:12). And next: 'You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal' (Exod 20:13-15). From which the Apostle Paul, being a learner of the law even if he were anyone else, was benefited, and writes: 'Let him who steals steal no longer, but rather let him toil, working what is good' (Eph 4:28). And he writes this also toward autonomous persons: 'Having laid aside falsehood, let each one speak truth to his neighbor' (Eph 4:25).

It follows to say that which is proclaimed also from the prophets toward autonomous persons. He says of Isaiah toward those held by sins and because of this ignorant of the energy of those who praise: 'Cease from your evils, learn to do good' (Isa 1:16). For having free and unrestrained choice, the ceasing from those things they have done...

Thus one also learns to do what is good. Toward such people through Isaiah the Lord says: 'Take away the evils from your souls in front of my eyes,' for he sees your hidden things. Therefore, let the removal of evils from the hidden part of the souls be striven for, not by word or by seeming, but according to truth.

Also Jeremiah, regarding the soul running in haste toward evil and longing for the most indulgent banquets, protects her, saying: 'Turn your foot from a rough road, and your throat from thirst. And she said: I will be brave, because he loved strangers and followed after them' (Jeremiah 2:23).

A rough road is that which is forbidden or filled with thorns; and shameful desires and unrestrained pleasures and 'the cares of this life' are the thorns, which grow most in the paths of those not working for virtue, according to the proverbial saying having thus: 'The paths of the idle are paved with thorns, but the paths of the brave are worn down.' For continuously and without interruption, those walking having patience and bravery wear down the places through which they pass, so that because of the continuous wearing, they do not grow as thorns, but as worn paths.

Even though there are many among all the prophets who do not lift up the mythical impiety of those having reshaped the natures, and who confirm the free will of rational substances, it is sufficient to have set forth these things, so that the word, being a reminder, may not go beyond what is necessary.

These things having been mentioned beforehand, the one speaking regarding 'those having given their backs, acting foolishly and weighing down the ears of those not listening' must be supervised. For they, he says, having arranged their heart to be disobedient to the not-listening to the law, have fallen by the sins that cast them down. For the forbidden things are not established haphazardly and as they happen to be to those unwilling, but from a prior disposition of the most indulgent having existed, according to which they arrange their own hearts to be disobedient; for they did this by their own choice, not by fate or by any other necessity driving this, as the prophetic saying clearly declares: 'They arranged their heart to be disobedient to not obey my law.'
Similarly, the invisible tyrant of the intelligible Egypt also weighed down and hardened his heart, as it is said many times in Exodus regarding...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Divine Wrath
english: His [heart]. Perhaps the heart of the one who despises is hardened and becomes heavy, having received lawlessness, being weighed down like a talent of lead. The Apostle writes to the one who despises the existing fountain of goodness: 'Do you despise either the wealth of his kindness and his tolerance and his patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?' (Rom 2:4). 'But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are treasuring wrath for yourself in the day of wrath' (Rom 2:5).

In this way Pharaoh and his heart were hardened. For, while being repeatedly subjected to great powers of those becoming rich in kindness, which are exhorting, but rather coercing, to come to recognition, the insolent man remained in audacity and roughness; the insolent man was being hardened, his heart being weighed down by the talent of lead, there being nothing other than lawlessness, whence, having enriched himself with the lead of lawlessness in like manner, 'he sank like lead in rough water,' as it is carried in the triumphal ode against him.

Since, therefore, no such heart was raised by God, but rather those having it possessed it by themselves, because of the hard and contrary, and being called stony—as we have such a ruling principle by ourselves—let us approach thus by choice to the one who removes the stony hearts, so that instead of them he may place fleshy hearts, tractable and well-guided, so that we may be able to keep his commands and ordinances, obeying the spiritual law, our heart changing from disobeying and not obeying the divine law into doing all things with persuasion that must be fulfilled according to law and the sent words in the Spirit of the Lord of the Pantokrator; and this is holy, as it was called a substance.

This also agrees with what was said here: 'Behold, I will command in my Spirit to my servants the prophets' (Zech 12:10). Interpreting what the sent words are and how they are given and where, he says they are given 'in the hands' of 'the prophets.' What the thought of this word turns out to be has been made clear previously in the small [matter]. Therefore, so that we do not repeat ourselves, often considering the same things, being satisfied with what has been said, we set forth the following words of the prophet.

A great [wrath] from the Lord of all. And there shall be such a way that they said and did not listen to him, thus they shall cry out and I will by no means listen to them, says the Lord of all (Zech 8:17). And I will cast them out into all the nations which they did not know, and the earth shall be destroyed following them from the one going through and from the one turning about; and they prepared an elect land for destruction.

The Lord, giving to each of the men according to his deed, to those committing many and great [sins] he is greatly angry, and he does this in part to those stumbling a little and few. For it has been said by him concerning the vessels of wrath being found fit for punishment: 'I indeed was angry a little, but they themselves persisted in evils' (Rom 9:22). And those accusing themselves for the things in which they acted lawlessly cry out to the merciful and compassionate Master: 'Do not be greatly angry with us.' For just as the way [is] 'being a just judge, strong and long-suffering, he does not bring wrath on every single day' (Ps 136:15), so in part he is angry with those being judged, not observing all their lawlessness.

These things being thus understood, if it were said that a great wrath from the Lord of all has come to be, we do not by any means call it great: 'for he will not take care to have mercy any longer, nor will he perceive in his wrath his mercies' (Ps 136:15). For of these indeed a father and source exists, but he brings the wrath until threatening to admonish; but if those sinning were to despise the threat, and by that trial of punishment were to enjoy themselves.

Having this pious reasoning, those possessing it cry out to the Benefactor: 'Do not be angry with us unto the end, or will you stretch out your wrath from generation to generation?' and again: 'God, you who having turned back will give us life, and turn away your anger from us.'

These things said concerning God of the Scriptures, let us not fall into such impiety and foolishness as to approach human passions toward the one saying: 'I do not change' (Mal 3:6), to whom the theologians say, the one [is]: 'You are the same,' and the other concerning him: 'With whom there is no change or shadow of turning' (Jas 1:17). For if he is the same, not changing, not being altered, not having a change of turning or a shadow, how would he stretch out for punishment? For nothing else is wrath or the stretching out for punishment.
Not thus indeed does God get angry, being impassive, but bringing...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Great Wrath and the Great Mind
english: The afflictions are like a help for the improvement of those asking for it, for the purpose of ceasing sin and the diseases and wounds from it. It is his to hear 'the one desiring to save all and to come to the knowledge of truth' (1 John 5:20); 'When the wrath of my spirit arises, I will heal again', as he says graciously, having been tested for healing through painful discipline: 'I will bless you, Lord, because you were angry with me; you turned away your wrath and had mercy on me' (Psalm 102:13).

A soul thus benefited praises the one surrounding her with affliction, saying: 'Let not my enemy rejoice over me, for I have fallen, but I shall arise; I will endure the wrath of the Lord because I have sinned against him, until he justifies my judgment, and he will execute my sentence, and he will bring me out into the light. I shall see his righteousness, and my enemy shall see it, and she shall be clothed in shame, she who says to me: Where is the Lord your God? My eyes shall see him; now he shall be a footstool' (Micah 7:8-9). The wrath of the Lord, leading to so many goods, proves not harmful, but beneficial, being skillfully led by a physician of souls 'healing every disease and weakness'. For how is it not salvific to be brought out into the light toward which the merciful God was angry, so as to finally behold the envenomed evil power falling into shame, having been clothed in it because it has become a footstool?

Since the cause of all goods brings about the unpleasing and painful things like a skillful physician, the prophet speaks as a theologian: 'And he himself was wise against them, and his word shall never be set aside' (Job 5:12). If, for the sake of the word of the only wise God not being set aside, he brings about afflictions, then the wrath that brings these about is not a passion or a change. The wrath of the only merciful one is presented as not a desire for punishment, and from what is said by the theophany Moses toward the one being glorified in a triumphal song against Pharaoh and his army: 'You sent out your wrath and consumed them like a reed' (Psalm 105:39). And wrath being sent out so that it might consume the reeds shown to be through fruitlessness, is not a passion having desire in the one being angry, vanishing when it goes out from the one being angry; therefore, the wrath sent out is not a passion, but a painful discipline.
