When the great wrath from the Lord Pantokrator has occurred, the reason is given: 'For it shall be,' says he, 'in such a way that they, transgressing his law and casting his words behind them, shall cry out thus, having fallen under punishment, and I will not listen to them, says the Lord Pantokrator.' Similarly, it is said in the writing of Moses by the righteous judge: 'They went toward me obliquely, and I will go toward them in oblique wrath.'

What then shall they suffer, those having fallen under great wrath? 'I will cast them out into the nations which they did not know,' he says, not having experienced the trial of their ferocity and crudity; but the Assyrians and Babylonians and all other barbarians to whom Israel sins and is ungodly is delivered, having fallen by their hands into the captivity of the law.

Regarding those who have thus, through crudity and beastliness, and incorporeal opposing powers, having been inhumanly roused against the captured captives, the Assyrians, Babylonians, and Egyptians are found by way of an ascent. For they are not mortal Assyrians, of whom the so-called great mind rules, concerning which it has been written in Isaiah: 'The Lord will strike upon the great mind, the ruler of the Assyrians' (Isa 5:5).

Concerning this also it was said in the prophet Nahum—and this is the seventh of the twelve: 'Woe to them! because your shepherds have entered into them, the Assyrian king has made your mighty ones sleep' (Nah 3:8). And a great mind was forbidden to the king of the Assyrians because of the malice and the terror of his wiles, as if not many saw his methods, or only those able to say: 'For we do not ignore his thoughts,' but we are able to grasp and refute them.

For so also, having seen the sophistical manner of his servant Elymas the sorcerer, he who does not ignore the thoughts of the devil strongly brought the refutation, saying: 'O full of all deceit and of all mischief, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord?' (Acts 13:10). This mind, ruling and reigning, is the Assyrians according to allegory; by another thought, it is the Babylonians of malice; and by another, the Egyptians, those of the spiritual ascent, the Egyptians and the Babylonians.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Allegory of the Land and the Body
english: Providence casts out those who are handed over to nations such as these because, while remaining within the divine laws, inwardly understanding and keeping them, they were not cast out; but after experiencing this, they began to seek and practice the causes of being cast out and handed over.

This is what the Apostle interpreted in many ways, writing once: 'Who, pretending to be wise, became fools (Romans 1:22), and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for a likeness of corruptible man and birds and four-footed animals and creeping things (Romans 1:23); therefore God gave them up to the lusts of their own hearts to uncleanness (Romans 1:24).' And again: 'Who exchanged the truth of God in a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25); therefore He gave them up to passions of dishonor, the dishonoring of their own bodies among themselves, as men behaving shamefully and unchastely toward one another, men committing shame upon men; likewise also their women exchanged the natural use of womanhood for that which is against nature (Romans 1:26).'

A third delivery they received: 'those having been handed over to a reprobate mind because they did not approve of having the knowledge of God (Romans 1:28),' as it follows that they would be 'filled with all unrighteousness (Romans 1:32)' and its various kinds, which the Apostle who wrote the epistle listed hereafter.

By these same deliveries, those cast out into the nations fell, because of the great wrath having come upon them from the Lord of all. And they were handed over to strange nations which they had never known through experience.

Having been cast out, upon whom the great wrath had become, into all nations they did not know, their land vanished from before them, they being relocated from it, so that no man was able to pass through or return. And since man was no longer upon it, and from every vegetation it vanished, no longer bearing green herb, no longer being of woody vegetation, which followed him...
And no longer are herds of animals upon it. But wickedness increases, because it was turned into a wasteland, though it was once an elect land by virtue of 'flowing milk and honey' (Exodus 3:8).

Regarding the history, allegorically, the good heart and beautiful land vanished, falling from bearing good offspring to bearing thorns, briars, and weeds, so that there is no longer a correct thought passing through it, nor turning back to it, especially since it was turned to destruction, although it was previously elect, having inhabitants, farmers, and shepherds.

These things can also be said regarding tropology: our body becomes an elect land, possessing temperance and purity, so as to allow passing through and turning back to it temperate and orderly ways, in order to bear the offspring and edible fruits of purity which the trees of virtue bring forth.

It sometimes happens from increased wickedness that the elect land, which through purity was inhabited, is turned to destruction and becomes desolate; which thing happened to all who repeat perfect chastity in order to please God, having guarded his own elect land, which is the flesh having been praiseworthily put to death, 'bearing the death of Jesus' (Galatians 2:20).

According to the twofold lifting up, the tropological and the allegorical, the land of election flows milk and honey, from which nourishment and spiritual enjoyment are composed, the honey being produced from the bee which preferred the wisdom of God, according to the proverbial saying protecting the industrious one here: 'Go to the ant and consider how she is a worker; having valued wisdom, she went forward, the labors of which both kings and commoners offer up for health; and she is both desirable and prosperous' (Proverbs 6:6). Along with this sweetness, the holy land flows milk, which the Apostle quenches for the little ones in Christ.
Both these things the holy bride of God's Word carries under her own [tongue], as is said in praise of her: 'Milk and honey under the tongue...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Milk, Honey, and the Deception of Serpents
english: Paul happens to be like a spouse, a bride according to the soul of the divine Bridegroom, having under his tongue—that is, the word—providing milk to those about whom it is said: 'You have become in need of milk, not solid food' (1 Cor 3:2). But to those he provides honey, saying they are perfect, handing over wisdom to them: 'But we speak wisdom in the perfect.'

He who has fallen from the chosen land has honey to exist there, concerning which it is written proverbially: 'Honey drips from the lips of a prostitute woman, which for a little while sweetens your throat, but later you will find it more bitter than bile' (Jer 12:8). To this honey from the lips of the prostitute, milk flows appropriately from the breasts of dragons; and these are wicked powers, just as the prophet Jeremiah says about them: 'And even dragons brought forth breasts, they suckled their young. Daughter of my people, like a sparrow in the wilderness' (Jer 8:7).

They say that those who took care to know the nature of reptiles, concerning the so-called horned ones, that having hidden their whole body in the sandy desert, they leave their horns above the surface, which moving, they entice the sparrows. For having taken the fantasy of falling upon worms, they are struck by the venom being injected into their mouths by the horns. Therefore the word says that those receiving the venom from those from whom dragons suckle; even if they are of the people of God, they are dried up 'like the sparrow in the wilderness' (Jer 8:7), that which was enticed by the said reptiles.

Thus it happened: 'The word of the Lord of Hosts came, saying: These things,' he says, 'says the Lord of Hosts: I have envied Jerusalem and Zion with great zeal, and with great wrath I have envied her. Thus says the Lord: And I will return to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and Jerusalem shall be called a true city, and the mountain of the Lord of Hosts a holy mountain' (Zech 8:2-3).

As the presented matter might be made clear toward a literal sense thus: There came a word of the Lord of Hosts saying the following things made manifest: 'These things,' he says, 'says the Lord of Hosts: I have envied Jerusalem and Zion,' recalling her to himself after she had been cast out and pushed away, as if she had been insulted by strangers. Not just by chance did I envy her, but in great wrath. From cohabiting women, to men, it was taken...
From cohabiting women, to men, it was taken...
has strayed from the bed
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shadow of the Law and the Mountain of the Lord
english: What exists when I say, 'when I turn back and dwell in the midst of it', or the calling again of that city 'true', no longer being a desert, but full of citizens and buildings, the temple and the houses having been raised up, to have as before cloisters, streets, cut-out squares and narrow ways.

Thus, Jerusalem having explicitly been called true, and the mountain of the Lord Pantokrator shall be holy as it was before the captivity, through the sanctifications habitually performed there, and the hymns and praises being raised up according to the words of the Psalmist, where it is said: 'To you is due praise, O God, in Zion' (Ps 87:2); and where: 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion' (Ps 87:1). After these things have appeared according to history, it is a time to contemplate those things regarding the spiritual ascent.

Concerning the so-called Jerusalem of the discerning soul—for Jerusalem is taken to mean 'vision of peace'—having slipped and therefore having become outside the divine chamber, a separation has occurred from that which previously dwelt with her, so that she is henceforth being dragged away in a prostituted manner by opposing powers, called in spiritual ascent Assyrians and Babylonians, so that her suitable husband no longer shows pity for her.

But since the matters of free choice do not remain in this state, for just as a turning occurs from virtue into vice and from piety into impiety, so likewise a change occurs from worse and harmful things into better and profitable ones, so as to know again the divine chamber which had departed, so that, as before being cherished, he himself zealously pursues her while driving away those who adulterously defile her. And in great wrath he works this, intensely indignant against those dragging her away, so as to say clearly: 'I have zealously guarded Zion and Jerusalem' (Jer 2:37).

In spiritual ascent, the soul is aiming at the unseen and the eternal, and a soul seeing peace has the rhythm of the following of virtues and divine understandings, for whom, having zealously cared in great wrath for her, he turns back to himself, and at the same time to her, attending to her supplications in providing what for which she prays unceasingly.
Thus, having been improved, she might be named true Jerusalem, no longer surrounding the shadowy and iconic things of the law, but the things through...

They signify the good things, concerning which the divinely inspired Apostle writes: 'The law of things to come has a shadow, not the image itself of the realities' (Col 2:17). And again to those believing from among the Gentiles: 'Let no one judge you in food or drink, in part of a feast and new moon and Sabbath, which is a shadow of the things to come' (Col 2:16).

The evangelical teachings are things about to be good in the received words, which the Savior said regarding the mysteries of the kingdoms, speaking to those who knew: 'To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens' (Luke 10:22). Zion and Jerusalem, which aim for and see the peace of their harmony, are lifted up, called true, being lived out according to the truth revealed in the shadow of the law, and 'searching the God-breathed writings.'

In harmony with the holy city being called true, the mountain of the Lord Pantokrator shall be holy and shall prosper. See if the mountain of the Lord Pantokrator is the word of the presence of the Son of God, concerning which in a certain song of ascents it is brought forth thus: 'Those having trusted in the Lord as Mount Zion' (Ps 125:1). For let our mind not be so impoverished as to think it is to be compared to or made like a sensible mountain, those having trusted in the Lord, having a vast virtue, as being shown to have spiritual blessings as blessed ones. For it is written in Jeremiah the prophet: 'Blessed is the man who has trusted in the Lord; and the Lord shall be his hope' (Jer 17:7). And in the Psalms: 'It is good to have trusted in the Lord or to have trusted in man' (Ps 40:4).

Since therefore it is not a sensible mountain, being a refuse of the earth, those having trusted in the Lord imitate—what must they think, or that concerning which Isaiah said: 'At the end of the days the mountain of the Lord shall become manifest' (Isa 2:2), shining and having been revealed 'at the completion of the ages, in order to abolish sin,' having loosed and made it vanish, having received the judgment of the Lamb. This mystery illuminating, John the Great said, showing Jesus: 'Behold the Lamb of God, the one taking away the sin of the world' (John 1:29).

Concerning the mountain having been shown, it is necessary to take also that which is announced in the seventy-fourth Psalm thus: 'Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in a holy mountain' (Ps 48:1). Of these according to the first...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Streets of the Spiritual City
english: Regarding the showing of an ascent, Zion must be turned back through a high allegorical understanding, calling the things philosophized by the one speaking to the Hebrews the true Jerusalem, writing: 'You have ascended, Zion, mountains and city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and church of the firstborn, who celebrate festivals with myriads of angels' (Heb 12:22), for which reason they are 'written in the heavens,' having been granted citizenship in the holy and heavenly city.

Such as the apostles also were, hearing from the King of all: 'Rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens' (Rev 3:5). This scripture of 'living' things is a 'book.' Concerning these blessed ones, the vessel of election is marked thus: 'With also Clement and the rest whose names are in the book of life.' The Lord of all says: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: Yet elders and elders shall sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each having his staff in his hand, from day to day. And the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls playing in its streets' (Zech 8:4-5).

As for a literal sense, the prophet's proclamation declares that Jerusalem is being restored to a deep and tranquil political state. For since there is no disturbance and all wars are shot away far from the beautiful city, with no fear of enemies expected at all, those having the age of elders from long duration and many days, men and women alike, shall yet sit as before the captivity in the streets, having staffs in hand; first the elders, and let it be known if also the elders [women]; for the staff is a symbol of honor.

Thus, those preceding in age being seated, the streets shall be filled with boys and girls playing, not being restless in the streets due to the bringing of infants, or enemies lying in wait, or expected wars.

Of the history spoken, let those things be said toward the intellect. The glorious Church is a spiritual city having streets, concerning which it is announced to the one holding it, the King of all: 'The city of God was spoken of as having been glorified concerning you' (Rev 21:2). For how could it not be song-worthy and much-praised, having been moistened by divine drinks...

Taking from 'the river of the water of life of God'. It is also said in the forty-fifth and fifty-first Psalms regarding the royal city and those receiving gifts near the one ruling it royally: 'The streams of the river gladden the city of God; the Most High has sanctified its tabernacle, God is in its midst, it shall not be shaken' (Psalm 45:7). For the Most High, having sanctified its tabernacle, dwells in the midst of the peaceful city being spoken of, never becoming outside of it, but remaining unshakeable within it.

2.248 The streets of this beautiful city exist as virtues and their actions, about which the wise man reports proverbially, characterizing wisdom thus: 'Wisdom is praised in exits, leads to boldness in the streets, and is proclaimed upon the edges of the walls.' For how could the wisdom of God not lead to boldness in the streets of the spiritual city, again saying another wise saying: 'Desiring wisdom, observe the commandments, and the Lord will supply it to you' (Psalm 119:2), each commandment being called a wide street because of its breadth, as to say to the hymn-singer toward God: 'Your commandment is exceedingly broad'?

2.249 One must observe whether it is said according to this thought by the bride of Christ in the erotic drama: 'On my bed in the night I sought him whom my soul loved and found him not; I called him, and he did not obey me. I will arise and go about the city, in the markets and in the streets, until I find him' (Song of Songs 3:1-4). For in the time of conjugal union and resting, whom he allegorically called night, having thought the divine bridegroom was present with her, she sought and found him not, and having called and not having him listening, it was so that something useful happened to her by being distanced, so that she might be more wounded by love toward him; for the love toward him is more raised by the distancing of the one being loved.

2.250 Having suffered this, therefore, she arose, rousing herself, and seeks him nowhere else but in the churches, which are holy marketplaces. There the appointed apostles and prophets and teachers discourse on the rites and mysteries of the truth of the kingdom of God.
2.251 In seeking him in the marketplaces and in the streets, already having been interpreted, she hastens to encounter the one being sought, so that finding him...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Selection and Character of Elders
english: He finds rest in himself. The Wisdom that leads boldness in the squares of the beautiful city, in which the Creator brought all things into being, is proclaimed nowhere else but upon the edges of the walls to those guarding and watching over the divine city, according to the voice of Isaiah spoken thus before the King of Kings: 'Upon your walls I have set guards by day and by night, who will never be silent, ever remembering the Lord' (Isa 62:6).

In the designated divine squares of the blessed city, serious elders and elder women will still sit as before, holding in their hands their own staffs, this being a symbol of kingship, this being a participation in priesthood, and moreover in didactic words.

It is fitting to take elders who have been sold for wisdom, according to what is carried in the most holy Wisdom of Solomon, having this: 'For old age is precious, not because of many years, nor is it measured by the number of years; but there is much wisdom among men, and old age is a life without blemish' (Wis 4:9). This is the spiritual age appropriate to the friend of God who was credited with righteousness, Abraham, whose faith 'was reckoned to righteousness' (Rom 4:3).

For it was said by the hierophant Moses in Cosmopoeia: 'Abraham, having departed, died, having been nourished in good old age, elder and full of days.' For these things are not said because of a multitude of years of the cycles of the perceptible sun. For those born before him were of more years, yet none of them was called elder or full of days. For the father of Isaac was the first of men to be named elder from the embassies of those named by virtue.

Concerning those having such a judgment, a polity, and a mental age, the Cause of all things and the Provider of all good things says to his faithful servant: 'Appoint with yourself seventy elders, whom you yourself know to be elders' (Exod 24:1). From which it is shown that neither the appointment nor the laying on of hands makes...
He shows those who are older not as those who were previously so, but makes them manifest. For it was strictly ordered that those whom the forerunner already knew to be such should be ordained.

The same is possible in Joel (Joel 3:5), one of the Twelve Prophets, who protects the command 'to choose elders'—not as a preceding election, but as a subsequent recognition for the sake of manifesting those who have already acquired virtue and its seniority. Concerning those possessing this honor, it is written in Proverbs (Proverbs 16:31): 'The glory of elders is many,' which are made manifest by wisdom.

Equal and of equal strength to these mentioned elders exist also according to the New Covenant. For the Apostle, writing to his disciple Titus (Titus 1:5), has likewise inscribed to others: 'For this reason I left you in Crete, that you should set in order the things that are lacking, as I commanded you, and establish elders in every city.' He mentions the characteristics of those previously appointed, those being placed into ecclesiastical ranks: monogamy, the best upbringing of children, and being perfected in the remaining virtues, whom he also calls bishops by ancient custom, as we have said elsewhere.

Immediately, indeed, it is brought forward in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 14:23) that 'Paul called the elders of the Church,' to whom he also says: 'The Holy Spirit has appointed you as bishops to shepherd the Church, which He acquired with His own blood' (Acts 20:28), and the following. To those having this rank, Peter, the foremost of Christ's disciples, addresses them in his epistle (1 Peter 5:1): 'I urge the elders among you.' And let us see what it is that he urges: to shepherd Christ's flock, not by compulsion, but willingly, so that, when the Chief Shepherd is revealed, they may receive the unfading crown of glory (1 Peter 5:4).
Those accounted as elders according to both covenants are kings, being according to Abraham, according to what was said by those who knew his excellence: 'King...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Prophetic outpouring and the metaphor of children
english: They do not merely say, 'God is with us,' but also, treating the chosen one priestally and sincerely, they carry the staffs of the approaching double excellence, sitting in the squares of the nearby city, each holding his own rod, which serves as a staff and a corrective word.

For regarding those who rebuke children, it is written by Paul: 'What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod or with love?' (1 Cor 4:21). According to this, the divine writing of Proverbs also argues, where: 'He who offers wisdom from lips, strikes a man without heart with a rod' (Prov 26:3); and where: 'He who spares the rod hates his own son, but he who loves disciplines him carefully' (Prov 13:24).

They participate in the honor and dignity of the elders through faith and practical virtue, having acquired seniority. Regarding such a way of life, Paul, the one speaking in Christ, says to Timothy, marking him: 'Honor widows who are truly widows' (1 Tim 5:5), meaning those who are deprived of all human things, having deeds bringing praise, having raised children as is necessary, generously hosting guests, having surpassed in service to God's servants, having nourished the poor, and adorning themselves with works of virtue toward all those nearby.

The apostolic teaching has, regarding these, the same syllables from which it begins: 'Let a widow be counted, not having become less than sixty years of age, a wife of one man, being testified by good works, if she has cared for children, if she has welcomed strangers, if she has washed the feet of saints, if she has helped those being afflicted, if she has followed in every good work' (1 Tim 5:5).

For the confirmation of the mentioned virtues requires the accompaniment of perfect age to the possessors of virtues, having reached a perfect number of years, not diminished to sixty years of age. Such was Anna the prophetess according to history (Luke 2:36-38), having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity, remaining a widow for a long time until eighty-four years of age. This number is also appropriate for the purity in widowhood, about which it has been said in others.

One is to see this same disposition also in the Old Testament. Such was the most courageous Judith, having famously possessed the title; for Judith is interpreted as 'praise.' And it is not unlikely to find many others adorned with seniority and honor, and especially those concerning...

Of these, it is said in the prophet from the face of God: 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy' (Joel 2:28), and the following until: 'And also upon my servants and my handmaidens I will pour out from my Spirit and they shall prophesy.'

Having understood for yourself, examine whether it is said concerning the elders alone to hold staves in their hands, or also concerning the elderly women. It is possible that it is written concerning both groups, but it seems more likely concerning men alone.

In the clarified streets in which those having been made wise by prudence and having grown old by an unblemished life stand, and little boys and girls are playing a praiseworthy play, through which the man David, according to the heart of God, performing all the wills of the one who chose him, spoke more boldly: 'Before the Lord I will dance and play' (Psalm 36:4).

It is possible to take little boys, wandering in the streets of the immortal city of God, who have endowed themselves with prudence through soft nails, so as to have incorruption with the most sharp dignity and an unsearchable healthy word.

Such were the children of the apostles, 'having been born again not of corrupt seed, but of incorruptible, through the living and abiding word of God' (1 Peter 1:23), 'as newborn infants having longed for the spiritual milk without guile' (1 Peter 2:2).

And it will also be useful in season what is said in Proverbs: 'That I may give cunning to the guileless, and perception and understanding to the young child' (Proverbs 1:5). And still in the same book the God-inspired one said: 'Hear, children, the instruction of a father, and pay attention to know understanding' (Proverbs 1:8).
Not altogether are these things said concerning males according to the body; for there are also souls that are male in prudence while they have a female body.

Consequently, regarding the attributed little boys, girls should also be included playing. And see if concerning these in the forty-fourth Psalm the song sung about the bride and the bridegroom praises them thus: 'Virgins shall be brought to the king behind her' (Psalm 45:14), making manifest the bride and the queen, the one standing at the right hand of the one dwelling with him, 'those near her shall be brought to you; they shall be brought in gladness and shall rejoice' (Psalm 45:15). Virgins being brought behind the bride who was led away to one man, the Christ.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Restoration despite destruction
english: The churches are incorruptible in spirit and body, being pure in thought and action.

Just as it was previously said that children are eunuchs according to the soul, but not only according to the body, so too virgins possessing holiness in thought and action do not have a female body by necessity. In the Revelation of John, the one hundred and forty-four thousand virgins were not such things according to the body; for it was brought forth: 'These are they who were not defiled with a woman; for they are virgins, and there is no deceit in their mouth; for they are without blemish' (Rev 14:4). Concerning all those strolling in the streets of the highly-praised city, it is brought forward like a single dance in one of the Psalms: 'Young men and virgins, elders with the younger, let them praise the name of the Lord' (Ps 148:12). Concerning the various ages of the inner man, and whom Jesus loved, he writes to the disciple: 'I write to you, little children, that your sins are forgiven you through his name' (1 John 2:12)—that is, the Savior—'I write to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning; I write to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one' (1 John 2:13-14). He calls 'little children' those who have just received the forgiveness of sins, whatever age they might be according to the outer man; he names 'fathers' those who are expert in the theology from the beginning; and 'young men' those having strength, remaining unassailable with the word of the exhorting one remaining in them, even if the struggle be 'against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against the spiritual forces of wickedness' (Eph 6:12). For how can those who have received from the All-Ruler Savior 'authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy' (Luke 10:19) not be being harmed? For the same thing is: 'nothing shall harm you' (Mark 16:18), to: 'nothing shall afflict you.' Immediately, therefore, concerning the one having received authority to tread upon serpents and all the power of the enemy, a triumphal hymn is sent up according to the word having this: 'He shall mount upon an asp and a basilisk; he shall trample the lion and the dragon' (Ps 91:13). Having said enough regarding what is set forth explicitly, let us set forth the following.
Zachariah 8:6: Thus says the Lord of hosts: If it seems impossible in your eyes...
Will the remnant of this people not be able to remain even before me in those days? says the Lord Almighty (Zechariah 8:13).

Having undergone destruction by wars, the visible and lower Jerusalem—as its citizens underwent much captivity—was seen by those unfaithful to the promises concerning its restoration to be being abandoned, as they considered it impossible for it to be inhabited brilliantly again, as if it were to have inhabitants of the mountain and the plain, and to have elders and elder women still sitting in its squares, with boys and girls playing in them.

But since 'all things are possible to God' (Mark 10:27), and He leads from narrowness to breadth, and from hopelessness to abundance, even if there be added to the remnant of the people surrounding here many who have died, it is not impossible for God, which is appearing impossible to them.

Just as when the metropolis of Judea was being sacked and undergoing extreme desolation, men lacking the resurrection of the soul thought it impossible to restore it to its former glory and prosperity, even though God had promised and was able to bring the preordained things to an end, so also the unfaithful and the poor in mind, seeing the Church having been driven into a corner most wretchedly during the persecutions against Christians, as if an upright corpse had fallen, thought it impossible to be restored, enjoying a deep peace toward the peace of the known ones: 'My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you' (John 14:27).

Therefore, instilling courage in those to whom He will give, He promised stability and a calmed peace; 'Take courage,' He said, 'I have overcome the world' (John 16:33); therefore, even if you have tribulation now, take courage, for you are to expect relief. For truth is a friend.

Those who attacked the Church and Christianity were so incensed as to want to dash the gathering places to the ground and consume the sacred books with fire. After such brutality held out for a little while, the small-minded thought it impossible to recover it to glory again.

But even if to those it seemed hopeless and unmanageable what happened, it has been proven possible and even easy for the one who has not despaired. For one can indeed see the places once dashed down [restored] to height.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Universal Call and Wisdom
english: Having been raised up more glorious than they were before, adorned with gold and with all worldly splendors that are passing, and with books once consumed by fire being remade with gold and gold-leaf, lying in the royal courts.

It seems both possible and paradoxical of God that through those by whom Christianity labored and was illuminated—and by these I say, not men, but those exercising the same leadership. More complete things concerning these are said in the commentaries of the prophet Isaiah.

The word provides faith to expect those things that seem to be lost in despair, for the Lord of all said he would perform them. Zechariah says: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west, and I will bring them in and cause them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and they shall be my people and I will be to them a God in truth and in righteousness' (Zechariah 8:7-8).

Just as a man who worships and serves God is addressed as a man of God, so his people is the one being filled by those who are God-fearing according to their respective capacities. He becomes his people, whom he saves from all the inhabited world and its ends; he promises, saying: 'Behold, I save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west, says the Lord of hosts' (Zechariah 8:7). This is not only the one from circumcision, but belongs to all the nations who believe in the Savior according to the Gospel.

For in the past, only one nation, that of the Hebrews, was a part and a lot of the Creator, according to the testimony of the hierophant saying: 'When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam according to the number of the angels of God, there was made a part of the Lord Jacob, a portion of his inheritance Israel,' through beauty of character and life, according to the testimony brought forth by the saints in the forty-sixth Psalm: 'He chose for us his inheritance, he loved the beauty of Jacob' (Psalm 46:4).

Similarly, it is demonstratively announced in the Mosaic teaching: 'Behold, a wise and knowing people, this great nation,' being God-fearing and abstaining from sins, according to that which was said in the perfect Wisdom of Solomon: 'Because he who not...

Having a poorly-skilled soul and a body misused by sin, one receives God's wisdom and the appropriate sacred knowledge belonging to it. This agrees in thought with what was said by a God-fearing man concerning God, speaking to the true man: 'Behold, piety is wisdom, and to abstain from evils is knowledge.'

Along with this, the nations live with this wise and knowing one, existing as a 'royal priesthood, a people for tending,' and all the nations are rejoiced, the Savior having become for them a good hope, according to the blessing of the Savior rising out of Judah, which also what is in Isaiah has in this way: 'There shall be the root of Jesse, and the one rising to rule nations; upon him the nations shall hope' (Isaiah 11:10).

Concerning the simultaneous joy and delight of all men, it has been written: 'Rejoice, O nations, with his people' (Psalm 117:1), no longer of one single Hebrew nation, but of all at once worshiping and serving God according to what is announced in the Psalms, where: 'All the nations shall serve him' (Psalm 22:27); and where: 'All the nations, all those whom you have made, shall come and worship before you, and shall glorify your name, Lord' (Psalm 22:27). And again: 'The ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and the patriarchies of the nations shall worship before him, because the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he is ruler of the nations' (Psalm 72:17).

Concerning the calling of all men, both Jews and Greeks, as the one people set forth by the prophet clearly announces, the Lord of all saying: 'Behold, I save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west, says the Lord of all' (Isaiah 11:12). Concerning the dance being gathered from all the climates of the inhabited world, the Gospel signifies the Savior having said: 'Many shall come from the east and the west of the sun, and shall recline in the kingdom of the heavens with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob' (Matthew 8:11). In harmony with the calling from everywhere, in the forty-ninth Psalm, the singer of the seventy-first says: 'God, the Lord of gods, has spoken, and has called the earth from the rising of the sun even unto the west' (Psalm 71:19). But when did this calling occur, or when was 'the splendor of beauty from Zion' (Psalm 50:5) of him revealed, the fulfillment of another...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Entering the Mystical Court
english: Regarding the prophecy held here: 'The deliverer shall shine out from Zion,' or 'because of Zion,' as Paul, the speaker in Christ and vessel of election, writes. When, then, did the God of the gods call from the rising of the sun even unto the settings, having spoken? Or was it when the people of the circumcision were cast off, having denied the Great King Savior, saying, 'We have no king but Caesar' (Matt 27:25), and 'His blood be on us and on our children' (Matt 27:25)? For having crucified the Savior, they pushed Him away, and the worship according to shadow and letter reached an end, as he says to them, 'It is not my will in you, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands, because from the rising of the sun and the settings incense is brought to my name in every place, and a pure sacrifice.'

What, then, is the incense and the pure sacrifice being brought in every place for the sake of glorifying God? The composer addresses the great king, saying, 'Let my prayer be directed as incense before you, the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice' (Ps 141:2). For in the past, when the shadowy worship had a place, it was in Jerusalem, 'the place where it was necessary to worship,' and to send up prayer, and to perform sacrifice.

But now, the shining of this true light having occurred and having enlightened the whole cosmos (John 1:9), the interpreted incense is brought in every place, and the sacrifice harmonious to it, with prayer-houses having been eagerly raised throughout the whole earth, so that the name of God might be glorified among all the nations, both the eastern and the western. According to another understanding, they glorify God in whom the sun of righteousness has risen (Mal 4:2), and in whom the light of the ungodly has set, concerning which it is brought forth in Proverbs: 'The light of the ungodly shall be quenched' (Prov 13:9). When this occurs, the Lord of All restores his people from the land of the risings and from the settings, in order that he might bring in the nations, not allowing them to remain outside like the crowds who hear the word in parables (Matt 13:10-15), so that...

Having entered into the mystical and spiritual court of Jesus, they become listeners to the clarity and knowledge of the parables, as the initiator says to them: 'To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven' (Matt 13:11).

Just as one existing outside, not in a place but in an external disposition, hears words, likewise the listener of the old covenant according to the letter and the shadow is to blame; for it is said concerning such ones who hear the law having been veiled: 'They read the law outside, and they called for confessions' (Lev 16:15), not reading the teaching of the life-giving Spirit while approaching.

This exceeds what is requested by a prayer sent back such as this: 'Open my eyes, and I will understand the wonders of yours out of your law' (Ps 119:18). That which is worthy of having the veil removed is the obscurity of the things read and the ignorance lying upon the intellect of the one encountering them as if it were not fitting. For there is a way to learn scientifically about these things from the writing Apostle: 'For until the present day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies upon the reading. But whenever he turns to the Lord, the veil is removed; and the Lord is the Spirit' (2 Cor 3:14-16).

What will exist, being granted by God, when the nations are brought in in the said manner, or when the Lord dwells in Jerusalem, the temple in it being filled with the glory of the Lord God Almighty in truth and in righteousness; for not only there with the truth, but also in other writings is righteousness remembered; for indeed in the fourteenth Psalm, 'that one walking blameless to work righteousness' is said, 'and to speak truth in his heart' (Ps 15:2). And in another Psalm: 'Mercy and truth met, righteousness and peace kissed; truth rose up from the earth, righteousness shone down from heaven' (Ps 85:10-11). And observe whether the truth [is] the mystical and opened contemplation of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Building of the House and Temple
english: It shows the dogmas of piety, the moral and practical virtue called justice, having a longing for salvation according to what was said about it: 'Learn to do justice, you who dwell upon the earth' (Ps 30:15).

What remains to be contemplated regarding the mentioned virtues? Mercy meets with truth, 'justice and peace have kissed' (Ps 85:10). For since the truth of God is great and has been lifted up, it is necessary that mercy be granted from the God who is the source of goodness, so that it may exist for men. But also justice, dissolving all injustice, the mother of all stability and of all war being averted, proclaims peace and harmony. Someone has also said that among the wise of men, peace and justice have harmony with themselves; for among all those justly pursuing the right, if it should happen so, every uprising and enmity will be driven out, as when peace prevails, equality and justice reign.

Having these things thus, the Almighty Lord is of truth and justice. For it has been said in the thirtieth Psalm, by him having the Lord as hope according to the beginning of the song: 'Deliver me, Lord God of truth' (Ps 30:2); and in the fourth Psalm: 'In calling upon me you heard me, O God of my justice' (Ps 4:12). It is in harmony with God being truth and knowledge, as the blessed mother of the holy Samuel said: 'Let not arrogance come out of your mouth, for God is a Lord of knowledge' (1 Sam 1:7). When we strive to enrich a people through good works and through true and pious knowledge of God, the Victorious One will also be our God, being made our own in truth and in justice.

Zach. VIII, 9: Thus says the Lord of hosts: 'Let your hands be strengthened, you who hear these words from the mouth of the prophets, from the day that the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, and the temple from which it was built.' The Almighty Lord commands the hands of the people lying down before the Lord of hosts to be strengthened, according to the words of the Lord God of hosts, from whom his house was founded, in the present days, from which the temple was built. And those are strengthened with piety and holiness of truth, according to the words...
Regarding what was said from the mouth of the prophets, from which the house of the Lord is founded and the holy temple is built.

Hands prevail in words when moral teachings are converted into works. For only then do the active hands of the soul convert into energy, when works with virtue happen to be woven together with the words, for those hearing, being not only hearers of law but also doers of work.

When, indeed, these things are practiced with sincerity and godliness, or when the people of God act and think with the word of piety, the divine house being founded and the temple being built according to the present days. The house of the Lord is being founded and the temple is being built, the fulfillment of that said in Proverbs: 'Wisdom built a house for herself, and raised up seven pillars' (Prov 9:1). Concerning this house and temple, the Lord who became man says to the Father: 'But a body I will complete for me.' Since the foundations of the house thus exist as if a holy temple having been built, the hands—that is, the practical powers—prevail according to the preceding luminous theories, called days.

Know if the glorious Church, about which the Apostle writes to Timothy his own disciple, happens to be a house founded and a temple built: 'But if I delay, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Tim 3:15). This is also submitted to the mind by the prophetic voice of Isaiah having it thus: 'He who says, Jerusalem: It shall be built, and I will found my holy house' (Isa 22:28). When, however, will this be, or when all those having adhered to the gospel will 'be built up on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ himself being the cornerstone, into a holy temple in the Lord, into a dwelling place' (Eph 2:20-22)?

In view of the things seen, and for each of the god-fearing, the house is being founded and the temple is being built, according to the testimony of Christ declaring: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come, I and the Father, and we will make a dwelling with him' (John 14:23). The hands of the disciples of Christ prevail, doing what...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Futility of Labor Without Reason
english: The Gospel proclaims that the Savior has fulfilled the law and the prophets, from which point the house was founded and the temple was built, upon the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the most holy Virgin Mary, the power of the Most High having overshadowed her. For then truly the words of the prophets before [us] were fulfilled, having reached the outcome which was decreed.

How then do the hands of those hearing the words of the prophets not grow strong, when there is born from the virgin her whose name shall be called 'God with us' (Matt 1:23)? For when the Lord is with us, our hands at once grow strong as if to shout in praise: 'The Lord of hosts is with us, our God is the help of Jacob' (Ps 80:17).

For having received the one who fans away evil, that is, Jacob, having acquired the surpassing strength of God Almighty, let us shout in triumph: 'God is with us. Know, O nations, and be humbled; listen, even to the ends of the earth. For if you are strong, you shall be humbled again, and any word you shall speak shall not remain with you, because the Lord God is with us.' When will these achievements be, either when our hands grow strong, the house having been founded and the temple having been built, according to all the interpretations rendered of the existing prophetic utterance?

Because before those days the wages of men shall not be for profit, and the wages of cattle shall not exist, and to the one going out and the one coming in there shall not be peace from oppression; and I will send all men, each one to his neighbor (Zech 8:10).

Having foretold many things concerning the coming glorious restoration to the benefited people and the rising of holy Jerusalem, the holy house being founded upon it and the temple being built for the benefit and joy of the people, whose hands grow strong in the prophetic words, before the days of the promise, when the city was laid waste, held by those who had captured it, the wages of men by no means had profit, vainly striving and acting without purpose.
Regarding the vain striving of men, and the wages of cattle not existing, not for something profitable, that is, striving or...

While they are toiling, having the wage of men as a burden and the wage of cattle not existing, when the house is being founded and the temple is being built; for only then is there peace from affliction for the one coming in and the one going out, I say, from the drawing up of sweat and toil for the sake of improvement and the end of those striving.

He said: there is by no means peace from affliction for the one coming in and the one going out, the work of men and cattle being useless and unprofitable; the wage of rational mortal animals shall be in vain and the wage of cattle shall not exist, as men rise up against each other, all stability and harmony having been fled due to the ferocity and wildness of hatred existing from passion and without moderation.

The word says: it is for the purpose of bringing back to reason men, because they seem to use reason while toiling and striving in vain, not to have the wage as a burden, but also not having the wage of those who are more beast-like through habit, from whom he forbids irrationality, and [commands] habit and [forbids] wildness: 'Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding' (Psalm 32:9).

For how can there be a wage for those not having understanding, doing all things with irrationality? Even if some men seem to be doing all things with bad skill, working without pay and uselessly, they do not have a profitable wage, because of 'wisdom not entering into their bad-skilled soul, nor dwelling in the body of sin which uses things wrongly,' having the wage of toil for that which is above virtue and piety.

For the soul that is acting, 'which remains for eternal life as food' and turns the holy commandments into works, the 'paymaster' God says: 'There is a wage for your works' (1 Cor 3:8). Equally with this comparison, concerning the unseemly workers, the Apostle Paul in Christ writes: 'Each one will receive his own wage according to his own work' (Rom 2:6).
Know precisely if only those things given for praiseworthy works are called a wage, as opposed to the punishments preferred for sins, which are named [punishments] but not wages.
What then will be added to the wage of men being a burden, and the wage of cattle not existing, or that peace from affliction shall not be?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Restoration of Peace and Prosperity
english: Of the one going out and coming in, of men being sent against one another, while he rules peacefully, 'each against his neighbor,' always killing and troubling one another. The hymnodist describes such a wild state in Psalm 11: 'Each spoke in vain in his heart; deceitful lips in heart, and in their heart they spoke.' Similarly, Jeremiah says concerning those lying in wait against one another: 'Do not trust in friends, and upon brothers do not rely, for every brother flutters and every friend will act deceitfully; they will not speak truth, their tongue has learned to speak lies.' Concerning such things also the psalmist David cries out: 'To me they spoke peaceful things, but in themselves they deliberate words of wrath.' And the prophet again says: 'He speaks peaceful things to his neighbor, and in himself he holds enmity,' making the treacherous and deceptive man manifest.

Of those striving thus and doing 'the works of the flesh' (Galatians 5:19), even if they seem to be men, the reward will not be to beasts, nor will the reward of the more beast-like exist. Cattle are to be rebuked in these things, the lovers of pleasure and lovers of passion, but men who profess the pseudonymous knowledge and 'the wisdom of this age and of its rulers' (1 Corinthians 1:20), having no profitable reward, are to be destroyed and not remain after this age and the life according to it. For when the light of the true one appears in the coming age, every deception having sophistry and irrational pleasure will be dissolved, so that their reward, which until now seemed to be, will no longer have or be to beasts, the one going out and coming in having no peace at all from the exhausting tribulation, each man being sent against his neighbor, so as to pursue and harm him.

And now I do not do according to the days that are before for the remnant of this people, says the Lord of all, but I will show peace; the vine will give its fruit and the earth will give its generations and the heaven will give its dew, and I will bequeath all these things to the remnant of my people (Zechariah 8:10-12). Having flowed into blessing, the cause of all good things promises no longer to do...

He says to those left of the people, as in the former days when the enemies ruled, having survived those whom they had captured, that he grants peace, and there will be prosperity and abundance, with the vine-bearing plants bearing much fruit, and the earth producing generations in abundance, and the sky giving dew, as God will inherit all things for the survivors of this people.

As a spoken word, the preceding things were promised at the time of the return of the captives, according to which the well-off, giving thanks, said: 'When the Lord turned the captivity of Zion, we became like those who are encouraged' (Psalm 126:1), when God no longer does to the survivors of the chosen people what happened in the former days when Jerusalem was desolate, but instead provides the peace of God, for which they sent up a prayer saying: 'Lord our God, give us peace.'

But the things of the bright restoration have surpassed [this] intellectually when he came, the one saying: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to preach to the poor, he has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, to heal the crushed in heart' (Luke 4:18). The same is promised also in the prophet Amos, saying: 'I will restore the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall build the ruined cities and replant them' (Amos 9:14-15).

Of these graces and gifts given by the Magnanimous, there will be peace, having risen with righteousness, in the days of the visitation of the one receiving from God the judgment of a king, concerning whom it is said: 'Justice and an abundance of peace shall rise in his days' (Micah 5:4), so that his peace shall have no limit, since it is not for one nation but for all the nations and the whole inhabited world being ruled by him, having spoken to those known to him and those wishing to serve under him: 'My peace I give to you,' he said, with much tranquility prevailing; and not doing [only] what happened in the former days to the survivors of Israel, he will prepare an exceeding abundance, giving the fruit of the vine and the native generations of the earth, and the appropriate dew of the sky.
But the spiritual theory of the truth is a vine of the soil of its own fruit, and that which...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Heavenly Dew
english: A perfected rational essence, having come forth from the true vine by the manner of participation. Concerning this leading, the Savior said in the Gospel: 'I am the vine, you are the branches; every branch remaining in me, the Father prunes it, so that it may bear more fruit' (John 15:1, 2).

Regarding these branches having the beginning of fruitfulness, it is written in the Song of Songs: 'Our vines are flourishing, they have given fragrance' (Song of Solomon 1:12). And the fruit, having progressed and having come to perfection, is harvested, and being cast into the winepress, it is crushed, and becomes a drink that gladdens the heart of the drinker, according to that said in the Psalms: 'Wine gladdens the heart of man' (Psalm 104:15).

Concerning the spiritual harvest, superlative songs have been written, such as the eighth, and the eighty-eighth, and the thirty-eighth; for these alone are the three Psalms from the hundred and fifty that were inscribed 'for the festivals.'

Harmoniously, according to the ascent, the given vine will yield its fruit and the earth will give its generations, having brought to fruition that which Jesus cast as seed upon it, to give a hundred, sixty, thirty, according to the interpretation of the parable; for the Savior interpreted the good and straight heart as a good earth (Matthew 13:8).

And these generations of the earth are given to the one sowing in tears, that is, with sweat and toil, the divine seeds, so that he may reap them in joy. For concerning these ones sowing, not in a sensible way but in an intellectual way, it is carried in a certain Psalm of the ascents: 'Those sowing in tears shall reap in joy; walking, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; coming, they shall arrive in joy, carrying their sheaves' (Psalm 126:5-6).

Concerning such straightness, being spiritual, the divine word exhorts in the prophet Hosea: 'Sow for yourselves unto righteousness, reap unto the fruit of life, light for yourselves the light of knowledge, seek the Lord until he comes...'

"...the offspring of righteousness." The vine gives its edible and fruit-bearing fruit and its offspring to the good earth, because heaven has given its dew. Let us consider what this dew is, knowing that the one giving it is heaven, which is perhaps not other than the man bearing "the image of the heavenly [one]" (Col 3:10), having "his citizenship in heaven" (Phil 3:20).

Concerning all those being formed according to the heavenly Savior, it is said in the plural in Psalm 18: "The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands." Concerning these things also, it is written in a great song in Deuteronomy: "Rejoice, O heavens, together with him" (Deut 32:1), making the Savior manifest. For how have they not rejoiced together and exulted, having been formed according to him, according to the teachings of the holy Apostle Paul, where he writes concerning those faithfully and sincerely God-fearing: "Whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Rom 8:29); and where: "Let us bear the image of the heavenly [one]" (Col 3:10).

Those having excelled in moral virtue and intellectual [virtue], "having been completed by the same mind and the same judgment" (Phil 2:2), must be said to have one heaven by agreement, giving spiritual dew. But also each of such people gives his own dew, similarly to the holy priest Moses saying: "Let my word be expected like rain, and let my words descend like dew" (Hos 14:5).

However, even if it is given by the interpreted heavens, it is first of all provided by the Master of the heavens, according to the divine voice of Isaiah having this: "The dead shall arise, and those in the tombs shall stand up, and those on the earth shall rejoice; for the dew from you shall be a healing to them" (Isa 26:19). And since concerning the intellectual dew, it being medicinal, those on the earth who happen to partake of it rejoice, and [it is for] the rising dead and those coming out of the tombs to partake of it.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Purpose and Human Responsibility
english: It must be said, especially when the perfect has come, that since one confronts face to face with the truth, seeing in part and through a mirror will have ceased, because the seeing of what is most full will have prevailed.

Regarding how this path is assigned, the blessing of Isaac upon Jacob is invoked, from which it begins: 'From the dew of heaven and the heaviness of the earth.' All that existed was given to the redeemed people from Babylon, as God's inheritance.

And since it is said passively that God will inherit all things for the remnant of the people—namely the fruit of the vine, the generations of the earth, and the dew of heaven—both ways it must be invoked, actively and passively.

Actively, it is said thus: Israel is a portion and an inheritance of God, through nothing other than virtues that approached, being chosen and done and seen voluntarily. The same thought holds for: 'Ask of me, and I will give you nations for your inheritance' (Ps 2:8), regarding all men inheriting from the Savior through pious faith and works of virtue.

If 'to inherit' signifies a passion [passive reception] by the falling verb, the understanding will be this: God will inherit all the aforementioned things, giving them in the manner of an inheritance to the remnant of his people, who are those saying according to the prophet Isaiah: 'Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a remnant, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah' (Isa 1:9). And with others: 'If the number of the sons of Israel were as the sand by the brim of the sea, the remnant shall be saved' (Isa 17:10). Having received these prophetic voices, the Apostle brings them forward saying thus: 'And in the present time there is a remnant according to the election of grace, not of works, for if it were of works, grace would no longer be grace' (Rom 11:5).

Having made clear what is possible for us regarding the present saying, we set forth the following. Zechariah 8:13: And just as you were a curse among the nations, the house of Judah and the house of Israel, so I will save you and you shall be in blessing.

Be courageous and strengthen your hearts. For the Lord of all says: 'In the way I intended to harm you by provoking your fathers,' says the Lord of all, 'and I did not repent; so I am now set out and intend in these days to do well for Jerusalem and the house of Judah' (Jeremiah 32:19).

To fall into afflictions and curses comes from nothing other than sin and impiety, since blessing is given by God to the righteous because of what they do and think rightly. For humans being self-determining, having free and autonomous choice, they do to themselves either punishments or the bringing of divine promises. Therefore, the way in which they undergo curses is the same way in which they undergo prosperity and blessing.

Immediately, indeed, He says He is the cause of all good for Judah and Israel: 'Since your fathers were impious and lawless, as to provoke me against them, I did not repent, but I brought what was likely for those who provoked to suffer; so now I am set out and intended to save those of Judah and Israel, and I did not repent' (Jeremiah 32:19).
And it is possible to bring forth testimony from these God-breathed writings.

The inhabitants of Nineveh once sinned and were impiously excessive, as the cry of their evil rose to God requiring punishment, as to say to the Provider and Judge of all: 'In three more days, Nineveh shall be overturned' (Jonah 3:4). Having learned this, the guilty ones, following the path of the one who threatened toward repentance, arrived at a state to confess and to do what would undo the preceding evil. Thus, those having changed their minds, the one who had pre-proclaimed the harm against them repented, receiving the cause of blessing; this did not happen regarding the Sodomites, because of the remaining impiety and sins of theirs, even though the merciful God wished to find a starting point for well-doing among them.
For He says: 'The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has filled [heaven], and their sins are exceedingly great. I will indeed go down to see if according to their evil, which has risen to me...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between knowing and understanding
english: They are completed; but if not, 'that they may know', he is not merely saying: Having been called out by the cry of great sins, I descend along with them so that the great sins might be found being practiced still, being completed by having fallen under the previously proclaimed punishment; but if they were found lying moderately as those who thought impiously and regarding the forbidden works, let him know them as ours, according to it having been written: 'The Lord knew those who were his, and let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from injustice' (2 Tim 2:19).

In this way of thought the vessel of election Paul writes to the Galatians: 'But once you did not know God, you were serving gods which are not gods by nature; but now having known God, rather having been known by God' (Gal 4:9). For he knows those knowing him, not taking the beginning of knowing them, but of examining them as knowing those having been foreknown, in no way regarding the worthless ones still adhering to wickedness when this is happening.

For it is said by the Savior to those remaining in evils until the time of the completion of the world and the manifestation of the judge of all things, of him being made manifest: 'Depart from me, workers of lawlessness; I never knew you' (Matt 7:23), that is, you never had an experience or a participation of me, nor I of you. For if he took to knowing by what is at hand, it would be the same as knowing; how did he know them as being workers of lawlessness?

Therefore, from the double [nature] of knowing and of not being carried along in the God-breathed writings, according to the other thing, the God who knows hearts knows all, both the righteous and the sinners; immediately, therefore, when the one coming 'sits upon the throne of his glory' to 'judge' kings 'living and dead' (Matt 25:31), he will separate the righteous from the sinners, so that he may lead those participating in righteousness and piety into the kingdom in order to inherit it, but the unrighteous and the wicked, not having loved the neighbor as themselves, he will send to punishment, saying: 'Depart, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire, prepared for the devil and his angels' (Matt 25:41). According to the manner

It is not about understanding, as he says to certain people: 'the knower of hidden things' and 'knowing the mind of all'; 'I have known that you have many sins.' Similarly in the Gospel: 'You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts, because that which is in man, when exalted, is an abomination to God' (Luke 6:46).

According to this theory, we must also understand what is continuously stated in the Gospel: 'But Jesus, having known their thoughts' (Mark 2:8), meaning they had happened to be [thinking] something; for they were staying [in thought] craftily and wickedly, thinking that 'the one knowing the mind of all' would remain hidden.

Just as knowing is according to understanding, against which ignorance is opposed, so also it is possible to know and not to know through experience. For if Paul writes about the Savior as 'did not know sin' (referring to the lack of experiential sin), we take the written thing to be equal to: the one not having experienced sin practically or intellectually. Understanding it as much as is in his power and by what kind of choice it is accomplished, and how he has come to it from the world.

This difference also extends to men; for it is said in Ecclesiastes: 'He who keeps the commandment will not know an evil word' (Eccl 7:29), that is, he will not set himself toward an evil word, the evil word being known by knowledge to the one guarding the divine commandment, which is the word of God; for since there is one knowledge of opposites, he who knows the good word also understands its opposite.

The Scripture announces the duality of knowing also concerning Adam, where on one hand it says he understood what the essence of the woman was—for after giving her after the shaping of the Creator, Adam said: 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman' (Gen 2:23)—and later, having known her according to the manner of experience; for it is written: 'Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain' (Gen 4:1). And this is brought about for every man living with a wife, in habitual conversation and in divine instruction.
Immediately also concerning the father of the prophet Samuel...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Certainty of Divine Promises
english: It is written: 'And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and he conceived, and she bore Samuel' (1 Sam 1:20). Regarding this, the meaning is said concerning Rebekah: 'She was a virgin, and a man had not known her' (Gen 24:67). And the virgin Mary, the unwedded one, having heard about the conception of a child from the great angel Gabriel, said: 'How can this be to me, since I do not know a man?' (Luke 1:34).

We consider that the present prophecy has not been bypassed in vain; for this has risen to clarity because of the unclearly spoken thus: 'I will come down so that I may see if they are complying according to their cry that is coming; but if not, so that I may know.' For it was necessary to reveal by what meaning it was said by God: 'So that I may know.'

God did not repent, having thought to punish and to expose the insolent upon something, remaining in the judgment against them; but from what source He repented, to see the opportunity in innate goodness.

Not having known [His intent] to bless Judah and Israel, [He waited for] their remaining in the virtue with which they took up [their task] from the exhortation of God and of His law; for it is said in one of the Psalms: 'He will give blessing to the lawgiver' (Ps 112:3), that is, to those guarding His divine law. Equally, it is brought forth in another Psalm, beginning from here: 'Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place? He who is innocent in hands and pure in heart, who has not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbor. This one shall receive blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Savior' (Ps 15:4).

For having been said spiritually: 'Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place?' an answer is given, delineating who is and what kind of person is the one about whom the question is, that [he is] by hands, that is to say, by action, innocent through purity of heart, not at all having taken his soul in vain, or deceitfully swearing to his neighbor, receiving upon these manly deeds both blessing and mercy from God his Savior. In agreement, it is also brought forth in Proverbs: 'Blessing...'

"...for the Lord upon the head of the righteous." The one who has grasped these saving things will not fall away from the promise, being led into the divine promises by the one saying: 'I have set to bless Judah and Israel, and I have not repented' (Zech 8:8). He remains by his grace so as to do well and to lead into eternal salvation those for whom he has not repented, confirming what he promised: even if your fathers provoked him through sin and impiety, and a curse spoke, he did not repent of the threat, nor did he grant you reconciliation from the evil you had through recognition, but therefore both now let your heart be courageous to expect the gifts from me.

For they shall certainly be of my willing and having set to bless you; for it shall be well with you, as you belong to Judah, the one confessing, and to Israel and Jerusalem. 'For wanting to save all men and to come into the knowledge of truth' (1 Tim 2:4), I threaten, I lash those opposing the knowing of the truth of the super-arrogant salvation, subjecting to a little pain those whom I want to improve and to do well. For thus, having been easily benefited, they shall be saved, my having set without regret to save and to do well those whom I have chosen, so that they may be part of and my inheritance.

If we also wish to have God in a propitiatory relation so that he may dispose well toward us, let our intellect, called the heart, be courageous, having made care for excellent works, so that the things of well-being and endless salvation may exist certainly and irrefutably, having been described and having been made manifest from all things, the curse which held on for a little. Therefore be courageous without doubt, expecting what the truthful God promised; for he having said: 'Be courageous' (Zech 13:7), without doubt the hoped-for good things are to be received.

Having sufficiently described the second volume concerning the prophet Zechariah, at which let us rest, beginning the third discourse, 'providing a word in the opening of the mouth' of God, who also enlightened the prophet with the eternal light.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Necessity of Practicing Moral Teachings
english: The truthful God, being the source and father of truth, never ceases from training and teaching those who have presented themselves ready to receive the gifts of the Holy Spirit. For he provides a word of wisdom and a word of knowledge without hesitation to those desiring to receive; for it is said in the epistle of James: 'If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from the giving God who does not reproach; and let him ask in faith, not doubting.' (James 1:5).

The proverbial saying agrees, having thus: 'The Lord gives wisdom and from his face knowledge and understanding.' (Proverbs 2:6). The wise man, proving wisdom according to the fifth [level], is thrice-blessed, having as teacher the God of all things; 'For blessed, he says, is the man whom you may train, Lord, and from your law teach him.' (Psalm 25:12). This training they have been placed to have, in whom the Lord and Savior said: 'You call me: the Lord and the Teacher, and you speak well; for I am.' (John 15:15).

This gift also exists for us through the unceasing prayer of those who offer up [prayers] on our behalf, wisdom and 'a word in the opening of the mouth,' so that without hesitation and as is necessary to receive the following from the present prophet, beginning from here.

These are the words which you shall do: each one speak truth to his neighbor and judge a peaceful judgment in your gates. And let no one reckon the evil of his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for I have hated all these things, says the Lord of all (Zechariah 8:16-17).

Of the words of God, those concerning moral and practical virtue are able to be put into practice, those having the contemplative and initiatory aspect to be viewed among the initiatory and discerning men.

For God, having commanded many things through the hierophant Moses so that works according to virtue might happen, those understanding the given words loudly confessed to pass over into the works that were given.
Having been told, they said to the deacon of divine blessings: 'All things which God has said we will do and we will listen.'

3.7 Since it is proper that moral words have a connection to doing and to having a thought of them, so that justly the just may be pursued, and soberly the sober, and bravely and prudently the brave and prudent things—for in this way practical virtues might be raised up along with thought—it is therefore necessary to not neglect listening to and doing the words of Jesus, him himself forbidding this: 'The one coming to me and listening to my words and doing them will be made like a prudent man' (Matt 7:24), and the following.

3.8 Then especially the words have the capacity to happen among the hearers when the teacher does what he tells others; concerning such a thing the Lord says: 'Whoever does and teaches men, this one will be called great in the kingdom of heaven' (Matt 5:19), the one not doing what he exhorts others to do being of the least, since he, while saying not to commit adultery, is seized by this very thing, and while forbidding theft, he also sacrileges the idols, being loathing them.

3.9 Or does not he who harms through scandal those who have dedicated themselves to godliness by breathing life into divine statues commit sacrilege? For he who harms such people will act with his hand and truly sacrileges through impious thoughts by transgressing the law in which he seems to boast, dishonoring God. If, therefore, no one is an evil teacher, let what he teaches moral lessons be shown in works; for in this way he will be an 'unashamed worker' (2 Tim 2:15).

3.10 With this opinion the Apostle writes to his own disciple 'to have incorruption, dignity, a healthy word, unsearchable' (2 Tim 2:15). Or does he not have a healthy, unsearchable word? For doing what he dictates to others and thinking what he prepares others to be praised for, he has a healthy, unsearchable word of the teaching.
3.11 Of this life, the practical and the cognitive, I say, the true healer of God intends to transform the following to the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Truthfulness and the Gates of Judgment
english: Since a prophet is at hand, named Malachi; and his word has it thus: 'The lips of a priest shall guard knowledge, and they shall seek law from his mouth,' [Malachi 2:7] desiring to learn from a divine teacher what must be known: orthodox doctrines and mysteries of the kingdom, and a law forbidding injustices and protecting the teachings of virtues.

3.12 Having learned what kind of words become practical for those to whom they belong, let us understand what kind of words possess knowledge and truth. 3.13 Moses teaching that 'In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth,' [Genesis 1:1] said this word so that we might truly know the creation and its Creator; and whatever other words of the Cosmogeny were written, they were said not so that we might do [them], but so that we might contemplate them; and upon every inspired scripture this instruction has prevailed. 3.14 And the Savior himself, in the Gospels, in some places commands those things which must be done, and in others hands down those which it is proper to know and contemplate. For that which is said by him: 'Learn from me, for gentle I am and humble in heart, and you shall find rest for your souls' [Matthew 11:29]; and again: 'If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me each day' [Matthew 16:24], are said for the sake of doing, as also that: 'Have mercy, and you shall be shown mercy' [Luke 6:36], and as many other commands of his same power. 3.15 But that: 'I am in the Father, and the Father is in me' [John 14:10], and that: 'I and the Father are one' [John 10:30], and also: 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' [John 14:9], and as many other things which are theologized in both Testaments, were spoken and written so as to be contemplated and to have true and pious knowledge. 3.16 The Holy Spirit showed which words must be done, and each one declares [this] individually and according to its kind. For that: 'Let each one speak truth to his neighbor' [Ephesians 4:25], is written so that it may be practiced in this way.
