Paul in Christ, clarifying this, exhorts the believers to the keeping of the commandment, saying most clearly: 'Having put away falsehood, let each one speak truth to his neighbor' [Ephesians 4:25]. 3.17 And before the Apostle, the Savior also handed down the speaking without law, saying: 'But I say to you, do not at all swear, but let your yes be yes, and your no, no' [Matthew 5:34-37].
This is most strictly guarded by each person speaking the truth to their neighbor; for in this way every false word and oath will destroy that most precise and perfect brotherly love.

If each person speaks the truth to his neighbor, a peaceful judgment will occur, without those striving to covet and do wrong still causing dissension. For how can they think that conflicts and injustices are still being raised, if each one announces the truth to his neighbor? The peaceful judgment is the same as the righteous judgment, concerning which much discussion has occurred previously.

Such a judgment is spoken of not only here, but also in other writings, to be fulfilled in the gates of the Hebrews. For it was said by another prophet: 'They hated me in the gates while rebuking, and they detested a holy word,' (Ps 5:5) as the ungodly make manifest. For regarding them, the proverbial ordinance forbids: 'Do not rebuke the evil, lest they hate you' (Prov 9:8). For they detest the holy word, and the one who performs this first offering does not have wisdom; rather, he loves the one who rebukes and the one who makes known what must not be practiced, so that the one hastening to be righteous may do so.

And since they always hate those who have believed in rebuking in the gates, the word promises to restore in the gates a judgment for the good and the useful, through a change occurring. If anyone were to seek for what reason the judgments and rebukes were performed not in some other place or part of the city, but in its gates, it is because what is to be spoken honorably and convincingly—since through the gate is the exit from the city and the entrance into it—it is fitting that the judges sit there to examine the lives of the citizens, so that they might easily cast out those being rebuked for what they are accused of, while those having a pure citizenship, once their state has been made manifest by the rebukes, remain within, and the city becomes even more inward.

Raised to the intellect, those having received from Jesus 'the keys of the kingdom of heaven' (Matt 16:19) are worthy of the presidency and the seat of judging, so that they might cast out those who have fallen worthy of being bound, but those not gripped by the bonds of sin, but being strengthened in them, they might lead in. Then most especially the peaceful judgment is fulfilled, when 'each one does not count the evil of his neighbor' (Rom 13:10), through an absolute forgetting of wrongs.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fasts of the House of Judah
english: harmful treatment

Acting. 3.31 Zechariah 8:18-19: 'And there came a word of the Lord of Hosts to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of Hosts: The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah for joy and for gladness and for good feasts; and you shall love truth and peace.'

3.32 The word of the Lord of Hosts having come to me, says the prophet, commanded to fast on the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth [of the month], making the month evident; for it is not possible for a tenth to be a Sabbath, as we previously noted. And it is indeed likely that the Lord of Hosts commands these things regarding the Hebrew month, in which the so-called day of atonement and humiliation is fulfilled, which the Jews observe as a public fast, having purified themselves during the fourth, fifth, and seventh [fasts] before coming to the public fast.

3.33 In what way and how fasting is conducted according to divine law was made clear in what preceded; regarding those things it must also be said now that just as one must turn away from sensual luxury, so too from allegorically harmful and poisonous foods. For those who have confessed, called the house of Judah, will receive joy, gladness, and good feasts as a well-being, celebrating them by thinking and doing what is necessary, according to what is said in the Psalms: 'A voice of joy and confession, the sound of those celebrating' (Psalm 47:1); and again: 'Establish a feast among those crowding to the horns of the altar' (Psalm 67:5). This is confirmed by what is announced in another psalm: 'A man's remembrance shall confess to you, and the remnant of a remembrance shall celebrate for you' (Psalm 42:5).

3.34 Good feasts are fulfilled when the spiritual Jerusalem lives peacefully, being a vision of peace, not when the feasts occur propitiatorily while enemies prevail. For when things are thus, God says: 'I have hated, I have despised your feasts, and I will not be fragrant in your assemblies' (Amos 5:21). And even further threatening: 'I will turn,' He says, 'your feasts into mourning and your songs into lamentations' (Amos 8:10).
3.35 May these painful things perish from the fellowship of the faithful, so that, having been called into joy and gladness, they may celebrate good feasts.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Restoration of Worship and the Vision of God
english: We perform a divine festival, loving deep peace and with it the truth. For where there is tranquility of thoughts and a settled state of soul, the delight and beauty of truth appears. Truth is seen most when serenity leads through the following of virtues and peace presides, with those having attained such well-being rejoicing and being propitious.

It is reasonable to ask from where we estimated the seventh month according to the Hebrews, in which the four [days] and the others were arranged to be fasts until the tenth day, or from what is written at the end of the prophecy of Zechariah set out for examination: 'And you shall celebrate the feast of the tabernacles' (Zechariah 8:23); for this is lawfully performed not in any month other than the one mentioned, just as the [feast] of trumpets and the fast [are]. For it is clearly learned from the Psalm that even the new moon of the seventh month is a festival of celebration, having it thus: 'Sound a trumpet at the new moon, on a day of solemnity, our feast' (Psalm 81:3).

The Lord of Hosts says these things: 'Yet many nations and many people dwelling in many cities shall come, and they shall gather, dwelling in many cities, into one city, saying, Let us go up to entreat the face of the Lord and to seek the face of the Lord of Hosts; I also will go. And many nations and many peoples shall come to seek the face of the Lord of Hosts in Jerusalem, and to seek the atonement of the face of the Lord' (Zechariah 8:22-23).

As the prophet explicitly announces, following the word of the Lord of Hosts having come to him, the coming restoration shall be propitious and festive for the multitude of the Hebrews, for the cities of Judah, and for the mother-city, Jerusalem. God commanded through Moses all Israel to celebrate three days of the year to Him in the place from which He brought them out, which was not any other than Jerusalem, from which it happened to hasten immediately from all the cities and villages of Judah to the mother-city, in which all sanctities and important mystical festivals were performed, all of which reached an end in the time of the captivity, outside of the nourishment of almost all the Hebrews.
This most wretched and miserable...

The prophet Jeremiah, being utterly devastated, says in the book of Lamentations: 'The ways of Zion mourn because no one comes to the festival; all her gates are destroyed, and her priests groan' (Lam 1:4-5). For how could the ways of Zion not mourn, having been deprived of those walking, with no one still hurrying for the sake of celebrating and making a festival in Jerusalem, and the gates being destroyed, torn away by those who seized them tyrannically?

In this desolation, the priests necessarily followed with groaning, seeing the time when God, whom He chose, was being treated without all pleasing readiness. These unpleasant things cease to be, as Zechariah says before pronouncing it: 'Many peoples shall still come' (Zech 8:23), making it clear regarding Jerusalem; for the seventieth year of the captivity is already entering, as we learned clearly from Him saying to God: 'How long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, this seventieth year?' (Jer 29:70).

Immediately after the Lord of Hosts has relented, the peaceful leading of Jerusalem is revealed to the one who prayed, such that, just as before, many peoples will come seeking the face of the Lord of Hosts, beginning again the words: 'Three times in the year all your males shall appear before me' (Zech 8:23), and 'Nothing shall be absent before the Lord your God' (Zech 14:23), meaning bringing sacrifices for the liturgy and other gifts and the festive offerings.

For such a diligent holy assembly, an appropriate end exists: to seek the appearance of the Lord of Hosts through litanies and holy prayers, Him looking and revealing Himself to the one who is lucid in mind and partaking of holiness, according to what was said in the beatitudes by the Savior: 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God' (Matt 5:8). In agreement with this thought, the lawgiver Paul writes to the Hebrews to 'pursue peace and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord' (Heb 12:14), appearing to those who do not disbelieve in Him and shining forth to those who keep His commandments.
In the Wisdom of Solomon, such a word is brought: 'Think about the Lord in...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Seeking the Lord through Sincerity
english: Seek him with goodness and simplicity of heart, for he draws near to those who do not test him and reveals himself to those who are not unfaithful to him. In the Gospel the Savior says thus: 'He who has my commandments and keeps them, that one is the one loving me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and reveal myself to him.' (John 14:21).

Many peoples in Jerusalem used to begin to seek the face of the Lord Pantokrator in this way, not so that they might find God in a place and a temple by wearing themselves out, but after sending up acceptable prayers, to have a pious understanding and a right mindset regarding the Lord Pantokrator being sought and being appeased.

What was spoken by the prophet regarding each [matter] for the sake of the uplifting of the glorious Church, which is led by the All-King Savior, having been glorified in the times of persecutions in every pleasant and peaceful state, how many peoples were brought back to it despite those who had suffered, and many inhabited cities, the churches of various settlements, so that those inhabiting everywhere in the aforementioned cities would be gathered into one city from many, through pious mindset and an unhindered life, upon the appeasement and propitiation of the face of the Lord and the seeking of him through acceptable prayers and requests for the sake of God being seen.

And since the things previously proclaimed were desirable and highly valued, and the prophet himself, having received the question of those hoping, desired to come to the same many peoples who were coming and inhabiting in more cities, he says: 'I too will go.'
And the multitudes are confirmed as most eagerly awaiting the things appointed, when he who foretold begins to hasten toward the things previously proclaimed.
It is possible to say from the person of the Savior: 'I too will go'; for as he goes, it is...
to appease the face
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ten Men and the Spiritual Jew
english: He says that joy is to be received, celebrating with myriads of angels and the firstborn of the Church, according to the apostolic writing: 'For you have come to the mountain and city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and with myriads of angels, in festival, and the assembly of the firstborn who are written in heaven.' (Hebrews 10:25). Zechariah 8:23 says: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'

The prophecy marks the time when many peoples and many nations will come to seek the face of the Lord of hosts, seeking nothing other than the visitation of the Savior to men, through whom Emmanuel was born of the virgin, remaining God among us; in the days of him having appeared on the earth and having lived among men, there will be a calling for all people, as the prophecy having this content makes manifest: 'In those days when ten men from all the languages of the nations take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man.'

To understand the will of the expressed prophetic word, first it must be observed who is the one Jewish man specifically named; I think it is none other than whom the Apostle signifies writing to the Hebrews: 'Manifest that from Judah our Lord has risen' (Hebrews 7:28), to rule and reign over the Jews who are in secret, by spirit and not by letter, being circumcised not in the flesh but in the heart; for concerning him we grasp that which is said in hymns by each one of discerning insight: 'My King, Judah.'

The same understanding is applied to the blessing said by Jacob having this content: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you' (Genesis 49:8); and with others: 'A ruler shall not depart from Judah, and a leader from his sides, until he comes for whom it is reserved, and he himself is the expectation of the nations' (Genesis 49:10). For it is not the expectation of one nation, but of all nations together, the fulfillment of the prophecy concerning the calling of all people having this content: 'There shall be the root of Jesse and the one standing to rule the nations, upon whom the nations shall hope' (Isaiah 11:10). Of this one rising from the root of Jesse and rising...

Because he is a true Jew from Judah, ten men from all the languages of the nations, seizing the edge of the garment, say to him as a leader and general, rather a high priest and king of kings: 'Let us go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.' It is evident that for the Jews according to the intelligible, those who worship God in spirit and truth (John 4:23), it is not in Jerusalem or on the Samaritan mountain. For just as the angels worship the Son of God in a place, about whom the Holy Spirit says: 'All the angels of God shall worship him' (Hebrews 1:6), so also the worshippers of God from among men do not worship in any place, but act intelligibly, 'in spirit and truth.'

Having these things set forth, a pattern is established to show how from all the languages of the nations ten men shall seize the edge, that is, the body of the spiritual Jew. The number ten mystically lies here through allegory, just as in other divinely inspired oracles about which we shall say next: first, saying how it is impossible that from all the nations and all their languages, though there be myriads and many people, only ten men, according to the number being readily taken, have followed Jesus; for he himself is the true Jew, having risen from Judah.

Might it be, then, that all the multitudes having come to the gospel from different nations and languages, and having knowledge of the Holy Trinity mystically, happen to be ten, similarly to what was said by Matthew of the parable by Jesus: 'Then the kingdom of heaven shall be like ten virgins' (Matthew 25:10); of those who have believed, all of whom happened to be the ten virgins, let the understanding be such.

Every man being a living creature has five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch; toward these and also according to the intellect he has the same: enlightened eyes, hearing, about which the prophet says, thanking the generous one: 'He added to me an ear for hearing.' And related to the hidden sight and hearing is smell, through which it is fitting to perceive the 'fragrance of Christ' and the breath of his spiritual myrrh. And there is also taste and touch beyond the common ones, through which it is possible to taste that Christ is Lord, and to touch and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Mystical Thousand and the Sabbath Rest
english: To touch the Word of life. Therefore, all who are ever disciples of the gospel, when they possess their senses incorruptible, both the external and the internal, they become ten virgins reigning under Christ; but if ever some, through laziness, leave the internal senses of the man to act only through the mortal ones, they will become five foolish virgins, returning only to the perceptible things, as if their own light were not being nourished, which will be an extinguishing and a remnant of oil.

According to the spoken manner, ten men are found traveling with the true Jew from all languages and nations, having kept both kinds of senses pure and incorruptible, according to what was said by the Apostle: 'Grace' and peace shall be 'with those loving our Lord Christ in incorruption.' It is probable that the lovers of the letter are ten men who have converted the Decalogue ministered by the great Hierophant into works; but also Christians having the name of Jesus beginning from the tenth element among both Greeks and Hebrews; for the tenth is in the elements not only of the Greeks but also of the Hebrews.

And so that the scientific theory of numbers may appear unforced and according to the God-breathed Scripture, there are many things to derive; but for the present it is sufficient to use the words of Paul the Apostle and John the disciple beloved by Jesus. For to the Romans he writes that God has said: 'I have left myself seven thousand men who did not bend the knee to Baal' (Romans 11:3), but that 'to fall upon the Lamb,' that is, the Savior, [is] 'one hundred and forty-four thousand virgins, with women not defiled' (Revelation 14:4).

For it is not possible to take these things through history; for how, leaving such a multitude of God-fearing men, did the great prophet Elijah not know, as to say: 'I alone am left, and they seek my soul to take it' (1 Kings 19:10)? And how is it also possible to take such thousands of virgins, especially men, in a word, especially when the Ascension of the Savior had not happened long before, as John is the perfection in men? But truly each of these has happened, not necessarily taking the numbers upon the sense...

remaining. For indeed, seven times a thousand men, without bending the knee to Baal, happen to be mystically subject to the Sabbath rest set aside for the people of God, having a kinship with the thousand and the seven composed from it. For often it is possible to see the number thousand being mentioned in a God-befitting manner, just as it is also announced concerning God thus: 'He remembered for an eternity the covenant of his word, which he commanded to Abraham for a thousand generations' (Ps 105:8). For among none of the things signified shall there be a thousand generations until the completion of the world, as has been more decisively demonstrated previously in other matters.

3.69 From this therefore mystical thousand, a seven is composed, according to which the truly God-fearing ones alone bend the knee to the Cause of all things. 3.70 But also the virgins who followed, with women, unpolluted, are subject to the number of the thousand-folds of one hundred and forty-four. 3.71 Moreover, the most improbable part of the history is made manifest from the orderly fulfillment of twelve thousand virgins and men from each tribe of Israel; perhaps not even from all of humanity could such a number be fulfilled through those loving Christ, while John is still rubbing about on the earth. 3.72 Since therefore the literal sense of the word cannot hold, we say there are such thousands of those living unloosened and without blemish because of the virtue pertaining to the number; for it is a square, of which every side is twelve thousands, and there is a great privilege of this number, as it will be clear to the one who has examined the Scripture.

3.73 And irrefutable clarity regarding these things has occurred in the commentaries of the Apocalypse of John and of the epistle of Paul to the Romans, which the one who reads will see the divine theorems regarding the numbers scattered in the Scripture, both that before the arrival of the Savior—this is the one called the Old Testament—and that after the coming of Christ, which is called the New. 3.74 In the land of Sedrak and Damascus, a word of the Lord (Zech 9:10), because the Lord surveys men and all the tribes of Israel, and Hemath within its borders. 3.75 The saints, being ministers of the divine word, receive it as God giving it, just as being God-taken, according to the one speaking in Christ, to preach the [word] of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Conversion of Tyre, Sidon, and the Nations
english: Knowledge will be increasing. In this way, Habakkuk, being seized by a divine catch, has seen a divine seizure; for it is written concerning him, 'Habakkuk the prophet saw a divine catch.' And here, therefore, regarding such a theophoric state, a catch of the word of the Lord is announced.

What is this catch of the word, and about whom does he intend to speak? In the land, he says, of Shadrach, and Damascus and Hamath, in the borders of Damascus, it happens, while God is watching the men and the tribes of Israel. Blessed indeed is the one seen by God, according to: 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous' (Ps 34:15), and he who asks to find this is speaking well: 'Look upon me and have mercy on me.'

Test whether the land of Shadrach is able to show the increasing of the old people, those having believed, saying: 'Learn from me that I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls' (Mt 11:29). And Damascus alludes to those called away from idols; for much dread is practiced by the Damascenes.

Therefore, also, having the opposite of those finding rest for their souls by the Savior being previously gentle and humble in heart, they are swearing oaths and being awakened, killing against the neighbors. Therefore, they are called 'blood-drinkers' in the voice of the Greeks and 'blood-sacks,' being found full of murder, as being men watched over by the Lord Pantokrator, those having come from the nations through faith, among whom the latter are those from the tribes of Israel.

All those mentioned, being wild before the divine calling, were happening in the borders of the land of the Damascenes, which Jesus, while still being a child, foretold, taking 'the dogs of Samaria and the power of Damascus against the king of the Assyrians' (Zech 9:9). See if this victory of the infant, not yet having the age to 'call father or mother,' alludes to the calling of the Magi from the east, having come from the east to Jerusalem to worship the one born there as king, being led by a star appearing to them, as the Gospel according to Matthew declares.
Tyre and Sidon, because they thought very much. And Tyre built fortifications for itself and stored silver like dust and gathered...
A small thing like the mud of the roads. For this reason the Lord will inherit it and tread its power into the sea, and this shall be consumed in fire.

Through the names set forth, the calling of all the nations is signified. For indeed all idolaters happen to be Tyrians and Sidonians. For that which is said in one of the Psalms, 'The daughters of Tyre shall worship him with gifts,' signifies the calling of the return of the nations who are 'having no hope and being atheists in the world.' According to the same sense, one must also interpret that which has in another song thus: 'Glory has been spoken of you, O city of God, and behold, foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of Ethiopians, these became there.' For then indeed they become in the city glorified by God, when the foreigners, the Tyrians, and the people of Ethiopians turn back from whence they had impiety and superstition, in order that they might become partakers of and an inheritance of God, having departed from the foreign wandering and the Tyrian and Ethiopian idolatry.

One should attempt to take along with the things set forth and those in the Gospel having this: 'Woe to you, Chorazin, woe to you, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon the powers had happened, long ago in sackcloth and ashes they would have repented' (Matt 11:21). For of the tremendous powers of Jesus having been accomplished, the citizens of Chorazin and Bethsaida, being Jews, did not repent; the Tyrians and Sidonians would have repented if they had happened among them; except if even then they did not see the extraordinary powers of Jesus, but later sometime having seen them, having believed in the one who accomplished them, they have come to repentance.

The calling which is expected of them is also made clear by the prophecy set forth having this: 'Tyre and Sidon because they thought exceedingly,' boasting as if 'to build strongholds' which it seemed they would be unshakeable; but sophistical and contentious words these are, on which, thinking greatly, the author took it to be that they were inaccessible and unassailable. Concerning such strongholds being striven for by the heterodox, as they shall be overthrown by those warring under God, the Apostle writes: 'The weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but powerful in God, for the overthrowing of strongholds, destroying arguments, and every exaltation being raised up against the knowledge of God' (2 Cor 10:4). For not
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fall of Tyre and the Inheritance of Nations
english: The apostolic word says that fortified strongholds are being undermined by reasoning, that is, by contentious arguments. Regarding Nineveh, being taken to mean 'becoming beautified,' she was thinking greatly of those things she had constructed in defenses and unassailable garrisons, which the destroyer of such things says: 'And you will be drunken and will be seen as a wanton, and you will seek for yourself a standing against enemies. Your strongholds will have the purposes of figs, and if they are shaken, they will fall into the mouth of one eating.' (Nahum 3:86).

For how would not the one drunken from the wine of debauchery be overlooked by the Foreknower of all things, whom the Apostle speaking in Christ forbids even the drinking of its wine, writing: 'Do not get drunk with wine in which is debauchery' (Ephesians 5:18)? For how is not the one harvesting from the vine of Sodom and the branch of Gomorrah like this, which Moses interpreted as being a dragon's wrath and an unyielding viper's venom, saying: 'Our enemies are foolish; for from the vine of Sodom is their vine,' and shortly after: 'Their wine is a dragon's wrath and an unyielding viper's venom' (Numbers 23:22)?

The one partaking of this drink into drunkenness is overlooked by the Guardian of God, as if she no longer finds a standing, with invisible enemies lying in wait, preparing the judgment of strong wars. And what will happen to this branch, or its strongholds, which she considered safe and unshakable, that they will become so weak as to be moved as having the purposes of figs, on which branch the fruit will fall into the mouth of one eating?

For the opposing enemy had indeed opened his mouth as being ready to receive for eating those falling from the strongholds, having been shown to be easily shaken through much weakness by the Trophaios Great King, having been given authority to tread upon the opposing phalanx, according to what was said in the Gospel by the Savior to the known ones: 'I have given you authority to tread' (Luke 10:19) upon others and 'over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall harm you.'

That falling into the mouth of one eating signifies being defeated, as it is testified by many scriptures, and most especially by this: 'A wandering sheep of Israel, lions drove him out; the King of Assyria first devoured him, and later the King of Babylon devoured his bones.' (Ezekiel 34:5). In the same way, even if the lions were powerful, standing opposed through their ferocity as opposing forces, they shall endure judgment when Israel, having been trampled by them, is set free, having been allegorically called a sheep, as the prophet triumphantly cries out: 'The Holy One of Israel belongs to the Lord, the beginning of his offspring; all who eat him shall err, and evil shall come upon them,' says the Lord (Isaiah 19:1).

The word strikes against the one who is drunken and crazed, bringing forth: 'Take water from the region for yourself, seize your strongholds,' of which they seem to be unassailable. For even if the sophistries once seemed unloosed and the quarrelsome words unshakeable, once the truth is revealed, they shall be shaken down so as to never again be exalted according to the knowledge of God.

Similarly, forts and walls will be called to be built unshakeably by those gathering in idolatry and a polytheistic plan; these are named Tyrians by the manner of allegory, being taken as Greeks in sound for 'gathering' and 'continuing.'

And since all the evil ones are such unto themselves, with nothing bad existing in essence, Tyre becomes a divine inheritance along with all those concerning whom it is said by the Father to the Savior: 'Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance' (Psalm 2:8). Being among the inheriting nations, Tyre herself shall be made subject after having seen the immense powers of Jesus and having repented.
For if previously she was acting insolently, building strongholds, and hoarding silver as if it were dust, and gathering gold as if it were clay, her power was torn apart into the life of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fear and Sorrow of the Philistine Cities
english: The people have become dizzy, referring allegorically to the sea, because the stored silver has not benefited them, being made worthless by the abundance of the earth's dust; nor has the gathered gold helped, being compared to the safety of muddy roads. Even if the accomplices of impiety sophistically argue and wander about, the things being labored for will be lost to destruction.

For how will not the wealth of those walking according to the truth, 'those bearing the image of the pig,' be thrown into the dust, just as the gold which they gathered is made like the mud of roads? For those walking are treading upon the mud of impious teachings, as if encountering countless slips. However, even if Tyre travels opposingly for a long time, she will be tested by a punishing fire, after which that about which the Savior said, 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and would I it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49), so that every harmful plant which is thorn, thistle, and weed may be consumed by it.

For it will be a good thing for Tyre to be tested by being thus consumed by fire, according to what was said by the Savior: 'Every one shall be salted with fire' (Mark 9:49). And it is also profitable for all her power to be cast down into the sea, in which the stored silver becomes like dust, and the gathered gold becomes like the mud of roads.

When her lofty power has been shattered into the sea, and she herself has been consumed by fire, what remains first shall be inherited by the Lord, which is His own handiwork; for so also all the nations shall become His inheritance, having turned away from all impiety and much-godly wandering.

Let all things said concerning Tyre be taken to heart concerning Sidon also; for the wickedness and impiety are the same, and the repentance and return to God are the same. Sidon has much proximity to Tyre in the healing of idols.

Ashkelon shall see and be afraid, and Gaza shall be in great pain, and Accalon, because she has been shamed from her hope. And a king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. And foreigners shall dwell in Azotus, and I will cut down the insolence of other tribes. And I will draw their blood from their mouths and their abominations from the midst of their teeth, and they shall be left, and of...

to our God, and they shall be as a commander in Judah and in Achzib like a Jebusite. And I will set a dedication in my house so that it may not be dispersed nor overturned, and I will not come upon them again, having driven them out, because now I have seen with my eyes.

3.100 Having seen the dark things happening to the Tyrians, Ashkelon had fear, dreading that she might one day fall to the same, and Gaza had much distress, but even Achzib endured shame, her hope having failed. 3.101 But what is the cause of Gaza's great distress, whether it is the loss of her king, or the fear of Ashkelon, whether it is that she has endured cruelties from those dwelling in her? Similarly, it will apply to Achzib and Azotus and generally to the other peoples. 3.102 Thus, regarding those who have [the word] toward the spoken [text], one should consider the things toward the promised outcome. Ashkelon, having been weighed as something precious and well-founded, taking up a mindful purpose, will see, no longer being blinded by the immediate pleasure and other passions, how to take up reverence, how to be numbered among those possessing such virtue, concerning which the proverbial decree says regarding wisdom and her father: 'He will guard the way of those who revere him' (Proverbs 3:6). The prophet lying there exhorts all men to arrive at this praiseworthy state, rather the word within him, saying: 'Let all flesh fear from the face of the Lord' (Psalm 2:11) Almighty. 3.103 Because not only dark things have happened to Tyre, but the existing prophecy has also pre-delivered the change toward better things, Ashkelon, having seen these, had a perfect reverence present from: 'The fear of the Lord surpassed all' (Psalm 34:7), and from: 'There is no lack to those fearing the Lord' (Psalm 34:9), all beneficial things being fulfilled, 'nothing being lacking to all good things of those seeking the Lord' (Psalm 34:10).

3.104 Consequently, for Ashkelon, having been frightened by the clear imposition of the praiseworthy change of Tyre, and Gaza will be greatly distressed, just as the one being wept over through repentance says: 'I will wet my bed every night, in my tears I will wet my couch' (Psalm 6:6). But when will the painful state be for Gaza, either when, knowing herself, she knows the coming [thing], her innate strength, that from the divine...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The many foolish children and the barrenness of the synagogue
english: Given naturally to the Word. Because so much has been managed for Gaza, which is being severely afflicted, and for Akko, which is being described as a barren woman, for thus it is interpreted: that her piercing hope will bring shame. And since the offspring is understood in two ways by way of ascent—one being that which comes from those able to speak to God: 'From your fear we conceived in the womb and labored and brought forth' (Psalm 139:13). And the other being the praiseworthy one, having the Bridegroom Word as her seed, being a pure one as opposed to one standing with adulteresses.

Concerning such a birth indeed, the Mother is spoken of by the Master of All: 'I will not have mercy on her children, because they are children of fornication; the mother fornicated, and they brought shame upon her who bore them' (Hosea 13:23). When the succession of children is thus divided in two, it is a blessed thing to undergo barrenness, she who was giving birth destructively from the invisible evil lovers; for this barrenness is for the sake of good, as she takes up the seed from God, from which a generation of offsprings shall be saving, as the result of the bride having been blessed and having become a many-child dwelling in the house of the husband, concerning whom it is said thus in the Psalms: 'To her who dwells barren in the house, a mother of children rejoicing' (Psalm 113:9); and in another scripture, after barrenness, being a child and many-child is brought forth: 'A barren woman has borne seven' (Isaiah 66:7). Concerning this, rather the prophet Isaiah cries out toward her: 'Cast away and cry out, she who did not labor, for the children of the wilderness are many more than those having a husband' (Isaiah 54:1).

The scriptures received are most pointedly alluding to the two calls, both the one from the circumcision and the one from the Gentiles. For the one had the law regarding the husband, bearing children from him; but the barren one was a desert of children, when, being godless, she had no hope at all in the world, according to what was written by Paul concerning idolaters (Romans 1:21). Having these things, when the true Bridegroom arrived, the barren one became a mother from him of divine offspring, seven named because incorruption and purity were coming forth, possessing these virtues of the mystical seven; nevertheless, the barren one having borne seven, she is settled by the husband, a mother of rejoicing children.
'She who was much in children grew weak' (Genesis 30:3), [but] many of her children having become...

Such a great number results in coarseness. For this is made clear also from the word, just as in the Gospel many are said to be those walking the wide road, having an end of destruction (Matt 7:13). In this same way also the sons of Israel, being led by the tyrant of the intellectual Egypt, many have become 'very foolish.'

Of these so-called many, the Apostle, setting himself apart and those who have believed in the same ministry as himself, writes: 'We are not as many who traffic in the word of the Lord' (2 Cor 4:2). By this view is also consistent that which is announced in the hymn by the Psalmist: 'Many will say to my soul' (Ps 51:11), and also: 'Many will stand against me' (Ps 55:23).

Because the synagogue of the circumcision has grown weak due to the coarseness of the children, although it has a man, the law, the one called mother from the Gentiles has become, although she was previously barren; the seven children having been made clear as 'reborn not from corrupt seed but incorruptible through the living and abiding word of God,' so as to be a multitude of children of the desert rather than of that living by law, to a man called allegorically. Through the showing of different children and their parentage according to the divine pedagogy, it will be for good that the soul having the readiness to give birth to children of destruction be made barren, it being a ruin and harmful to be made barren of the quick-grasping [soul] from the seeds of the God-Word. Therefore it is proper to avoid such a barrenness, so that a generation of heavenly and good children may exist.

These things have been observed in the interpretation of Accad regarding a barrenness being received, her being made barren as casting away the hope and expectation of a multitude of useless children. These things existing in Accad, her expectation passing away, 'the king was lost to Gaza.' And who this turns out to be has been said previously. For a king of her exists, the ruler of her, passion, that is, the word. And if the ruler before the better conduct and polity, the loss of this was slight; but if [the ruler] after the improvement and [the one] upon the flesh of the dragon, but also 'those biting and devouring one another' (Prov 6:27) 'have abominations in their paths and blood in their mouth' (Prov 6:28) to the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Visionary Eyes of God and the Fulfillment of Prophecy
english: Whatever is removed, those freed from the murderous insolence remain to the Lord. For when all evil joined to mankind is taken away, the image and likeness according to which they were created from God remains.

Since 'man, being in honor, not understanding' (Ps 49:20), fell in a manner 'as if cast down to the mindless beasts' (Ps 49:21), when bestiality and the beastly state are removed, the honor 'remains to our God,' the rational being being revealed of the man having become upright, the many crooked thoughts being excluded; for God having made man upright, they themselves sought vain thoughts, existing in many through coarseness.

Immediately indeed in the present prophetic word, the things that happened according to what the Ashdodites, the citizens of Gaza, and the inhabitants of Accacre did having been taken away, those created according to the image and likeness of God shall remain and they themselves shall sincerely confess to our God, as if 'making Judah thousands'; for one is taken into confessing. And each one, sincerely confessing with princely choice, is a thousand-leader. But even Accacre shall be according to the Jebusite, being taken into a step.

These things having happened, God builds an anathema for those having been benefited, having a high fortress, so that remaining within, standing firmly, they may not wander any more here and there being carried about lawlessly, nor even turning back again to those sins which they have left behind, 'forgetting them, stretching forward to those things before' (Phil 3:13), to reach 'the prize of the upward call' (1 Pet 2:9). These things having been achieved, more so the gifts of God, no longer does an enemy exist to drive out, all the things lying about wildly having been destroyed.

The tyrant of the spiritual Egypt once pursued the people of God, speaking boldly and arrogantly: 'Having pursued, I shall seize; dividing, I shall scatter the curs; I shall fill my soul; I shall ascend by my sword; my hand shall rule'; and still speaking these things arrogantly, he has become a coward, all his proud words having been overturned, so as to no longer be able to drive them out. This very drama the king of the Assyrians also endured; for myriads as many as...

Having threatened [the enemy], he was immediately removed, and much of his army was laid waste in a single hour by one angel, just as the Scripture declares, saying that one angel had removed one hundred eighty-five thousand [Numbers 24:20], so that the people of God might no longer be driven out to perish.

The Benefactor and cause of all blessed salvation says: 'Therefore it is no longer driving out, because I have seen with my eyes,' referring to the contemplative power, concerning which the Apostle writes: 'All things naked and laid bare to the eyes of God' [Hebrews 4:13] and His word. It must be said a second time that those seeing are the eyes of God, which are the supervising angels of human affairs, about whom the Hymnodist says: 'His eyes look upon the nations' [Psalm 86:8].

Nor did he fail to call the contemplative men, whose visions the divine have inscribed, the eyes of God; for since the body of Christ, which is the whole Church of the saved, is participating, there exist discerning eyes, as the apostolic word makes manifest. Indeed, those seeing the eyes—which have been interpreted according to all the meanings of the speaker—will be the ones supervising the one driving out.

This should also be attributed to the prophecy: since the eyes had seen the Savior coming for the benefit and salvation of all, the one driving out was released, 'being given authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions and all the power of Satan' [Luke 10:19]. Furthermore, the Savior, the Triumphant One, is presented to those present thus: 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; cry out, daughter of Jerusalem' [Zechariah 9:9], and the following of the speaker, which must be set forth according to the word as follows:

Zechariah 9:9-10: 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; cry out, daughter of Jerusalem; behold, your King comes to you, just and saving. He is gentle and riding upon a donkey and a young colt. And he will destroy chariots from Ephraim and a horse from Jerusalem, and the war-bow will be destroyed, and a multitude and peace from the nations. And he will cause the waters to cease, even to the sea and the rivers, the overflows of the earth.'
The Evangelists say that the lying prophecy was fulfilled when Jesus, having ridden upon the donkey and the colt and having been led from the village opposite, which was made manifest by God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Savior King and the Prophetic Fulfillment
english: Providing for those clarifying the Gospels, about which we too have spoken as far as possible in the commentaries on Matthew. Therefore, now along with those, the things of the prophet must be contemplated.

He commands the daughter of Zion to rejoice quickly and intensely, and the daughter of Jerusalem to proclaim that the King Savior is coming justly and saving, gentle and having established himself upon a colt and a new foal (cf. Zech 9:9), so that the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem may be destroyed, and he adds a war bow, a multitude of nations, and peace. When these things are accomplished, the one coming will be for the casting out of waters until the sea and the driving out of rivers of the land.

What each of these intends, I will proceed to say. The daughter of Zion is the contemplative soul of good things, observing the unseen eternal things; for Zion is interpreted as a place of observation, and a settled commandment. For how could the contemplative soul of truth not perform the divine commandment, taking hold of it for works, as it has been emboldened to say: 'The commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes' (Ps 118:105); and again: 'Your commandment is very wide' (Ps 118:97) 'and your servant loved it.' Just as such a soul is the daughter of Zion in the said manner, so might someone also be the daughter of Jerusalem, a soul seeing 'the peace which surpasses all understanding' (Phil 4:7).

The word commands both, the one to rejoice intensely at the arrival of the true King, the other, as having ascended above, to proclaim the coming All-King. For Jerusalem precedes Zion, and therefore the daughter of Jerusalem precedes the daughter of Zion, as the one is commanded only to rejoice, the other also to proclaim. For one can rejoice having only accomplished a practical life, whereas the one rejoicing and proclaiming has contemplation, because the Word of wisdom and knowledge has received the superabundant gift of the Holy Spirit. But to rejoice intensely...

Prophecy commands that at the arrival of a king, one must proclaim [him], who is simultaneously saving and found to be just, being no one other than Jesus. For who is so saving and a savior of the world as 'God with us, Emmanuel,' born from the experience of a woman not having a man, fulfilling the prophecy that says: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son' (Isa 7:14). The angel named the child Jesus, marking this mode of the virgin bearing without a man, and giving the reason for this designation thus. For this, he says, he shall be called Jesus, 'for he will save his people from their sins' (Matt 1:21).

Immediately after Mary gave birth in Bethlehem, a great angel appeared: 'A savior has been born to you today,' he said, 'who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David' (Luke 2:10-11). Those proclaiming his descent here were arranging themselves around the born Christ, according to Isaiah: 'Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, a savior is coming to you' (Isa 60:1); and this is no other than he who announced about himself, Jesus: 'The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10); and again: 'Just and saving, there is none beside me' (Isa 45:21).

For how could he not be saving, the one raised up by the Father as a horn of salvation in the house of David, according to the fulfillment of Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, saying: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who visited and made redemption; he raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David' (Luke 1:68-69).

Regarding the coming king being just and saving, he also stands gentle, mounted upon a colt and a foal; for he himself says about himself in the Gospel: 'Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls; for my yoke is kind and my burden is light' (Matt 11:29-30). Everyone who carries the kind yoke becomes a subject of him upon whom the gentle king has mounted.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Errors of Ephraim and the False Waters
english: And since the Savior is not only the one for those yoked under his good yoke, but also for those just called, and he has mounted a new colt, which was still untamed and without a bridle, so that he might also tame it, just as the best horse-tamer would.

In this understanding, both the called peoples are signified by the word: those from circumcision, yoked under the yoke according to the letter and the shadow of the law, called a heavy yoke; and the one immediately called from all idolatry and superstitious handling. Because those yoked to the law according to the letter bore a heavy yoke, the apostles say about it in their own Book of Acts that 'neither we nor our fathers were able to bear' (Acts 15:10) the heavy yoke of the law.

Similarly, Paul, speaking in Christ, writes to the Galatians, who wish to be circumcised sensually after the gospel: 'Stand fast, therefore, and do not be held again by a yoke of slavery' (Galatians 5:1). For it was no longer following to place the disciples of the gospel under oppression and the heavy yoke, having been persuaded by the one who said: 'My yoke is good' (Matthew 11:30).

Likewise, the gentle king has mounted the new colt mentioned, 'so that he might create the two into one new man in it' (Ephesians 2:15). For thus one people and one Church shall be composed from both the callings.

Equally in the Gospels it is written about the colt released from the opposite village, so that he might come to Jesus, being tamed by mounting upon him by the Savior (Matthew 21:2-7); for it is said that not yet had any man sat upon him, which is shown by the word that the Gentiles had not yet transitioned for any didactic reason; for they were atheists in the world, having no true hope; but even if before the faith they were an unbridled colt, yet since the Christ rising from Judah has shone upon them, expectation has risen for them, according to what is said about him: 'And he himself shall be an expectation of the nations' (Isaiah 49:6), and again: 'Nations hope upon him' (Psalm 22:21).

Having been greatly benefited by the two callings from the mounting of the righteous and saving and gentle king upon them, the chariots of Ephraim are destroyed (Hosea 10:13), and the horse from Jerusalem, and with them the bow of the most brutish and wild wars, from which [he] departed...

The 'fiery darts of the evil one' refer to the passion for immorality, as those being burned are those being consumed by shameful passion. The collections of the heterodox and their irrational dogmatizing are the chariots of Ephraim. It has often been shown that heresies stand by the designation of Ephraim, because Jeroboam, who led the ninety-five schisms, was from the tribe of Ephraim; just as the Savior is called Judah because he is called from the same tribe to be a ruler of the Church, so the leader of bad doctrines is called Ephraim, promising much fruit by persisting in the deceived.

Regarding the perishing chariots, they say in the Psalms concerning those who ride and drive: 'Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. They are fallen, and are fallen: but we are risen, and are risen up' (Psalm 20:7). They agreed to sin and impiety. To each one having such an opinion, the king says in the law: 'I will not be with many to do evil; neither will I join with a multitude to bear false witness' (Exodus 20:16). Concerning this destructive thing, which leans toward evil, the personified prostitute in the Proverbs, whoever she may be, has cried out to each one who is shamelessly and boldly acting: 'A sacrifice of righteousness have I offered, today I pay my vows' (Proverbs 8:14).

If all things interpreted by the Great King are taken away, this too shall be: 'The waters shall be poured out unto the sea,' making them manifest to be salty and not drinkable, and 'the outbursts of the rivers of the earth,' waters flowing down to the sea. The words there are impious through saltiness, falsely claiming to have the outbursts of the sweet and drinkable rivers of the earth. Such are those of Pharaoh, who, sitting enthroned, boasts saying: 'The rivers are mine, and I have made them.' The drinking of these is forbidden by God in Jeremiah the prophet: 'And now, says he, what have you to do with the land of Egypt, to drink the waters of Gihon? and what have you to do with the land of Assyria, to drink the waters of the rivers?' (Jeremiah 2:18). The outbursts of the rivers of the earth are said to be likely and
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Blood of the Covenant
english: Logical expositions are being made about them with elegance, because their marriage seems to possess sweetness.

Zechariah 9:11-12: 'And you also in blood of covenant sent forth your prisoners from a pit not having water; you shall sit in a stronghold, prisoners of the assembly, and instead of one day of your sojourning, double I will repay you.' The word commanded by the one in the prophet, or rather God, to Zion and Jerusalem—to the one to rejoice exceedingly, and to the other to proclaim the coming king, saving and strong and being gentle—turns the word toward him who is coming, saying: 'And you also in blood of covenant sent forth your prisoners from a pit not having water' (Zechariah 9:11). For where was it necessary for the prisoners to be, or to be cast down into a pit not having water by those laboring against them? One finds many of the holy men having been cast into waterless pits by those attacking and murdering against them.

For instance, Joseph, being envied because of the goodness and beauty coming toward him, was thrown by those unjustly envying into a pit not having water. Likewise also the wisest Daniel, the friend of God, was thrown by the Babylonians into a pit not having water, so that he might be shown to be without water, being led through there by the lions, not being able to live if he had been filled with waters. And again Jeremiah, the great prophet, the opponents threw into a pit full of mire. And no one of those thus attacked remained without help, God of them having sent them unhurt out of the waterless pit.

And since these things were being fulfilled symbolically, see lest the pit is waterless, being shown through the symbols, the Hades of the ungodly and sinners, there not being any life-giving water, because there is no praiseworthy moisture there at all.

Immediately, for instance, the rich one having been made there, [of] purple and fine linen... [text broken] ...daily... in fire a flame... a shower of water... he did not find... as the earth... of death... the burning and the flame...

The blasphemer, called a tongue... has already been given as the word... and Jeremiah, from this... through the dry pit... [in] hunger. In the dry pit... before the arrival of the Savior... having been [cast] by the tyrants... in Hosea the prophet... 'I will test them in the bonds of my love' (Hosea 2:14).

The bonds and the feet of wisdom are equal, having a longing for it: 'Place your feet into its feet' (Proverbs 4:26). Those having been thus born, for a certain time, are sent from there according to a certain house, after their death. 'Not by corruptible silver or gold, but by the precious blood as of an unblemished lamb, handed down from the father in a futile manner' (1 Peter 1:18-19), and this is Christ.

Having received, having given, the new covenant is a cup... with this blood of Christ Jesus... having died... they went forward into the holy... clearly [being] of the bonds of the blood of the covenant. Undergoing the death of the covenant, as the Apostle writes: 'For a covenant upon the dead is valid, lest it cease when the one who establishes it lives' (Hebrews 9:17).

Immediately also Moses, the great high priest, having received the book of the law of the covenant, having taken blood [to] the dead, said: 'This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord commanded and established toward you' (Exodus 24:8). [For] whom death...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Walls of the Church
english: The shadowy [image] of the calf, the new [covenant] being confirmed by the [blood], as Paul [says] to those believing in the old covenant: 'If the blood of bulls and goats and the sprinkling of the sin offering sanctifies those who are communing toward the purity of the flesh, how much more does the blood of Christ cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living and true God' (Hebrews 9:14).

What and what kind of security will there be for the prisoners sent out from the pit lacking water, as the Word declares, saying: 'They shall sit in strongholds' (Isaiah 33:16), clearly meaning the praiseworthy 'prisoners of the synagogue' of the glorious Church, no longer having 'a hole or a wrinkle.' But the fortresses are salvations; there the prisoners of the synagogue sit resting, having been carried out from the waterless pit.

Previously the Word revealed certain strongholds which Tyre and Nineveh built; let us see what are the ones now mentioned as praiseworthy, in which the prisoners of the divine synagogue are guarded with rest.

In the divine writing of Proverbs, reverence is called a stronghold for those establishing holiness and righteousness, thus: 'A stronghold is the fear of the Lord' (Proverbs 14:26). He, having been covered by the fear of God, surpassing this covering, wishing to be guarded by God Himself, says to Him through prayer: 'Become for me a protector, a strong place to save me' (Psalm 31:1); and again in Psalm 31: 'You are my refuge from the distress that surrounds me, my joy, deliver me from those pursuing me' (Psalm 30:1-2). Equally in Psalm 30, entreating to find an unassailable guard: 'Become for me a protector, he said, a place of refuge to save me' (Psalm 31:1).

But also he who, having competed in the good contest and finished the good race, having kept the faith, is himself kept by it; which he also shows as being securely walled and existing unassailably, joyfully crying out with those nearby: 'Behold, a strong city and our salvation; it shall set a wall and a circumvallation' (Zechariah 9:12). For how is the city not unassailable, having a wall and a circumvallation, which...
What is the Church? It has an inner wall consisting of the spiritual law and the elevated contemplation, and an outer wall, outside the secure wall, which is the explicit and historical writing.

And still, by another metaphor, there is a wall of the well-fortified city: the faith concerning the Trinity and the Only-begotten Son of God, who is the Word of God, truth and the Wisdom of God, which is appropriately surrounded by this understanding of the Word's incarnation and the birth from the unwedded Virgin Mary.

It can be said that the pious thoughts of the Church according to the doctrines of truth serve as a wall guarding it, while the moral teachings and the keeping of the commandments serve as an outer wall.

It could also be said otherwise: that the strong city is previously walled by the scientific contemplation of the intelligible and incorporeal things, having as an outer wall the knowledge of the sensible things of the visible world and its parts and the divine providence governing them.

He who sits in this city and in its praiseworthy fortifications, being a bondservant of Christ, lives fearlessly, expecting to receive double in return for what he has been afflicted with: consolation and comfort; for it has been promised to the benefited multitude: 'Instead of one day of your sojourning, I will repay you double' (Isa 61:7), the comfort being doubled for those who have undergone affliction.

Take the sensible image of contemplation from the most manly Job. For just as the things previously taken from him were doubled upon him, so those who have trained themselves perfectly toward piety 'have a promise of life, both of the present and of the coming' (cf. 1 Tim 4:8), not of the life that is near, which only pities those who hope in it alone, but of the life which is able to exist now for those believing, according to what was said by the Savior: 'He who believes in me has eternal life' (John 6:47), and again: 'And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the true God, and Him whom you sent, Jesus Christ' (John 17:3).
He who possesses this life directed toward him will enjoy it being multiplied when the perfection comes and truth is seen face to face.
And more introductory, this too could be said: that death [comes] to all men...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Archer and the Arrows of Love
english: Because the body was separated from the soul by the transgression of the first man, the body was being distressed as if to undergo a long-lasting sojourn; instead of existing for one day, God has doubly repaid by raising and giving the soul its body, so that it does not merely receive the same thing, but instead of a corrupt and dishonorable and weak and psychic body, an incorruptible, strong, and glorious body, and this very body is spiritual.

The one paying attention to the reading of the God-breathed oracles and many other things will understand how God doubly repays the one having been relocated for one day. Regarding what is explicitly said: the people, having been relocated into the captivity of enemies, were not only redeemed, but also ruled over those who had seized them; when this happened, those who had been slightly afflicted had joy.

Zechariah 9:13-14: 'Because I have bent my bow against you, Judah, I have filled Ephraim, and I will raise up your children, Zion, against the children of the Greeks, and I will touch you as a warrior's sword. And the Lord shall be over them.' The Father bent a bow for Himself for the Savior rising out of the tribe of Judah, from which He releases arrows aiming at salvation. And see the difference: the destroying bow of Ephraim is named after being used against the enemy. For it is said in Psalm 67:13 regarding satanic powers of enemies and all the heterodox: 'Ephraim, bending and shooting with the bow, how were they turned in the day of battle,' having grown weak and being overthrown, clearly showing the shattering of the shields? For it is said: 'Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be shattered.' The shattering of the bows is the ruling principle of the combatants, from which evil words are sent, the judgment of unheeded arrows about which the divine word says: 'Their tongue, shooting a missile, is deceitful, their words...'
The words of those promising false knowledge are full of the venom of a serpent, killing those who receive them.

But such are not the arrows of the powerful Savior, about which it is said in the forty-fourth Psalm regarding the blessed and excellent archer: 'Your arrows are sharp, mighty' (Ps 44:3), which instills divine love in those struck by them, as if speaking like a blessed bride possessing divine love: 'I am pierced by love.' And behold the paradox: the same Savior is the bow, the archer, and the arrow. For in the present prophetic word spoken to Him by God, it is said: 'I have bent you, Judah, as my bow' (Jer 48:10); but in the Psalm, those praising Him say: 'Your arrows are sharp, mighty' (Ps 44:3); and He Himself says about Himself in Isaiah: 'He has made me like a chosen arrow; He has hidden me in His quiver' (Isa 49:2). For how could the one fashioning those who are being pierced as chosen not be a chosen arrow, hidden in the quiver which He possessed from the flesh of Mary?

Once this divine bow is bent, from which the arrows that strike are released into divine love, Ephraim is struck, being overturned and shown to be weak, according to what was said by the sub-text of the Psalm: 'The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, how were they turned back in the day of war' (Hos 7:7), when the great God, bestowing grace, raised up 'the children of Zion against the children of the Greeks' (Joel 2:28)? The generations of Greeks are signified in these things: those advocating false knowledge and all those having impiety, by which the impious send out destructive arrows against those who have not taken up 'the door of faith.' The children of Zion are those advocating the truth, being raised up by God who reigns over them. What then is Zion, the mother of the children being raised up by God, or the [one] previously clarified a little, whose...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Arrow and the Light of the Soul
english: The daughter is commanded to rejoice intensely and suddenly at the appearance of the strong and saving King.

"God feels for Judah like a warrior wielding a sword," effecting salvation in both ways: just as a bow was strung for a blessed erotic desire, and just as an excellent general feels for a sword, being a warrior, in order to strike down those set in opposition. It is also written about this in the forty-fourth Psalm: "Gird your sword upon your thigh, O Mighty One, with your beauty and your splendor, because of truth and gentleness and righteousness, and your right hand shall lead you wondrously" (Psalm 45:3). For how would the right hand not lead wondrously the one who has girded a sword upon his thigh, the Mighty One, paradoxically striking those being struck?

It is indeed his own to hear [the enemies] being told regarding his divine power: "You Ethiopians are wounded by my sword." For having been wounded by him saying these things, casting off the life of the Ethiopians, they shall take up immortality, as it might be said graciously: "The brightness of the Lord our God shall be upon us" (Psalm 18:10), since, having washed us of the cause of all good things, we were shown bright and white, according to the one speaking with boldness: "You shall wash me and I shall be whiter than snow" (Psalm 51:7).

But from where did the Ethiopians come, those being wounded for good so that they might be put to death regarding impiety, or having been born from the devil, desiring to do his lusts? For it has been said about him that he is black, because of the approaching dark ignorance and malice, as is shown in the book of repentance called the Shepherd, and in the Epistle of Barnabas.

And we also have been struck saving-ly by the living and active Word, about whom it has been written: "The Word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword" (Hebrews 4:12), so that having been put to death in the flesh, we might be made alive in the spirit. And let us be struck also by the chosen arrow, sent from the drawn bow; for thus we shall be raised up, happening to be children of Zion upon the generations of the Greeks.

Many, being children and sons of the Greeks, strove according to the dogmas of piety, as to leave behind many writings; but they were overwhelmed when the ecclesiastical men of God rose up against them.

Let us overturn the contentious arguments of those with confidence, saying: 'The weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but are powerful in God, demolishing arguments and lifting up every height against the knowledge of God' (2 Cor 10:4-5). When the children of Zion rise up against the Greeks, the Lord, having accomplished this, will be 'over them' (Zech 9:14), uniting those who rise up with those against whom they rise up, as they are prepared to reign with one mind and one judgment, having created the Greek and the Jew into one new man.

And he will go forth like a flash of lightning, and the Lord God of hosts will sound the trumpet and will go forth in the fury of his indignation; the Lord God of hosts will protect them (Zech 9:14-15). When God has drawn the bow against Judah, a flash like lightning will go forth, piercing and striking toward divine love, so as to become the light of the world, which is able to be called a perfect soul or a glorious Church: 'I am wounded by love.' And it is not only there that the things sent from the divine bow are luminous; in Habakkuk it is said toward God: 'Your arrows shall go forth as light, into the brightness of lightning of your weapons' (Hab 1:8). There is no difference between saying it in the plural or the singular; for we take generally a flash going forth like lightning, of which kinds there are many among the individual flashes.

The word piercing toward desire, taking up the virtues according to kind and the doctrines according to part, is a flash in the general sense, while specific ones exist regarding each virtue and each doctrine of words, and for this reason they are named as flashes in the plural. Furthermore, just as one flash goes forth like lightning and many [go forth] into light according to Habakkuk, so all things sent from the bow drawn by God are bright arrows. And this is Judah.

It has been made clear previously that these things are announced concerning the one rising out of the tribe of Judah, the Savior. When the divine flash goes forth like lightning so that the inner man and the eyes of the heart may be enlightened, the Lord God of hosts sounds the trumpet, awakening also the inner hearing, so that having received the perception of the existing benefit, one may respond gratefully: 'The instruction of the Lord opens my ears' (Ps 119:16), after he has given me the habit of hearing. And see whether not by thought...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Trumpet of Truth and the Armor of Light
english: The thing given by God is one trumpet and another lightning. For since the things announced clearly, piercingly, and loudly are heard, they are likened to a trumpet; but since they enlighten the mind, being the eye of the soul, they resemble lightning.

Just as all the divine things are bright and loud for those being benefited by free will and for ourselves, so a warning becomes against those turning back easily; whence it is appropriate to compare the one coming like a lightning bolt to the Lord Almighty blowing the trumpet, that the benefactor might be shaken in warning, with much goodness being presented by God walking in a storm of warning, so that he might not be completely cast out, the warning being at times corrected, as it happened regarding the Ninevites (Jonah 3:4).

For having said the one warning: 'In yet three days Nineveh shall be overturned' (Jonah 3:4), it seemed appropriate to shake them in warning and to cause them to turn, so that the place of repentance, given outside of the warning, might make those who had ceased from what they previously were doing to repent. In this way also Adam, as soon as he heard the voice of his wife being deceived by the serpent, received a sense of a branch of the Lawgiver, so to speak: 'I heard the voice of your feet walking' (Gen 3:11), before the transgression, being present and conversing.

And indeed, [the Lord] is not departing from the Jews when they sincerely kept the law and ministered to the one who gave it, nor has he entirely abandoned them to walk in a storm of warning, saying concerning them: 'I have left my house, I have abandoned my inheritance' (Jer 12:7). The abandonment is clearly shown, Jesus saying in the Gospel: 'Behold, your house is left to you' (Luke 19:42).

The purpose and the end are shown to be for the good of those being left, from the coming of: 'And the Lord Almighty shall go in a storm of his warning,' 'The Lord Almighty shall protect them.' For when it seemed to depart in warning, he helped just so, putting forward for them his invincible shield, concerning which it is said in the Hymns to the one being benefited: 'His truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Ps 5:12). Since it is said nearby how the Lord Almighty blows the blessings by him clearly and loudly, scriptural testimonies regarding this [are gathered]...

The Holy Spirit protects the herald of the truth, raising his voice like a trumpet, so that his teaching, which he brings to war, might rouse those fighting for God against those arrayed militarily against them, and also to call them to the festive assemblies. These things lie in the God-breathed oracles, sometimes with enigma, sometimes in historical narrative.

To show that blowing the trumpet means making things manifest, the words spoken by Jesus to those wishing to give gifts to the poor in the nearby region are sufficient: 'When you do alms, do not sound a trumpet before you.' For he wants this virtue to be practiced in secret, because vainglory is contrary to it and the praise-seeking is clearly performing it; but the command forbidding it is also transgressed: 'What you hate, do not do to another.' For to give gifts to those in need—so I phrase it—is, unfortunately, not to be a friend to the one being benefited, since the giver follows him and does that which he himself does not wish to suffer.

Therefore, when the Lord Almighty enlightens those being helped by him, making manifest what he grants, he blows in a trumpet, defending those well-disposed, so that they may remain unassailable and unharmed, surrounding them clothed in the invincible shield, having put on the whole armor of their ruler and king.

It would also be for us 'to put on the weapons of the light' and 'to take up the shield of faith,' so as to say with boldness: 'You are my help and my defender; my God, do not delay.' [Zach. IX, 15–16: And they shall devour them and subdue them with stones of the sling, and they shall pour out their blood like wine and fill as a bowl for the altar. And the Lord shall save them in that day, as a flock of his people, because the holy stones roll upon his earth.]

God, having set the Jew like a bow and having raised up the sons of Zion against the children of the Greeks, shall be their victory, as the Greek generations are consumed by those raised up against them, like archers straightly casting stones, so that the stone-throwers might be filled, drinking their blood very eagerly by the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shepherd and the Living Stones
english: While they are sling-stoning and filling the altars like bowls.

When the sons of the Greeks suffer the things lying before them, such as being driven into stones and their blood being poured out, the Lord will save such as many as stand guard as having become a people like sheep; for after that, the powerful stones will become movable, having been built up with the divine foundation, so as to roll upon the earth of God, becoming light and movable as the weight and stoniness is lifted from them. For so, rolling upon the holy earth of God, they will build themselves up, harmoniously stepping into the walls of the holy city and the building of the temple of God.
What is meant by the being driven into stones by slings, those being consumed by those standing guard under God the Pantokrator, should be contemplated.

The corrective words of rebuke, like stones sent straight by a sling, will consume the sinners, so that they are no longer enemies of God, the wickedness having been consumed through which they were opposed to the grace of God, after they were struck down by the stones of the sling being made against them. For just as 'love covers a multitude of sins' (1 Pet 4:8) does not allow them to remain, having hidden the sins by making them vanish from all, so the rebuking and corrective words coming upon them, by which they are sling-stoned, will cover them, becoming their covering, the pouring out of the wine-like blood of them being a joy, as to gladden and pour out abundantly those who are pouring, so as to become altars, bowls, vessels of joy serving for use.

For how does one not partake of the divine, he who offers a sacrifice of praise and righteousness? For just as those performing the rite in an improper way cover the altar with tears, the most corrective [voice] saying to them: 'You covered my altar with tears; is it still worthy to look upon your sacrifice, or to receive a gift from your hands?' (Mal 2:13) Let these things be said to those sacrificing after impiety; but to those performing the rite piously, as their sacrifices are to be acceptable, the altars will be bowls making joy, so that, having been made sacred, they may be saved, being revealed in a luminous state, on the intellectual day, when they shall be saved, being transformed into a people of God like sheep.

For the first state of those beginning well and as they ought, is to be led like a flock by the best shepherd, so that after these things, having been promoted from sheep to a people, they might be made kings by the one who was previously their shepherd; those who, after being enriched, shall be a people of the Pantokrator and parts of the city being built by the Lord of Powers.

Stones that were rolling upon the earth of God because they had become hollow and light, being placed upon an immovable foundation, having become stones, build; Peter, the spokesman of the apostles, writes: 'To whom approaching, a chosen precious stone by God, and you yourselves, as living stones, are being built into a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ' (1 Peter 2:5).

If concerning such ones those who give glory say, 'If these should be silent, the stones would cry out,' they proclaim holiness and the glory of God's earth, which all sings to Him, having worshiped Him, according to that which is written in the Psalms, where it says, 'Sing to the Lord, all the earth' (Ps 95:1), and where it says, 'Let all the earth worship you and sing to you' (Ps 66:4).

Taking the 'overflowing like wine' (Zech 9:17), the shoulder and toward slaughter were sought by those being consumed, casting it with the word in battle and in the stance of wars, seven books concerning the wise man.
Zechariah 9:17: That if there is anything good, it is His; and if anything beautiful, it is from Him, grain for youths and fragrant wine for virgins.
