That which is principally acceptable and good exists, and that which is uncontradictedly praised is found, agreeing with the prophetic word in the epistle concerning him: 'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning' (Jas 1:17).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Deception of Baal Prophets and the Drought of Elijah
english: A shadow. Therefore, this one alone gives good things to those asking him, as he is the one whom the soul finds, and as he is the one raising up desire, the Lord, who fills your desire with good things. Faith and knowledge must stand over his giving of the good, so as not to fall into error. For example, thought is a good thing, and a useful good thing is addressed as beautiful.

To say it hymnologically: 'Make good,' learn from the loud-voiced Isaiah to make the beautiful; the Apostle says to hold fast to the beautiful with an apostolic voice: 'Test all things, hold fast to the beautiful, abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thess 5:21). 'For if anything is good, it is of him; and if anything is beautiful, it is from him,' in harmony with 'milk for young men and fragrant wine for virgins' (1 Cor 3:2), and these things are perceived by the sense of fire and the hand. For it is not spiritual and of a soulful man to not receive the things of the Spirit, regarding such things as folly, so that the senses of the inner man are defiled. For how would the sense of smell and taste not be harmed by not tasting the Lord, according to what was said: 'Taste and see that the Lord is good' (Ps 34:8), and the comprehension of the holy breath of his name, according to: 'Myrrh has been poured out for you, therefore the maidens loved you' (Song 1:3)?

Zach. X, 1–3: You ask for rain from the Lord at the right and wrong time; the Lord made visions and winter rain, he will give to each of them vegetation in the field. Because those who utter maxims spoke labors, and the diviners [spoke] false visions...

They spoke false dreams and made vain calls; therefore they were dried up like sheep and were harmed, because there was no healing. My anger was provoked against the shepherds, and I will visit the lambs.

When wickedness prevails, drought occurs often, as God judges; therefore the one raging against such things is to be calmed, lest falling [into error], as if instead of God they were flattering demons; [it is better] to be calmed, as to receive prophecies and dreams from them. Such a deception occurred to the Hebrews in the times of Elijah the great prophet, when rain did not become upon the earth for three years and six months, as all things were driven to despair, as an assurance of death, and other animals were ruined through the scarcity of their fodder.

This harm having prevailed, it was the custom for Israel, having been benefited many times by God in such things, to be surrounded by Him and to ask rain from Him so that prosperity might exist. This they have not done, because deception has prevailed, as those seeking from idols are able to drink [in] what they are not able to provide. And madness came from Jezebel, the wife of the one ruling the Hebrews, being exceedingly an idolater, as she had ensnared him and her husband.

In her days, therefore, the prophets of Baal increased, being an image of the Sidonians, prophesying and uttering [words] and this very thing being found by them being highlighted in dreams, always daring to follow predictive paths, variously lying when favorable weather arrived, so as to no longer ask for the provision of rain, 'that rises the sun upon the good and the bad and rains upon the just and the unjust' (1 Kings 17:14). Since, therefore, those submitted to [me] have fallen into such ignorance, God, taking pity on those thus submitted, cast upon the prophet to say: 'Ask for rain' (1 Kings 18:41).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Prayer for Rain and Spiritual Instruction
english: In a fitting time, 'from the end of the earth He brings clouds and makes lightning into rain' (Jeremiah 31:37), as was prophetically announced in Jeremiah. The word, instilling confidence, exhorts one to ask for rain in its proper season; it brought forth: 'The Lord made a vision and a winter rain.' And not once, but many times from above—unless ungodliness having prevailed among the Hebrews has so much disposed them as to make them unworthy of receiving God-sending gifts.

Since, therefore, God always gives drink to the earth for the sake of men, it is proper to seek Him out when drought occurs, and not to pay attention to false divinations, [the text is broken here regarding the toil and labors of those who speak of dreams and deceivers]. This was held [as it was already said concerning Elijah, a servant of God], a single time; for then and then rain occurred. As it is written regarding Jacob, he addressed [us] by letter, saying: 'Elijah, a man with passions like ours (James 5:17), prayed that it might not rain, and it did not rain for three years and six months,' when drought came upon [the land], to which he added: 'The prayer of a righteous man is powerful in its working (James 5:16).'

From these things being done thus, it is necessary to flee always toward God in times of affliction, and not to pay attention to demonic deceptions, the proof of which has been the seeking of God, which will clearly be [seen] with those in royal histories. Sufficiently, as I think, in accordance with the explicit word of Zechariah, one must also attend to the lifting up. Spiritual rain is the God-given teaching, which has been written thus: 'Let the clouds rain down righteousness' (Zechariah 9:6), by which command is given not to give rain when, allegorically speaking, a vineyard is bearing fruit...
early... late
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: False Prophets and the Wandering Flock
english: "...to us like a preceding and following rain upon the earth." One must understand by thought another preceding rain, which is the word concerning the incarnation of the Savior, and a following one, which is the word concerning his theology. Those who have enjoyed both of these waters say: 'The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14). This same understanding is held by that which was written to the Corinthians by Paul: 'Even if we knew Christ according to the flesh, but now we know him no longer' (2 Cor 5:16). To provide the former answer regarding the two covenants, one should use that: 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, set apart for the gospel of God, which he foretold through his prophets in the holy Scriptures concerning his Son, the one born of the seed of David according to the flesh, and declared to be the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness' (Rom 1:3-4).

A third understanding is also stated: let the things 'known and prophesied in part' (1 Cor 13:12) in this present age be taken as a preceding rain, while the 'face to face' seeing which will be shown in the coming age is the following rain. And let these things also be affectionately spoken: let the corrective discipline of morals and appropriate practical virtue be a preceding watering, while the following one is the knowledge of the mysteries of God the Word.

This double rain will exist, God himself providing it, when we proceed toward knowing the Lord through inquiries and the searching of the God-breathed Scriptures and the training appropriate to unhindered contemplation; for when these have been prepared beforehand, the Lord being sought will be found 'ready as the dawn,' becoming a preceding and following rain to the earth that received the seed of Jesus. For in this way the following things will bear fruit, as the spoken word makes manifest what was previously brought forward: resurrection, life, and perfect knowledge, as it says: 'For it will rain upon us like a preceding and following rain upon the earth. And we shall rise and live and stand before him and know' (Hos 6:3).

Having been filled with these God-breathed good things, the one who has sought the Lord as a weary person will release himself from the sayings of false prophets who are more like dreamers than those seeing actual things. Such are those who have launched heresies into Christianity, 'not understanding either what they say or about whom they affirm things' (Acts 17:21).
"attending to the deceptive spirits and teachings of demons, in the hypocrisy of liars, having cauterized their own conscience."

Those who have cast aside watching and sobriety are carried away by false dreams, being swept along by passion, as they sleep and drink at night; for concerning those who are dreaming and always desiring to slumber, it is written: "Those who sleep at night sleep, and at night they drink," being deprived of the light of the truth. Therefore, even if they ever promise a comforting parable, they call out in vain; for no pasture or herb shall come from their supposed divinatory proclamation. Thus they wither like sheep not having pasture, concerning which the holy man said: "The Lord shepherds me, and I shall not want anything; into a place of green pasture, there He has pitched my tent" (Psalm 23:1-2). And this fertile pasture is found by the one entering and exiting the door, other than that of the Savior who declares: "I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved and will go out and find pasture" (John 10:9).

Being deprived of this, those attending to dreams and false divinations will wither like animals not having feeding-grounds, as they can no longer exist in them being greatly afflicted, the wrath of God being provoked against the faulty shepherds because of their laziness regarding the flock, so that the lambs might be tested by the wrath of God the Shepherd, and the feeding lambs being rebuked and afflicted, just as they themselves will wither along with the gathered sheep.

Indeed, harm has surpassed the flock because of the leaders who fell into ungodliness, about whom God Himself says: "The shepherds were unfaithful to me, and behind useless things they went" (Ezekiel 34:2-10), as they attend to both divination and false dreams being promised, just as the sheep themselves are being harmed, undergoing destruction. For it was most strictly said by Him who tends all: "My people became lost sheep, and their shepherds drove them away," so that the lambs themselves were also afflicted, no longer having the benefit of the feeding pasture. Yet, even if they were thus divided among themselves, through the goodness of the Good Shepherd, the "Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" was set up for them.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shepherd and the Warrior
english: Wherein the prophecy says: 'Like a sheep led to slaughter and like a lamb before its shearer being silent' (Isa 53:7), which the Baptist, having more pointedly as a prophet, said: 'Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). And once the sin of the world having been removed, the sheep having been benefited no longer have drought or kindred evils, nor the lambs whom the speaker visited: 'And my wrath was provoked against the shepherds' (Zech 11:6).

It is also necessary for us to become under the good chief shepherd, who dwells in the place of green pasture for those being shepherded by him, so that entering and going out, applying ourselves inwardly and outwardly to divine words, we may be experienced in blessedness and eternal life. And the Lord God the Pantokrator, being the one who after being angry heals beneficially those who fell by the indignation, will visit his flock, which happens to be the house of Judah, that is to say, of the one confessing; for Judah is interpreted as confessing. The Lord God Pantokrator, being, visits his own flock; concerning which it is also said in Micah: 'And he will stand and see and will shepherd his flock in strength, the Lord' (Micah 2:12), being Savior. And the Lord God the Pantokrator will visit his flock, the house of Judah, and will array them like his well-ordered horse in war (Zech 10:3). And from him he looked, and from him he arrayed, and from him the bow in wrath; from him will go out everyone departing in the same (Zech 10:4). And they shall be as warriors trampling clay in the roads in war and will be arrayed, because the Lord is with them (Zech 10:5).

That the Lord God Pantokrator is the Only-begotten Son of God, this has been demonstrated previously. For the Trinity being of one substance, the one being begotten being of one substance with the one who begotten, the Savior is Lord God Pantokrator from the Lord God Pantokrator. For how could he not be Lord God, 'who was in the beginning with God' (John 1:1)? And just as 'through him all things came to be' (John 1:3), so also he holds and reigns, as to be for this reason Pantokrator. This, then, is the one being theologized, having arrived to find and save the human race, which having fallen like a sheep from the hundred of the rational [beings], like a best shepherd...

He set his own life as a ransom for which he came to save, as if to oversee his own flock, being the house of Judah, concerning which it is said: 'Judah, your brothers shall praise you' (Ps 105:15). And since a rapid change of progress occurs for those being benefited, he arranges those completing his flock, like a fine horse, 'all having been equipped with one mind and one purpose,' as if to become a best charioteer from a shepherd, riding salvationally.

This good has increased by having sent an embassy of those having longing for his arrival, saying: 'Mount the horses, and your riding shall be salvation' (Ps 44:3). From the house of Judah, from a flock having become a fine horse, he looked out and arranged from it a bow, from which he sends arrows, words concerning punishment and threat; concerning which he who arranged the bow said: 'I will satiate my arrows with blood' (Ps 18:14), and again: 'My arrows will complete them.' It was also said previously that punishments are called arrows for some profound reason. In the seventh Psalm, indeed, concerning the judge of all, living and dead, it is said: 'He has bent his bow and prepared it, and in it he has prepared instruments of death; he has worked his arrows for those being burned' (Ps 7:12-13).

What then will happen when the Lord God the Pantokrator looks out from Judah and arranges from it a war-bow, or when those having suffered well by him from the [people] of Judah become experienced warriors of war? He will go out in the same manner, the one going out prepared for war, so that to tread the mud of roads, many falling, as mud shall become from the blood. And this happens to those conquering, but not to those being defeated. For those having turned to flight are pursued and hasten, but those charging and hastening, showing their knees through fear, tread the mud of the blood of the slaughtered, returning like the one going out on horseback.

When these [righteous] ones exist, the Lord their God will be fighting for them and about them, as to say graciously: 'The Lord of strengths is with us, a defender is our God Jacob' (Ps 46:7), and again: 'In God we will do strength, and he will bring to nothing those crushing us' (Ps 46:10).' God with...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The False and True Riders
english: Having confidence in themselves, they will line up against those against whom they have the fight and the war, as each one might say thankfully: 'The Lord is my light and my savior; whom shall I fear? (Ps 27:1) The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I shrink in cowardice? (Ps 27:2) In the approaching of those who do evil to eat my flesh, those who afflict me, and my enemies themselves have grown weak and fallen; (Ps 27:3) if an encampment is lined up against me, my heart shall not fear; (Ps 27:3) if a war rises up against me, in this I hope.' (Ps 27:5).

Having the same courage, he who sings the third Psalm also was emboldened to say: 'I will not fear from ten thousands of people surrounding me.' (Ps 3:6). To those thus arrayed, the word, encouraging them, says: 'One of you shall pursue a thousand, and two shall put ten thousand to flight' (Lk 10:19), not of men alone as warriors, but also of the invisible.

To those having the struggle, those fighting for Christ and having clothed themselves in His good fortune say: 'Our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers and powers and the cosmic dictators of this darkness and the spiritual things of wickedness.' (Eph 6:12). For, having been surrounded by all these warriors, he who, by the designation of God, is like an unassailable shield, trembling with courage, says: 'Encompassing, they have surrounded me, and by the name of the Lord I defended myself against them.' (Ps 18:4). The same thing this one also cries out triumphantly: 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who shall harm me?' (Ps 27:7).

And the riders of horses shall be put to shame. (Zech 10:5) And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will let them dwell, for I have loved them, and in no way will I turn them away, because I am the Lord their God, and I will listen to them. (Zech 10:6) And they shall be as warriors of Ephraim, and their heart shall rejoice as if in wine; and their children shall be seen and shall be glad, and their heart shall rejoice in the Lord. (Zech 10:7)
Those greatly trusting in a cavalry line, when the requirements of war arise from a purpose, [are] shame...

They are being deceived, having learned through experience that 'a false horse is for salvation.' Concerning those fighting in this way, the choir of the saints says: 'These are in chariots and these are on horses, but we shall rejoice in the name of the Lord; they themselves were overthrown and fell, but we have risen and been set upright' (Ps 20:6). Similarly to these, the tyrant of Egypt and all those marshaled with him were dejected when they were crushed in the Red Sea, as a victory hymn began to be sung against them from: 'I will sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored; he has thrown horse and rider into the sea' (Ex 15:1). Concerning these riders, it is also said in one of the Psalms: 'From your rebuke, O God of Jacob, those standing on horses have been unseated' (Ps 68:17).

Who, then, are these who are being overseen? If horses are understood to be human bodies, because they are skittish and unruly, souls are found to be riders who are not disciplined, not skillfully subduing the horses upon which they ride; therefore they also endure shame, being tossed about, as the prophetic word says: 'The riders of horses shall be put to shame' (Ps 68:25). According to another understanding, the pompous and sophistical men were understood to be horses, upon whom evil powers ride in a disorderly manner, not knowing how to guide with reins but being carried by a disorderly force, who, because they approach the four-footed passions unskillfully, shall be put to shame; they fall into pits because they doze and slumber, not enduring the things of those who ride salvationally. For the soul that subdues and leads the body surrounding it is not a mere passenger, nor a rider, but a horseman, skillfully controlling the hooves.

Likewise, certain divine powers, riding with equestrian skill, are carried among the best of men, being carried by the force of divine teaching, having as leader and first-fruit the one whose horsemanship is salvation, concerning whom it is said: 'Mount upon your horses and your horsemanship...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Spiritual Offspring and the Divine Vineyard
english: Salvation. An ancient wise man commanded that horsemen be distinguished from mere riders, calling one false and the other praiseworthy; for he who holds back without skill, not guiding the horse with reins, is merely a rider, as the aforementioned wise man demonstrated, whereas the one practicing the art of horsemanship is called righteous. Immediately, as the great prophet Elijah was being taken up, Elisha the God-inspired one cried out, 'Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!' (2 Kings 2:12). For the one riding most excellently, having guided his own vehicle, ought to be called a horseman, not merely a rider.

Since this distinction between horseman and rider exists, it is not the horsemen but the passengers who will be disgraced, as they slumber while those riding with skill are sober and watchful, guiding the reins; therefore, those proven as victors bring victory, while the passengers of false horses are disgraced. Those of Judah are being disgraced, but the house of Joseph lives and shall be saved by the King of Kings, God; from the parallel of Joseph and Judah, the Savior who became man exists, since from Judah he rose up and provided food to those suffering from famine and starvation, so that he might ultimately be shown to be full of bread, having received the greatest prosperity; for it is said concerning the offspring of Mary that those who previously famished because they lacked spiritual food were filled with good things, which their intelligent Joseph provided. Indeed, he has come to such abundance that, just as in the wilderness he nourished those deprived of food into a flock, he fed large multitudes from very few loaves.

Having strengthened the house of Judah and the house of Joseph, God promises to let them dwell, for no other reason than that he loved them. But when will this be? When they are enjoying what they have; he persuaded them with promises, concerning which it is written here: 'Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it come upon the heart, what God has prepared for those who love him' (1 Cor 2:9). And the promised things shall be for them, in the manner of 'I have not turned them away, but I look upon and care for them,' the Lord being 'their God.' For I will hear of them being exceedingly fruitful according to Ephraim (Hosea 2:14), interpreting fruitfulness as their intellect having eaten and rejoiced, as in wine...

Having been harvested from the true vine, about which much clarity has already been given. What results from the drinking of the divine wine? Or is it to be made glad from beholding the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven and other things which possess a high contemplation, by which one will see God, having approached with a pure heart 'by the character of his subsistence,' as he calls the existing one an 'image' and character 'of the invisible God': 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)?

Not only will these themselves enjoy the promises of the holy visions, but also the children themselves whom they have begotten by divine instruction and imitation of an excellent life. For the Apostle in Christ writes to the Corinthians and the Galatians: to the former, 'Through the gospel I have begotten you' (2 Cor 5:17); to the latter, 'My children, whom I again labor for until Christ is formed in you' (Gal 4:19). And Peter, the foremost of the apostles, writes as to his own children the letter he has engraved: 'As children of obedience, not being conformed to the former manner of life' (1 Pet 1:14). And Barnabas also, an apostle with Paul, having been placed at the circumcision, having sent a letter to the faithful according to the gospel, addresses it as to sons and daughters. And the hymnist addresses those being born from him according to virtue: 'Come, children, listen to me, I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the man who desires life and loves to see good days?' (Ps 33:8).

The children will be made glad in mind, in the heart so named, in no one other than their Lord God, saying to each of those living according to the divine Gospel: 'Enter into the joy of your Lord' (Matt 25:21). 'I will signal them and I will bring them in, because I will redeem them, and they shall be multiplied because they were many; and I will sow them among the peoples, and those far off shall remember me. They shall bring up their children and return. And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and from the Assyrians, and I will bring them in, and into Galilee and into Lebanon I will bring them, and not even one of them shall be left' (Zech 10:8-10). The Lord, intending to bring in those alienated by the manner of captivity, does not do this all at once, but by signaling His benevolence to those receiving it. This—
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Spiritual Multiplication and the Seed of Abraham
english: The practice of contemplation is especially brought forward in the Gospels; for Jesus, desiring to give rest to souls, says, 'Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and you will find rest for your souls; and take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; for my yoke is good and my burden is light' (Matt 11:28-30). By saying, 'Come to me and I will give you rest,' he signifies how he judges them worthy to receive him into himself so that they might lift off his yoke, which is good, and the light burden.

This divine exhortation is also brought forward in Isaiah, with the Holy Spirit crying out: 'Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of your God has risen upon you. Behold, darkness and gloom will cover the earth, but upon you the Lord will appear' (Isa 60:1-2). He emphasized as a sign that it is fitting to be enlightened by the existing true light: 'But upon you the Lord will appear, and the glory of your God will be seen,' signifying how the royal souls, held by the King of all, go forth by the light of the one receiving them, and the called nations into the gospel by the brightness of the glorious Church, as Jerusalem is being led upward, since one sees 'the peace of God surpassing all understanding' (Phil 4:7) through perfect height and royal eminence.

For whose sake does he signify and receive them, saying in harmony: 'Because I will redeem them and multiply them, because they were many' (Hos 2:23)? He redeems them from the law of captivity of shoulders and unclad tyrants who had led them away from their own commonwealth.

The manner and how the restoration to liberty is exalted lies in other writings. Indeed, one of the saints cried out to the benefactor: 'My joy, redeem me from those who persecute me'; and again: 'Redeem me, Lord God of truth.' Peter, the foremost of Christ's disciples, makes manifest a turning away of those who had rushed from their former wickedness, writing to the faithful: 'You were not redeemed from your futile, ancestral way of life with corruptible gold or silver, but in the precious blood of Christ, the lamb without blemish and without spot' (1 Pet 1:18-19). The Savior, having redeemed, promised this.

The statement, 'I will multiply them because they were many,' is necessarily relevant; it refers not only to a multiplication in number, but also to an excellence in honor, similar to the blessing spoken by God toward Abraham: 'I will increase him, and I will multiply him, and I will bless him, and he shall be a blessing; a father of many nations, being revealed as a gift of God.' He becomes a father of many nations not merely according to the flesh, but according to the intelligible, clearly meaning that his children and sons are those who do his works and possess faith.

Indeed, the Savior himself, most strongly rebuking those who claim to have Abraham as a father according to the flesh, said: 'If you are children of Abraham, do the works of Abraham' (John 15:16). By this understanding, 'the vessel of election,' the apostle Paul writes to the Church, clarifying how the holy patriarch is a father of the nations, asserting: 'As many as are of faith, these are sons of Abraham, being blessed with him' (Galatians 3:7). The same view is proposed by that prophecy brought forth in Isaiah: 'The few shall become thousands, and the least a great nation' (Isaiah 60:22).

Taking these things in a sensory way provokes laughter, since many saints did not bear children at all: namely Elijah and Elisha, and John the Baptist, of whom no one greater was praised in deed or holy knowledge; they in no way bore children, so it is appropriate to understand the multiplication of those possessing such promises spiritually, 'because they were many.' For the righteous did not begin to multiply and become many only in this present life, according to the assigned understanding; for they were many even before this present life.

These, being many, were like seeds that he sowed among the peoples so that they might partake of their virtue. Just as seeds thrown into the earth transform the lying soil to become offspring and fruit, so those sown among the peoples and the nations bring those whom they have sown into their own quality, as if becoming imitators of their virtue. No one errs in saying that those who heard were sown by Jesus, saying: 'Go and make disciples of all nations' (Matthew 28:19); and even to the same in the [Gospel] according to John: 'For this reason I said to you,' that is, I appointed and demonstrated, 'that you might go and bear more fruit' (John 15:16), and the fruit...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Migration of the Soul
english: He will be glorified.

I think that in this way the saints are taken captive with the peoples and into Babylon and Assyria, so that by imparting their own virtue they might show themselves to be ears of grain and offspring of saving seeds. This will be consistent with the remembering of the Lord by those who had drifted away from him through sins and impiety. Especially these promises fit those who have believed from the nations. For it has been said concerning them in the 121st and 1st Psalm: 'All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before him, for the kingdom is the Lord's and he is the ruler of the nations.' For how could he not rule and be the master of those remembered who have turned to him, as to worship and glorify the one who holds them as a benefactor?

What will follow for those remembering the All-King, or that it might happen in a non-literal sense regarding 'the city of the living God,' being heavenly, according to what was said: 'You who are far off, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem ascend to your heart.' Those having been benefited by their own Savior, being as it were servants and many-children by spiritual upbringing, will rear their own children, imparting intellectual food, as it is announced concerning each one according to the writing of the divine Proverbs: 'A righteous father brings up his children well.'

This can be understood toward spiritual upbringing, and also according to history; for being a righteous father, Zechariah reared well John the Baptist, who was his child, just as Abraham reared Isaac, and Isaac reared Jacob; and he himself, Paul the divine, reared profitably and praiseworthily those whom he had begotten through the gospel. For it is possible to hear him writing to the Corinthians: 'I gave you milk.' Similarly Peter writes to the faithful in the dispersion: 'Having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible through the word of the living and abiding God, as newborn babes, long for the spiritual milk, so that in it you may grow unto salvation.' In this same way also the evangelist John, having begotten the disciples through him by a way of instruction, writes to the whole Church: 'Children, keep yourselves from idols.' Toward the rearing...

They will find their own children, those who have become fathers, and they will turn them back with divine exhortations and instructions, so that they may no longer be with evildoers in ungodly lands, this being granted by God, as He Himself said: 'I will bring them back from Egypt, and from the Assyrians I will receive them' (Exodus 20:22; Jeremiah 31:8), so that they may no longer be subdued by the spiritual tyrant of Egypt, nor be held by the ruler of the Assyrians, called 'the great mind' because of the cunning and absurdity of thoughts, which the common people do not refute, but only those speaking God-wisely say: 'For we do not ignore his thoughts.'

It is possible to call the same tyrant the ruler of the Egyptians and the Assyrians through another energy; and even if different evil powers were signified by various names, it does not grieve, for such a thing is not impossible, with many being 'rulers and powers of this darkness, but also cosmic rulers and spiritual wickedness' (Ephesians 6:12).

The provider of great gifts, having freed from Egypt and Assyria those who are well-rearing their children and those who begot them, promises to bring them into Gilead and Lebanon, with no evil king still bothering them. And see if he brings into Gilead those who strive to have the migration of martyrdom, the movement from wickedness into virtue; for the one repenting from sin into righteousness, from ungodliness into godliness, is being migrated, as the righteous are being migrated in a different way from the introduction of instruction into the following progress, and from that into the succeeding one, until that very end, with which nothing other good exists, being the final object of desire.

In this way, concerning those being migrated, the hymnist says: 'They shall go from strength to strength' (Psalm 84:7). And they are also migrated from the shadow of the law into its truth, those having ascended above the killing letter (2 Corinthians 3:6) and becoming in the life-giving Spirit. It must be supervised whether even a partial knowing and prophesying undergoes migration; but the witness of the migration or sojourning shall be, acting contrary to itself, possessing the proof. Those brought in by God into Gilead are being brought into Lebanon.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fragrance of Divinity and the Unity of the Fullness
english: Having been made divine: for the Lebanon declares divinity in what was said by the divine bridegroom to the divine bride cohabiting with him, who was being a divine soul and an 'exalted Church' most intensely regarded as 'having no more a wrinkle or a line or anything of this sort' (Song of Songs 4:7); 'The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.' This could be said toward each of those having been made divine through participation in the God the Word, concerning whom it was said by the Savior: 'He called those gods to whom the word of God became' (Psalm 82:6). 'The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.' In the plural, garments are virtues by type, with which 'the queen standing at the right hand' of the all-king bridegroom is adorned.

It has been said to wise men that the divinity which the Magi brought to the child born of Mary, with gold and myrrh and frankincense, is shown by such a thought: since the one born of the virgin is simultaneously God and man, but also is a king, according to the one confessing his divinity, it is fitting to bring frankincense as a gift, and to present gold along with this frankincense because he confesses him as king. For it is said in the seventy-first Psalm, and that the one who has arrived is king and gold is presented to him, thus: 'Give the king his due judgment' (Psalm 71:11), and with other things: 'And he shall live and gold shall be given to him from the Arabia' (Psalm 72:10). In truth, and not by opinion, the one being glorified as a man will not be [divine] because he is mortal and is destined 'by the grace of God to be above all death' (Romans 6:9), and myrrh was presented among the gifts. This gift declares that he has been buried, the one who has overcome all death. Likewise, those around Joseph and Nicodemus perfumed with myrrh the body of Jesus which was brought from the cross.

When the great-giver God has brought into Gilead and Lebanon those redeemed from Pharaoh and from the Assyrian, no one of the enemies remains any longer, not in being—for it is impossible to turn a rational essence into non-being, even if he sins and acts impiously in all things and greatly—but in no longer being an enemy and an adversary to those redeemed by God. Most especially this will be when 'God is all in all' (1 Cor 15:28) becomes, 'for all having met the perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ,' 'having been perfected in the same mind and the same purpose,' of whom the Son said to the Father: 'Give to them that they may be one in us, just as I and you are one' (John 17:21). Namely, of all having received the fullness of divinity, no one remains any longer divided from the union as being outside and by himself. 'For then all sorrow, pain, and sighing will depart' (Rev 21:4), the multitude according to number will also depart, into one man of all those having met.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Allegory of the Net and the Sea
english: They shall glory in the Lord their God, and in his name, says the Lord (Jeremiah 9:24).

Continuously in the divine words, the manner of the earth and the cosmic movement of the sea are brought forward. The evangelical parable concerning the net indicates nothing sensible, all of it pronouncing an ascent; for the net cast into human life upon a field of the fishes in it, so named allegorically, is the God-breathed scripture, manifoldly woven by 'the manifold wisdom of God.' But the sea is the condition regarding us, widening and broadening for the greedy and the passion-loving, near to those remaining in the motionless; for the fish does not leave a voice, nor does it have a distinct appearance, since even its sensation is not precise.

Even if the fishes being caught by it have nothing manifest, because of the weakness of their soul and sensation, nevertheless the holy men, being fishermen and catchers of fishes, do work and in the multitude of the water of the sea. Concerning them indeed it has been written in divine hymns: 'Those descending into the sea in ships, doing work in many waters, they themselves saw the works of God and his wonders in the depth.'

Human lives descend into the surging, salt-filled swell in human ships, which are bodies, in order to do work in many waters, fishing and steering; for each of the intelligent ones has steering, being one of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. For it has been said that 'the comprehension and the steering' of the Holy Spirit is a gift. In being a pilot, the intelligent one and fisherman exists, having that art about which Jesus said to the known ones: 'Come after me and I will make you fishers of men' (Matthew 4:19).

Those doing work in many waters see the works of the Lord and his wonders in the depth, approaching as if to the judgments of God, encountering a great abyss. For even if they are unsearchable, but having the Spirit of God who searches its depths, they see in the depth the wonders and works of God.

See also another work of those descending into the sea, being announced in the prophet Isaiah: 'They shall be cast in ships of foreigners, they shall manage the sea at once' (Isaiah 23:3); saying ships of foreigners regarding the bodies because they are of a different nature from the souls that are sailing, being substances not of intellect, and this very thing according to...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sea and the Dragon
english: having been created in the image and likeness of God. But these [false teachers] manage the sea, hunting the dragon within it, taking from it those souls which they have deceived by a deceptive and misleading teaching. Regarding how the dragon dwells in the sea, the hymnographer in the 103rd Psalm is proclaimed, saying: 'This sea is great and spacious, where ships travel, small creatures along with large ones, this dragon which you made to play with it.' (Psalm 103:26).

One must observe that whereas here the sea is great and spacious for those who dwell with the dragon, it is narrow for those rushing out of it. For just as the gate is narrow and the road is compressed for the righteous who seek eternal life, and a wide and spacious road exists for the wicked and the greedy, leading many into destruction, so also the allegorically interpreted sea is found narrow 'for those afflicted in everything' through godliness 'and not being distressed,' as it is said with conviction: 'That through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom.' (Acts 14:22).

The waves of the interpreted sea are beaten down by the one ruling and holding it, to whom the saints are said to cry out: 'You rule the dominion of the sea and you calm the surge of its waves.' (Psalm 93:4).

Jesus established this both perceptibly and intellectually, rebuking the foaming sea according to the apostolic vessel and the wind that had raised its waves, so that immediate calm and clarity might occur, with the water and air becoming still.

When the waves of the sea were allegorically rebuked, the depths of the rivers were also made dry, concerning which the king of Egypt, named dragon because of his venomous and serpent-like nature, stumbling, said: 'The rivers are mine, and I made them.' (Exodus 14:12). Those having experienced the sea being narrowed, its waves being beaten down, and the depths of the rivers being dried up, approaching the one who accomplished these things, they return a hymn of thanks, saying thus: 'He who turns the sea into dry land, they shall walk in a river on foot,' which makes manifest the drying of their depths and the beating down of the sea's waves.
When the waves of the sea are beaten down and all the depths of the rivers are made dry, the insolence of the Assyrians is destroyed, and the scepter of Egypt shall be taken away, no longer...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Strength in Christ vs. Assyrian Pride
english: The [reigning power] is [at stake], and the insolence of the Assyrians prevails. For both types of insolence exist: some through being slanderers, others through being arrogant and insulting out of pride.

When the opposing forces are destroyed, those traveling through a narrow sea are strengthened by their Lord God, each saying thankfully, 'The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation' (Exodus 15:2). And again, 'I will love you, Lord, my strength' (Exodus 15:2). Likewise, Jeremiah says to God, 'My strength and my help and my refuge, Lord my God' (Jeremiah 33:2). The same is said by the hymn-singer and prophet Jeremiah, and Paul, speaking in Christ, writes most powerfully, 'I can do all things in him who strengthens me' (Philippians 4:13).

Once the insolence of the Assyrians is removed and the kingdom of the Egyptians is destroyed, being armed with the beneficial appellation, they boast against those being overthrown, except each one saying, 'May it never be to me to boast except in the cross of Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me and I to the world' (Galatians 6:14). For the world having been crucified so that it no longer operates, being prevented from where it wishes to go and doing what it loves, the servant of Christ is crucified to it, so that even though his feet and hands are prevented from operating, he will unceasingly boast, declaring, 'I have been crucified with Christ.'

He who possesses this confidence bravely in Christ boasts according to what was said, 'Let him who boasts boast in the Lord' (1 Corinthians 1:31); for one who does not boast cannot, in a psychic or somatic way, or even regarding things external, boast in anything of his own. For all these things have been forbidden: 'For let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong in his strength, nor the rich in his riches, but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows the Lord, to do righteousness and justice in the midst of the earth' (Jeremiah 9:23-24).

This same voice, the mother of the prophet Samuel sent up, thanking for the birth of a child born contrary to expectation, only substituting prudence for wisdom. And there also exist for us brave deeds from God, so that we may give thanks to the generous one who desired them.

Having sufficiently described also the third word concerning the prophet Zechariah, there we may rest, entreating the God who increases visions 'to give a word in the opening of the mouth' (Zechariah 1:17), toward the following, as if to clarify, if it should seem good to him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegorical Interpretation of Animals
english: Having a wisdom according to God, a well-structured and very precise understanding, one says: 'You shall speak a parable and a dark saying to men of understanding and riddles.' For words spoken with concealment turn out to be riddles. Likewise, the present word of the prophet, being brought forth enigmatically, brings forth a concealed teaching. An enigma is this: 'Open, Lebanon, your gates' (Song of Solomon 4:1).

For it is not toward the perceptible mountain, which is soulless, nor the woods within it according to sense and imagination, that the command is made, so that the gates of Lebanon might be opened and the fallen cedars of the pines might crash; but toward men, arrogant and proud, falling into lawless idolatry toward 'the ruler of this age' (Matthew 13:38).

Incorporeal powers... wisdom... promised... to understand... the mortal rational animals and the other rational beings moved by word. But when trees and wild woods... the man who became like God in image and likeness, who had honor from the Creator, was joined with the creatures that are without understanding, God-fearing and lovers of pleasure, having become passionate... from these things the prophetic word says: 'Donkeys became lustful, each one toward the wife of his neighbor' (Hosea 14:4), regarding all divine things and the presiding divine reason.

'Do not become like a horse and a mule which have no understanding' (Psalm 32:9), the horse being an analogy for one who lacks restraint, devouring the marriages of others and violently mounting foreign women. The fool proven to be turned toward [sensual] things shall be called a mule, and especially the soul promising virginity without...
of understanding. For a certain foolish woman, even if she seems to be cleansing her body, she is an adversary rather than a bride of the Word.

There are many names of animals applied loosely to humans, such as donkeys and camels, called so because they bear the burdens of wickedness, being imposed upon them by predatory demons and opposing powers. The great prophet Isaiah, taking up such things, said, 'their wealth is upon donkeys and camels' (Isaiah 61:7). For these things thus announced are not historical, having the understanding by way of allegory. And the Savior, protecting his own disciples, says allegorically, 'not to give the holy thing to dogs nor to cast pearls before swine' (Matthew 7:6). For dogs and swine are flatterers and lovers of pleasure, rejoicing with the lawless, the filth of the gods.

For the dog is a lowly animal, shamelessly approaching with lustful hands, being both a flatterer and a provocateur. Does not he who reviles the Pelasgian provoke in a way, buzzing with accusations? Concerning such men, the loud-voiced Isaiah has cried out: 'All are dogs, not knowing understanding, and they are evil' (Psalm 22:16). Just as such men are dogs, having other evils toward others, and the swine were those washed from the filth of the passions, and again curling themselves to them.

Concerning those having such a mind, the great disciple of Christ Peter writes thus: 'It had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than having known, to turn back to the things behind from the holy commandment delivered to them. There happened to them that of the true proverb: a dog returning to its own vomit, and a sow washed into a rolling in the mire' (2 Peter 2:22; Proverbs 9:1). To such men, the holy [one] said, to give...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Allegory of Lebanon
english: The Savior makes those who return from the evil they lived in to become followers of repentance regarding the sin they cast away. Just as it is not necessary to share the holy knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven with such people, so it is not fitting to compare the divine pearls—which are the words of the wise, decorating the inner man and his ears—to swine.

Does not the one disciplining them not feel insulted by the one saying, 'Compare with wise words your ear' (Prov 23:26), and by the one saying to the Word of God, 'Incline your ear to the words of my mouth' (Ps 89:8)? One must not compare the most beautiful and fine pearls, which the merchant of the kingdom seeks and hunts, to the interpreted swine, so that they do not trample them, having ignored their use and their beauty.

Having set forth testimonies to show that men have been treated as senseless, fake animals, it remains to set forth the Scriptures, showing how some men are praiseworthy in being similar in disposition and movement to certain animals. Are not these the very ones about whom the Savior says, 'My sheep hear my voice' (John 10:27), and again, 'I am the good shepherd and I lay down my life for the sheep' (John 10:11)?

The sheep of Christ are those establishing stability and gentleness, from whom the flock is completed, concerning which the Holy Spirit says through the prophet, 'And the Lord shall stand and see and shall shepherd his flock in strength' (Ezek 34:23). By such an analogy of 'the vessel of election' (2 Tim 3:15), Paul, speaking in Christ, took up the law 'you shall not muzzle an ox while it treads' (Deut 25:4), after setting it forth and bringing it in: 'Does God not care for the oxen? Or does he speak in any way about us?' (1 Cor 9:9), as the apostles make clear: 'that the plowman ought to partake of the plowing, and the one muzzling in hope of sharing' (1 Cor 9:10).

Finding many such things by the one paying attention to the reading of the God-breathed Scripture, lest the word be stretched beyond what is necessary, let him proceed regarding the Frankincense and its woods, having it thus: 'Open, O Frankincense, your doors, and let fire devour your cedars; let the pine wail, because the cedar has fallen, because the great princes have greatly suffered' (Zach 11:1-2).
You have been uprooted, oaks of Bashan, because the adjacent forest has been scattered.

The name Lebanon, for the sake of allegory, signifies either idolatry or pride and arrogance. For in the Song of Songs, the Church from the Gentiles is the bride of Christ; he says, 'Come from Lebanon, O bride, to ascend and pass through from the beginning of faith' (Song of Songs 4:17). Having received the word of Christ from the beginning, she comes to the one calling her from practical wickedness into moral virtue, and from ignorance and unbelief into a divine knowledge and a faith surpassing all through perfection.

Just as the spoken word 'Lebanon' signifies the impious service of idols and demons, so it represents pride in the saying, 'Lebanon shall be changed like Mount Hermon,' which is to say, the haughty and self-willed person shall be brought to the knowledge of the circumcision being led into the heart by the spirit; for Hermon is interpreted as the knowledge of circumcision. He who possesses this knowledge corrects his blindness, having learned from Jesus to be humble in heart and spirit.

By this twofold Lebanon, the prophet, who is inspired by the Spirit—rather, the Lord through him—calls out to open its doors, so that the cedars within the doors of it may be devoured by fire; and these are the idle demons and the haughty men, being crushed by the voice of the Lord, according to how it is sung in the 18th and 20th Psalm in this manner: 'The voice of the Lord crushing cedars; the Lord shall crush the cedars of Lebanon' (Psalm 28:16).

Since these are wild plants and do not bear edible fruit, in Isaiah it is written concerning others thus: 'The day of the Lord of hosts upon every arrogant and proud and high and lofty thing,' and after a few words: 'and upon every high cedar of Lebanon and upon every balsam tree of Bashan' (Isaiah 13:11). These such wild woods are grown up for idolatry and pride, being crushed and consumed by fire along with those who assemble sophistically about them, according to what is said in the same Isaiah: 'And the Lebanon shall fall with the lofty ones' (Isaiah 2:12).
For idolatry falls along with the demons who assemble with it and with sophist men; likewise also the haughty ones.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Oak and the Doors of Lebanon
english: Men with arrogance will fall when God opposes the proud, according to what is said in the writing of the Divine Proverbs: 'God opposes the proud' (Proverbs 16:5).

Regarding those thus exalted, those who are making blindness right through God send up a prayer, saying: 'Stretch out your hands against their pride to an end,' and with other things in the same Psalm: 'The pride of those hating you continually shall ascend to you' (Psalm 18:5).

Concerning the Lebanon which is given a double meaning, the divine word stands to open its gates. For when pride and idolatry have been opened and spread out, the fire of punishment will consume the cedars—those men who were exalted and the demons who look down upon others, not being other than 'the rulers of this age,' human and, as the Scripture says, 'fleshly wisdoms' (2 Corinthians 10:5), teaching 'heights puffed up according to the knowledge of God' (2 Corinthians 10:5).

When the cedars are devoured by fire, the firs lament, falling because of the stronger ones called cedars. And perhaps the unspiritual evil powers are called cedars, with the firs being the names of the heterodox and wise of this world and age who work under them.

The enigmatically spoken thing is released by the following word: 'Greatly the magnates were afflicted.' These are the ones swelling at the beginning, not men alone, but also the unspiritual rulers of this age.

Concerning these arrogant leaders, and in Nahum the prophet—and this is the seventh among the Twelve Prophets—it is said to Nineveh: 'And upon your glorious things they shall cast a lot, and all your magnates shall be bound in fetters' (Nahum 2:9), so that they might not do the forbidden things with easy release and hands not hindered; for it is for good to be hindered by 'hands entwined with iniquities.'

Having been greatly afflicted, the Basanite trees, the intertwined grove is torn down; and a grove is a place of wild trees bearing no nourishing fruit. And this is torn down, as its thickened vegetation is consumed by fire.
Lamenting trees do not turn out to be soulless plants, but, being led up allegorically, the souls of men who...

And opposing powers. It is not to be ignored that oaks, at times, signify all kinds of wood, and at other times a specific kind of wood. For when we call all woods oaks, the one cutting them is called a wood-cutter, and those made from them are called oak-wood, from which the name for oak-planks is derived, and the fruits of trees are called acorns. Regarding the general name, there is a specific kind of wood that is an oak, just like cypress, fir, or boxwood.

The doors of Lebanon, which the divine word protects from being opened, are the same as those of death, concerning which the singer in the ninth Psalm says about God: 'He lifts me up from the gates of death' (Psalm 9:13). Regarding these, as being the presence of evil, it is proverbially said to the wise: 'Do not approach the doors of her house' (Proverbs 7:18), and also concerning all false glory and impiety: 'A foolish and impudent woman becomes a loud-mouthed vessel, who does not know shame; for she sat on a seat by the doors of her own house, openly calling to those passing by' (Proverbs 9:13).

He who has drawn near to these doors strikes the doors about which the Savior said: 'Knock and it shall be opened to you' (Matthew 7:7), concerning which Wisdom says in Proverbs: 'Blessed is the man who listens to me, and the man who keeps my ways, staying awake at my doors every day, guarding the weights of my entrances' (Proverbs 8:34).

He who stays awake at these doors every day does not approach the doors of the prostitute and foolish woman who pretends, nor the doors of Lebanon which ought to be opened, the perceived security being destroyed, so that those lying within may appear as to what formlessness they possess, being hated and abandoned, for no one who wishes to see them is sober.

That which has been said concerning various woods is not spoken about soulless things, and it can be seen from many scriptures, especially prophetic ones, the exposition of which has already partially occurred; but it is sufficient to remember the prophet Ezekiel, as if Pharaoh and Assyria were woods. These are evil powers, the one the tyrant of Egypt and the other of Assyria, having roots and shoots raised up from much water, which, in imitation, envied the trees of the paradise of the enjoyment of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ruin of False Leaders
english: Having large branches, imitating both firs and pines.

For how could they desire and imitate such great tyrants, to the point where it is possible to perceive them as tangible woods, in whose side-branches and limbs all winged creatures dwell and wild beasts give birth? In order that the prophecy might be easily understood, we set aside a part of it, having it as follows: 'Behold, an Assyrian cypress in Lebanon, and beautiful in its side-branches, and thick in its cover, and high in its greatness; and its beginning became in the midst of the clouds; water nourished it, the abyss raised it up, its rivers led around the plants of it, and its systems sent forth into all the woods of the plain. Because of this, its greatness was raised above all the woods of the plain, and its branches were enlarged and its side-branches were raised up from much water. In the spreading out of it in its side-branches, all the winged creatures of the heaven sheltered, and under its branches all the beasts of the plain gave birth, and in its shadow every multitude of nations dwelt' (Ezekiel 31:3). And it became beautiful in its height because of the multitude of its branches, because its roots became into much water. And many cypresses in the paradise of God and pines are not like its side-branches, and firs did not become like its branches; no wood in the paradise of God was made like it in its beauty because of the multitude of its branches, and the woods of the paradise of the enjoyment of God envied it.

The same or similar things have been said regarding what was spoken about Assyria and about Pharaoh. It should not be ignored that most of our brothers refer Pharaoh and Assyria to the devil, allegorizing them according to various thoughts, sometimes Pharaoh and sometimes Assyria. Those bringing this interpretation, let them say: what are the woods of the paradise that envied the devil, not being soulless but being living, rational animals, clearly? And it is nothing wonderful that the names of woods are categorized among rational animals, when even the wisdom of God is sometimes called a true vine, and sometimes the Tree of Life. The voice of weeping shepherds, because... (Zechariah 11:3).
Their greatness has been brought to misery; it is the roar of lions, because the thicket of the Jordan has been ruined.

The leaders of the peoples, who are shepherds of them both priestly and teaching-wise, turn out to be like sheep, while there are those presiding kingly rather than tyrannically as lions. And since both types of rulers are called shepherds and lions, it is necessary for all the subjects to be brought as sheep and other cattle, having a tendency toward the shepherds who graze, and toward the lions for the cattle. It has been said indeed in Proverbs: 'A lion is stronger than cattle, who does not turn away nor falls upon every cattle' (Proverbs 28:17).

Having fallen into misery, those under the teachers—rather, false teachers—and those lying tyrannically over them, the shepherds lament, not being sparing of the flocks, but having been deprived of shameful gains and for the sake of seizing pleasures, so that they might not serve the Law-giving God and Him who has given them to rule, but rather their own bellies.

Concerning the heterodox, the divinely-inspired Apostle writes, correcting the peoples of the Church: 'Do not be carried away by strange and varied teachings; for it is good to be established by grace' (2 Timothy 3:6-7), and again: 'For such teachers serve their own bellies, not Christ, deceiving the hearts of the simple through exploitation and greed' (2 Timothy 3:6-7), appearing as pastures through simplicity.

These, having suddenly come into perplexity, lament the things they desire to be pleasant, their greatness having been brought to misery, which they thought they had deceitfully; likewise also those who rule tyrannically roar, the Jordan having been ruined where they spoke and were hidden, thinking they had cover and safety through ferocity.
With many woods already being cut down and having been torn apart, as it has been said nearby, the adjacent forest is being torn apart.

Much is to be found in the Scripture signifying those presiding with raw and wild temper, being called lions approaching in judgment. Immediately indeed in the prophet Jeremiah, lions are said to be the hot-tempered ruler of Babylon and the tyrant of Assyria; and thus the prophecy has: 'Israel is a wandering sheep, lions have driven him; the first the king of Assyria devoured him, and later his bones the king...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Wickedness of Unfaithful Shepherds
english: One must avoid this way of thinking, as the seventy-first Psalm regarding men and evil powers says: 'Their wrath is like the likeness of a serpent, like a deaf and plunging shield whose ears will not hear the voice of a singer or a pharmacist being medicated by a wise man. God crushed their teeth in their mouth; the molars of lions the Lord has broken' (Ps 68:15). For we do not think it pleasant to suppose only the molars of the sensory lions are being crushed by God, while all their bodies remain without harm.

Thus says the Lord of Hosts: 'Shepherd the sheep of the slaughter, which those who owned them were slaughtering and did not care, and those selling them said: Blessed is the Lord and we have become rich, and their shepherds suffered nothing upon them' (Zech 11:4-5).

Regarding those appointed to instruct and shepherd the rational flock, some preside according to the will of God, while others preside impiously and erringly. Concerning both of the ranks of shepherds, it is possible to gather testimonies from the Scripture.

Concerning those who excellently perform the oversight they were handed, it is said by God: 'I will give to them'—clearly to the flocks—'shepherds according to my heart, and they shall shepherd them, shepherding with knowledge' (Jer 3:15). Concerning those who thus shepherd the flock with knowledge, the Christ-bearing Apostle remembers those placed in the Church with the apostles and prophets, as teachers and evangelists. And perhaps apostles and prophets, teachers and evangelists, are those who gnostically and prudently instruct the assembly of Christ, shepherding those possessing a practical life and presiding over good works, not unskillfully returning the faith and the understandings of Christians, while those who oppose the skilled shepherds through faultiness are named impious; the God...

For he says regarding them and that other wickedness is at work: 'The priests did not say: Where is the Lord?' And those holding to my law did not believe me, and the shepherds were impious toward me,' and the following.

4.52 Those impious in this way and fornicators turn out to be, perhaps also licentious, but certainly also mixing with diverse and foreign doctrines, they subject [people] to demons and to 'the wisdoms of the rulers of this age' (Eph 2:2). Immediately, for instance, 'those not having tested God to have in knowledge, having been handed over to a reprobate mind (Rom 1:28), do what is not fitting, licentiously reproaching one another, men performing indecency with men, but also their females having abandoned the natural use of womanhood contrary to nature and suffering, but also women licentiously approaching women.'

4.53 Regarding the impious shepherds' sensual licentiousness toward God, and lusting with evil powers, according to that which is said in the Psalms toward the provider of piety: 'Behold, those distancing themselves from you shall perish, you having destroyed all the fornicating one from you. But for me to cling to God is good' (Ps 73:2).

4.54 Concerning the impious law-keepers, in Jeremiah it is brought as being announced toward the fornicating soul: 'And you had many shepherds as a hindrance to yourself' (Jer 2:36), and also: 'You have fornicated with many shepherds; and you returned pretending toward me, says the Lord' (Jer 2:8).

4.55 Having separated the good law-keepers from the handlers, a command is given to those who are skilled, having this character: 'Shepherd the sheep of the slaughter,' either those already slaughtered or those worthy of this suffering or those unjustly being plotted against. The latter is shown in the one hundred and nineteenth Psalm, of those being plotted against unto death, saying toward the benefactor God: 'Because of you we are being killed all the day, we were counted as sheep of the slaughter' (Ps 119:71), and also: 'You gave us as sheep for food' (Ps 119:75).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Mercy of the Creator and the Judgment of the Shepherds
english: For they are not slaughtered by the lawless overseers for any other reason or to be eaten, regarding which it is said, 'If men rise up against us, then they would have eaten us alive' (Ps 116:6). But they failed in their murderous haste to say graciously, like those who were rescued, 'Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us into the trap of those pursuing Him' (Ps 116:6).

Those who think they are owners and not shepherds of the flocks entrusted to them, slaughtering the sheep with a knife—and this is their sophistical discourse, proclaiming impious attitudes—did not regret or repent for what they acted in robbery and murder. For they carelessly sell those things which are not their own as if they were theirs, and with shameless audacity they shout that they have grown rich, while those who strive to please the one who deems the All-King to be the shepherd of the flock do not slaughter nor prevent those which the sheep logically entrusted, so that they might unjustly grow rich from greed and shameful gains.

In order that such a thing might not happen through the inattention of the overseers of the Church, the proclaimer of the apostles, Peter, cries out, thus writing: 'I exhort the elders among you to shepherd the flock that is among you, not by compulsion but willingly, not exercising dominion over the appointed ones, so that, when the Chief Shepherd, Christ Jesus, is revealed, you may receive the unfading crown of glory' (1 Pet 5:2-4); meaning those who exercise dominion, namely the sheep of Christ, while the negligent shepherds are acting, selling for shameful gains the divine flocks so that they shout, 'We have grown rich,' devouring those whom they lift up through scandals.

Thus, having harmed and done evil to the peoples, the sheep allegorically called, their false shepherds suffered nothing from them, not sympathizing with the flock according to the one saying: 'Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is stumbled, and I am not burned?' (Rom 15:1). Into this love the divine instructors are led by the Savior becoming a pattern for them, as the God-wise Evangelist John calls out to those who worship God according to Christ: 'That He,' clearly that Christ, 'set His soul as a ransom for us, and we owe to lay down our souls for one another' (1 John 3:16).
Those having such a mind toward those who embrace the same and think the same, being brothers sympathetic, [to] those slaughtering the...

The sheep handed over to them oppose those who speak with insolence, saying: 'We have become rich; we have acquired sheep through shameful gain, and having devoured them, we suffer very little because of them.' (Zach. XI, 6–7: 'Therefore I will no longer spare those inhabiting the land, says the Lord, and behold, I am handing over men every man to the hand of his neighbor and to the hand of his king, and they shall cut down the land, and I will by no means come out of their hand.' And I shepherd the sheep of the slaughter toward Canaan.)

Since those entrusted with the care of the logical sheep despised them, neither sympathizing with nor caring for their salvation, but selling them to strangers through shameful gain, the Lord Almighty threatens no longer to spare the land, that is, those dwelling upon it, handing over the weaker ones to the tyrants through whom they suppose to have strength and brutality, so that all those upon the land may be cut down, handing over every man into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king, no longer by lawful means but by tyrannical rule.

God repeats these things in the manner of a threat, so that those toward whom the threat is directed may cease from sinning through the fear of what is expected. For God never fails his own works, as the all-virtuous Wisdom of Solomon says: 'Spare all, O Despot, soul-loving one, loathing nothing of what you have made, for you did not fashion anything in hatred.' 'For you created for the sake of being, and the generations of the world are salvific.'

Having experience of this exceeding goodness of Him who has composed all things and provides for all things, those who serve Him bring a petition on behalf of the people, saying: 'Spare, Lord, your people, and do not give your inheritance to the ruin of the nations that will begin to prevail over them, lest the nations say: Where is their God?'
To such an extent did the Cause and Guardian of all spare the race of men, as to give His Son as a ransom for all, into death, so that He might redeem those dying by reigning over death.
The Apostle, becoming a mystagogue of this exceeding salvation, writes concerning God: 'He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Rods and the One Shepherd
english: Him—how will He not also grant all things with Him to us? Sparing us, He did not withhold the Son; for He is impassible and the destroyer of all harm, but we are mortals and subject to passions. Therefore, if He had been sparing of the Son, not having given Him up to 'taste death for all' (Hebrews 2:9), we would have remained in the ruin that holds fast through the transgression of the divine commandment; but so that we might be set free, the guardian gave up His own Son, not to be harmed by dying, having been revealed as Savior, having been given up for them.

Having these things thus, if God says: 'I will no longer spare those dwelling on the earth,' He admonishes by the fear of threat, so that they might not fall by being executed, but might come out of the sin that holds fast, no longer being subject to execution. He makes manifest the manner of not sparing anymore, saying 'to deliver men into the hands of their neighbors and into the hands' of the 'evil king whom they chose, so that the earth might be cut off' (Isaiah 17:1), as they oppose one another as 'men who are dying.' These are those walking according to the flesh in strife and jealousy. Men who are such are delivered into the hands of those whom they had as neighbors, [namely] demons, through greed and material disposition. For then they are most able to be admonished, having been delivered to those whom they thought were friends and neighbors, having been tested by their coarseness and ferocity; and they will flee also from the one who rules tyrannically, having experienced his hardness. For even the people of the Hebrews desired in such a way to be set free from the insolence of the Egyptians, having known their turbulence and their lawless dominion.

When the earth is cut off, that is, when those upon it are revolting, God shepherds the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan, the prepared punishment. It was also said previously that the sheep of the slaughter are those ready to suffer and those already slaughtered, when we received that which was being reported by the afflicted to the Benefactor of all: 'You gave us as sheep for eating' (Psalm 50:5), and again: 'We were counted as sheep for slaughter' (Psalm 50:6). Understand whether the shepherding of the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan denotes something praiseworthy, being interpreted as the prepared [place], perhaps of those being led in through being managed by harm.

Working out an unchangeable salvation through pains brought on pedagogically, about which the law-giving apostle Paul writes, marking these things: 'The godly sorrow works out unchangeable repentance unto salvation, bringing about the death of the sorrow of the world' (2 Cor 7:10). Therefore, this [worldly sorrow] must be rejected, but the godly one must be unchangeably opposed, bringing about salvation according to God.

4.71 Zechariah 11:7: 'And I will take for myself two rods—the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Union—and I will shepherd the sheep. And I will separate the three shepherds in one month, and my soul will be burdened by them, for their souls were pressing upon me. And I said, I will not shepherd you.' 4.72 From the person of the Savior, the prophet Zechariah 11:21 announces the things concerning the two rods which he had taken for himself.

4.73 Nothing else is signified in the passages concerning the rods except a scepter of rule, rather a symbol of kingship. 4.74 Since therefore the whole human race is divided into the people from the circumcision and into the Church called from the Gentiles, the God of the Jews and the Gentiles, being both Savior and King of them, took for himself the two scepters, so that from both he might work out one kingship.

4.75 And the prophecy will be understood from the evangelical utterance; for just as one kingship was shown under one king from those having believed among the Gentiles and the Jews, so also one flock is shown under one shepherd, the true one, who has set his soul down for the sheep. Thus the evangelical voice is announced by the Savior: 'And I have other sheep which are not of this fold; them also I must bring together, and they will hear my voice, so that there will become one flock and one shepherd' (John 10:16), saying that the other sheep are to be those from the Gentiles believing in the Gospel, not from the Jewish fold.

4.76 It is the same thing, the two flocks becoming under one shepherd, as it is the two scepters coming under the same king. But when will this be fulfilled? Perhaps when it happens: 'Rejoice, O nations, with his people' (Zech 9:7)? 4.77 And it is also said differently: 'And I have other sheep which are not of this fold,' the fold being called that of the sheep of this earthly world in which those bearing the body are wearing out [their lives], being delivered...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Three False Shepherds and the Soul
english: These souls, having dwelt in the underworld until now, are gathered just as the good shepherd gathers them, having come to them when he 'died for all' in order that 'he might rule over the living and the dead.' If one rules the living and the dead with royal power and pastoral knowledge, the two flocks and kingdoms have been shown to be one.

When this has been established, the polyarchy will be destroyed, as the true shepherd removes the bad rulers—three shepherds in one month, that is, in one single cycle. These three removed leaders are to be considered: the Jewish priestly order, those called unjust prophets by them, and those who reigned from Jeroboam. For all these were causes of harm among those who were ruling. It has been said in Hosea: 'Priests have hidden the way of the Lord, Sicaim has murdered, they have done iniquity in Israel' (Hosea 4:6), and even in the same prophet: 'Israel shall be afflicted like the prophet who went astray' (Hosea 4:12).

Many things are written regarding the unlawful kingship that split God's people, such as: 'Hear this, O priests, and house of the king, be appalled, because the judgment is against you, that you have become a snare to the vision, and like a net spread out over the Sea of Tiberias' (Habakkuk 3:8/Amos 8:1-2). Against those who thought so poorly, the holy Jeremiah cries out most strictly from the presence of the All-King God: 'The priests did not say, Where is the Lord? and those upholding the law did not seek me, and the prophets prophesied unjustly, and the shepherds were ungodly toward me, and they followed after unprofitable things' (Jeremiah 2:11).

Understand that the kings of Israel, besides the priests and prophets, were also found to be ungodly shepherds toward Him. Also, the false teachers should not be ignored, who claim to be ungodly shepherds toward God. These three called shepherds are removed in one month by 'the great High Priest Jesus, having opened the heavens,' being a true prophet, concerning whom a divine pre-announcement was said: 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers' (Deuteronomy 18:15). To be both high priest and prophet, and also king, is as it is said concerning the Father: 'I have raised him up as king...'

And all his ways are straight; he will build my city, and will return the captivity of my people, not with ransoms nor with gifts (Isa 54:17; Isa 60:14). And he himself, the one building the spiritual city of God and redeeming the people, says about himself: 'I have been made king by him upon the holy Mount Zion, I proclaim the command of the Lord' (Isa 62:6).

Regarding the things observed concerning the three shepherds, it is necessary to oversee that three false ones are to be considered as shepherds, the impious ones being removed who are impious toward the Trinity. For some of them have much inclination toward being impious toward the Father, others toward the Son, and others toward the Holy Spirit.
