And perhaps those thinking [the Father is] the father of the Son are blaspheming toward the Father, diminishing the Father because of their impiety toward the Only-begotten Son, who is the God Word of wisdom and truth, those who were previously thinking [him] to be a creature from non-being and blaspheming concerning his own offspring. And they are also fighting against the Spirit, glorifying [him] as if he were one of the creatures.
And the three ranks of the deceived atheists think [wrongly] concerning the Trinity, but each, as has already been said, has a different impious inclination.

And the impious shepherds in this way will be uprooted in one month; for until the present age, the false teaching holds the promise, to be destroyed when a perfect illumination of the true light occurs after the present evil age and the transient life, upon which alone those hoping are more merciful than all men.

And the uprooting of the three wicked leaders happens, under the heavy law falling upon them of the king who threatens these things, since they do hateful things to him. And his soul is said to be characterized in several ways.

According to one, and an easy one, it is that which he has as a perfect man, which he sets aside in order to receive it again. He has indeed set it as a ransom, having given it instead of many, as the mystagogue of the truth, John, writes about him thus: 'Because he laid down his soul for us; and we owe to lay down our souls for one another' (Eph 5:2); and having risen from the dead, he received it, 'not having been left in Hades' (John 14:18). According to another view, the soul is every man having been made to belong to this Savior who says these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Peril of Abandoned Flocks
english: To serve as an 'man in Christ' is to say that there is no difference in stating that man is a soul of God. For Elijah is called a man serving God and a soul of God; likewise Moses the hierophant, and if anyone else partakes of the same holiness and virtue.

There is no need for many testimonies now, since much proof has already been given; for it is sufficient to take up the voice of Paul and Peter. For what Paul wrote: 'Every soul'—that is, man—'must be subject to the superior authorities' (Rom 13:5); and what [Peter] said: 'That is, eight souls were saved,' saying eight souls regarding those saved in the ark during the flood: Noah and his three sons, his wife, and the three living with his sons (1 Pet 3:20).

This so-called soul of God is weighed down by the three shepherds being removed in a single month, being indignant at the one removing them from the Savior. And their removal happens because, like the manner of lions, their souls were being torn by savagery against the true shepherd.

Since the coarseness of the shepherds is described, the good chief-shepherd, regarding the sheep lost by the wicked shepherds, says in the manner of the threat 'I will not shepherd you,' especially since they were still being [lost] by the harmful ones; for they had not yet been removed; for 'I will remove the three shepherds' shows that they were at the height of being placed over the flocks led astray by them.

By what manner and for whose sake one of the rods is called beautiful and the other a fragment, it should be made clear in the places where they will not yet be exposed. But now it is necessary to say with God: 'Let the dying die, and let the lacking fail, and let the remnants be eaten, each one the flesh of his neighbor' (Zech 11:9).
Under the good shepherd overseeing the flock, each of the sheep is cared for in the necessary way. Immediately, also, the Lord Jesus says: 'My sheep hear my voice and follow...'

“...to me, and I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish for ever,” just as each of those completing the divine flock cries out concerning the shepherd: “The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing. In a place of green pasture, there He has made me abide; by the waters of rest He has nourished me, He has restored my soul. He has led me upon the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.”

Thus, when the spiritual nourishment is neglected due to their own idleness, left behind by the one saying, “I will not shepherd you,” the opposite happens to the flocks, such that the dying indeed die, having been distanced from the one saying, the shepherd, concerning his own sheep: “I came that they might have life and have it abundantly, having laid down my life for the sheep.”

In the dying of the dying, and in the failing that shall cease, having been desolated of protection, just as each of those who have fallen away from the proper pasture of the neighbor to eat their flesh, having turned into savagery. By this savagery, the Church of the Galatians having fallen, it is fittingly written against her by the apostle Paul: “But if you bite and devour one another, see that you are not consumed by one another.” Concerning thus being reduced to a beast-like state, the hymnist sings: “In the approaching of those doing evil to me to eat my flesh.”

Furthermore, if even those were so determined, the one remaining unharmed says: “Those who trouble me and my enemies themselves have grown weak and have fallen.” And the prophet Jeremiah, concerning the beasts who attempt harm against the diligent, says: “Holy Israel, the Lord is the beginning of his generations; all those who devour him shall err, and evil shall come upon them, says the Lord.”
And indeed, it is better to say 'to devour' each one the flesh, rather than the soul or the mind of the neighbors.
The one having escaped from this savagery, rejoicing for himself and for those near him, cries out: “Blessed is the Lord, who does not...

title: Prophetic Symbolism and Shifts in Person
english: "He gave us for hunting to those walking their paths." Zachariah 11:10–11: "And I will take my good staff, and I will cast it away to scatter my covenant, which I had distributed to all the peoples; and it shall be scattered in that day, and the Canaanites shall know the sheep being guarded, because it is the word of the Lord."

Because the people of circumcision were abandoned by the shepherd due to their unfaithfulness toward him, the lying ones encountered [the consequences], as if the dying were dying and the vanishing were vanishing, and the remnants were turned to eat the flesh of their neighbor.

A calling occurs of the Church from the nations having believed in Christ, which he also named a praiseworthy staff, that is, a kingdom, saying: "And I will take the good staff." But this surpassed what the Father said to the Son: "Ask from me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance."

Because the royal scepter was cast away by the one having taken all the nations as inheritance, the covenant toward all the peoples was scattered, concerning which it is said in Deuteronomy in a great song in this manner: "When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God." This covenant having been scattered by Christ, the angels no longer presiding over the nations, an inheritance and a portion has become all the nations of the one who cast away the good staff upon the dissolution of the covenant toward all the peoples.

And this excellence is perfected in that day prepared by the sun of righteousness, which Abraham, the father of all the nations of the believers, rejoiced to see, having been blessed in his seed, all those of the nations fulfilling [the promise], men having their faith reckoned as righteousness.

Concerning this day, the whole choir of holy men and angels sings and declares: "This is the day which the Lord made; let us rejoice and be glad in it" (Ps 118:24), being sons of those to whom the Savior said: "You are the light of the world" (Matt 5:14). "The day has approached, that we may walk decorously as in a day."
Having endured these divine exploits, the Canaanites shall know, being sheep being guarded, "that it is the word of the Lord" regarding the lying ones...

Being a signifier of great and exceeding mysteries, which it is necessary to understand, [it is] both a rod and a covenant toward all the peoples. 4.112 The Canaanites were being called out from the nations, prepared to become the inheritance of the Son of God, through which they had blindness regarding what was spoken: 'Learn from me that I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls' (Matt 11:29).

4.113 Zach. XI, 12–13: 'And I will say to them: If it is good in your sight, give, having stood my wages, or refuse; and they stood my wages, thirty pieces of silver. And the Lord said to me: Cast them into the potter's house, and consider if it is tested, in the manner in which I was tested against them. And they took the thirty pieces of silver, and threw them into the house of the Lord into the potter's house.'

4.114 The prophetic words, being uttered enigmatically, abruptly change the persons of those speaking and of whom they speak; and indeed, from many utterances, it is possible to believe and to demonstrate the doctrine. But in order not to mishear the word, one must take from Jeremiah, spoken in the presence of God, thus: 'Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem and see if there is anyone doing faithfulness and mercy' (Jer 3:4), or 'judgment' as some of the manuscripts have, 'and I said: As the Lord lives, they say; therefore they do not swear upon a lie.'

4.115 For having God spoken to the holy men: 'Run to and fro through the squares of Jerusalem and see if there is anyone in it doing these things,' those having received the command answer: 'As the Lord lives, they say'; toward whom God says: 'Therefore they do not swear upon a lie.' See how many changes of persons are brought about in these few symbols, not being dispersed according to the letter but in the understanding.

4.116 Just as it is regarding the received testimony, so it is in the voice of Zechariah having been set forth. For the Savior having said—for He himself is the one announcing the things set before regarding the rejection of those of the circumcision—and having announced furthermore regarding the calling of the nations who formerly were idolaters, He says from another beginning: 'I was answered and I said to them,' that is, to the Jews: 'If it is good and just in your sight, give, that is to say, having determined, my wages; but if not, refuse, declining...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Deceitful Wages and False Doctrines
english: My words. For those who agreed that my wages were thirty pieces of silver. It is appropriate to receive both a wage and silver. Often, the divine teachings and the word are signified by this name: 'The words of the Lord are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace, tested, cleansed in the earth seven times' (Ps 12:6). And again, it is said proverbially: 'The tongue of the righteous is like refined silver' (Prov 10:20). For the word is signified by the name of the tongue.

And since not all silver mentioned allegorically is praised, but some is also reproached, thus God says to the false teachers of Israel: 'Your silver is worthless' (Jer 6:30); He does not mean a physical coin, but a deceitful word. And regarding those who use it to describe the discerning ones, to say of the generation producing these things: 'Call them rejected silver, for the Lord has rejected them,' it is manifest that they are deceitful and forbidden things.

This understanding is the proverbial ordinance brought forth thus: 'Silver given with deceit should be regarded as shards.' For the deceptive and contentious word brought forth with deceit by sophists—even if it seems to be about great things, the so-called 'exaltations, puffed up according to the knowledge of God'—is to be announced as being to be regarded as shards; such are those who are described as 'those who set their minds on earthly things' (Col 3:2), whom Isaiah said are 'those shouting from the earth' (Isa 28:9).

Since there is indeed a difference between logical silvers, having established the wage of those of the circumcision against those who toil over them as thirty pieces of silver, the Father says to the one having received the thirty pieces of silver: 'Cast them into the treasury and test if it is worthy' (Matt 27:5), the silver given, 'in the manner in which I was tested' on their behalf. For thus it will be revealed whether I am providing worthily the wage for which I accepted toil on their behalf, 'laying down my life and giving it as a ransom for many' (Mk 10:45).

Having said these things of the Father, I say this: Cast the thirty pieces of silver into the treasury, the one 'having become obedient unto death' (Phil 2:8) without hesitation, following what was commanded; they took, He says, the silver and threw it into the house of the Lord into the treasury (Matt 27:5). When this was fulfilled, it became known of the Pharisees and the others from...
The reward of circumcision is deceitful, just as those searching the scriptures which testify concerning the Savior as he spoke them have considered it to be a counterfeit coin.

For often in the Gospels the wicked word of those being accused is exposed, as in: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; and in vain they worship me, teaching commandments of men as doctrines' (Matt 15:8), nullifying the commandment of God through their harmful tradition. Likewise, those proposing an unproven word concerning whether it is necessary to give tribute to Caesar or not are exposed, as they themselves were accused of being deceitful and speaking with much cunning from that very moment; for when being asked, the Savior said: 'Show me the coin' (Matt 22:19), meaning 'whose image and inscription it has.' And those saying: 'Caesar's,' were strongly rebated upon hearing: 'Therefore render to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God' (Matt 22:21).

And not only do the Jews approaching the Savior in a testing manner possess an unproven word, but also the heretics in Christianity who pseudo-doctrinalize, 'walking in cunning and deceiving the word of the Lord,' diverting and distorting the will of the God-breathed oracles; whom one must also reject, considering their deceitful word to be as counterfeit silver. Is the word of those setting two unbegotten principles, good and evil—and these are Manichaeans—not unproven? And [is it not unproven] of those saying the Son is a creature and dividing the Holy Spirit from Father and Son? And [is it not unproven] of the impious ones regarding the incarnation of the Savior, those thinking the Savior appeared and was not true?

Not only is the counterfeit silver made manifest from the crucible of the house of God, but also the genuine [silver] bearing the image and character of the All-King Savior, 'having been purified sevenfold,' which must be held and in which one must prosper by possession. They are grasping that those whom Judas received, thirty pieces of silver from the Jews in order that he might betray the Lord (Matt 26:15), are signified also from the spoken word, and [this is] the greatest indictment of the Jews who gave and of Judas who received the thirty pieces of silver for betrayal. For it was necessary for them a reward...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Restoration of the Divided Kingdoms
english: to provide to the one who labored for the salvation of them and of the whole cosmos, but not so that 'the one who vivifies all things' might be denied.

4.128 It is necessary to cast the blasphemies, which the Jews bring against the Savior crucified for the sake of the whole creation, into the house of the God-breathed writings and into the vessel contained therein, so that they may be convicted of being unheeding, rather than opposing the prophecies concerning Christ and his cross.
4.129 Zach. XI, 14: And he cast away the second rod, the staff, to scatter the covenant between Judah and between Israel.

4.130 Our Savior and Lord has taken two rods, the beauty of which he first summoned, having previously cast away that called beauty, revealing the mysteries already made clear; now, having cast away the one called the staff, he scattered the covenant between Israel and Judah.

4.131 What is the staff called the staff? From the great song it is again to be learned. And the things of the song are held thus, as they were previously set forth: 'When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to the number of the angels of God, and there became a divided people of the Lord, his Jacob, a staff of inheritance, his Israel.' These things are said concerning the whole nation of the Hebrews being one rod and one portion. And for a long time the whole nation remained unsuitably acting as one rod, according to that which is proclaimed in the Psalms to the King and Forethinker of all: 'Remember your assembly, which I will gather from the beginning; I will redeem the rod of your inheritance.'

4.132 This one kingdom was divided into two leaderships, as Judah is called, and Ephraim, with those remaining in Jerusalem having the succession under the house of David from the tribe of Judah, and those having descended into Samaria having Jeroboam as leader, having sinned against Israel, being from the tribe of Ephraim.

4.133 And for a long time the wickedness of the division remained, with the king of Judah and the tyrant of Samaria apostatizing and contending against one another, until God may have mercy, and again show the twelve tribes as one kingdom, with only Judah holding as...

Concerning this restoration, it is brought forth in Hosea the prophet, the All-King saying: 'The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah shall be gathered, and they shall set for themselves one beginning and shall ascend from the land, because great is the day of Jezreel' (Hosea 2:23).

One must attend to the prophecy declaring that those being restored into one kingdom ascend from the land, making it clear that they exist down in the land, having been scattered by their own division away from the single hegemony. After the covenant of the schism having worked in the midst of Judah and Israel for a time, a scattering and a resolution of it occurs by the grace of the Savior, so that from the departure of the difference of the schisms, the so-called splintered rod might become one under a single king as before, he having the succession from Judah, so that there might be one flock and one shepherd existing under the lawful king of the whole nation.

Concerning such a restoration of the two kingdoms into one lawful beginning, it is brought forth in the prophet Ezekiel; and thus the prophetic voice has: 'And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take for yourself a rod and write upon it Judah and the sons of Israel lying near to it; and a second rod you shall take for yourself and write it: To Joseph, the rod of Ephraim and all the sons of Israel placed toward him. And you shall join them to one another to yourself into one rod to bind them, and they shall be in your hand' (Ezekiel 10:9-11).

And it shall be when they say to you, sons of your people, saying: 'Do you not announce to us what these things are to you?' (Ezekiel 11:17). And you shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will take the tribe of Joseph through the hand of Ephraim and the tribes of Israel lying near to him, and I will give them upon the tribe of Judah; and the rods shall be upon which you have written them in your hand before them, and you shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I take the whole house of Israel from the midst of the nations, where they entered there and were, and I will gather them from all those around them and I will bring them into the land of Israel; and I will give them into one nation in my land and in the mountains of Israel' (Ezekiel 11:14-16).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Rods and the One Kingdom
english: And one ruler shall be over all of them as king, and they shall no longer be for two nations, nor shall they be divided again into two kingdoms (Ezekiel 37:24).

And with other things: 'And I will cleanse them, and they shall be to me as a people, and I will be to them as God. And my servant David shall be ruler in the midst of them, and he shall be one shepherd to all, because they shall walk in my commands and my judgments shall be kept and they shall do them. And they shall dwell upon their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob' (Ezekiel 37:23).

And with a little more: 'And David my servant shall be their ruler forever. And I will make for them a covenant of peace, an eternal covenant shall be with them; and I will place my holy things in the midst of them forever. And my dwelling shall be in them, and I will be to them God, and they shall be to me a people. And the nations shall know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them by the being of my holy things in the midst of them forever' (Ezekiel 37:25, 27-28).

When the harmony of the prophetic enigma has appeared regarding the division of the one rule into two kingdoms and the restoration of these into one rule according to the prophecy of Hosea, it follows, having been read through the history, to understand the things concerning the two rods which the Son of Man took for himself.

For it must be understood through them the callings of the two peoples, both from the nations and from the circumcision, joined into one scepter of kingship, according to the meaning of the apostolic writing, which says: 'He is our peace, who makes both the two one and having broken down the middle wall of the partition, so that he might create the two in himself as one new man' (Ephesians 2:14), the Greek and the Jew.

For when one was Judaizing and the other was Hellenizing, two rods and two men existed, divided by the difference of religion, as if they were not under one king. But when the true leader shone forth, to whom the saints say: 'Your kingdom is a kingdom...'

Regarding those who are 'of the ages', the victorious one is shown to be one people, all of whom are men, having been called under one God and King, 'having preached peace to those far off and peace to those near' (Eph 2:17), so that both sides might be constructed into one kingdom in the Spirit, existing under the one God and King.

4.144 And the one called from the Gentiles is a rod upon which Judah the confessing was written, while the one from the circumcision is the scepter lying to Joseph. Each of the two in the enigma of the two rods should be clarified in detail and according to themselves in the [commentary] on Ezekiel, if God would call upon His own goodness to speak of them; but as for the present need, we say they are for allegory.

4.145 Of the two having become one rod of rule, one was raised by the Father, the one according to the flesh who was raised by God from David, who having become an eternal shepherd and king according to humanity, having been shown to be the leader of a peaceful and eternal covenant, will rule steadfastly and peacefully for ever unto the ages, his kingdom never ceasing.

4.146 It is fitting to this thus peaceful state, in the midst of those beginning, that the holy mysteries of the kingdom of God be given to be dwelt in by him, the generous one, in the midst of those being both saved and sanctified, of so great and far-reaching good, to be fulfilled according to the time of the incarnation, just as the Word having become flesh dwelt among his own (John 1:14), so that having advanced even more, they might behold 'his glory, the glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14).

4.147 Not unseasonably, as it were, has it been clarified, despite a digression, concerning the two scepters which the Son of Man took for himself (Zech 11:7), so that having joined and bound them together, he might show them as one rod.
4.148 And this good thing will exist perfectly when 'the fullness of the Gentiles having entered' (Rom 11:25), into the highest blessedness, 'all Israel shall be saved' (Rom 11:26).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Gluttonous False Teachers and the True Shepherd
english: implements to shepherd

They think they have glory by making their own bellies gods through all-devouring, as if serving the belly and not the Lord Jesus, just as the Apostle writes about such people: 'they do not serve the Lord Jesus but their own belly' (Phil 3:19).

4.154 Having such a mindset, the false teachers and false shepherds have only meager and insufficient food as the best reward for their teaching, being persuaded by the one who led them to this, saying: 'The worker is worthy of his food,' as they say and write more boldly: 'We are satisfied with the present,' meaning foods and coverings. Immediately, they also say of those they lead into this: 'We have brought nothing into the world, because we are not able to bring anything out. Having foods and coverings, we shall be satisfied with these.'
4.155 Those having virtue in this way speak boldly, saying: 'Silver and gold we do not have' (Acts 3:6).

4.156 Such teachers are useful; they do not crave the flesh of those being shepherded, having a desire for their spirit, 'striving' with them 'to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace' (Eph 4:3). Therefore, they do not turn away the ankles of those, but they steady and raise them up, so that they may run in the straight ways of the Lord and do what is necessary, having also the ankles of the hands made healthy.
4.157 And I said this regarding the ankles being of the hands, having learned this from the all-wise Daniel.

4.158 This may perhaps be equal to the turning of the ankles, or equivalent to what is said by the great prophet Elijah to those wavering between two paths: 'How long will you limp on both sides? If the Lord is, go after him; but if Baal, go after him' (1 Kings 18:21).

4.159 Clearly and vividly, having spoken in the manner of a threat, the prophet protects the shepherd who does not visit the failing sheep, nor seeks the scattered one, nor binds or heals the broken one, nor strives to direct the whole one so that it might be even more healthy; he urges the prophet to take shepherd's tools without skill or experience of a good shepherd, so that he might learn who is the one to whom he prophesies.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sword of Separation and the Antichrist
english: The power of those things commanded to him. For those who do not understand the words press upon those performing the works of the teacher.

Since, therefore, regarding an inexperienced shepherd lacking the art of shepherding, the holy one receiving God had to understand the listeners, he perceived the spoken vessels sensually, so that he might speak about them and what they signify when asked by those seeing that he had taken up shepherd's vessels not as an experienced man but as an inexperienced one. Much is thus managed in the prophets, especially in Ezekiel. It is not unlikely that things concerning the Antichrist, regarding such a destructive shepherd, are pre-announced, as is found in many writings. He said, 'the elect sheep, whose flesh he eats,' not absolutely and truly the elect, but those chosen as dear and familiar to the one eating their flesh. 'O you who shepherd the vain and who have abandoned the sheep: a sword upon his arm and upon his right eye; his arm being dried shall be dried, and his right eye being blinded shall be blinded' (Zech 11:17). Rather than merely blaming, the divine word threatens the false shepherds who have turned away and abandoned the sheep, hunting the vain, making shameful gain manifest, and the destruction of the flesh which they were entrusted to nourish, as concerning each of them or as if all were done through the same wickedness: 'A sword upon the arm,' that is, his work. Often it has been demonstrated that the arm signifies, according to allegory, a work.

What then is the sword upon the arm and eye of the wicked shepherd? Either the punitive word of which God says in Isaiah to those who follow the law: 'If you are willing and would obey, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword' (Isa 1:19-20). Concerning this defensive sword, God says again in Jeremiah: 'I will stretch out my hand against all who dwell in the land,' because they would undergo these harmful things. According to another understanding, the sword may be the divine, dividing word which separates those clothed in the hands from them. Immediately indeed in the Gospels the Savior says: 'Do not think, he says, that I came to cast peace...'

not of the earth, but a sword. For the evangelical teaching does not prepare one to live in peace with earthly things and the earth, but divides from it those who think earthly things and bear the image of the swine.

This sword of use is given by way of a judgment to Abraham, so that he might depart from the earth and from his kin and from the father's house, the earth being understood as the body in which he was surrounded, and kin as those who are of the same kind and were brought up together, and the father's house is the spoken word of the mind, as one of the wise interpreted concerning the Mosaic education. What was said to the divine bride, or rather to his father, is equivalent to what was said to Abraham: 'Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and forget your people and your father's house, for the King of your beauty has desired you, and He is your Lord' (Song of Solomon 2:10-13). For it is the same thing to forget one's own people and the father's house as to depart from the kin and the father's house for the one driven to this.

The aforementioned punitive sword, having come upon the arm and the eye, that is, upon the practical power and the contemplative power, like a punishing shepherd dries the arm, removing all moisture and soft suppleness so that it may be deadened. And it will blind the eye and blind it, the one which seems to the possessor to be right, but not being such in truth, but being crooked and left and perhaps something even more inferior.

And these words were also struck by the Antichrist, promising to have a strong and living arm through the signs and wonders which he performs, being false, and a right eye, partaking of the glance of the haughty king of the Assyrians, concerning whom the Lord Himself said: 'I will strike upon the great mind, upon the king of the Assyrians' (Isaiah 7:20), boasting arrogantly: 'I will provide the strength of the nations, and with the wisdom of understanding I will remove the borders of nations, I will seize the whole inhabited world with my hand.' Having thus shouted this insolently: 'There is no one who will escape me or oppose me,' the Antichrist, being a son according to impiety, boasted to have a strong arm and a right eye, which is the arm dried by the previously interpreted sword, and the...

title: The Creation of Heaven, Earth, and Man
english: It blinded the eye by cutting off his right hand to prevent sight. Regarding this, Paul writes according to the word to the Thessalonians: 'Until the lawless one comes, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and will overthrow by the appearance of his coming' (2 Thess 2:8).

Each of the heretics is considered the right eye, proselytizing a pseudonymous knowledge; and every sorcerer makes himself all of his arms into enormous powers; both of these, one being dried up as an arm, the other being blinded as an eye by the aforementioned sword. It is possible to bring forth clear witness of these from the Bible of the Acts of the Apostles.

A certain Elymas the sorcerer, performing works of enchantment and bringing forth teaching, perverting as he wished those who were near to the faith, was considered to have a paradoxical and penetrating mind, thinking greatly and regarding himself as a leader; to him, approaching with strong refutations and divine energy, the divinely inspired Paul said: 'O full of deceit and of all craftiness, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord? Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind and not seeing the sun for a time' (Acts 13:10).

Simon the sorcerer had the same image of impiety as Elymas, which Peter himself demonstrated by the power of God, the drying up of nothing having occurred to his right arm and the blinding of his right eye (Acts 8:23). Sufficient, as I think, having clarified those things concerning the wicked shepherd of infinite scope, it should be set forth, beginning from another region, of the prophet.

Zach. XII, 1–3: The burden of the word of the Lord upon Israel: says the Lord, stretching out heaven and founding earth and molding a human spirit in it: 'Behold, I set Jerusalem as a shaking threshold for all the peoples around, and in Judah, and there shall be a guard around Jerusalem. And it shall be in that day I will set Jerusalem as a stone to be trodden by all the nations; everyone who treads upon it shall be mocked, and all the nations of the earth shall be gathered to it' (Zech 12:1-3).
The prophet Zechariah foretells the things happening to Judah and Jerusalem and to those dwelling after the cross of Jesus, having received a word from the people.
The Creator, having stretched out the heavens, having laid the foundation of the earth, and having fashioned the human spirit within it.

It was previously stated how prophets become possessors of the word being given to them, by which they foretell the things that are to come. In order that the same things might not be announced many times, what has already been said is sufficient.

God stretches out the heaven and lays the foundation of the earth, bringing these most interconnected creatures from non-existence into being, in which all else exists, as the Revealer says: 'And the heaven and the earth and all the host of them were completed' (Gen 2:1). Immediately, beginning of the Creation, he clearly said: 'In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth' (Gen 1:1), that is, he stretched out the heaven and laid the foundation of the earth.

Often the manner of the stretching out of the heaven and the laying of the foundation of the earth has been observed, as these words are made clear by God saying: 'I alone stretched out the heavens,' and by the hymnographer concerning the Creator: 'He laid the foundation of the earth upon its stability; it shall not be moved for ever and ever' (Ps 104:5). He who spread out the heaven by stretching and established the earth on foundations also created man, 'fashioning in him his spirit,' that is, weaving and uniting the soul as it is fitting for the body, so that a single composite living being might be formed from soul and body.

The spirit of man is not fashioned from nothing, but in him; for it is not of a bodily nature but of a rational nature. Rather, the body of man is fashioned beforehand, according to what was said by Moses: 'God formed man from dust of the earth' (Gen 2:7). Having known this manner of creation, the magnanimous and most courageous Job spoke to the Creator: 'Remember that you formed me of clay, and to dust you turn me back again' (Job 10:9).

But also concerning the generation of the composite from soul and body, he says: 'Your hands have made me and fashioned me' (Ps 139:13), the body having been fashioned, he fashioned the soul, which is called spirit, which he fashioned in man, participating from the composition of sensory power, so that the whole man might be shown to have become an ensouled, sensing, living being. With this having been thus observed, it might be said also differently: the
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Desolation of Jerusalem
english: The spirit of a man being shaped within him is that about which the Apostle writes: 'Who knows the things of man, except the spirit of the man that is in him' (1 Cor 2:11), being something other than the rational soul, called a 'hidden man of the heart.'

The shaping of it is not like that of the body, but is that which the holy hymn-writer prays should exist in his heart, saying: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Ps 51:10). And a clean heart is being shaped according to virtue and being stamped by another holiness, so that it may act and think strongly and harmoniously.

This opinion, which belonged to Judith, who struck down the tyrant Holofernes, the wisest elders, praising her, said to her: 'Good is the formation of your heart' (Judith 9:11). The formation and the shaping are homonymous with those of the body; for these indeed, in opposition to the being shaped, signify a material underlying substance, representing the shaping of the spirit through the stamping of concepts and rational phantasms.

He who stretched out the heavens, laid the foundation of the earth, and shaped the spirit of man within him, threatens to lay waste and overthrow the city and land of the Jews because of the audacity of the atheists who struck at the Savior who had arrived—for indeed, with cross and blows He surrounded the one who gave His soul as a ransom, the one who bore the sin of the world—even though He had come for the salvation of all.

And what is it that is being pre-announced as a harsh thing against those who killed Christ? 'Behold, I set Jerusalem as a shaking threshold, and Judea around all the peoples' (Matt 22:45/allusion), He says, meaning that it no longer has any seat or security, having been abandoned by the one who founded and guards it, fulfilling the manner of the threat pre-announced in Isaiah: 'The daughter of Zion shall be left forsaken' (Isa 54:6), and in Jeremiah, regarding Him who, turning away from her because of her impious insolence, said: 'I have left my house' (Jer 12:7)...

“I have left my inheritance, I have given my beloved soul into the hands of its enemies.” (Ps 69:8). For before the leaving and the handing over, there existed house and inheritance and a beloved soul, concerning which these things are said by the speaker later because of the impiety against him: “Behold, your house is left to you desolate.” (Lk 19:44).

And not that the doors but the gate-posts shall be set; for the whole security is not struck from all, but the one according to the shadow and the letter, being an entrance of the outsiders of the law, what is said, “the requirements of the flesh lying ahead until the time of correction.”

And since the threatened hardships touched even the sensible Judah and its metropolis—for it was cast down so that no longer stone lay upon stone—the surrounding peoples of the foreign nations, not being permitted to enter to tread upon the holy ground, tread upon it, as if treading upon a bare and common stone by unwashed feet.

Jeremiah, having foreseen this gloomy thing with a long prophetic gaze, lamenting and wailing for the city falling into such wickedness, spoke mournfully: “How did the city, once filled with people, sit alone? Was the one filled with nations reckoned as a desert?” (Lam 4:1).

The Savior, approaching Jerusalem, said that these things would happen to her: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, if you had known also the things toward peace; but now they have been hidden from your eyes; for your enemies, coming, will surround you, making a trench around you,” (Lk 19:44) as having been abandoned to be leveled to the ground, all the warring nations having come around you, as to see you desolate: “For when, he says, you see Jerusalem surrounded by encampments, you know that its desolation has approached.”

These things have risen to her as a trial by the murderers, when the Romans seized them and pulled down their cities and humiliated them, turning away by the law of captivity, rather being torn away from the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Trampling of False Horses and the Opening of Eyes
english: Having been nourished [as if] no longer having a land or a place of their own, the lands are being plundered everywhere.

Concerning this wrath having reached its end so quickly in Judea and those dwelling in it, the writer of their sufferings himself composed a very large collection, describing both them and their places, so as to see unceasingly how fully what the Savior and Zechariah had said prophetically was fulfilled, beginning from: 'I set Jerusalem as a shaking threshold' (Zechariah 11:1). Having set its gates to be shaken, with a surrounding region also shaking it, all the uncircumcised nations, having mounted upon it, trample it contemptuously like an unclean stone, no longer coming as to a temple and a holy ground, unprotected and not with the proper cleansings and purifications. Therefore, mocking, they mock it like a ruin, with all others mounting upon it 'as a field to be plowed' (Psalm 10:9).

Regarding the spoken word, let that which is toward the intellect also be spoken; all the heretics through whom they think badly and act, 'build Zion in blood and Jerusalem in iniquity' (Isaiah 1:7). For how is it that they do not build Zion in blood, causing scandal and pouring out the blood of those whom they deceive? Therefore also they build Jerusalem in iniquity. That those being deceived are wronged by the deceivers, the Scripture of the divine Proverbs declares most clearly concerning such things, saying thus: 'They shall be filled with their own impiety; for because they wronged the helpless, they shall be slain, and the scrutiny shall consume the impious' (Psalm 10:9).

The Word of God sets the shaking thresholds for the city being built by hand, so that they might be overthrown by strong reproof, so that it might be trampled by the surrounding peoples, the pseudo-Jerusalem having been shown to be trampled like a defiled stone, so as to mock those who mock the pseudonym, those having known its illegitimacy and uncleanness, who ambassador the truth and the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.

And since not a few are mocking, but all the nations, in the falling into poverty, it was rightly said that all the nations shall be gathered against it. Jerusalem is trampled like a stone when the sun of righteousness has risen, making a mental day, which has already been much remembered. In that day, says the Lord of all (Zechariah 12:4)...
I will trample every horse in frenzy and its rider in folly; and upon the house of Judah I will open my eyes; and I will trample all the horses of the peoples in blindness.

In the things foretold by the prophet, regarding horses and their riders, a clarity has come in many ways; wherefore most of them are now keeping silence, only remembering for the present need of how this has been seen. Deceitful men, established by lying words, exist as 'false horses for salvation,' having riders and passengers who are deceptive spirits and hypocritical, lying-speaking demons of whom they act as ambassadors for the teaching, putting forward 'the wisdom of this age and of its rulers.'

Those having horses thus, God tramples on the day which He Himself makes, according to what was said in the manner of blessing toward the one being dazzled: 'The Lord shall be to you an eternal light' (Isa 60:19). And God tramples the false horses not because they do not exist at all, but so that they may not perceive concerning those things of which they speak and are being confirmed, with the destruction of their wisdom and the nullification of their understanding; which happening, the rider of each such horse will be in folly.

This economy having been worked out, God will open His eyes upon the house of Judah, being the 'Church of the living God' (1 Tim 3:15), reigning in it by the Savior having risen from the tribe of Judah, toward whom the theosophists say: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you; your hands are upon the loins of your enemies, and the sons of your father shall worship you' (Isa 60:3).

Upon this house of Judah, the Benefactor opens His eyes, the overseeing and watchful powers, as each of those receiving the illumination and the grace says in the manner of prayer: 'Look upon me and have mercy on me.' And all the righteous enjoy the gift of the Great King, 'having His eyes upon them and His ears toward their prayer' (Ps 34:15).

Regarding the trampling in frenzy of the returned horse and in folly of its rider, and all the horses of the peoples being trampled by the Forethinker of all things in blindness. These are those who lust adulterously and fornicatiously, concerning whom the prophecy says:
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Judgment of the Leaders and the Wheat and Chaff
english: “They became women, each one serving her neighbor's wife.” For the animals that serve [lust] are struck toward goodness in blindness, so that they may no longer look sharply toward lust. For this deprivation of the eyes will be received by the soul as an uplift of sobriety, so as to correctly see what remains to be done and what is fitting to work.

Indeed, the sorcerer Elymas, who sees wickedly, was blinded for a time, casting off the vision of deception, so that later, having regained sight, he might behold 'the sun of righteousness.' For it is not useless that the sun, which is to be seen, is seen such that when one has endured blindness, he sees the light.

And the commanders of Judah shall say in their hearts: 'We shall find for ourselves those dwelling in Jerusalem in the Lord of all-ruling God their own' (Zach. XII, 5). Concerning the praiseworthy Judah to whom it is said: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you,' his commanders are those serving under him, the power of the king of all, having been revealed as 'the firstborn and servants of the word,' namely the apostles of Christ.

It must be noted that even if all the spirit-bearing men, both prophets and all others who are subject to Judah—teachers, evangelists, those thus designated as commanders—seek to find none other than those dwelling in the Jerusalem that sees 'the peace surpassing all understanding' and the heavenly city of God, concerning which 'the vessel of election,' Paul speaking in Christ, writes: 'You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem' (Heb. 12:22).

The one fulfilling this fair city as an excellent and lawful citizen, being steadfast according to holiness and the rest of divine virtue, becomes unshakeable, according to that which is said in Psalm 1 of the steps: 'He who dwells in Jerusalem shall not be moved.' And he dwells in it forever, remaining under the one ruling over it.

And the aforementioned commanders find those dwelling in the divine 'city, of which God is the artisan and creator,' as sons and disciples to themselves; just as Paul found Silvanus and Timothy and the evangelist Luke and the other acquaintances around...

Memory is brought forward in his epistles and in the Acts of the Apostles. And Peter, the true disciple of the Savior, likewise found Mark the evangelist and others more. Likewise also John, the disciple loved by the Lord. But those whom he found dwelling in Jerusalem are brought forward in his book of Acts.

And all those presiding over the apostolic Church find those who hold the same faith through right teaching, being citizens of the true and spiritual Jerusalem, as if because of this they dwell in it. Of the leaders who are assigned, the Lord God Almighty is the one holding and ruling them.

In that day I will set the leaders of Judah as a firebrand among the wood and as a torch of fire in a reed, and they shall consume on the right and on the left all the peoples around, and Jerusalem shall dwell yet for itself (Zechariah 12:6-7). And the Lord will save the tents of Judah as from the beginning, so that the boasting of the house of David and the pride of those dwelling in Jerusalem over Judah may not be magnified (Zechariah 12:7).

In the time, the day which he spoke of because of the light, the leaders of Judah find for themselves those dwelling in Jerusalem, being set by God as a firebrand among the wood and as a torch of fire in a reed, so that on the right and on the left all the peoples may be devoured around. As a firebrand among the wood and a torch in a reed, the leaders of the intelligible Judah are set, so that by the fiery and luminous Word they may consume the unfruitful and material volitions. For trees not producing good fruit are being cut down and thrown into the fire; they are wood being handed over to punishment, so that the worst quality of them may be consumed, just as the stalks, being reed and not wheat, are consumed by fire. For it has been said in the Gospel that, when Jesus is cleansing the threshing floor in which he has a winnowing fan in his hand, the wheat is being brought into the storehouse of the promises—these are the righteous men—but the chaff will be burned with unquenchable fire, as the worst volition is consumed when those with private volition are found to be unfruitful (Matthew 3:12).
Concerning such things, it is said by the prophet Micah by the Savior: 'Woe to me that I have become as gathering reed in...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Virtue, Protection, and the Tabernacles
english: Like a barren one and as a small leaf in a vineyard where no cluster exists for eating the firstfruits. Having spoken with an enigma regarding the fruitlessness that had occurred, he makes it manifest in the following words: 'Woe, O soul, because a pious one has perished from the earth, and the upright one does not exist among men; all are judged into blood, each one crushing his neighbor with crushing. They prepare their hands for evil.' For how should they not be punished, being consumed by the punishment of fire, those who are driven by the said evils.

Toward one of the interpreted ones of the chiliarchs the Lord says: 'I have given my words into your mouth as fire, and this people as wood, and they shall be devoured' (Jeremiah 2:22), through which he chose to have fruitlessness. This same thought exists in that prophesied in Isaiah: 'And the light of Israel shall be as fire, and it shall consume like grass the wood, and it shall be consumed from soul even to flesh' (Isaiah 10:18), that is, from the intention of the mind even to evil deeds; for through the soul he touched the intention, and through the flesh the deeds.

Those placed as a snare of fire, the chiliarchs, accomplish the same thing as the coal taken from the spiritual and heavenly altar by a Seraph; who, having brought it to the mouth of the prophet, removed his iniquities and cleansed his lips. But whom do the snare and the bright lamp of fire consume—the right and well-named ones? It is time to say. The well-named shadows of the ungodly and the sinners are well-known in themselves; but those who falsely pretend to be virtuous are thought to be right.

Both, indeed, are forbidden, the divine word says: 'Make straight paths for your feet, and direct your ways. Do not turn to the right or to the left' (Proverbs 4:26-27), neither into excesses nor into deficiencies; for both are evils. Of freedom—and this is the social choice—when it is lacking, the well-named deviation is stinginess, which is thought to be right, while profligacy is the consuming of resources not on what is necessary and as it should be, but upon the prey of shameful pleasures. Since therefore both the stingy man and the profligate man are found worthy of rebuke, both the snare of fire and the bright lamp are extinguished. Through many it has been demonstrated to us how, middle...
Since virtues are present, their deficiencies and excesses are found to be evils, in which we have written about virtues by word.

What has been said—that right and left are found almost around all men, being in a circle around all the peoples—has been spoken. When the peoples around the holy city experience punishment, it shall be inhabited as it is by itself, guarded by the one who built it and chose it, according to what was said concerning its safety: 'Mountains are around it, and the Lord is around his people' (Zech 2:5). Concerning such a guard, it is also brought forth in the present prophet as the Pantokrator: 'The Lord as a wall of fire' (Zech 2:5) shall be around it, which was made clear in the beginning of Zechariah, when Jerusalem is being inhabited as it is, and those who militarily besieged it have fled, according to what was said by the one dwelling in it: 'All the nations encircled me, and in the name of the Lord I defended them' (Zech 8:13), and the following words.

What, then, is brought forward in harmony with the holy city inhabiting as it is, or with the Lord saving the tabernacles of Judah as in the beginning, if not other things being the specific virtues? Concerning these, the proverbial ordinance proclaims: 'Tabernacles shall stand, having been made firm.' Concerning what is becoming to them as beloved, the hymnodist sings, asserting: 'How beloved are your tabernacles, Lord of Powers' (Ps 84:1). For how could they be celebrating, being full of things desired? For a voice of rejoicing and confession is heard of those celebrating, singing not elsewhere but in the tabernacles of the righteous.

The Lord saves the tabernacles of Judah as in the beginning, before evil and impiety of men seize hold. It is possible to say, as from the beginning, that the tabernacles being saved are the bodies in which we are surrounded. And salvation will come when our corruptible body, the dishonorable and weak, puts on incorruption, both glory and power, becoming a spiritual body from a psychic body (1 Cor 15:42-44). Often, having been attributed to be tabernacles, the progresses are called so—for these are houses of those walking—and these are saved from God as from the beginning, of the perfect state and of virtue being added.

The things spoken shall exist from God as good, so that, each of the saved boasting in the Lord, no one is still throwing himself upon himself, but upon the cause of the perfect good, the boasting of the house.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Protection of Jerusalem and the Davidic House
english: in blindness

In how the Lord protects those dwelling in Jerusalem, as each of them fulfills what was said concerning 'the one dwelling in the help of the Most High': 'His truth shall surround you with a shield' (Ps 91:4). And in another psalm, the Lord protects those fearing him, as each says: 'Because you are my shield, into your hands I will commit my spirit' (Ps 31:5).

For those dwelling in the spiritual Jerusalem, it exists to take on and put on the panoply of God, having girded the loins in truth and having feet secured in the footwear of the preparation of God-like peace, and moreover having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and above all to take on the shield of faith, in which the burning arrows of the evil one will be extinguished (Eph 6:16).

While the King fights for all creation, a shield to himself for those dwelling in the great city Jerusalem, strength and power shall be, as to take up strength for the one previously weakening in them, the house of David, the 'Church of the living God' being the temple of God, as each of those having ecclesiastical knowledge and virtue cries out in the manner of a hymn: 'The Lord is my strength and my song, and he became for me salvation' (Ps 118:17).

And since those saying these things, walking upon the earth, have a heavenly citizenship (Phil 3:20), as they are not yet equals among those raised from the dead, it is fitting that the house of David, interpreted by a skillful hand, shall be an angel of God, yielding the gift and the excellence toward the one born from the immaculate Virgin Mary, called 'the angel of great counsel,' as Isaiah, who many times pre-proclaims his coming descent, said from the presence of the choir of the saints: 'A child is born to us and a son is given, and his name is called the angel of great counsel' (Isa 9:6).
It is necessary to attend to the precision of the prophecy being revealed to us: that the infant from Mary has been born, and that the Only-begotten from the bosom of the Father has been given.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Restoration of the Nations
english: For a son was given, not that a child was born to us according to those who think impiously, nor has the child of the virgin been born, nor has the Father given the Only-begotten Son, according to Paul of Samosa, Photius the Galatian, and Artemas and Theodotus who similarly sinned about them.

These, therefore, were ostracized from the Church, having been seen to be altogether impious; but we, holding the ancient mindset of the assembly of the faithful, confess that the God-Word has arrived, having taken up a perfect human being of soul and body and spirit.

Because the Father gave the Son so that the child might be born, John the Evangelist most clearly declares him, the one having become man, having said about himself: 'For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that everyone believing in him should have eternal life' (John 3:16). This has the meaning in that which was sent to the Romans by the Christ-bearer Paul, having it thus: 'God sent his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, so that he might condemn sin in the flesh' (Rom 8:3).

These things are necessarily said to me because of the aforementioned Photius and his teacher Marcellus, saying that the flesh is the sent son, not at all being called the Son of the God-Word. Further refutation of their pseudo-knowledge has become available to us, when it was set forth to speak concerning the Son of God—I mean the God-Word and his becoming-man.

It is possible, according to another theory, to say that the one born from Mary is a house of him who is the capable Creator of all things by his hand, becoming an angel before the ones being blessed and dwelling in the holy Jerusalem; but an angel became [manifest] before them, clearly [showing] the great will of God.

In the day that approaches after the passing of the night of ignorance and malice, about which the Apostle writes saying: 'The night has passed, and the day has drawn near; let us walk decently as in the day' (Rom 13:12), the benefactor Lord seeks to purge all the nations coming with stability and...

He comes in the manner of the great king to the city of the great king, Jerusalem; and this is Jerusalem. The nations, all those estranged from the truth and from piety, are being sought for restoration, not so that men cease to exist—for that is impossible—but so that they may no longer be evil and wicked.

For if he had intended to destroy humanity quickly, he would not have sought to do this, being able to turn all things from being into non-being. For if he brought things from non-being into being and called the existing things into existence, he was able to overturn their existence much more, but it was not his will. Thus it is said of him by the all-wise Solomon: 'He created all things into being, and the generations of the world are salvific; there is no medicine of destruction in them' (Wisdom 16:24).

Just as the Lord and our Savior has come to seek the lost race of ours and saved it, so, seeking all the nations coming to Jerusalem, he saves them, destroying the causes of the harm that has existed for them from lawless deeds and alien thoughts, so that, peace having prevailed, the nations no longer come against the divine Jerusalem, having cast away the restless manner and the war-loving mind.

And the word 'coming' signifies that those boarding arrive as enemies and strangers, as the proverbial saying says to the one conducting himself peaceably: 'Whenever you sleep, you will sleep sweetly, and the onset of the ungodly shall not come to terrify you.' Since the restoration of the nations sought by the Foreknower of all things and Savior is being accomplished, it has been shown that on the foretold day, he who promises good things upon the house of David and those dwelling in Jerusalem will pour out a spirit of grace and compassion, he who is the 'Father of mercies' and the giver of the Holy Spirit. This is demonstrated from the God-breathed Scriptures. Concerning this gift, Paul writes: 'The love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit given to us' (Romans 5:5).

And Solomon says in his Wisdom: 'Who will trace the things in the heavens, if you have not given wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from the highest? And thus the paths of those on earth were corrected, and men were taught those things pleasing to you' (Wisdom 7:0). And the Provider of the Spirit himself in Isaiah to...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prophetic Fulfillment of the Crucifixion
english: Some say, 'I have given my Spirit upon you,' and again regarding such a thing, he says to others, 'I have given my Spirit upon him.' The generous gift is made manifest by the word, 'I will pour out a spirit of grace and mercy' (Ezekiel 36:26), as it can be learned from other sayings; for God says, 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh' (Joel 2:28), which signifies a rich giving, just as also, 'The love of God is poured out in our hearts' (Romans 5:5).

From the apostolic voice, it is presented that the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of grace, it being written: 'If anyone violates the law of Moses, he dies upon two or three witnesses without mercies; how much more do you think he will deserve a more severe punishment, he who has trampled the Son of God, and considered the blood of the covenant common, and has insulted the Spirit of grace in whom he was sanctified?' (Hebrews 10:29). It is joined to the fact that the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of grace by another saying of the Apostle, which is brought forth thus: 'There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:4), and again: 'For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge, to another faith in the same Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:8-9), and the enumerated following different gifts.

The Spirit of grace and mercy is being supplied by 'the Father of mercies.' It has been said toward this in other commentaries that the God of all is the Father of mercies of the Divine Word and the giver of the Holy Spirit. Knowing from what is written who is generously giving the Spirit of grace and mercy, we shall follow to see who the house of David and those dwelling in Jerusalem are. It was made clear that both are able to signify the Church existing, both Jerusalem and the house of David as one.

Regarding the prophecy: 'And they shall look upon me instead of those whom they have looked upon with contempt, and they shall wail for them as for a beloved, and shall grieve with a grief like that for a firstborn' (Zechariah 12:10). Having fallen into great distress, the Jews who struck [the Lord] are prevailing with loud wailing and grief, just as if they were wailing for a beloved one who has died and grieving over a firstborn son, 'before the wrath reaches its end upon them,' as if their fatherland were to be dug up and they were to become wandering vagabonds in all the land. Because of these things...

They were made known by the vote of God's providence through a holy thing which they performed by placing the Savior of all upon the cross; from this present matter it is to be learned. For he says of the one suffering by them: 'They shall look upon me instead of those from whom they looked down' (Ps 22:6). Were they not acting impiously and irreverently when, mocking Jesus being hung as the stake, they said: 'Behold, the one destroying the temple of God and raising it up in three days (Mt 26:61). He saved others, but he is not able to save himself' (Mt 27:42). 'If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!' (Mt 27:42).

These things and other things of the scoundrels mocking, the evangelist writes to be fulfilled by the prophecy having such a character: 'They shall look upon him whom they pierced' (Zech 12:10), which differs in single words from: 'They shall look upon me instead of those from whom they looked down' (Ps 22:6). For those having investigated the Hebrew dialect say that the existing [text] of Zechariah was translated into the evangelical [Greek], that is, the evangelist having brought it, for he was a Hebrew; or from another having interpreted and received it, that is, Aquila or Theodotus or someone else having brought the Hebrew word into Greece.

We have been led forward to say these things because some are seeking where it is said among the prophets: 'They shall look upon him whom they pierced' (Zech 12:10), not being found anywhere among those published of the Old Testament. It is probable that the grief is upon the beloved and the pain is upon the firstborn of those who murdered, since the cruel things came upon them, killing Jesus, being a firstborn Son and beloved.

It has been seen many times that 'the beloved' signifies two things: the one worthy of being loved and the Only-begotten Son. But both exist in Jesus Christ, being the Son of love, that is, of God, concerning whom it is written: 'God is love' (1 John 4:8), but also only-begotten, for he is the only-begotten Son from the Father and from the holy Virgin Mary. In that day the mourning shall be magnified in Jerusalem like the mourning of a reaper in a field being cut down, and the earth shall be cut according to tribes, tribe by itself and their women by themselves, the tribe of the house of David and their women by themselves, the tribe of the house of Nathan by itself and their women by themselves, the tribe of the house of Levi...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Allegorical Trees and Vines
english: Each tribe is distinct in itself, and so are their women; the tribe of Simeon is distinct in itself, and so are their women; all the remaining tribes are distinct in themselves, and so are their women.

The trees named allegorically in the Scripture act of their own accord, sometimes bearing good fruit by choice, and sometimes poison and harm. For instance, the Israelite people, having been planted by God as a 'true all-fruitful vine,' have turned into a vine of bitterness, becoming worthy of being cut down, since they have brought forth 'clusters of gall and bitter grapes,' according to what is written: 'Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire' (Matt 3:10).

Just as the vine of good fruits turned to bearing hand-held fruits, so the plants of the streams, having become evil from good, suffered the hardship of being cut down, as the present word shows. It is said regarding plants bearing edible fruit in the Song of Songs by the Bridegroom Christ: 'I will go down to the garden of the spring, to see if the vine has blossomed, if the streams have blossomed' (Song 2:15).

Having descended into the trial of life, called a winter torrent, he saw the vine and the streams having the beginning of fruitfulness, which is signified by the blossom. After the blossoms, the perfect fruit having been shown, the bride of the Word, the Church wedded to Him, had desire to be filled with what the Bridegroom provides. Therefore she says to Him: 'Give me to drink from the fragrant wine, from the water flowing from my spring' (Song 2:5). The water of the flowing spring heals not only thirst, but also, as a help being offered, improves the one receiving it.

The fruit of this plant, lying under the skin, has a great composition arranged broadly and thickened in harmony, as if to say to the Bridegroom: 'As a skin of a pomegranate, O bride' (Song 4:16), showing in you the redness of modesty and the great order and composition of the fruit under the skin.
The trees thus interpreted are cut down through their own negligence, with 'the axe at their roots' (Matt 3:10), similarly to the vines not bearing fruit.
Every branch not remaining in me is cut off and thrown into fire
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegorical Interpretation of Tribes and Genders
english: Regarding the burnt offerings of the altar. According to this prophecy and in ancient history, it is forbidden; for after the ark was constructed by Noah according to the command of the one guarding all, through a fearsome deluge, so that Noah and his house might be preserved from all harm, the season of rain already being upon them, the Lord says to the righteous: 'Enter, you and your sons and your wife and the wives of your sons' (Gen 7:7), so that inside the ark the men might find themselves by themselves and apart from the women, so that marital intercourse might not be performed during the corruption of the human race, all flowing apart except for the four couples entering into the ark, no longer remaining in a state of union between men and those living together; when the earth had dried and the flood had subsided, they go out of the ark, according to a command given by God: 'Noah went out, and his wife with him, and their sons and their wives' (Gen 8:18). For since the threat against men was hindered, the cohabitations were released, so that the human succession might increase from infancy.

Similarly to those thus viewed concerning Noah and those from the prophet Joel, and now being lifted up to a terrible lament, the word intends for men to cut themselves by themselves and likewise for women to cut themselves, in order to perceive the impending calamity. And behold the precision of the command, not only dispersing the different tribes from themselves, but also the same-natured men from women and vice versa; for it says: 'a tribe according to itself and their wives according to themselves.' He says a tribe of the house of David, those who by royal and sufficient practical power act in such a way. And since men differ from women not only by history, the one giving birth and the other conceiving, but also by analogy, the souls that sow lessons to other souls...

Men should be called in a teaching manner those who receive lessons from others rather than generating them from themselves, being allegorically matched with women. Similarly, regarding Nathan, Levi, Simeon, and the remaining tribes, let the variation of men and women remain regarding explicit meaning and thought. The tribe of Nathan and that of Levi, possessing prophetic citizenship and knowledge, exist as healers of God. For Nathan is a prophet, and Levi is a priest; for from him, according to history, those who heal God are priestically descended.

Another among both is Simeon, being interpreted as 'one who hears' or 'a listener,' signifying those who are listened to by God inclining toward their supplications, especially since they themselves are listening to the divine commands. Just as the men named are separate, while the women remain as themselves, so also the remaining tribes live similarly in being cut off.

It was precisely shown that the cutting off must occur not in any other city but in Jerusalem, from which the leading one looks especially toward an ascent; for even in the captivity, the people had just now experienced what the prophet said. Understand if it is according to such a purpose, as the conclusion of the world approaches, according to that written by John: 'The last hour is' (1 John 2:18), and when the human race is multiplied, the Apostle writes: 'The time is compressed; therefore let those who have wives be as if they had none' (1 Cor 7:29), outside of the men who are perfecting virginity and the widowed women living for Christ and those who have renewed their virginity, so that they may sincerely and without distraction attend to the prayers.
In that day every place shall be opened in the house of David and those dwelling in Jerusalem and for the movement and for the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Destruction of Idols and False Prophets
english: Sprinkling. On many a day already spoken of, with clarity, regarding others it will be so: every place in the house of David in Jerusalem will be opened, a movement occurring toward a divine sprinkling.

But the place being opened in the house of David is the God-breathed Scripture, especially that before the coming of the Savior; the place being opened is this Jerusalem, which is the heavenly and the mother of the righteous, existing as the 'city of the heavenly God of the living.'

In these things, the place to be omitted is not the body that circumscribes and limits, but that which divides into propositions and problems. The intellect will see a movement of these thus-treated places from the letter toward the spirit and from the shadow toward the truth; and, having summed it up, one might say, from the temporal toward the eternal, from the visible and low things toward the high and invisible.

And what follows the movement, or a pouring-over bringing perfect purification? This sprinkling is accomplished by the blood of the Savior, concerning which writes Peter, the most preeminent of the apostles, addressing those to whom he sends the epistle, saying: 'Grace to you and peace be multiplied, for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ' (1 Peter 1:2).

The divine blood sprinkles the conscience of those worshiping the living God, 'redeeming from the empty manner of received tradition' (1 Peter 1:18) those who are performing [it], as the wise instructor presents in the same epistle, thus: 'Knowing that not with corruptible things, silver or gold, were you redeemed, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot' (1 Peter 1:18-19).

Those pouring over toward the acquisition of a pure heart, repeatedly and continuously entreating toward the ability to desire purity, as one says: 'Wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow' (Psalm 51:7). Toward this purity, 'being a pure and undefiled worship' (James 1:27), the holy word exhorts: 'Wash, that you may become clean' (Ezekiel 36:25), it advises.

If the love of this spoken pouring-over enters even us, let us hasten to dwell as citizens in the intelligible Jerusalem being ruled by David, so that every interpreted place may be opened to us, having been moved from the shadowy toward the original and true wise contemplations.
On that day, the Lord says, 'I will destroy the names of the idols from the earth and they shall no more be a memory; and the false prophets and the unclean spirit I will remove from the earth.'

When the previously foretold movement becomes a sprinkling and the truth, the various forms of the heterodox, called idols tropically, shall be destroyed from the earth, no longer deceiving men, the tropical idolatry being exposed by the revealed truth and all false prophecy being annulled and the unclean spirit working it, being present in man before the faith into Christ.

It is also possible to say concerning the sensible idols and the demons concerning them that they shall be destroyed from the earth. But that the statues are indicated by this designation, it is possible to learn from the hymn-singer saying: 'The idols of the Gentiles, silver and gold, they have feet and they do not walk' (Psalm 115:4), and the following. That the demons defiling their shrines are called by the same name, the prophet Isaiah teaches beginning from there: 'Demolish, the carved images in Jerusalem and in Samaria; for in the same way as I did in Samaria and with its carved images, so will I do to Jerusalem and to its idols' (Isaiah 2:18).

In demolishing idols, both carved and cast, it is not the works of craftsmen that are being demolished, nor things that are natural to be demolished; for the energy is breathing life into them. For the demolition is a meaningless sound emitted by an animal by a passion of the soul. This meaning has been demonstrated in many ways in the memoirs concerning Isaiah, with the testimony of Solomon the Wise, having it thus: 'For equally hated by God are the impious man and his impiety; for what has been done with the doer shall be punished' (Wisdom 1:13).

These things were said to the wise man concerning a carpenter man and carved wood by him according to the form of an animal, and just as it is not able to demolish that which does not have a soul, as it was called a mere shadow, so it is not able to be punished effectively. Therefore, let these things be taken up concerning the demons wandering about with the soulless statues. While the idols are being destroyed from the earth, the false diviners and those who once promised false predictions are removed from it, false prophets in judgment by the divine.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shame of the False Prophet
english: Being called for instruction, he is being convinced of this same thing along with them and of the unclean spirit. For how can the spirit of the diviners and bird-diviners not have the impurity which comes from impiety?

This same word could also be applied to the protectors of heresies, who have happened to be full of demons and deceiving spirits. For regarding them the Lawgiver Paul writes thus: 'Some will depart from the healthy faith, paying attention to deceiving spirits and demonic teachings, in the hypocrisy of false prophets, having been cauterized in their own conscience' (1 Timothy 4:2).

It is not to be disturbed if the unclean spirit is spoken of in the singular in the prophet, but the deceiving spirits are spoken of in the plural in the Apostolic Scripture. For those things which are taken individually according to each are generally called one spirit. And it is also good to say that the naming of the names of idols is being destroyed, as if their mention were no longer to be, because of their vanity and foolishness, even though they exist only as a designation and not as a power.

Zach. XIII, 3: 'And it shall come to pass, if a man prophesies any more, his father and his mother who begot him will say to him, "You shall not live, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the Lord"'; and his father and his mother who begot him will run against him in his prophesying (Zechariah 13:3).

Once the false prophets and the unclean spirit have been removed from the earth, if a man should still dare to prophesy out of frenzy and madness, he would be so much a laughingstock and subject to rebuke, that even his parents would not believe him, but would vote for his death, announcing: 'He shall not live anymore because he has spoken falsely upon the name of the Lord,' he being found not a prophet but a false prophet.
By these things, the false prophet is rebuked by his father and his mother, who run against him and join in his downfall, rebuking his sophistries and his deceptive words.
