Because the phrase 'those who begot him in his prophesying' is ambiguous, it should be expanded into both meanings. One way it might be understood: those who begot him as a man have a disposition toward him as humans guarding parents, because he speaks falsely in the name of the Lord, and they join in his downfall by voting against him. The other way it might be attributed thus: his father and his mother...

They join in mockery against him, those who brought him forth into prophesying, having fathered him as a false prophet through upbringing and procreation, having generated him through imitation and teaching, and who are clearly possessed of a false-prophetic disposition.

It is not in vain that such an 'man' has been reproved; rather, because he walks falsely 'in strife and jealousy' according to the flesh, he holds the name of man, similar to those to whom it was said, 'You indeed die as men' (1 Cor 3:4), and concerning those unworthy of the Divine Spirit, the Lord says, 'My Spirit shall not remain in these men because they are flesh' (Rom 8:9).

Zechariah 13:4–6: And on that day the prophets shall be ashamed, each from his vision in his prophesying, and they shall put on haircloth instead of those [garments] by which they lied. And he shall say, 'I am not a prophet, because a man has fathered me from my youth.' And I will say to him, 'Why are these wounds between your hands?' And he shall say, 'Those which were struck in my beloved house.'

Those who promise foreknowledge experience shame because their pre-proclamation is falling away. Since, therefore, the indictment of the false prophet comes not from others alone but also from those who fathered him, for this reason he is ashamed, his prophecy having been exposed, so that he is left to revile himself and to be clothed in haircloth. For a man confesses that he has existed from youth, the youth of which now denotes not age but a young and impetuous character.

For the wicked one, not possessing prudent wisdom nor honorable old age, nor a life without blemish, passes through life with ignorance, according to the proverbial saying: 'Folly is widespread in the heart of a youth, and a rod and instruction are far from him' (Prov 13:24). He, finding this state to be the worst, offers a plea to God: 'Do not remember the sinfulness of my youth and my ignorance' (Ps 25:7).

He who is exposed as speaking falsely in prophesying, being ashamed of his vain vision—which is more like divination than true prophecy—confesses that he is not a prophet nor was he advanced from among the prophets to this.
And since, being clothed in haircloth, he is being coerced yet denies not in truth being a prophet, it is said to him: 'Why then the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shepherd and the Sheep
english: Wounds between your two hands? Regarding that which he says: 'She was struck in the house of my beloved,' even those who begot me are not enduring [it] as a prophet, as if bringing wounds against me.

It is possible to call the house of the beloved the house of the false prophet, knowing the multitude loved by him who divines, in order to subject him to afflictions. And these things are to be applied to those who hold different opinions in Christianity.

The false repentance of one wearing sackcloth is brought in [the context of] Isaiah against those fasting and praying, becoming a rebuke against the hypocrites: 'For if you bow your neck like a yoke and bend your neck and put on sackcloth and ashes, you will not even call it a pleasing fast' (Isa 58:5). I do not say this as if no one benefits from the painful discipline and harsh diet, which then becomes beneficial when it is accomplished along with repentance.

The Ninevites, indeed, having repented with much wickedness according to the preaching of the prophet Jonah (Jonah 3), have escaped after the threat of a great destruction of their city. The hymn-writer also agrees, where he says: 'In that they were bothering me,' making the enemies both visible and invisible apparent, 'I put on sackcloth and they were humbling my soul in fasting' (Ps 69:13), and in another Psalm: 'I made my clothing sackcloth, and I became a parable to them' (Ps 69:34).

From this state thus occurring, of gloominess for the sake of acquiring good things, he who attains them, having changed into joy, says: 'You have turned my mourning into joy, you have torn my sackcloth and girded me with gladness' (Ps 30:11).

Zechariah XII, 7: 'A sword, has arisen against my shepherd and against the man, the citizen of him, says the Lord of hosts: Strike the shepherd and let the sheep be scattered, and I will strike my hand upon the shepherds.'

From this prophecy, the evangelist Matthew took up what was said in the Gospel according to him, when, Jesus having been seized, the disciples having been scandalized and having fled, he said: 'So that what was said through the prophet might be fulfilled: I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered' (Matt 26:31), saying strike and wound the death of the shepherd of the true flock, who is above reason, 'having laid down his soul.'

"himself for the sheep," "given as a ransom for many." Regarding the assault that occurred in this way, where the hands of the excellent lawgiver were struck and his feet were dug up, it is his own to hear the Father saying: "Whom you struck, they themselves persecuted, and upon the pain of my wounds they themselves added" (Psalm 21:6). For the murderers, having struck the one whom God delivered over to them, added to the pain of his wounds, increasing the assault while pursuing him.

The holy thing attempted by the wicked—the one who, setting himself forward for the sheep, stood as a protector, having the Hebrew people as his citizen—the drawn sword was raised against his own shepherd and his citizen. Thus, the drawn sword killed indeed the citizen, but did not harm the shepherd of the flock, having accepted death for the sake of the sparing of the flock.

For how could he, the one affirming to God, "Save my soul from the sword" (Psalm 34:13), not remain free from all harm? This voice is carried in the twenty-first Psalm, spoken from the person of the whole Savior being brought forth. Having had the soul saved from the sword after sending up the prayer, his citizen fell by the sword of execution, according to that which was said in Amos the prophet: "Let all sinners of the people perish by the sword" (Amos 9:4). The same punishment is alluded to by the prophet in Wisdom by God: "You, Ethiopians, are wounded by my sword" (Wisdom 9:13).

Those being struck by the sword of God are called Ethiopians, those who shared in the wickedness and sin of the devil, being named so from his blackness. For in the Shepherd and in the Epistle of Barnabas, Satan is approached as black, having fallen from brightness and virtue and the intellectual whiteness which only the one being whitened by God can have.

Having the shepherd struck in the said manner and because of this the sheep being scattered, he stretches out his hand toward the shepherds, the high priest and the elders and the Jewish law-teachers who agreed against the good shepherd having been set forth for the sheep, so that they might have his soul's salvation. And the scattering of the sheep has increased, and the [hand] of God being stretched out upon them and the flock under them...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Third Group and the Refining Fire
english: Since the fourth word has been sufficiently described regarding the 'I will stretch out my hand over the shepherds' (Zechariah 13:7), spoken by God, providing the beginning of the fifth, we shall proceed from the sixth word having this character.

And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, that two parts shall be destroyed and cut off, but the third shall be left in it; and I will pass through the third through fire and will consume them, as silver is consumed by fire, and I will test them, as gold is tested; he will call upon my name, and I will listen to him, and I will say: This is my people, and he will say: The Lord is my God (Zechariah 13:8-9).

The time is marked by the name of the day, revealing in which the two parts of the captured people shall be destroyed and cut off, the third being shown as tested, passing through fire, and being burned according to how silver is purified and being tested according to how gold is tested. This third of the captives, thus purified and tested, calling upon the name of God, shall have God listening to him and saving him; to whom it will harmoniously belong to reward the people who have been benefited by his listening, God being shown to them in the manner of being their God, as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were. For to all other men God is as Creator, but uniquely to the patriarchs, who worship and revere him.
Having considered these things more holistically, let us see next what the two parts are that are being destroyed and abandoned, and what the third is that is being improved and led into salvation.

It is sufficient to consider the division into three of the captured Hebrew people. Many of those deported from their own land and fatherland into the captivity of those who prevailed, having entirely fallen from godliness into idols, worshipped as if to serve the... and

To worship the beast and the dragon, and alongside these, to bow to the mute image of Nebuchadnezzar the tyrant; while others were not doing this, but were acting lawlessly against Judaism and as if they should not change, such as were the elders who remained, adulterously unfaithful, and those who agreed with them against the more prudent Shushan.

Among those who had worshipped idols and were acting lawlessly as Jews, there was another excellent and God-fearing rank in the captivity; they did not fall into dread, nor did they break the law, but were holy and pleasing to God, from whom many men were recorded as saints, of whom are the clearly revealed prophet Zechariah, and Daniel, and those around Azariah, the prophet Ezekiel, and the high priest Jesus the son of Joshedek, and others more, changing through moral virtue and the knowledge of the truth and of God.

The impious parts, two, the Greek and the Jewish, because of what they had done, being a tormentor, are being destroyed and failing, so that through a more strenuous discipline they might cast away the harms that had come upon them. Of this having been done, by the judgment of the divine providence, the third part, being divided from the two parts, is sanctified and made better by the Giver of good things, the Divine Word, being led through the purifying fire and 'burning with the spirit,' concerning which the same One saving all things says: 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and would I were it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49), and again: 'Every one shall be salted with fire' (Mark 9:49).

Concerning him also the great John, 'of whom no one greater was raised among those born of women' (Matthew 11:11), teaches concerning himself: 'I came baptizing in water unto repentance' (Luke 3:3), but concerning the Savior of all: 'He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire' (Matthew 3:11), sanctifying and purifying, making it clear [that it is] those through the Holy Spirit, and those through fire, or the same ones both in the Holy Spirit and in the fire.
Those having come through fire, being the third of the captives, the improving one, at whom God breathed upon the one being called, from the face of Himself toward the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Third Perfection and the Testing of the Word
english: They say they desired salvation: 'O God, you tested us, you burned us like silver is burned; you brought us into a snare, you set tribulations before us'—or 'into our midst'; for it is also carried in many manuscripts—'you brought up men upon our necks, we passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into refreshment.'

Similarly in Isaiah, regarding the one who helps and does good, it says: 'Do not fear, for I am with you; and if you pass through water, rivers shall not overwhelm you; and if you walk through fire, flame shall not burn you, for I am with you' (Isa 43:2). When, then, does anyone pass through fire and remain unharmed, unless he has possessed the voice of God, concerning which it was said: 'The voice of the Lord breaking a flaming fire' (Ps 29:7)? Just as the people crossed the Red Sea with the holy rod without any loss, as the flame of the fire was broken and divided, so the crossing proceeds without being consumed by the flame.

What remained of the third in the Hebrew plurality, the two parts having been destroyed and having ceased, was tested according to the intellect, both gold and silver, passing through fire. Similarly it is carried in Wisdom: 'Just as gold and silver are tested in a furnace, so are chosen hearts before God' (Wis 2:5). The same thought is held by what the apostle Peter writes in his epistle, exhorting to bear tribulations bravely and magnanimously, especially those concerning faith.

And his word has it thus: 'In which rejoice, though you may sometimes be grieved in various trials, so that the testing of your faith may be found more precious than gold being tested by fire; for it shall be found unto praise and glory' (1 Pet 1:6-7). In agreement, James also addresses the disciples of the Gospel: 'Count it all joy, beloved brothers, when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of you works patience; and let patience have a perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing' (Jas 1:2-4). For thus, having been prepared, those to whom the word is addressed, having been burned like silver according to the word and having been tested like gold according to their own intellect, shall have God listening, calling upon His name, as He benefits them as a people.

To turn from the benefactor to their own God. The matter laid before is being tortured and is otherwise clear. In the Church of Christ, there are some practicing superstition and others Judaizing among them, even as they also sincerely fear God, in whom the apostles, being said to speak wisdom, have all progressed as far as to reach 'a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of the knowledge of the Son of God' (Eph 4:13).

The two destroying parts will be cut away, so that they may no longer practice superstition or Judaize according to the ways of the Ebionites. For when this has been endured, only the perfect of the Church will remain in it, so that they indeed may be made 'the people of God' (1 Pet 2:10), and He himself may be confessed as 'their God' (Ex 21:6).

Understand precisely even if a third theory may be said regarding the things set forth. Each of the virtues lies in the middle of two evils, excess and deficiency: courage and temperance, the one being the middle of rashness and cowardice, the other of intemperance and foolishness, just as piety has excess in superstition and deficiency in impiety. Similarly, the free man, being social and giving, has the best middle, of which profligacy is excess and stinginess is deficiency.

And since of those sinning, some by excesses—doing rashness, superstition, and profligacy—and others by deficiencies—doing impiety, cowardice, and stinginess—these two ranks and parts must necessarily be destroyed and cut away having fallen under punishment, the third being perfected, being refined and tested like silver and gold, which is the word and the mind, in order to be tested and perfected according to the following virtues, having surpassed the deficiencies and excesses.

It is said from property and another scientific thought thus: 'those bearing the image of the swine', partaking of a material disposition, become unclean, approaching that which is called an indefinite duality toward some. And according to the Scripture, indeed, the unclean of the animals are taken two by two, while the clean are brought into the ark seven by seven, belonging to the incorruptible virgin week (Gen 7:2). And since those bearing the image of the swine are two, the quality of these is also cut away and destroyed, so that the third may be revealed as tested 'of those bearing the image of...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Desolation of Women and Property
english: The wise man applies each word of the text to each of the fulfillments. It is possible to understand that the third remains in that day on which these things previously spoken shall occur.

Behold, days are coming of the Lord, and your dogs shall be divided in you (Zach. 14:1-2). And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war, and the city shall be captured, and the houses shall be plundered, and the women shall be violated, and half the city shall go out in captivity, but the remnant of my people shall not be destroyed from the city (Zach. 14:2). He says 'Days of the Lord' according to how the burdensome and punishing things come upon the guilty, and there are many witnesses to this by understanding. And in Isaiah, indeed, the time of God's punishments is called a day thus: 'A day of the Lord comes, unyielding, in fury and wrath, to lay the whole inhabited world waste and to destroy the sinners from it' (Isa. 9:3).

Since, therefore, he announces fearsome things shall be to those against whom God is indignant because of their grasping impiety and other sins, it is fitting he says there shall be days of the Lord in which there will be most pitiful wickedness toward Jerusalem and its citizens. For why is it so pitiful and unyielding, that the dogs which the coming enemies took, to be divided in its midst because of much existing weakness? But this does not always happen; for there is a time when those who plundered, far from the city, rather the land, having carried off the spoils, are divided, fearing that they might be prevented from dividing them in the city by those who have captured breathing.

After the word having spoken: 'Behold, days are coming of the Lord, and your dogs shall be divided in your midst' (Zach. 14:2), the Lord immediately says to gather against them all the nations for war, just as a day becomes one of mobilization, of the armies of the gathered nations toward the waging of war against Jerusalem. For toward it is announced the dividing of its dogs in it, and even the houses of the inhabitants shall be plundered, and their women shall be violated. For what manner of way is painful and extremely unyielding is the dividing of those who grasped, in the sight of the citizens, especially when not only the common and...

Not only public treasures but also those of each person, as their houses are being plundered; moreover, regarding all these things, it is both sorrowful and heavy to be shamefully violated, seeing those who live together being unable to prevent the lawless act after much weakness has taken hold, just as half of the city itself has been torn away outside its own town, seeing nothing of this kind among those being guarded by the right hand of God. These are the ones fulfilling the third [part], it having been said that they shall be saved after the two parts have been destroyed and left behind.

5.26 Such a harsh providence the divine word threatens also in Isaiah; and thus the prophetic speech has: 'Those who are gathered together,' turned toward one another, 'shall fall by the sword; and your children shall be thrown down before you, and your houses shall be plundered, and your women shall be taken' (Isa 5:17).

5.27 The excess is shown in the women suffering violence from tyrannizing enemies in addition to the men living with them, and from what was said to the worthless priest Amaziah by the prophet Amos, seeing sharply: 'Your wife in the city shall commit fornication, and your land shall be measured with a cord' (Amos 8:2). Both the threatened things are painful and cause agony to those living together, seeing the cohabitants inside the city and not outside it, being corrupted in their lawful marital rights by the most savage enemies, and their own land being measured with a cord, while the owners are present and are not strong enough to prevent the violence.

5.28 It happened... such things happened many times to those dwelling in Jerusalem and in Judah, the Jews being taken by the nations because of the impiety they received, having killed the Lord. 'For having watched, and having studied the emptiness and futility of the peoples, and having brought forward the kings and the rulers, having been gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ, God incited them and stirred them up, speaking in wrath against them and in His own anger unsettling them,' just as the Apostle wrote the same concerning those killing the Lord and the prophets and driving out the apostles: 'The wrath has come upon them to its end' (Rom 11:22).
5.29 It was also said previously as a Jewish historian,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Descent and Motion
english: Joseph, his name, wrote truly and with precision the misfortunes, famines, and other much more distressing evils that were coming upon the nation, which the beauty-loving reader, rejoicing in reading, is inclined to see toward a love of learning and a fear of not suffering the same.

He says [that they are] not being driven out of the city by the cruel tyrants, whom God tests in fire as silver and gold are tested, in order that their vainglory and condemnation might be known. [Zechariah 14:3-4: The Lord will arise and line up against those nations as on a day of battle. And his feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives that is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives shall be split in two, half of it toward the east and half toward the sea, a very great chaos.]

God, being incorporeal, rather exceeding all spiritual substance, is without reception of those things pertaining to bodies—colors, forms, and magnitudes—I say, whence he is invisible. For every visible substance must exist under forms, magnitudes, colors, and their adjacents, but God is invisible, as many words of the Scriptures testify, being a spiritual substance, nor does he move transitionally, nor does the whole exist in a place.

It is sufficient to receive the testimony having such [characteristics]: 'Who is the image of the invisible God' [Colossians 1:15], and again: 'To the King of the ages, the incorruptible invisible God' [1 Timothy 6:16]. The apostolic words and the evangelical ones declare the same: she [the Scripture] having thus: 'No one has seen God at any time; the only-begotten God who is in the bosom of the Father has made him known' [John 1:18], and again: 'Not that anyone has seen God, except the one who is from the Father' [John 6:46].

Since, therefore, these things are rightly said and thought concerning God, the more bodily things concerning him announced economically in the divine Scriptures must be understood spiritually and appropriately. For the manner of him being said in the prophet: 'I have not changed' [Malachi 3:6], and of the theologians saying similarly, the one hymnographer to the one being glorified saying: 'But you are the same,' and: 'But you remain,' and of Jacob writing about the...

Suffering and unchangeable. 'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning' (James 1:17). And just as we grasp and understand the words concerning his repentance and his wrath and those of the neighbors, so, since he is incorporeal, we receive the words concerning ascending and descending, and going out and coming in, in harmony with the thought concerning him.

Therefore, in the present prophecy where it is written: 'The Lord will go forth' (Zephaniah 1:15), we do not imagine a changing motion; for such motions belong to bodies. 5.36 Since, therefore, it does not fit to confess these things concerning an invisible essence, yet they are carried in the divinely inspired oracles, it is necessary to oversee how they must be understood piously. 5.37 Being a fountain of goodness and 'full of grace and truth' (John 1:14), the cause of all things, descending in sympathy with those being managed by him, becomes outside himself as if he were among them. For the Lord and our Savior says in the Gospels concerning himself: 'I went out from God and I have come; for I did not come from myself, but he sent me' (John 16:28). With the same thought the prophet Habakkuk spoke toward him: 'You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your anointed ones' (Habakkuk 3:3). 5.38 And just as he goes out and comes to those being saved, so much more when he is wroth or wars. For it is written concerning Michael: 'Behold, the Lord goes forth from his house, and he shall be among us for a witness and shall descend' (Jude 1:9), and in Isaiah: 'The Lord of powers will go forth and will crush war, and he will arouse zeal and will cry out against his enemies with strength' (Isaiah 63:3). 5.39 Considering these things in a God-befitting manner, God is said to go out 'upon the nations, that he may array himself against them as in a day of war' (Zephaniah 1:15) when 'his feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives toward the east' (Zechariah 14:4); for where must his feet stand, since he is no longer moving in indignation, according to what was already previously said: 'And the Lord will sound the trumpet and will go forth in the threat of his wrath' (Zephaniah 1:16)? In this way, Adam heard the voice of the feet of God, the fearful one, having received the sensation of him leaving and walking away from him who previously was with him and conversing with him. 5.40 The Savior said by this thought in...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Olive Trees and the Heavenly Citizenship
english: Regarding the Gospel, to the Jews who have become outside the truth: 'Behold, your house is being left to you' (Luke 2:3), and previously in the prophet: 'I have left my house, I have abandoned my inheritance' (Haggai 2:9), and the following. However, even if it has happened outside among those abandoned through impiety, nevertheless his feet stand unshakeably upon the mountain, where a planting is to be established, bearing fruit that is saving and guarding by the divine light and loosening diseases and pains. And they shall stand not in lowly planting, but in height and remaining on a mountain, from the risings of the divine light of the sun of righteousness.

What then is exceeded, [by] the standing of the feet of the Lord toward the risings of the mountain of olives, or the dividing of the divine planting, so that the part of it having cast its roots toward the risings remains, while the rest has passed into the sea, where there is great chaos? And since in the Scripture one finds olives praised and [others] reproached being gathered together, let us see which of these are set down in the light and the rising, and which ones have turned toward the sea.

The holy hymn-singer, crowing about himself, announces: 'I am like an olive tree bearing fruit in the house of God.' And concerning the one having perfected piety, in one of the Psalms of the Ascents he is carried: 'Blessed are you, and it shall go well with you. Your wife is like a vine flourishing in the trellises of your house; your sons are like olive shoots around your table. Behold, thus shall a man be blessed who fears the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem, and may you see sons of your sons' (Psalm 128:3-6).

No one who encounters this psalm sincerely is so slow and dull as you think, [believing] that all these promised things approach every pious person; many have possessed [it], the fear of God perfecting the one having it, according to that which is written: 'There is no support for those fearing him' (Job 27:4), and it is clear that [it is] God, not at all the material things they have possessed. For Elijah, indeed, the...

A great prophet, and Elisha his disciple, and—what am I saying?—John the Baptist, who became 'among those born of women no one is greater than him' (Matt 11:11), did not possess any of the things enumerated sensually, not having lived with women, nor having had sensual children; but even if they did not participate in these sensual things at all, they had sons and grandsons through an elevation, having been blessed by God in Zion and having seen the good things of the true Jerusalem, having arrived at the mountain of Zion and at Jerusalem, which is the heavenly city of the living God.

5.45 The olive trees thus attributed and their young shoots have their planting in the Mount of Olives toward the east, to be transplanted into the paradise which God planted in Eden toward the east. And the thing being announced is not paradoxical; for if the repentant robber, having confessed the King as Savior, heard from him: 'Today you shall be with me in paradise' (Luke 23:43), how much more will those who lived their whole life or the greater part of it in this way receive such a promise, as they can say with boldness: 'For our citizenship is in the heavens' (Phil 3:20), and again: 'Groaning on earth, we have a citizenship in the heavens' (2 Cor 5:1).

5.46 One must be planted toward this blessedness by elevation, and the wild olive tree, having been grafted into the holy root and becoming fruitful upon the good olive tree, as the singer says with the same boldness: 'But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God' (Ps 52:8), of the branches having been cut off through unbelief—and these are the Jews who committed the murder—being found in the sea, that is, by the waves and the salt of the affairs of the world, where there is great chaos.

5.47 In agreement with the Apostle and in Jeremiah concerning the branches having been cut off, God, expressing His opposition toward the assembly of the circumcision, says: 'What has the beloved done in my house to make an abomination? Are not sacrifices and holy meats...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The North Wind and the Approach of God
english: "Will they take the wickedness from you, or will they flee in these things?" Having rebuked her who, the divine word seeing, had done an abomination in his house, the Lord calls her name an olive tree of easy access; your branches have become useless. For how have the branches that fell through their own unfaithfulness become useless, especially having moved into the storm of life, in which there are billows and a multitude of salty and bitter waters.

Regarding the unfaithful branches having come to the sea and being torn apart by a very strong wind, it is said concerning this ruined city—the Jewish one, I say—and by another prophet, who is Micah, by God: "I will scatter the stones of it into chaos and I will uncover its foundations" (Micah).

When these gloomy things have come upon the wretched synagogue of the Jews, it is necessary for us, those having believed in the Savior, to become a fruitful olive in the house of God and toward the rising in the mount of olives, so that we may also be transferred into the divine paradise by the grace of God, becoming imitators of Christ, concerning whom it is written: "Behold, a man, rising is his name" (Zechariah 14:4).

"Half of the mountain shall lean toward the north and half of it toward the south. And the gorge of my mountains shall be blocked, and the gorge of my mountains shall be joined up as far as Asher, just as it was blocked in the days of the earthquake in the days of King Uzziah of Judah" (Zechariah 14:4-5).
The half, he says, of the mountain—clearly the mount of olives—will lean toward the north, toward the one deviating into the sea and the chaos, the other half reaching toward the south.

What are the north and the south? From the Breath of Breaths, the Church having been ravished by her own bridegroom, is to learn, saying: "Arise, north, and come, south, blow upon my garden and let my aromas flow."

The north in these things is the evil power, rather Satan himself; the south, being the Savior himself, is approached as the bridegroom. Therefore, when the very cold north is present, the flow of the divine aromas is hindered, the pores being choked because they become thickened due to the coldness of the north and become hard; the bride flees from this and calls to the south, so that by his warmth [she may...]

From the sources of the intelligible, the fragrances flow, concerning which it is said toward the bridal chamber of the spiritual spouse: 'The fragrance of your myrrh is above all spices' (Song of Solomon 1:3). The north wind is said to have heat and to be an invigorating breath, having learned that fire exists and came to cast upon the earth, as he himself announced saying: 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49).

It must be said: 'Arise, north wind,' not by voice alone but in reality, so that it may be sent from afar. In deeds, he says: 'Arise, north wind,' to the faithful soul saying to the teacher who speaks: 'Turn away from evil and do good,' and to the Apostle who wrote to the whole Church: 'Test all things, hold fast to the good. Abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thessalonians 5:21-22). The north wind, driving the abstention from every kind of evil and the turning away from evil, urges the south wind to come so as to draw near to it through pious faith and moral virtue. For thus, to those being thus prepared, the provider of all good things comes, as the theologian James wrote: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you' (James 4:8).

Having the longing for His presence, and being near to: 'Come, south wind,' in that bridal drama he hints: 'Come, my sister, let us go out to the field' (Song of Solomon 2:10). This is equivalent to: 'Arise, north wind, and come, south wind,' and to: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you, resist the devil and he will flee from you' (James 4:7-8), as the one resisting the devil says to him: 'Arise, north wind,' and the one drawing near to God entreating the south wind to come to him, the God Logos, concerning whom in the song of the prophet Habakkuk, according to some interpreters, it is brought forth instead of: 'God will come from Thaman,' [as] 'God will come from the south wind,' the coming of the Father from the south wind of the bride, according to that which is said by Him in the Gospel: 'He who receives me receives him who sent me' (John 13:20). For in whatever way he who sees Him sees the Father, so the one receiving Him receives the Father abiding in Him, in whom is His Only-begotten.

What will happen when turning toward the north and the south of the clarified mountain of olives, or when the gorge of the mountains of God is blocked and is joined even unto Asahel? The gorge and the joining could not be understood otherwise than by having known what the mountains of God are.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Earthquake in the Days of Josiah
english: Regarding his mountains, the prophets have said in accordance with the subject that there is a height belonging to them not only of knowledge and wisdom, but also of the application of practical life. For concerning these things, the hymn-singer spoke toward the origin of all: 'You shine wondrously from eternal mountains' (Ps 103:2). For how could they not be eternal mountains, from which God wondrously illuminates the knowledge of the truth and broadly the knowledge concerning the Trinity, those who gaze upon unseeing eternal things according to the apostolic exhortation (2 Cor 4:18)?

The abyss of the depth of the obscurity of those things spoken in enigma is a gorge of these mountains, which he who came to fulfill the law and the prophets (Matt 5:17) has unblocked, having leveled with his own teaching and presence the rough and uneven ground of those things spoken with concealment, so that it might appear easy to traverse through smoothness. This having happened, the gorge of the mountains was joined to the text through the appearing of harmony, up to Asaph, who was called 'deaf to the feet' because of the speed of his walking, according to the sharp-seeing gaze; for this animal is perceptive, as the appellation itself shows from the word 'gazing'. Therefore, up to Asaph, the attachment of the mountains shall be, being known to the perceptive.

In the same way, the obstruction of the mountains has occurred as in the days of the earthquake, which existed in the days of Uzziah, the king of Judah. We have not found a perceptible earthquake having occurred at all while Uzziah was reigning, neither in the Kingdoms nor in the Chronicles; therefore, what is written about him must be understood allegorically. And see lest a shaking occurred during Uzziah, intending to seize the priesthood for himself. For having entered into the temple of God, and having approached the holy altar, he attempts to offer sacrifice through himself and not through the priests (2 Chron 26:16). The daily priest, most boldly asserting this transgression, while coinciding with the others, saying: 'It is not yours, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but that of the priests,' he was distressed, and he stretched out his hand with anger to be seized by the guards to harm them; but immediately his hand was struck, as if to cast the tyrant out of the temple instantly, having been struck by the holy [place] as far as the porch, because of his insolence.

[...] having taken a practice not fitting for another except for the priests presiding in the temple. 5.62 Regarding the encounter with that which it is determined to draw to itself, the works of the kingdom were hindered by the unclean leprosy, while he was performing them, the rest of his son who was about to receive the rule. 5.63 In the days of the earthquake from the commingling, a precipice became attached to the mountains, in the days of Judah, while Ozias was reigning. 5.64 The earthquake now being declared lies also at the beginning of the prophet Amos: 'For words,' says Amos, 'which came from Tekoa, two years before the earthquake in the days of Ozias,' the earthquake being said here, according to the circulating Jewish tradition, of the vision appearing to Isaiah, concerning which it has been written thus: 'It happened in the year in which King Ozias died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted-up throne, and Seraphim were standing around him, six wings to the one and six wings to the other' (Isa 6:1-2), and after a little: 'And the other cried to the other: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth, full is the heaven and the earth of his glory' (Isa 6:3).

5.65 Full is the heaven and the earth of the glory of God became, after the death of Ozias with which he practiced lawlessness. For how could there not be a shaking of change toward the better having happened by the seeing of God, so that the heaven and the earth might be filled with his glory, and a removal might occur of the lawlessness of the one discovered in seeing the divine vision, and a remission of the sins of all the people? 5.66 In the days of the death of Ozias, who desired to plunge the divine laws, desiring to seize for himself the priestly service not fitting to him, there was attached that which he had newly cut through by a cleavage of the laws, so that the priest might again unhinderedly perform his own things in the temple, and the king, attending to the protection of those in authority, was no longer touching the priestly things because the care of the holy things was not to be held by him. 5.67 Or is Asael here a name of a place; let him be heard by the one having circled the places of Judah, having grasped something that seems accurate. 5.68 And the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him. In that day there shall not be light. And there shall be frost and ice one day (Zech 14:5-7).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Eternal Day of the Lord
english: And that day is known to the Lord. And it shall not be day nor night, and towards evening there shall be light.

The present voice is able to signify a second and glorious appearance of the Savior, concerning which John in Revelation spoke highly and God-appropriately thus: 'Behold, he comes with the clouds, and every eye shall see him, and those who pierced him' (Rev 1:7). This understanding is based on what the Savior said concerning himself: 'Clouds shall see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory' (Matt 24:30). For how could he who comes royally not shine with much glory? And he comes also with much power, with the saints coming with him, not of men alone but also of angels. For it follows that 'those having become his attendants and servants' and 'the ministering spirits having been sent for service' shall shine with him, so that he himself may be known as their king and they as his powers, that is, an army.

On the day in which the Lord God shall come, there shall not be perceptible light, because of the true and eternal light making him [bright], according to what was pre-proclaimed in Isaiah concerning the perfect illumination, having it here: 'The sun shall not be your light by day, nor the rising of the moon shall light your night, but the Lord shall be to you an eternal light, and your God shall be your glory' (Isa 60:19-20). It must also be said thus: those not possessing light need that which shines upon them, not needing this when they themselves have become light.

Since therefore in the future age, called allegorically 'day', 'the righteous shall shine like the sun in the kingdom of their own Father', having been made light and shining themselves, they pass through the day not needing an external light. And indeed in this life, having enlightened themselves with the light of knowledge as having heard from the Savior: 'You are the light of the world' (Matt 5:14), they pass through in a bright state not from another, but from light of themselves and of a day being present, concerning which the choir of the saints sings: 'Let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us' (Ps 33:3). Toward this spiritual Jerusalem having much holiness, the prophet says, being seized by God and having the Holy Spirit: 'Be enlightened...'

“Shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come upon you, and the glory of your God has risen upon you. Behold, darkness and gloom will cover the earth upon the nations; but upon you the Lord will appear, and the glory of your God will rise upon you. And kings will go to your light, and nations to your brightness” (Isa 60:1-3).

How is it not that it exists bright and illuminated, since this is being announced—the light having come to be from having been illuminated, as if divine brightness were being revealed? Understand, if possible, how so to impose upon the coming prophetic voice.

When the Lord Pantokrator comes with His saints, the state of those being judged will be such that each one who is ignorant of his own [deeds] will not have light, so as to need “the one illuminating the secrets of darkness and revealing the purposes of hearts” (Heb 4:13), so that, “having been revealed before the judgment seat of Christ” (2 Cor 5:10), they may receive what is worthy of what they did through the body, both good and evil.

And since there will be confusion and turmoil for those being judged, being gathered together and being tossed about, on a single day there will happen heat and ice to the souls of men, in the expectation of those being liberated from the gloomy and the oppressive, as the Gospel proclaims.

The day of the Lord, being continuous and not being interrupted by a night intervening, will be known to God, “since the existing light has no darkness at all” (Rev 22:5), and for this reason, being neither day nor night, but the day being eternal, the sun no longer making the day, nor the moon illuminating the night, according to the prophet, as it was said nearby, the Lord being eternal light. Even if ever indeed some should enjoy the day, toward evening there will be light, as God illuminates all things.

This day, being thus understood and occurring, will be known to the Lord, being worthy of His knowledge, according to what is signified and written: “The Lord knew those who were His” (2 Tim 2:19). This voice does not contradict the Gospel voice which says: “Concerning that hour and that day no one knew, nor the angels, nor the Son, but the Father alone” (Matt 24:36). Many things concerning the Gospel have been observed in the notes to Matthew according to a previous arrangement, which the lover of beauty will encounter, only being said now that the
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Division of Living Water
english: To know and not to know means that one must grasp one thing or another, rather than the knowing and not-knowing signifying something else.

Zach. 14:8–9: And in that day living water shall come out from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea and half of it to the last sea, and it shall be thus in summer and in winter. And the Lord shall be king over all the earth. On the known day of the Lord, living water shall come out from Jerusalem, 'of the heavenly city of the living God,' of which the half shall be toward the first sea, the rest half toward the last sea, going, the same thing happening not only in summer but also in spring, over all the earth, that is, of the humans, the Lord reigning.

Since nothing sensible or historical is being manifested by the prophecy, all of it must be received by anagogical lifting up. For the living water coming out from the intelligible Jerusalem, which sees the peace of the Church, is the spiritual law, or rather the knowledge of ecclesiastical understandings, which, going out toward the sea, makes it sweet and makes it calm, being driven out against every winter and overturning it.

This indeed the vision has attained clarity, as we were explaining recently the one in Isaiah having it thus: 'The whole earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea' (Isa 11:9). For just as the divine love, that which is from God toward those experiencing good, and that of the benefactors toward the magnanimous, 'covers a multitude of sins' (1 Pet 4:8), vanishing [the sins], but not guarding [them], and covering what was done crudely, so the knowledge of God, existing as living water, covers the seas, changing them into sweetness and something drinkable.
Thus the living water coming out from Jerusalem into the first and last sea, having lifted up every dizziness and storm, every saltiness and bitterness, prosperity and calm...

He will prepare a spring and a fountain so that seas shall no longer be. Living water having been divided, it came upon them; for one half of it went into the first, and the other half went into the last, which has received it, not in the summer alone but also in the springtime.

And of such a benefit existing, the Lord will rule over all the earth, according to the things said in the Psalms, where it says: 'The Lord has reigned, let the earth rejoice' (Ps 96:1), and where it says: 'Say among the nations: The Lord has reigned, and indeed he has established the inhabited world, which shall not be shaken' (Ps 97:1). Then the inhabited world is established so as to remain unshakeable, when the first sea, being the assembly of the Jews, has been made sweet, and the last, being the calling of the Gentiles. Both these seas were being filled with disturbance and storm before the reception of the gospel and the faith into the Savior, and rather into the Holy Trinity.

Try if it is possible to divide the living water into the two covenants, the new and the old, this happening when the water has become outside of Jerusalem. And from it there went out a little while 'into the whole earth' arrived 'the sound' of the words of God and 'his words to the ends of the inhabited world', as everywhere a 'sweet fragrance' is being spiritually 'offered to God and a pure sacrifice', since the Lord has been greatly revealed among all the nations.

The living water having been divided into a half and a half into the two covenants, it was within in Jerusalem, being guarded under the shadow of the law and of the antiquity of the letter, rather being covered, while the peak of winter was holding; but when the spring was received, the things having blossomed upon the earth and the voice of the vintage calling in the land, according to that which was said in the Song of Songs, 'the fig tree has yielded its figs, the vines are fragrant, the winter has passed, the rain has gone, it has departed, the flowers appeared in the land' (Song 2:11-12).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Knowledge of the One True God
english: Because a spiritual spring has come to be, and the rest of the month of new moons has arrived, we celebrate the feast of passing, called Passover by the Hebrew voice, in which Christ is hidden, so that, bearing his spiritual flesh and his holy blood, we might 'celebrate the feast with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (1 Cor 5:8), through which we shall also complete the festival of the high feast and that of the weeks, called Pentecost, in which we shall reap perfect gleanings and most full ears having come to be from those that blossomed in the spring.

Concerning both of the seasons, the holy one said, praising God: 'You prepared sun and moon, harvest and spring, you made these, remember your creation' (Ps 74:17), this whole earth, I mean indeed humanity, with only one reigning after the destruction of death, from Adam until Moses reigned and the devil held his power.

A testimony of water becoming living is taken from the Gospel of the Savior, who said: 'But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him shall become in him a spring of water living, leaping into eternal life' (John 4:14), and again: 'He who believes in me, just as the scripture said, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly' (John 7:38). For just as the one drinking from the water which Jesus gives shall have a spring of living water in him, so rivers of living water shall flow from the belly of the one drinking.

In that day the Lord shall be one, and His name one. He shall encircle all the earth and the wilderness from Gaber to Rehob, according to the south of Jerusalem; but Rama shall remain in its place; from the gate of Benjamin to the first gate, to the gate of the corners, and to the tower of Anameel, to the royal substructures, they shall dwell in it, and there shall no longer be a curse, and Jerusalem shall dwell securely (Zech 14:9-11).

When the aforementioned things exist as a gift of God, the polytheism of such a kind will be destroyed, by the one alone having composed all things and being known and confessed. For in the past, while there was difference between the last and first sea, the calling of the Jews and the Greeks—for these seas were given—it was not confessed by all that there is one God. The idolaters thought many to be gods, one...

Even the Jews. But when the gospel has come, the knowledge of the one and only progenitor has risen above men, as Paul, speaking in Christ, writes: 'Is God not only of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles? Yes, also of the Gentiles, since God is one' (Rom 3:4). For this is what it signifies, that God is one.

Therefore, on the day in which the expected one, the Only-begotten Son of God, is to come, with all error and false glory being abolished, the one and only true God shall be confessed, so that those having possessed the knowledge of the truth may alone worship and serve him, since the works of hands are no longer being [called gods], as the divine Logos says: 'The gods who did not make the heaven and the earth, let them perish from the earth and from under the heaven' (Jer 5:4).

It has been said in the previously set forth passages that the Lord will destroy all the woods from the earth, removing from it the unclean spirit, so that the demons are no longer considered gods, concerning whom the theologian says that to him 'the unmanifest and the hidden things of wisdom' are revealed by the Master of all: 'All the gods of the Gentiles are demons.'

Not only, therefore, when these pseudonymous gods have been refuted by no longer being supposed to be gods will the one God be known, 'having turned' the apostates 'from idols to serve the living and true God' (1 Tim 1:1), but also by being piously seen that neither the world is God, nor any part of it, nor are men still worshipping or revering the creation instead of the Creator, so as no longer to worship the sun and the moon or serve them.

In this way, the oneness of God will remain, on the day in which the sun of righteousness makes and shows himself, and his name will be one. For it is signified by one name, being in agreement with the exact thought and having piety of all, the fulfillment of what was said in the hymns: 'Wonderful is your name in all the earth' (Ps 8:1), and again: 'You have magnified your holy name above all' (Ps 113:3), and again: 'As your name, O God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth' (Ps 72:17). In agreement with the hymn, the prophet Habakkuk also says these things concerning the true God: 'The earth is full of his praise' (Hab 2:14).
Since everywhere on the earth the designation of the one God has been proclaimed and glorified, another name...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Gate of Benjamin and the Cornerstone
english: It is not a sign that signifies God. But most especially this will be the case when the prayer said to others toward God, 'Hallowed be thy name,' is being fulfilled. For in a certain way the name of God is being used to be blasphemed and profaned among the Gentiles because of those not thinking or acting accordingly to Him; but it is being sanctified when the appropriation of God is revealed unmixedly, having been shown through all things to be good and excellent, with God becoming all in all at the consummation of things.

The name of God is sanctified also when it was not yet lying before idols and images and the creation as being one among all things. Once God being shown to be one and His name being shown to be one, what is to be received as a matter of command? Around all the earth and even to the desert, 'The Lord is one' and His name shall be confessed. The desert here is to be understood as the Church from the Gentiles, and the land as the people from circumcision. For both peoples shall serve one Lord, knowing no other than the God who has spoken: 'Besides me you shall know no God' (Isa 43:10) and besides my name, which is magnified over all.

When hearing of one God, we say the Trinity, as the significance is to be thought to be concerning the Father, not neither the Son and Holy Spirit. For there is one divinity of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, as it has been demonstrated through many things in the word concerning the Son.

Once one Lord being shown and His name being one around all the earth and even to the desert, the thought 'from Abel' took its beginning, which is taken as a testimony, concerning which the Savior taught in the Gospel, saying: 'Search the Scriptures, for these are they which testify of me' (John 5:39). In agreement also the apostle Paul writes 'that the righteousness of God through the faith of Jesus Christ is being testified' (Rom 3:21) by the law and the prophets, from the divine testimony having been known that God is one and His name is one 'until Rehum,' interpreted as being exalted or lifted up. For where was it necessary for the divine testimony to reach, except to the high and lofty mind, the testimony being a demonstration of it?
It says also in a place: The testimony and the height exist and are found according to the south of the spiritual Jerusalem. It has been said concerning the south.

Regarding what was previously taken from the Vision of Visions: 'Awake, north, and come, south' (Ezekiel 37:9). Therefore, so that we do not repeat the same things many times, being satisfied with what was said then, it is necessary to proceed to the following.

'He shall remain at a place,' he says, not moving from one place to another, but being interpreted as being suspended or having been suspended. For where must the one who reaches a height surpassing all remain? Being suspended or in a high place, not descending nor moving; for it is appropriate and profitable to remain in holiness for those who have reached the end and that perfection after much progress.

The Gate of Benjamin, being taken as the right or the son of days, is the introduction of the divine mysteries and the dogmas of the straight way, through which one enters having been enlightened in everything and acting and thinking rightly, being called a son of the right and of the days. Understand if the son of light is a son of days, concerning whom the Savior also said to those near him, 'the sons of this age are wiser in their generation than the sons of light' (Luke 11:30), to whom it is written: 'Even as children of light, so walk' (Ephesians 5:8).

'From the gate' of the enlightened and the righteous, which is 'first' because it happens to be an introduction, 'even to the gates of the corners.' The gates and corners are understood in two ways: once as being entities that are praised, because they make the walls one, the head of which, the cornerstone, Christ has been proved to be the foundation and the end: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner' (Psalm 118:22), being also the foundation of those being built upon it, to whom the wise architect, having placed the head of the Church, characterizes thus: 'Having been built up on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus being the cornerstone' (Ephesians 2:20).

And Paul had the Savior called a cornerstone, having taken from above from the prophecy of Isaiah upon himself the prophetic word from the face of God: 'Behold, I lay in Zion a chosen and precious cornerstone, and I will lay it in the foundation; and he who believes in him will not be put to shame' (Isaiah 28:16). And Peter, the disciple of Christ, in his epistle placed the Lord, being a living stone, as the foundation and the head of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Tower of Circumcision and Spiritual Wine
english: Concerning the holy building of the Church. 5.107 Alternatively, it can be said concerning the corners that they are as if they were false, in which hypocrites having stood pray, swelling with ambition, so that they might be shown to be God-fearing. For these corners, which begin from the first gate, are no longer saving. For there is no other corner or break from the straightness, since [gapped] being led into knowledge or virtue, they do not become outside the straightness, but in corners [gapped] they have friction and wear.

5.108 In these corners, the prostitute masquerading also sits with her hands in the marketplaces, that is, falsely glorifying shameful things. 'For in a house, she says, her feet do not rest; for she wanders outside for a certain time, and for another time she sits at every corner of the marketplace,' [the deception] of the rejoicing youth. For she, while prowling, is able to hunt nothing other than this youth being devoid of reason, nor is she approaching the one who has been defeated by prudence and has a precious old age in an unblemished life.
5.109 Since also praised corners were found in the Scripture, let us understand their difference, so that we may see which ones it is necessary to flee and which ones it is not fitting.

5.110 The gates after the gate of Benjamin and according to the first rank are corners, the entrances of those being united and harmonizing, which it is good to enter—for they are of righteousness—concerning which a command is given: 'Open the gates, let the people guarding truth enter' (Ps 118:19), and the following: the hymnodist has cried out concerning these: 'Open to me the gates of righteousness; having entered into them, I will confess to the Lord' (Ps 117:19). The non-good corners are not called corners at all, but rather this very thing of the street corners; and street corners, not those in which wisdom leads to boldness, but those of the marketplace and the wide space forbidding [one] to the destruction.

5.111 And the praised entrances reach as far as the tower of Anemiel, interpreted as circumcision by grace. But the grace of circumcision exists not as that being performed according to the letter of the flesh, but as that being made life-giving according to the spirit of the heart. And the tower of Anemiel may be the citizenship according to the Gospel and the hidden Judaism.

For from where the Savior taught, saying to the disciples: 'Which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sitting down calculate if he has the things for completion, lest ever having laid the foundation and not being able to finish, those watching begin to mock him, saying: This man began to build and was not able to finish' (Luke 14:28); it is spoken by way of a parable concerning practical and contemplative life. But not such are those having the grace of circumcision; for having laid the foundation, they fulfilled the building, as to lay down a house and a crown.

For having set out to build a tower of their own life, they completed it, so as to have in it a refuge and a secure dwelling, because they watch for the enemies approaching from afar. Having fulfilled this, the builder says gratefully to the one who worked with him: 'You have guided me, that you became my hope, a tower of strength from the face of an enemy.'

He who has reached as far as the grace of the tower of circumcision and as far as the banquets of the great king Christ, dwells on a vine to receive the grapes being harvested from the true vineyard and its fruit-bearing branches, so that he, the one gladdening the heart of man, might make wine.

Concerning such things contemplated and concerning the banquets, songs and psalms were written. For our mind shall not be so impoverished as to receive concerning sensible banquets and banquets of the spirit-bearing men through the provision of the Holy Spirit as having spoken, but concerning high things of the intellect.

That which is said in the Song of Songs by the bride to the companions of the bridegroom, 'Bring me into the house of wine, arrange love upon me' (Song of Solomon 1:2), assists in dwelling upon such banquets.

Of those having been fulfilled by the presented prophecy, there shall no longer be an anathema, since Jerusalem now dwells with the trust upon the king, having learned that 'it is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man' (Psalm 40:4), and the proverbial saying: 'Blessed is he who has trusted in the Lord' (Jeremiah 17:7). How then, these things existing, is there still an anathema to be contemplated? For this is said in two ways,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Jerusalem and the Church
english: When the prohibition is shown by the wording, and when the thing set apart and confessed to God is shown. Regarding the former, it should be said as it is written: 'If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be anathema' (1 Cor 16:22), and having it thus: 'No one speaking by the Spirit of God says: Anathema Jesus' (1 Cor 12:3). For this being the meaning, Paul wished 'to be anathema for the brothers and kinsmen according to the flesh' (Rom 9:3). And regarding the latter being signified: of the word anathema, there are many things to gather from the history of the Scriptures, which the philologist will find for himself.

When Jerusalem shall indeed dwell with certainty, no one shall still be to be anathematized in it, nor any foundation, the carved things and the earthen things having been destroyed from it. For these things having become outside, it shall dwell certainly having the spiritual safety, concerning which the prophet Jeremiah expressed, having said: 'And blessed shall be the man who has trusted in the Lord' (Jer 17:7).

And this shall be the fall, which the Lord will cut off all the peoples who turned against Jerusalem; their flesh shall fail while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes shall run out from their sockets, and their tongue shall fail in their mouths (Zech 14:12). This fall is for those who have encamped against it and surround it with trenches. What indeed is it that he pre-pronounces for those circling the beautiful city Jerusalem? They shall fail, he says, their flesh standing on their feet, that is, from much hunger or thirst of the expected evils and calamities. To this extent indeed the failure of their flesh shall be, as to hide their eyes and for them to come out of the sockets and for their tongue to fail in their mouth.
But this wickedness has exceeded not only those who circled and besieged the sensible Jerusalem, but also those who persecuted the Christian...

...and the Church of Christ, Jerusalem being [viewed] by way of an ascent. The history of Christians contains many things both terrible and true; [they] were judged by divine decree against those who attacked the servants of God and the gathering places, to scatter them into the ground and deliver the divine books to fire. More extensively regarding such things has been treated for us in the commentaries on Isaiah, which we send forward to the beautiful ones for reading as an exhortation.

God strikes those who surrounded Jerusalem by way of wars, so that they might fall from the steady state which they guarded by remaining in superstitious worship. When this fall occurs profitably, a resurrection and a standing shall be received, having praises exceeding all.

Concerning this vision, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, the justified Simeon, receiving into his arms the infant born of the virgin Mary, says that he shows this: 'Behold, this lies for a fall and a resurrection of many' (Luke 2:34-35).

For on his account they fall, and the fleshly [ones], so that having been raised according to the holiness of God they might be shown secure, having been firmly established in faith and other virtue, according to that which was written by the Apostle to the ecclesiastical [ones]: 'In faith you have stood' (1 Cor 16:13). And this standing occurs with the Savior Jesus; for it is to him that one must learn, saying: 'There are some of those standing here who shall by no means taste death' (John 8:51).

Those thus benefited cast off the fleshly mindset and the eyes seeing badly, so that they might no longer be in the flesh, but in the spirit, and no longer live wickedly and adulterously, but uprightly and soberly, killing the deeds of the body with the spirit and turning the eyes away from vanity, lifting them toward God so as to say: 'To you I lifted up my eyes, you who dwell in heaven' (Ps 123:1), and again: 'The...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Wealth of Judah and the Garments of the Church
english: My eyes are always toward the Lord.

Similarly, according to the theory applied, one should attempt to take what was said in the Gospel by our Savior, as previously brought forward: 'I came into the world for judgment, so that those not seeing might see and those seeing might become blind' (John 12:47). For the eyes of those seeing sinfully, having been hardened in seeing badly, there will be a dimming regarding seeing rightly and holily.

It is possible also to apply another understanding to the Gospel. Since the Jews, blaspheming the Lord impiously while unfaithfully denying Him, it was fitting that they be blinded, according to what was said in a prophet: 'The servants of God were blinded' (Isa 53:7), those falsely promising to serve Him; and when this happened, those called from the Gentiles into faith rose up, since it had come to pass that he said: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me, having sent me to preach to the poor, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind' (Luke 4:18), having enlightened them with His own wisdom, according to what is written: 'The wisdom of a man lights up his face' (Prov 15:30).

One should also take up what was proclaimed in the Psalms: 'The Lord makes the wise blind' (Ps 146:8), so that they might no longer be shown as blind but as seeing sharply, once the eyes of those seeing wickedly have been hindered and have fallen away from their own pupils—and these are the natural meanings—the eyes that see God. Man raises these eyes toward Him just as he says: 'To You I lifted up my eyes, You who dwell in heaven' (Ps 123:1).

After the flesh has been subdued, whose mindset is enmity toward God, and of those seeing impiously with eyes flowing from the interpreted pupils, so that those seeing sharply may be shown, concerning whom the Apostle writes the word having this expression: 'The eyes of the heart having been enlightened' (Eph 1:18), it is said in harmony that the tongue should also be ordered in the mouth of those having a harmful and material-matter-centered speech, so that what is said by the wise to the Master of all may exist: 'My tongue shall meditate on Your righteousness alone' (Ps 103:2). [Zechariah 14:13-14: And it shall be in that day a great confusion of the Lord upon them, and each will take hold of the hand of his neighbor. And his hand will be joined to the hand of his neighbor...]
Not his. And Judah will array himself in Jerusalem and will gather the strength of all the peoples around him, gold and silver and clothing in a very great multitude.

In the day of the Lord, what the prophet taught was accomplished: a great ecstasy of the Lord upon them, the Lord granting it, the ecstasy here declaring a wonder through negligence and thoughtlessness. For in the prophet Hosea, what is written: 'The sons of Israel shall turn and shall seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they shall stand astonished at the Lord and at His good things' (Hosea 14:2), declares a wonder, or, as some have said, a marvel. Of the same thought exists also that which is written by Habakkuk: 'I have understood your works and was astonished' (Habakkuk 3:2). The prophet says that the ecstasy thus interpreted having come from the Lord upon those being benefited, has become enlarged.

When this happens, 'Judah will array himself in Jerusalem,' concerning which it was said: 'Judah, your brothers praised you,' the Judah who confesses above all. But the receiving Judah arrays himself, confessing in the true Jerusalem, in which 'he who dwells shall not be shaken for ever,' in order to gather around him the strength of all the peoples, gold and silver and a multitude of garments, which is very great.

Often it has been made clear also in other divinely inspired writings, and to the prophet who is set forth for examination, to signify the mind enlightened by the sign of gold and the prudent and exact word by the analogy of silver. Therefore it is appropriate to apply fittingly the gold and the silver and the garments, the great multitude of which the holy Judah has gathered around him from all the peoples, that is, from all those having believed from the nations.

For clothing and garments, according to divine analogy, are the virtues according to kind and the actions performed according to them, and the doctrines of piety and the mysteries of the truth. With these garments she is covered: the bride of Christ, being the Church, and a queen, as it is sung in the forty-fourth and fourth Psalm: 'The queen stood at your right hand, arrayed and adorned in gold' (Psalm 45:13), and adds: 'In embroideries...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fall of Horses and Mules
english: Adorned and variegated with gold.

For the Holy Spirit does not teach regarding bodily pleasures to such an extent as to think so, but rather regarding garments that clothe and adorn the inner man, about which it is commanded in Ecclesiastes: 'Let your garments always be white' (Eccl 9:8), which God himself clothes and endows the soul that speaks thankfully: 'I will rejoice in the Lord; for he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and the robe of gladness' (Ps 30:5).

Toward this one swelling with worldly pleasures, the one providing her the same as a bridegroom says: 'I have clothed you in fine linen and purple' (Zech 14:8), fine linen being the beautiful and subtle thoughts and works woven out, and purple being the actions and words of the senses woven together, like the purple growing from the earth, so as to be compared to the sensible things.

Judah, being arrayed as a gathering, seeing the peace of the strong Jerusalem by intellect, gathered the spiritual treasures of the people which are gold, silver, and a great abundance of garments, clearly signifying the mind and the word according to the interpretations by allegory, and the provided clothing being gathered in great abundance. Sufficiently having become clear regarding the present word, we set forth the following to him.
And this shall be the fall of the horses and the mules and the camels and the donkeys and all the cattle that are in those encampments, according to this fall (Zech 14:15).

Just as nations that stood badly have fallen blessedly and risen praiseworthily, as it was correctly interpreted, so the horses, mules, camels, and donkeys according to allegory, having fallen from the position in which they are such, will rise salvationally upon a special good.

For the mares having become those that lust after the mates of their neighbors, they have fallen from the passion of the lover and the state of adultery, in order that they might rise in a praiseworthy resurrection, concerning which Jesus said to those being instructed: 'Arise, let us go from here' (Matt 20:22), and toward the Church having become his bride from the nations he cries: 'Arise, come, my beloved' (Song 2:10). The apostolic [teaching] possesses this understanding here: 'Arise, you who sleep, and rise from the dead' (Eph 5:14)...

"...seeing, and Christ will shine upon you." Similarly to the fall of horses, the mules will also fall, because of a sterility of soul, such as they are called. Concerning both of these animals, the divine Word says to men: "Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding." (Psalm 147:10). Just as the promiscuous and the many-partnered are called horses, so too a mule might be said allegorically of a virgin possessing an incorrupt body, though not necessarily being holy in the Spirit. Because of such a sterility, even the one who has been castrated is called a mule, not for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, but for the sake of pleasing men.

After the fall, the horses and mules, having been assigned [that role], will rise up and will have the power to charge against those for whom the saints said: "Mount upon your horses, and your cavalry is salvation." (Psalm 147:8). Likewise, the mule will undergo the transformation interpreted by David, whom I call the Savior, riding and charging royally.

In the same manner, the camels and the donkeys and all the other cattle found in those encampments, as is clearly shown, will fall down and rise up. According to the fall of the horses and those called as such, men who study the divine law by rote, but without distinguishing what is to be practiced from what is not, are camels according to tropology.

For indeed, the students of the law, who lift up words by 'nibbling' and devouring 'as if chaff' the pre-laid food, do not break the weapon nor sharpen the claw; they are found to be unclean, not distinguishing the practice from the non-practice. Such are the Jews according to the flesh, who do not divide the Spirit from the letter, nor the truth from the shadow, nor even the things being clearly performed from those being acted out through wickedness, whence it is thus: They are considered a "sinful nation and a people full of sins," because there is not enough for purity from emptiness, that is, to study in vain, according to that which is said concerning them: "The people have studied in vain." (Jeremiah 2:8). For having been born outside the instruction of the one "who begot them and exalted them," all heard as one: "A son who abandons the keeping of his father's instruction will meditate on evil words." (Proverbs 28:7).
Of those according to...
